__notes__.note.synthesis.residue-and-the-predictio: The calibration residue was not derived (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}). Under the area-law hypothesis it is the reciprocal of four times the counted modes' mean thermal entropy, so the registered value $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ of Prediction \claimref{pred.boundary-mode-density} is the case in which every counted mode has zero Killing weight. The one weight assignment the series makes, the s-wave convention of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}, does not give that value under any reading of which modes are counted. Counting arrays gives $0.3470$ against $0.3607$, about four per cent low; counting every mode drives the residue up without bound; counting only the zero-weight modes leaves $0.0272$ nats per array outside the area law. Since (Q) is adopted for one step only and the result is a conditional reformulation, this neither meets nor fails the prediction's kill condition. It does mark where the prediction is exposed: a derivation that fixed the weights as (Q) does would return a residue other than the registered one and so, by the kill condition, refute the intrinsic-clock premise (IC).
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-step-4e-compute: The chain's pairs are fermionic; the directly derived spectrum is Fermi-Dirac. The observed Hawking flux is dominated by photons, whose occupancy is Bose-Einstein. The bridge is bosonisation, and its setting is not imported: the boundary modes form a one-dimensional fermion array with the boost as its clock, which is exactly the setting of the boson-fermion correspondence \cite{PressleySegal1986}, met from the physics side by the standard s-wave reduction of near-horizon field theory \cite{RW2005}. \emph{Scope declaration, once for the section:} every statement here concerns the s-wave-reduced sector; the four-dimensional lift is a point of contact at the end, flagged as assembly. One matter of notation belongs in the declaration. The paper carries three index sets for the boundary modes: the points of $E \cong \R \times S^{2}$ (Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-one-sided-completion-singularity}), the $\mathbb{Z}$-array of this section with weights $\omega_k = \kappa k$, and the Planck cells of the stretched singularity (Step 6a). Axiom (C1) names the identification of the first with the third; the identification of the first with the second, the aggregation of $E$'s sphere factor into a single s-wave array with a filled sea, is likewise an identification and not a theorem, made here as part of the s-wave reduction and flagged as such.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-eviction-theore: The theorem's content is that under boundary-mode locality the falling branch is not a statistical effect and not the outcome of a scrambling mechanism: it is the window's contents, read off. Typicality is not used anywhere, and neither is any assumption about where correlations are deposited, because under (L$_E$) nothing the window does can move a marginal. What the theorem does not deliver, for any mode the chain admits, is exact saturation of the envelope: maximal entanglement is $c_k = s_k$, which by the thermofield angle $\tan^{2}\theta_k = e^{-\omega_k/\TH}$ is the zero-frequency case $\omega_k = 0$; the linear assignment of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} supplies exactly one such mode, the sea level, so saturation, which needs every window member at zero frequency, is unavailable to any window of two or more members; at every nonzero weight $h_k < \ln 2$ strictly, and the falling branch runs strictly inside the capacity. What this paper claims without typicality is therefore the envelope, the exact rising branch, the quantified falling branch $S_R = \sum_{W} h_k$ and the endpoint, and not the saturated Page curve, which remains available on exactly two routes: typicality (Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality}), or the zero-frequency idealisation. the section “The finite-mode model: the dissolution step by step” exhibits the shortfall in numbers, and Proposition \claimref{singularity.models-entropy-sequence-exactly} states the conclusion.
__notes__.note.state-selection.setting-fixing-rate: The calibration converts rapidity to time. What remains is to fix the modular period in rapidity, and here the input is a regularity condition. This section states it, shows that the framework supplies its habitat rather than importing it wholesale, and derives the temperature.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-fixing-rate-whe: The Euclidean-regularity reading of the period is Gibbons-Hawking \cite{GibbonsHawking1977, HartleHawking1976}; the proposition's contribution is the exact rational-function form $dF/d\varrho = f'/2$ in $F = \sqrt f$ and the period computed rather than chosen.
__notes__.note.singularity.what-does-residual: Remark \claimref{note.singularity.declared-residual-size}'s question, whether the physical dynamics on the singular boundary is generated within the supplied class or carries a differential or pairing term, splits into two halves of different kinds. A differential term would hop occupation between points of $E$ and would break the joint diagonality that Step 6b uses, and off the vacuum it entangles, as any hop does (the script exhibits one on $|10\rangle$); but it cannot move the vacuum, and so cannot create entanglement from it. A pairing term moves the vacuum, and only a pairing term does. The premised content of (L$_E$) is thereby separated into its two parts, both class-relative in the sense of Theorem \claimref{singularity.class-relative-no-go-no-supplied}: the exclusion of pairing terms, which is the statement that the closure supplies no generator in the $\nu(\nu - 1)/2$-dimensional tangent of the vacuum ray, and the exclusion of the unsupplied hops, the differential dynamics, which lie in the stabiliser and are excluded by the premise for the diagonality Step 6b uses rather than for what they do to the vacuum. Its necessity, Corollary \claimref{singularity.envelope-endpoint-why-boundary-mode-locality}, is the statement that one generator in the tangent, acting once on one pair, is what the return of the boundary modes needs. The framework compares two Witt decompositions and does not derive them; nothing here changes that, and the derivation of the one pairing angle the chain uses, the angle of Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}, remains outside its reach (Proposition \claimref{singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-internal}).
__notes__.note.singularity.steps-status-what-still:
Collecting: hypothesis (i) is Theorem \claimref{singularity.purity-output-partner-commutant}; hypothesis (ii) is not needed for the form at all (Theorem \claimref{singularity.descended-form-state-independent}), and its per-mode content follows from (P) (Theorem \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal}); hypothesis (iii) follows from (R) (Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, whose gluing condition is stated by evaluation and does not presuppose a modular group); and the value of $\TH$ follows from (R) with the period computed in Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}, and provably from nothing internal (Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}, Proposition \claimref{singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-internal}). The exact equilibrium condition (G) is not a premise of this step: it is examined and found too strong for the evaporating boundary modes (Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes}), the class the chain uses is Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}'s, and the one place the chain later adopts the (G) member is Step 4e's (Q), for the equilibrium reading of the Planck sector alone. The status line in the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} is accordingly \emph{proved from (P), (R)} rather than \emph{up to a state}, where (R) is the KMS condition at the geometric period, imposed mode by mode; the premises of the later steps, (Q) in Step 4e, (C1) to (C3) in Step 6a and (L), (U), (C), (I), (L$_E$) in Step 6b, are named where those steps are proved.

Four things remain open and are recorded as such. (a) (R) is an import, and Proposition \claimref{singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-internal} shows it cannot be removed by strengthening the framework's statements at the singular boundary; the open route is the spectrum-condition restatement of Remark \claimref{note.singularity.cost-r-dictionary}, which belongs with T9 \cite{ButlerT9}. (b) (L$_E$) is a statement about which generators the localisation theorems supply; the class-relative no-go is Theorem \claimref{singularity.class-relative-no-go-no-supplied} (the section “The metric-level sheaf, and the hopping exclusion”): no supplied generator hops, the supplied class being the second quantisations of function-linear maps of the mode line bundle and the products of the parity sections, an ultralocal class of multiplication operators. What would settle the premise outright is Remark \claimref{note.singularity.declared-residual-size}'s residual question, whether the physical dynamics on $E$ carries a differential or a pairing term; the necessity witness of Corollary \claimref{singularity.envelope-endpoint-why-boundary-mode-locality} is itself a pairing rotation, which the theorem's criterion does not exclude; Proposition \claimref{singularity.l-stabiliser-tangent} reads the two residual types in $\mathfrak{so}(2\nu)$. (c) Theorems \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}, \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic} and \claimref{singularity.purity-output-partner-commutant} and Proposition \claimref{singularity.two-kms-functionals-sign} are proved in the matrix factor, which is where this step works, and their multi-mode applications, Corollary \claimref{singularity.universality-temperature-under-g} and Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes}, extend them to finite collections of modes factor by factor, and where the section “Step 4e: compute in the completion; from fermions to photons” invokes them on the $\mathbb{Z}$-array the reading is through finite mode subsets, on which every quantity involved is defined, no global entropy being claimed on the infinite array; in the field-theoretic setting the horizon algebra is a type III$_1$ factor, the Gibbs form is unavailable, and the KMS condition must be used directly, in the simplex form of Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-general-form}, with \cite{KayWald1991} as the template. (d) Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii} treats the sphere directions of $E$ as inert, correct for Schwarzschild by symmetry; the corresponding statement over a rotating horizon, where $\kappa$ is still constant but the Killing flow is not the static one, is untouched, and belongs with the Kerr programme of \cite{ButlerT4, ButlerT6}.
__notes__.note.state-selection.dictionary: The standard alternatives sit on the line as follows. $\beta_k = \infty$ for all $k$: the Boulware analogue, ladder unoccupied, no radiation, zero deficit, excluded by (R). $\beta_k = 2\pi/\kappa$ for all $k$: the Hartle-Hawking and Unruh analogue, the GMC state, selected by (R). $\beta_k$ finite but not constant in $k$: no geometric modular flow by Corollary \claimref{singularity.universality-temperature-under-g}, so a state for which the modular clock is not the Killing boost at all. $\beta_k = 0$: the tracial state, infinite temperature, excluded with the other boundary case. The chain's contribution to the dictionary is that the entries are points of an explicitly parametrised line rather than incommensurable constructions.
__notes__.note.state-selection.true-price-r: Premise (R) is not derived from the transport principle, and this note does not claim otherwise. It is the same premise that every derivation of the Hawking temperature uses: regularity of the Euclidean section at the bifurcation point in \cite{GibbonsHawking1977, HartleHawking1976}, regularity on the horizon in \cite{Unruh1976}, nonsingularity of the quasi-free state in \cite{KayWald1991}, the short-distance condition in \cite{FredenhagenHaag1990}. Dropping it gives the Boulware alternative \cite{Boulware1975}, which in this framework is the $\beta = \infty$ endpoint of the line: an unoccupied ledger, a descended state that is pure, a deficit of zero by \cite[Thm.~9.3]{ButlerT5}, and no flux. What the framework contributes is not the premise but its habitat. In a metric formulation the Euclidean section is a separate construction; here, by Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected}, the object whose periodicity is being demanded is the second member of the very eigenplane pair that Step 4b's curvature equation selects, and its period is fixed by the double cover of the rotor group, not by a coordinate choice. The premise is thereby stated in the same algebra as the rest of the chain, and its content is exactly one number.

angle.hop-sea-filled-pairing.technical:
Let $V = (a_{1} + a^{\dagger}_{1})\Gamma_{0}$ on the pair, with $\Gamma_{0} = (-1)^{N_{0}}$ and $\ket{11} = a^{\dagger}_{0}a^{\dagger}_{1}\ket{00}$. It is unitary and Hermitian with $V^{2} = 1$, and conjugation by $V$ fixes $a_{0}$ and exchanges $a_{1}$ with $a^{\dagger}_{1}$: it is the particle-hole automorphism of the right mode. It carries the hop ground state $\psi = \tfrac35\ket{10} + \tfrac45\ket{01}$ to $V\psi = \tfrac45\ket{00} + \tfrac35\ket{11}$, the even thermofield pair at the sample point, with the same left marginal $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$.

The hop generator becomes a pairing generator, $VHV^{-1} = 7N_{0} - 12(a^{\dagger}_{0}a^{\dagger}_{1} + a_{1}a_{0})$, with the same spectrum and unique ground state $V\psi$, and the equal-frequency boost becomes the number-difference boost, $V(N_{0} + N_{1} - 1)V^{-1} = N_{0} - N_{1}$. Read with the right mode's occupation inverted, the hop is the pairing.
angle.hop-sea-filled-pairing.lay: In the two-mode model, swap the roles of "particle" and "empty slot" on one side only. Under this swap a term that hops particles across the horizon becomes a term that creates or removes pairs, and the lowest-energy state of the hopping model becomes exactly the paired, thermal-looking state used in the earlier analysis of the singularity. The view from the other side does not change, so the two models describe the same correlation.

The script checks the unitarity, the automorphism on the four ladder operators, the image of $\psi$, its parity and marginal, the conjugated generator against the pairing generator entry by entry, its ground state, and the conjugated boost. angle.imported-singularity-papers-state-.technical:
This entry restates the singularity paper's state selection for a horizon pair. A state vector of the pair that is boost invariant up to phase and cyclic and separating has the form $\cos\theta\,\ket{00} + \sin\theta\,\ket{11}$, and its one-sided marginal $\operatorname{diag}(\cos^{2}\theta, \sin^{2}\theta)$ is the Gibbs state for the number operator with $\tan^{2}\theta = e^{-\beta\omega}$; the sample point $e^{-\omega/T} = \tfrac{9}{16}$ corresponds to $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$. The algebra does not fix $\beta$: every automorphism of the mode factor that intertwines the boost flow acts on $\beta$ only through $\{\pm 1\}$.

The value comes from the geometry and a premise. The surface gravity is $\kappa = 1/4M$, the Euclidean section is smooth at the bifurcation sphere exactly for the period $2\pi/\kappa$, and premise (R) imposes KMS at that period mode by mode. The supplied class of boundary-mode generators, the number-diagonal class that the boundary-mode locality premise (L$_E$) admits, is ultralocal, and the s-wave array has weights $\omega_{k} = \kappa k$ with its sea level at $k = 0$, the convention of premise (Q).
angle.imported-singularity-papers-state-.lay: For a pair of modes straddling a black hole horizon, the states that look the same under the horizon's boost form a one-parameter family, and each of them looks thermal from one side. The algebra alone cannot say which temperature is right; it is set by requiring the geometry to be smooth at the horizon, an assumption (premise (R)) that gives the Hawking value. This entry gathers those earlier results, together with two further premises it rests on: that the framework's own dynamics never moves particles between points (premise (L$_E$), boundary-mode locality), and that the modes are jointly in the simplest thermal state with evenly spaced energies (premise (Q)).

For the horizon pair, a state vector that is invariant up to phase under the boost and cyclic and separating for the pair factor has the form $\cos\theta\,\ket{00} + \sin\theta\,\ket{11}$ with $\cos\theta\sin\theta \neq 0$ (the cyclic and separating hypothesis excludes the product vectors $\ket{01}$, $\ket{10}$, which are also invariant up to phase); its one-sided marginal is $\operatorname{diag}(\cos^{2}\theta, \sin^{2}\theta)$, the Gibbs state for the number operator at $\tan^{2}\theta = e^{-\beta\omega}$; the sample point $e^{-\omega/T} = \tfrac{9}{16}$ has $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$. Every automorphism of the mode factor intertwining the boost's phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK})$ acts on $\beta$ through $\{\pm 1\}$ only. The surface gravity is $\kappa = 1/4M$, the Euclidean section is smooth at the bifurcation sphere exactly for the period $2\pi/\kappa$, and (R, \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) imposes KMS at that period mode by mode. The supplied class (\claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality}) is ultralocal, and the s-wave array of Step 4e has weights $\omega_{k} = \kappa k$ with its sea level at $k = 0$ (by \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}). \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lem.~7.2, Thm.~7.3, Thm.~7.16, Prop.~7.18, Prem.~7.19, Prop.~7.25, Rem.~7.26, Prem.~7.30, Rem.~7.33, Prem.~8.1, Thm.~C.8, Rem.~C.9, Prop.~A.2]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}, \claimref{singularity.modular-descent}, \claimref{singularity.schmidt-forcing-proved-outright}, \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}).

angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hy.formal: For a Wightman field theory in Minkowski space, the modular group of the algebra of a wedge with respect to the vacuum is the one-parameter group of boosts preserving the wedge, with modular parameter $t$ corresponding to rapidity $2\pi t$, and the modular conjugation is the CPT operator composed with the rotation by $\pi$ about the boost axis, which acts on spacetime as the wedge reflection $(x^{0}, x^{1}) \mapsto (-x^{0}, -x^{1})$; the hypotheses are the spectrum condition (positivity of the energy-momentum), Poincar\'e covariance and locality. The abstract form: if a von Neumann algebra $M$ with cyclic separating vector $\Omega$ carries a one-parameter unitary group $U(a)$ with positive generator, $U(a)\Omega = \Omega$ and $U(a)MU(a)^{*} \subseteq M$ for $a \geq 0$, then the modular group of $(M, \Omega)$ acts on the translations as the dilation $\Delta^{it}U(a)\Delta^{-it} = U(e^{-2\pi t}a)$. For the free massless field the modular groups of the wedge and double-cone algebras are geometric, and for a conformal net on the circle the modular group of an interval's algebra is the M\"obius flow fixing the interval's endpoints, again at $2\pi$. On a spacetime with a bifurcate Killing horizon the same mechanism gives the Hawking temperature for states regular across the horizon, and a stationary quasi-free state that is regular is unique and KMS at $\kappa/2\pi$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{BW1975, BW1976}; \cite{Borchers1992}; \cite{HislopLongo1982, BGL1993}; \cite{Sewell1982, KayWald1991}; the Rindler case \cite{Unruh1976}.
angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hy.technical:
The Bisognano-Wichmann theorem: for a Wightman field theory in Minkowski space, the modular group of the algebra of a wedge with respect to the vacuum is the group of boosts preserving the wedge, with modular parameter $t$ at rapidity $2\pi t$, and the modular conjugation acts on spacetime as the wedge reflection $(x^{0}, x^{1}) \mapsto (-x^{0}, -x^{1})$. Its hypotheses are the spectrum condition, Poincaré covariance and locality.

Borchers' abstract form: if a von Neumann algebra $M$ with cyclic separating vector $\Omega$ carries a unitary group $U(a)$ with positive generator, fixing $\Omega$ and with $U(a)MU(a)^{*} \subseteq M$ for $a \geq 0$, then $\Delta^{it}U(a)\Delta^{-it} = U(e^{-2\pi t}a)$. The same factor $2\pi$ appears for the wedge and double-cone algebras of the free massless field, for interval algebras of a conformal net on the circle, and on spacetimes with a bifurcate Killing horizon, where a stationary quasi-free state that is regular is unique and KMS at $\kappa/2\pi$.
angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hy.lay: These are the standard theorems of quantum field theory that produce the factor $2\pi$ behind the Unruh and Hawking temperatures. They say that when energy is positive and the theory respects relativity and locality, the natural internal clock of the region on one side of a horizon is the horizon's boost, running at a fixed rate. The entry records their hypotheses, since those are what any attempt to use them must supply.

angle.value-parameter-dynamics.formal: For every rational point $(c, s)$ of the unit circle with $cs \neq 0$ and every rational $t$ with $tcs > 0$, the hop generator $H = \varepsilon N_{0} - t(a^{\dagger}_{0}a_{1} + a^{\dagger}_{1}a_{0})$ with $\varepsilon/t = (s^{2} - c^{2})/(cs)$ has $c\ket{10} + s\ket{01}$ as its unique ground state, with eigenvalue $-tc/s$, and left marginal Gibbs for $N_{0}$ at $q = c^{2}/s^{2}$. The Gibbs parameter of the marginal, and with it $\beta\omega = -\log q$, is determined by the ratio $\varepsilon/t$ of the couplings together with the sign of $t$ (by the ratio alone for $t > 0$): $c/s$ is the root of $r^{2} + (\varepsilon/t)r - 1 = 0$ with the sign of $t$.
angle.value-parameter-dynamics.technical:
Take the two-mode hop generator $H = \varepsilon N_{0} - t(a^{\dagger}_{0}a_{1} + a^{\dagger}_{1}a_{0})$, a rational point $(c, s)$ of the unit circle with $cs \neq 0$, and a rational $t$ with $tcs > 0$. Choosing $\varepsilon/t = (s^{2} - c^{2})/(cs)$ makes $c\ket{10} + s\ket{01}$ the unique ground state, with eigenvalue $-tc/s$, and its left marginal is Gibbs for $N_{0}$ at $q = c^{2}/s^{2}$.

So the Gibbs parameter of the marginal, and with it $\beta\omega = -\log q$, is fixed by the coupling ratio $\varepsilon/t$ together with the sign of $t$. A hop can select an entangled ground state with a finite $\beta$, but the value of $\beta$ is set by the couplings.
angle.value-parameter-dynamics.lay: In the two-mode model with a hopping term, the lowest-energy state can be made to look thermal from one side at any of a whole family of temperatures. Which temperature appears is set by the ratio of the two strengths in the generator and the sign of the hopping strength. So the finite model shows that a hop can produce a thermal-looking state, but by itself it does not fix one particular temperature.
angle.value-parameter-dynamics.typing_note: No edges: the proof is a self-contained finite computation; the link to rate rigidity is made only in a following remark.

proofs.main: The one-particle block $\begin{psmallmatrix} \varepsilon & -t \\ -t & 0\end{psmallmatrix}$ has $(c, s)$ as an eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda = -tc/s$ exactly when $\varepsilon c - ts = \lambda c$, i.e.\ $\varepsilon = t(s^{2} - c^{2})/(cs)$; the other one-particle eigenvalue is $\varepsilon - \lambda$, and the three gaps, to it and to the sector energies $0$ and $\varepsilon$, are $ts/c + tc/s$, $tc/s$ and $ts/c$, all positive exactly when $tcs > 0$. The script confirms the eigenvector, the gaps and the marginal at seven points, $(\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$, $(\tfrac{5}{13}, \tfrac{12}{13})$, $(\tfrac{8}{17}, \tfrac{15}{17})$, $(\tfrac{7}{25}, \tfrac{24}{25})$, $(\tfrac{24}{25}, \tfrac{7}{25})$ and $(-\tfrac35, -\tfrac45)$ at $t = 60$ and $(\tfrac35, -\tfrac45)$ at $t = -60$. Given $\varepsilon/t$, the ratio $c/s$ is the root of $r^{2} + (\varepsilon/t)r - 1 = 0$ with the sign of $t$ (the two roots have product $-1$) and $q$ is its square.

angle.within-supplied-class-spectrum-con.technical:
Let $H$ be a generator in the supplied class on $\nu$ modes, a polynomial in the number operators, and let a cut divide the modes into two sides. Then $H$ is diagonal in the joint number basis, so a unique ground state is a number basis state: a product across the cut with a pure marginal on each side, an eigenvector of every $N_{k}$ and of every boost generator $\sum_{k}\omega_{k}(N_{k} - \tfrac12)$, and Gibbs on a side at no finite $\beta$. This is a Boulware-type state.

If the ground state is not unique, the ground space may contain entangled states, but the spectrum condition singles out none of them: for $H = (N_{0} - N_{1})^{2}$ on the pair, the ground space $\operatorname{span}\{\ket{00}, \ket{11}\}$ contains both the thermofield pair $\tfrac45\ket{00} + \tfrac35\ket{11}$ and the product state $\ket{00}$. Within the supplied class, positivity of the energy selects a Boulware-type state or no state, so Claim G fails at the state-selection step.
angle.within-supplied-class-spectrum-con.lay: The framework's own dynamics for the horizon modes never moves particles from one mode to another. This result shows that with only such dynamics, asking for the lowest-energy state either picks out a state with no correlation across the horizon, which is not thermal on either side, or picks out nothing because several states tie. So within that dynamics the requirement of positive energy cannot by itself select a thermal state.
angle.within-supplied-class-spectrum-con.typing_note: No edges: the supplied class enters as an explicit hypothesis (a polynomial in the number operators), so the singularity paper's results defining it are vocabulary rather than premises.

proofs.main: (i) By Theorem \claimref{singularity.class-relative-no-go-no-supplied} the supplied class is ultralocal, every generator in it a multiplication operator in the joint number basis, so a polynomial in the commuting projectors $N_{k}$. A polynomial in commuting projectors is diagonal in their joint eigenbasis; a diagonal matrix with a unique minimum has that basis vector as its unique ground state. A number basis state is a product of single-mode number states, its marginal on any set of modes is the corresponding number state, pure, and it is an eigenvector of each $N_{k}$. A Gibbs state $e^{-\beta K}/Z$ at finite $\beta$ for a single-mode boost $K = \omega(N - \tfrac12)$ is $\operatorname{diag}(1, e^{-\beta\omega})/Z$, of rank two, and a pure marginal has rank one. The script draws random rational diagonal generators on two and three modes with every cut, and for each draw with a unique ground state (at least three such draws in all) confirms the product form, the rank-one idempotent marginals on both sides, the eigenvector property, and, for a single-mode side, the absence of a Gibbs parameter. (ii) The stated $H$ has eigenvalues $0, 0, 1, 1$ on $\ket{00}, \ket{11}, \ket{10}, \ket{01}$; the script checks the ground space and that both named states are annihilated by $H$.

dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-alge.formal: On the window of the boundary mode space the number-conserving bilinears satisfy the free-boson current algebra exactly in the completed limit (with the finite-window deviation an explicit difference of edge operators), and the current sector is modular-invariant. Under the singularity paper's premise (Q) (\cite[Premise~8.1]{ButlerT5}: the joint state of the mode array is the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with the marginals its premises (P) and (R) fix, with the linear s-wave weights $\omega_k = \kappa k$ and the sea level at $k = 0$), the induced state is KMS, thermal at $\TH$-analogue temperature, for the joint modular flow; without (Q) only the marginals are thermal. The charge-zero sector is canonically the bosonic Fock space, an assembly-level identification the singularity paper bases on the boson-fermion correspondence \cite{PressleySegal1986}. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[\S 8, Premise~8.1]{ButlerT5}; the finite-window quantification \cite[\S 6]{ButlerT7}.
dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-alge.technical:
On a window of the boundary mode space, the number-conserving bilinears of the fermion modes satisfy the free-boson current algebra exactly in the completed limit, and on a finite window the deviation is an explicit difference of edge operators. The current sector is invariant under the modular flow.

Under premise (Q), which takes the joint state of the mode array to be the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with the marginals fixed by (P) and (R), with linear s-wave weights $\omega_{k} = \kappa k$ and sea level at $k = 0$, the induced state on the currents is KMS for the joint modular flow at the $\TH$-analogue temperature; without (Q) only the marginals are thermal. The charge-zero sector is identified with the bosonic Fock space at assembly level, through the boson-fermion correspondence.
dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-alge.lay: Pairs of fermion operators on the horizon modes behave exactly like a free boson field, with precisely identified corrections at the edges of any finite set of modes. If one further assumes that the modes are jointly in the simplest thermal state (premise (Q)), the boson field is thermal at the Hawking-type temperature; without that assumption only the individual modes are known to be thermal. This entry imports these results from earlier in the series.

hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantifi.formal:
Let the ladder carry the linear s-wave weight assignment (the convention T5's Premise (Q) adopts, a modelling input here as there; Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}): level spacing $\epsilon$, sea at level $0$, I-state occupancies $n_k = (x^{-k} + 1)^{-1}$ with $x = e^{-\beta\epsilon} \in (0,1)$ the Boltzmann factor of the level spacing. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Detailed-balance identity.)} For every $k$ and $m \ge 1$, exactly,
\[
n_k - n_{k+m} \;=\; \bigl(x^{-m} - 1\bigr)\; n_{k+m}\,\bigl(1 - n_k\bigr).
\]
\item \emph{(The Planck factor, exactly, in the bilateral limit.)} Summing (1) over $k \in \Z$,
\[
\sum_{k \in \Z} n_{k+m}\,(1 - n_k) \;=\; \frac{m}{x^{-m} - 1} \;=\; \frac{m}{e^{\beta\epsilon m} - 1}:
\]
the current two-point function $\langle a_m^\dagger a_m\rangle_I = \sum_k n_{k+m}(1 - n_k)$ (a Wick computation) is exactly $m$ times the Bose-Einstein value at $\TH$, with no vacuum correction in this normalisation. The factor $m$ is the free-boson normalisation: on the bilateral ladder the currents are used only inside expectations, and $\langle [a_m, a_m^\dagger]\rangle_I = \sum_k (n_k - n_{k+m}) = m$, the telescoped left side of (1), matching the finite-window scalar of Proposition \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split}; the unit-normalised boson is $\hat a_m = a_m/\sqrt{m}$, whose occupancy $\langle \hat a_m^\dagger \hat a_m\rangle_I = 1/(e^{\beta\epsilon m} - 1)$ is the $n_-$ of the lift.
\item \emph{(Window tails.)} For the window $[-K, K]$ with the sea at the centre, i.e.\ the sum of (2) restricted to $k \in [-K, K-m]$ (both mode indices inside the window), the bilateral sum exceeds the window sum by a positive amount bounded by $2m\,x^{K - m}/(1 - x)$: exponentially small in the distance from the sea to the edges, in units of the level spacing.
\end{enumerate}
hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantifi.technical:
On the bilateral ladder with level spacing $\epsilon$ and the sea at level $0$, carrying the linear s-wave weight assignment as a modelling input, the I-state occupancies are $n_k = (x^{-k}+1)^{-1}$ with Boltzmann factor $x = e^{-\beta\epsilon} \in (0,1)$. They obey the exact detailed-balance identity $n_k - n_{k+m} = (x^{-m}-1)\,n_{k+m}(1-n_k)$ for every $k$ and every $m \ge 1$.

Summing over $k \in \Z$, the left side telescopes to $1$ in each of the $m$ residue classes modulo $m$, so $\sum_{k} n_{k+m}(1-n_k) = m/(e^{\beta\epsilon m}-1)$. This sum is the current two-point function $\langle a_m^\dagger a_m\rangle_I$, so the unit-normalised boson $\hat a_m = a_m/\sqrt{m}$ has exactly the Bose-Einstein occupancy $1/(e^{\beta\epsilon m}-1)$ at $\TH$. On the window $[-K, K]$ with the sea at the centre, the bilateral sum exceeds the window sum by a positive amount at most $2m\,x^{K-m}/(1-x)$.
hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantifi.lay: A ladder of fermion levels, filled thermally in the Fermi-Dirac pattern, can be repackaged into collective boson modes. Given the s-wave modelling convention for the ladder, this result shows by an exact algebraic identity that on the infinite ladder those collective modes have exactly the Bose-Einstein thermal occupancy at the Hawking temperature. On a finite window of levels centred on the filled sea, the answer falls short only by a positive amount that shrinks exponentially as the window edges move away from the filled sea.

proofs.main:
(1) With $u := x^{-k}$ and $w := x^{-m}$ (the I-state occupancies of \claimref{hawking.i-state} on the linear s-wave weights of \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}): $n_k - n_{k+m} = \tfrac{1}{u+1} - \tfrac{1}{uw+1} = \tfrac{u(w-1)}{(u+1)(uw+1)}$, and $(w-1)\,n_{k+m}(1-n_k) = (w-1)\cdot\tfrac{1}{uw+1}\cdot\tfrac{u}{u+1}$: identical. The script checks it as an identity of rational functions in the formal variable $u$ at several rational $w$.
(2) The terms $n_{k+m}(1 - n_k)$ decay like $x^{|k|}$ in both directions, so all sums converge absolutely and may be regrouped. Fix a residue class $k = r + jm$, $j \in \Z$: the class sum of the left side of (1) is $\lim_{j_0 \to \infty}\sum_{j=-j_0}^{j_0}\bigl(n_{r+jm} - n_{r+(j+1)m}\bigr) = \lim_{j_0 \to \infty}\bigl(n_{r-j_0 m} - n_{r+(j_0+1)m}\bigr) = 1 - 0$, the interior terms cancelling in adjacent pairs; there are $m$ residue classes, and dividing by $(x^{-m}-1)$ via (1) gives the display. The Wick computation: in the gauge-invariant quasi-free state, $\langle \psi^\dagger_{l+m}\psi_l\,\psi^\dagger_k\psi_{k+m}\rangle$ has vanishing disconnected part for $m \ge 1$ (the two-point function is mode-diagonal) and connected part $\delta_{kl}\,n_{k+m}(1 - n_k)$.
(3) Bound each term two ways, both valid for every integer index: $n_{k+m}(1-n_k) \le n_{k+m} \le x^{k+m}$ and $n_{k+m}(1-n_k) \le 1 - n_k \le x^{-k}$, since $n_j \le x^j$ and $1 - n_j \le x^{-j}$ are each the statement $1 \le 1 + x^{\pm j}$. The terms missing from the window sum are those with $k > K - m$ or $k < -K$, all positive, so the difference is positive and at most
\[
\sum_{k > K-m} x^{k+m} + \sum_{k < -K} x^{-k} \;=\; \frac{2\,x^{K+1}}{1-x} \;\le\; \frac{2m\,x^{K-m}}{1-x}.
\]
The script verifies instances of the bound exactly, and checks that the window sums at $K = 30$ and $K = 40$ agree with the closed form to within the proven tails, all in exact rational arithmetic.

hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-.formal:
In the finite window, exactly and as an operator identity,
\[
[\,a_m,\, a_m^\dagger\,] \;=\; B_m - T_m, \qquad
B_m := \sum_{k=1}^{m} N_k, \qquad T_m := \sum_{k=L-m+1}^{L} N_k ,
\]
with $N_k = \psi_k^\dagger\psi_k$: the deviation from the infinite-volume central value is a difference of \emph{edge operators}, supported on the lowest and highest $m$ modes. Consequently, for $2m \le L$, on every state in which the bottom $m$ levels are filled and the top $m$ levels are empty (an \emph{edge-clean} state), $[a_m, a_m^\dagger]$ acts as the scalar $m$: the free-boson relation holds exactly, not asymptotically, on the edge-clean subspace. Moreover $[a_m, a_{m'}] = 0$ for all $m, m'$, exactly; and for $m \neq m'$ the cross commutator $[a_m, a_{m'}^\dagger]$ is a difference of bilinears supported on the lowest and highest $\max(m, m')$ modes, which annihilates every state that is edge-clean at depth $\max(m, m')$.
hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-.technical:
Take a window of $L$ fermionic modes and the currents $a_{m} = \sum_{k=1}^{L-m}\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{k+m}$. Then, exactly, $[a_{m}, a_{m}^{\dagger}] = B_{m} - T_{m}$, where $B_{m}$ and $T_{m}$ are the total occupations of the lowest and highest $m$ modes. The deviation from the infinite-volume central value is therefore a difference of edge operators, and on every edge-clean state (bottom $m$ levels filled, top $m$ levels empty, with $2m \le L$) the commutator is exactly the scalar $m$.

Moreover $[a_{m}, a_{m'}] = 0$ exactly, and for $m \neq m'$ the cross commutator $[a_{m}, a_{m'}^{\dagger}]$ is a difference of bilinears supported on the lowest and highest $\max(m, m')$ modes, which annihilates every state that is edge-clean at that depth.
hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-.lay: On a finite set of fermion levels, certain collective operators behave almost like a free boson field. This result locates the discrepancy exactly: it comes only from the lowest and highest few levels. Whenever the bottom levels are full and the top levels empty, the boson relations hold exactly rather than approximately.
hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-.typing_note: No edges: the proof uses only the canonical anticommutation relations of the window, which the statement sets up itself.

proofs.main:
The fermionic bilinear commutator is $[\psi_a^\dagger\psi_b,\ \psi_c^\dagger\psi_d] = \delta_{bc}\,\psi_a^\dagger\psi_d - \delta_{ad}\,\psi_c^\dagger\psi_b$, an instance of the CAR (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}). With $a_m^\dagger = \sum_{l=1}^{L-m}\psi_{l+m}^\dagger\psi_l$:
\[
[a_m, a_m^\dagger] = \sum_{k,l=1}^{L-m}\bigl(\delta_{k+m,\,l+m}\,\psi_k^\dagger\psi_l - \delta_{k l}\,\psi_{l+m}^\dagger\psi_{k+m}\bigr)
= \sum_{k=1}^{L-m} N_k - \sum_{k=m+1}^{L} N_k ,
\]
after shifting the index of the second sum. The shared middle range cancels pairwise: for $2m \le L$ the terms $k = m{+}1, \dots, L{-}m$ appear in both sums and cancel, leaving $B_m - T_m$; for $2m > L$ the two sums instead share the empty middle and the overlap $k = L{-}m{+}1, \dots, m$ of $B_m$ and $T_m$ cancels on the right-hand side, so the identity $\sum_{1}^{L-m} N_k - \sum_{m+1}^{L} N_k = B_m - T_m$ holds in both regimes. On an edge-clean state (which requires $2m \le L$ to be non-vacuous), $B_m$ acts as $m$ (each bottom mode occupied) and $T_m$ as $0$. For the cross commutators, the same computation gives
\[
[a_m, a_{m'}] = \sum_{k}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m+m'} - \sum_{k}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m+m'} = 0
\]
exactly, both surviving sums running over the same range $1 \le k \le L - m - m'$; and, for $m > m'$,
\[
[a_m, a_{m'}^\dagger] = \sum_{k=1}^{m'}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m-m'} \;-\; \sum_{k=L-m+1}^{L-m+m'}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m-m'},
\]
every surviving index within $\max(m,m')$ of an edge. Each bottom term annihilates an edge-clean state because its target level $k$ is occupied; each top term because its source level $k + m - m'$ lies in the empty top band. The case $m < m'$ follows by taking adjoints, $[a_m, a_{m'}^\dagger] = [a_{m'}, a_m^\dagger]^\dagger$, with the same band support; it annihilates edge-clean states by the mirrored argument (creation onto an occupied bottom level, lowering of an empty top level). The script verifies the identity on the full Fock space of an eight-mode window, state by state.

hawking.full-uniqueness-given-dynamics.formal: Among all states of $\mathfrak{A}$, $\omega_I$ is the unique $\tau$-KMS state at $\beta$.
hawking.full-uniqueness-given-dynamics.technical:
On the boundary-mode algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ with the boost dynamics $\tau$ at inverse temperature $\beta$, the I-state $\omega_{I}$ is the only $\tau$-KMS state at $\beta$, among all states and not only within the quasi-free class.

This follows from the imported uniqueness theorem for the ideal Fermi gas, whose hypotheses the definition of the algebra and its dynamics satisfies: the unique KMS state is the quasi-free state with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$, which the quasi-free calculus identifies with $\omega_{I}$. The dynamics and the value of $\beta$ are inputs here, not derived.
hawking.full-uniqueness-given-dynamics.lay: Once the horizon modes' time evolution and the temperature are given, there is exactly one equilibrium state at that temperature, and it is the I-state. This uses a standard result about ideal gases of fermions. It does not explain where the time evolution itself comes from.

hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-inter.formal:
\emph{Premise (I), the interface identification:} the horizon-sector state feeds the exterior modes in the standard way, i.e.\ the occupancy of each near-horizon channel is carried to the corresponding asymptotic channel by the exterior propagation. This is the same assumption every derivation of Hawking flux makes, from \cite{Hawking1975} onward, and it is this assembly's one non-theorem joint. Under (I), the emitted flux in each channel $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ equals (with $\mathcal{N}$ the count of emitted quanta)
\[
\frac{d\mathcal{N}}{dt\,d\omega} \;=\; \frac{1}{2\pi}\,\Gamma_{s\ell m}(\omega)\; n_\pm(\omega), \qquad
n_\pm(\omega) = \frac{1}{e^{\omega/\TH} \pm 1}
\]
(the upper sign for the fermionic species, the lower for the bosonic sector), with $\Gamma_{s\ell m}$ the classical transmission coefficient through the Regge-Wheeler or Teukolsky barrier. The joints: (i) the barriers and their transmission coefficients are properties of the exterior metric, and by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-exterior-exactly-general-relativity} the framework's exterior description \emph{is} classical general relativity on the invertible region, exactly and not asymptotically, so $\Gamma_{s\ell m}$ is inherited verbatim, mode by mode \cite{ReggeWheeler1957, Teukolsky1973}; (ii) the occupancies at the horizon are Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} for the fermionic species and Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}'s (Q)-conditional half for the bosonic sector, both at exactly $\TH$ with the temperature's coefficient fixed geometrically (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation}); (iii) given (I), the displayed formula is the definition of filtered thermal flux: the framework's flux prediction equals Hawking's \cite{Hawking1975, Page1976}, greybody structure included.
hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-inter.technical:
Under premise (I), that the occupancy of each near-horizon channel is carried by the exterior propagation to the corresponding asymptotic channel, the emitted flux in each channel $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ is $d\mathcal{N}/(dt\,d\omega) = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\Gamma_{s\ell m}(\omega)\,n_{\pm}(\omega)$ with $n_{\pm}(\omega) = 1/(e^{\omega/\TH} \pm 1)$, the upper sign for fermionic species and the lower for the bosonic sector, and $\Gamma_{s\ell m}$ the classical transmission coefficient through the Regge-Wheeler or Teukolsky barrier.

The joints: the transmission coefficients are inherited verbatim, because the framework's exterior description is classical general relativity on the invertible region; the horizon occupancies are the continuum I-state for the fermions and, conditional on premise (Q), the bosonic sector, both at $\TH$ with the coefficient of the temperature fixed geometrically; and, given (I), the displayed formula is the definition of filtered thermal flux, so the framework's flux prediction equals Hawking's, greybody structure included.
hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-inter.lay: Radiation leaving a black hole is thermal at the horizon, but part of it is scattered back by the black hole's gravitational field outside the horizon, so what reaches a distant observer is filtered. This result combines the framework's thermal horizon state with the ordinary general-relativistic filtering, under the interface premise (I), that what is emitted near the horizon is carried outward in the standard way. For the boson-like part it also relies on a further premise, (Q), about the joint state of the modes. The outcome is the usual Hawking spectrum, including its filtering factors.

hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised.formal:
Helicity is not additional structure imported into the framework: it is the eigenvalue of the distinguished $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ charge of the completion's conformal storey (the twistor storey: $\Cl(2,4)$ with its conformal spinor space $\CS$), and the four-dimensional mode space of each massless species has a canonical place in it. The joints, each with its provenance:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{Joint J1: the transform, classical.}) By Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-penrose-transform}, the helicity-$s$ mode space is the cohomology at homogeneity $-2s-2$; photon kinematics are at homogeneities $-4$ and $0$ ($s = \pm1$), graviton kinematics at $-6$ and $+2$ ($s = \pm2$).
\item (\emph{Joint J2: the charge, proved in the series.}) The ordering shift is proved in the correspondence paper (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift}), and Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift} derives the homogeneity $-2s-2$ from it: the classification parameter of Joint J1 is an internal charge of the completion, so the helicity ladder is part of the ascended kinematics rather than a phenomenological label.
\item (\emph{Joint J3: the reduction, modelling.}) The current boson of the s-wave theory (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}) is the s-wave reduction of each such four-dimensional field, and the lift from the boundary modes to the field is the standard partial-wave reconstruction, each helicity sector identified through the transform of Joint J1: the near-horizon reduction of field theory on the Schwarzschild exterior identifies each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel with a two-dimensional mode, which is where Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}'s modelling input enters, flagged as such in Remark \claimref{note.hawking.which-dynamics-what-level}.
\end{enumerate}
The composite statement is the conjunction of the three joints with the provenance displayed: J1 is classical, J2 is Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} together with Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift}, and J3 is the one modelling joint. The homogeneity table is checked by the script.

The composite statement is the conjunction of the three joints and holds under premise J3.
hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised.lay: Massless particles such as photons and gravitons carry helicity, a measure of how they spin about their direction of motion. This result reads helicity as a charge already present at the framework's conformal level, the level whose spinors describe light rays, by combining a classical theorem of Penrose (his transform) with a calculation proved earlier in the series. Connecting it to the horizon modes relies on one modelling assumption, the standard reduction of four-dimensional fields to spherical waves near the horizon.

hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift.formal:
On functions on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor functions), realise the palatial relation of Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} by $\bar Z_\nu = -\hbar\,\partial/\partial Z^\nu$ (the realisation with the palatial sign $[Z^\mu, \bar Z_\nu] = +\hbar\,\delta^\mu_\nu$), let $\Upsilon := Z^\mu \partial_\mu$ be the homogeneity (Euler) operator, its eigenvalue written $\mathsf{h}$ in sans serif to keep it clear of the one-particle Hamiltonian $h$, and let the helicity operator be one half the distinguished charge, $\mathsf{s} := \tfrac12\, q(\id)$, the standard helicity operator on $\CS$ (twistor helicity) \cite{Penrose1969, EPW1981} in the symmetric ordering that Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} forces storey-wide. Then, as an operator identity,
\[
q(\id) \;=\; -\hbar\,(\Upsilon + 2),
\]
so a function on $\CS$ homogeneous of degree $\mathsf{h}$ is an eigenfunction of $\mathsf{s}$ with eigenvalue $s\hbar$ if and only if
\[
\mathsf{h} \;=\; -2s - 2.
\]
The $-2$ is exactly the ordering shift: without the symmetric-ordering shift of $-\hbar/2$ per complex dimension (over the complex unit $I_6$) the offset would vanish. Combined with Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-penrose-transform}, the classification parameter of the Penrose transform is the completion's own $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ charge, its offset supplied by the ordering. The computation is not new to the series: it appears, without being stated as a result, inside the proof of \cite[Thm.~5.7]{ButlerT9}, where T9's script also checks it; what this proposition adds is the statement at result level, in the transform's context, discharging the homogeneity half of the successor problem T9 assigns to this paper (the transform itself stays open).
hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift.lay: In Penrose's description of massless fields, a field's helicity is read off from how its function on the space of conformal spinors scales. This result shows that the particular offset in that rule, the "minus two", comes from the order in which quantum operators are multiplied at the framework's conformal level. The rule that sorts massless particles by helicity is therefore part of the framework's own algebra.
hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift.typing_note: Added the Penrose transform because the statement's closing clause (the transform's classification parameter is the completion's charge) is obtained by combining with it; the operator identity itself needs only the ordering-shift fact. The existing pin on that fact is @1 while it is now at version 2; left for the repin pass.

proofs.main:
With $\bar Z_\nu = -\hbar\,\partial_\nu$,
\[
q(\id) \;=\; \tfrac12\sum_\mu\bigl(Z^\mu \bar Z_\mu + \bar Z_\mu Z^\mu\bigr)
\;=\; \sum_\mu Z^\mu \bar Z_\mu + \tfrac12\sum_\mu [\bar Z_\mu, Z^\mu]
\;=\; -\hbar\,\Upsilon - \tfrac12\cdot 4\hbar \;=\; -\hbar\,(\Upsilon + 2),
\]
the commutator term being $\sum_\mu[\bar Z_\mu, Z^\mu] = -4\hbar$ by the palatial relation, one $-\hbar$ per complex dimension of $\CS$ (over $I_6$); halved by the symmetrisation, this is Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift}'s shift of $-\hbar/2$ per complex dimension, totalling $-2\hbar$, and it is the only place the ordering enters. On a homogeneity-$\mathsf{h}$ eigenfunction, $\Upsilon f = \mathsf{h} f$, so $\mathsf{s} f = -\tfrac{\hbar}{2}(\mathsf{h} + 2)\,f$, and $\mathsf{s} f = s\hbar f$ if and only if $\mathsf{h} = -2s - 2$. The script verifies the displayed operator identity on all monomials of degree at most three in the four components of $Z \in \CS$, and the resulting homogeneity table at $s = \pm 1, \pm 2$. The reading of $\mathsf{h}$ as the classification parameter of the transform rests on \claimref{hawking.imported-penrose-transform}, which classifies helicity-$s$ fields by homogeneity $-2s-2$.

hawking.i-state.formal:
Consider the boundary-mode algebra with its boost dynamics (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}) at inverse temperature $\beta = 1/\TH = 2\pi/\kappa$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Existence, exactly on windows.)} The quasi-free state $\omega_I$ with the Fermi-Dirac symbol
\[
A_I \;=\; \bigl(1 + e^{\beta h}\bigr)^{-1}, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad n_j = \frac{1}{e^{\omega_j/\TH} + 1},
\]
restricts on every window to the Gibbs state of $H_F = \sum_{j \in F}\omega_j N_j$ and is KMS there, exactly (Lemma \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}); it is the unique quasi-free extension of these window states, and it is $\tau$-KMS at $\beta$ on the full algebra by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-limits}.
\item \emph{(Gauge invariance is forced.)} If a quasi-free state of $\mathfrak{A}$ is $\tau$-KMS at $\beta$, its pairing vanishes: the state is gauge-invariant automatically.
\item \emph{(The symbol is derived.)} Its symbol then satisfies the operator identity $A(1 + e^{-\beta h}) = e^{-\beta h}$, equivalently $A = e^{-\beta h}(1 - A)$, whence $A = A_I$: within the quasi-free class, the state whose modular clock is the geometry's clock is unique, and its two-point data are forced.
\end{enumerate}
hawking.i-state.technical:
Take the boundary-mode algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ with its boost dynamics $\tau$ at $\beta = 1/\TH = 2\pi/\kappa$. The quasi-free state $\omega_I$ with Fermi-Dirac symbol $A_I = (1+e^{\beta h})^{-1}$, that is occupancies $n_j = 1/(e^{\omega_j/\TH}+1)$, restricts on every window $F$ to the Gibbs state of $H_F = \sum_{j\in F}\omega_j N_j$ and is KMS there exactly; it is the unique quasi-free extension of these window states, and it is $\tau$-KMS at $\beta$ on the whole algebra.

Within the quasi-free class the converse holds. Applying the KMS identity to two creation operators shows that the pairing vanishes, so a quasi-free $\tau$-KMS state at $\beta$ is automatically gauge-invariant. Applying it to a creation and an annihilation operator, with the CAR, gives $A(1+e^{-\beta h}) = e^{-\beta h}$, hence $A = A_I$: the two-point data are forced, and $\omega_I$ is the unique quasi-free state whose modular clock is the geometry's clock.
hawking.i-state.lay: The boundary modes in this black-hole setting can be placed in a thermal state at the Hawking temperature, each mode filled according to the Fermi-Dirac rule. This result shows that this state exists and is thermal in the precise algebraic sense, both on every finite set of modes and on the whole system. It also shows that among the simple Gaussian (quasi-free) states it is the only one that is thermal for the geometry's boost time evolution, which turns the phase of each mode at its own frequency, so its occupation numbers are derived rather than chosen.
hawking.i-state.typing_note: All three uses are genuine premises: the Gibbs lemma for window KMS, the inductive-limit fact for the full algebra, and the quasi-free fact for the window product state and for determination by two-point data.

proofs.main:
(1) On a window $F$, the quasi-free state with diagonal symbol is the product state of Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra} with $n_j = (1 + e^{\beta\omega_j})^{-1}$, which is exactly the Gibbs density matrix of $H_F$: $e^{-\beta H_F} = \bigotimes_j \mathrm{diag}(1, e^{-\beta\omega_j})$, normalised; the script builds the two sides independently and confirms the identity in exact arithmetic. Lemma \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite} gives the KMS identity on the window, exactly; the script verifies it on a three-mode window at rational Boltzmann factors, on a spanning set of pairs. The windows are nested with dense union and the dynamics preserves each, so Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-limits} passes the KMS property to $\mathfrak{A}$.
(2) Apply the KMS identity to the pair $x = a^\dagger(f)$, $y = a^\dagger(g)$, with $f, g$ supported in windows (so that $\alpha_{i\beta}(a^\dagger(f)) = a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)$ is again a generator):
\[
P(f, g) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(f)\,a^\dagger(g)\bigr) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(g)\,a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\bigr) \;=\; P(g,\, e^{-\beta h}f).
\]
Antisymmetry of creation operators gives $P(f, g) = -P(g, f)$, so $P(g, (1 + e^{-\beta h})f) = 0$ for all $f, g$ in the dense span of the windows; $1 + e^{-\beta h}$ is bounded with bounded inverse and preserves that span, so $P = 0$.
(3) Apply the KMS identity to the pair $x = a^\dagger(f)$, $y = a(g)$:
\[
\omega\bigl(a^\dagger(f)\,a(g)\bigr) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a(g)\,a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\bigr)
\;=\; \ip{g}{e^{-\beta h}f} - \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\,a(g)\bigr),
\]
using the CAR $\{a(g), a^\dagger(f')\} = \ip{g}{f'}$. In symbols: $\ip{g}{Af} = \ip{g}{e^{-\beta h}f} - \ip{g}{Ae^{-\beta h}f}$ for all $f, g$ supported in windows, i.e.\ $A(1 + e^{-\beta h}) = e^{-\beta h}$ on the dense span, i.e.\ $A = e^{-\beta h}(1+e^{-\beta h})^{-1} = (1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1} = A_I$ (all four operators bounded, $h \ge 0$ here). By (2) and Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}, the state is determined by its two-point data, which are forced, so $\omega = \omega_I$. The mode-diagonal scalar identity $n = e^{-\beta\omega}(1-n)$, equivalently the detailed balance $n/(1-n) = e^{-\beta\omega}$, is checked by the script as an exact identity of rational functions.

hawking.i-state-continuum.technical:
Let $\mathfrak{h}$ be a separable one-particle space with self-adjoint $h$, $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ the continuum mode algebra with the quasi-free dynamics $\tau$, and $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$. The quasi-free state $\omega_{I}$ with symbol $A_{I} = (1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ is $\tau$-KMS at $\beta$; when $h$ has pure point spectrum, its finite spectral windows are instances of the exact window theorem, as for the tower's mode space.

Any quasi-free $\tau$-KMS state has vanishing pairing, and on the dense $\tau$-invariant core of bounded spectral subspaces the KMS identity forces its symbol to equal $A_{I}$, so within the quasi-free class the continuum I-state is unique. Because the imported ideal-Fermi-gas uniqueness theorem holds for general self-adjoint $h$, $\omega_{I}$ is also the unique $\tau$-KMS state among all states.
hawking.i-state-continuum.lay: The earlier result about the horizon's equilibrium state was proved for a countable list of modes. This result carries it over to a continuous range of frequencies, as real radiation needs. The same thermal state, at the Hawking temperature, is again the only equilibrium state, and the energies need not be positive for this to hold.
hawking.i-state-continuum.typing_note: Added the imported Fermi-gas uniqueness, on which the closing all-states clause rests, and the continuum mode space definition to about; the full-uniqueness corollary is cited as the countable-mode analogue and is not used as a premise.

proofs.main: (3) is the computation of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}(3) with the stated core in place of the window span: the core is $\tau$-invariant, $e^{-\beta h}$ preserves it and is bounded on it, and density plus boundedness of $A$ and $A_I$ extend the bounded identity $A = A_I$ from the core to $\mathfrak{h}$; the unbounded identity is used only on the core, where $1 + e^{-\beta h}$ acts bijectively. (2) is Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}(2) on the same core. (1): the state $\omega_{A_I}$ exists for the symbol $0 \le A_I \le 1$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}); its two-point function satisfies the two-point KMS identity by (3) read backwards, and Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-two} upgrades the two-point identity to the KMS property of the state. What this paper certifies independently, and the script checks exactly, is the window case, where no imported calculus is needed. The closing uniqueness clause rests on \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness}, which gives a unique $\beta$-KMS state, the quasi-free state with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$, for any self-adjoint $h$.

hawking.imported-penrose-transform.formal: Massless free fields of helicity $s$ on (suitably convex regions of complexified) Minkowski space (complexified with the unit $I_4$, points $u + I_4 w$) are in natural isomorphism with the first cohomology of the corresponding region of the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor space) with coefficients in $\mathcal{O}(-2s-2)$: the homogeneity $-2s-2$ classifies the helicity-$s$ field. \emph{Provenance:} Penrose \cite{Penrose1969}; the sheaf-cohomological form \cite{EPW1981}.
hawking.imported-penrose-transform.technical: The Penrose transform identifies the massless free fields of helicity $s$ on suitably convex regions of complexified Minkowski space, the complex unit being $I_4$, with the first sheaf cohomology of the corresponding region of the conformal spinor space, with coefficients in $\mathcal{O}(-2s-2)$. The homogeneity $-2s-2$ therefore classifies the helicity-$s$ field.
hawking.imported-penrose-transform.lay: A classical result of Penrose says that every massless field, such as light or gravitational waves, can be encoded as a geometric object on the space of spinors of conformal geometry. The encoding depends on the field's helicity only through a single integer describing how that object scales.

hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-a.formal: For every operator $A$ on $\ell^2(J)$ with $0 \le A \le 1$ (the \emph{symbol}) there is a unique gauge-invariant state $\omega_A$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ with two-point function $\omega_A(a^\dagger(f)\,a(g)) = \ip{g}{Af}$ and all higher truncated functions zero (Wick determinants). More generally, a quasi-free state (all truncated functions beyond second order vanishing) is determined by its full two-point data, the symbol together with the pairing $P(f, g) := \omega(a^\dagger(f)\,a^\dagger(g))$, and gauge invariance is exactly $P = 0$. On a finite window with diagonal symbol this is the explicit product state $\bigotimes_j \rho_j$, $\rho_j = \mathrm{diag}(1 - n_j,\, n_j)$ in the occupation basis, which the script realises exactly. \emph{Provenance:} Araki \cite{Araki1971}; \cite[\S 5.2]{BratteliRobinson1997}.
hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-a.technical:
For every operator $A$ on $\ell^2(J)$ with $0 \le A \le 1$ there is a unique gauge-invariant state $\omega_A$ on the CAR algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ with two-point function $\omega_A(a^\dagger(f)\,a(g)) = \ip{g}{Af}$ and all higher truncated functions zero, so that the higher correlators are Wick determinants. More generally, a quasi-free state is determined by its symbol together with its pairing $P(f,g) = \omega(a^\dagger(f)\,a^\dagger(g))$, and gauge invariance is exactly $P = 0$.

On a finite window with diagonal symbol the state is the explicit product $\bigotimes_j \rho_j$ with $\rho_j = \mathrm{diag}(1-n_j,\, n_j)$ in the occupation basis. This is standard material, imported from the literature.
hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-a.lay: For fermions there is a class of especially simple states, called quasi-free, in which every correlation is fixed by the two-point correlations alone. This imported result says that each admissible choice of occupation data gives exactly one such state that is invariant under phase rotations, and that a quasi-free state is invariant in this way exactly when a certain pairing term vanishes. On finitely many modes with no mixing these states simply occupy each mode independently.

hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector.formal: Two halves, at two levels. \emph{Unconditional:} on a window of the boundary mode space, the number-conserving bilinears (currents) satisfy the free-boson commutation relations exactly in the completed limit, with an exact finite-window operator identity whose deviation is a difference of edge operators; and the bilinear subalgebra is globally invariant under the modular boost. \emph{Conditional on T5's Premise (Q), joint quasi-freeness with the s-wave weights:} the restriction of the Fermi-Dirac KMS state to the bilinear subalgebra is KMS at the same temperature (an instance of Lemma \claimref{hawking.kms-restricts-invariant-subalgebras} below), giving the Bose-Einstein occupancy at $\TH$ for the s-wave sector; the linear weight assignment is the s-wave reduction's convention, adopted there as part of the premise. \emph{Provenance:} T5 \cite[Prem.~8.1, Thm.~8.2]{ButlerT5}; the correspondence itself is classical \cite{FrenkelKac1980}. The exact edge identity is reproved, in the form this paper needs, as Proposition \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split} below.

hawking.imported-thermal-representation.formal: The GNS representation of $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ in the state $\omega_I$ is the Araki-Wyss representation: a doubled Fock space carrying two commuting copies of the CAR, with the GNS vector entangling them pairwise and the modular operator of the GNS vector implementing exactly the flow $\tau$ at inverse temperature $\beta$. \emph{Provenance:} Araki-Wyss \cite{ArakiWyss1964}; textbook form \cite[\S 5.3]{BratteliRobinson1997}.
hawking.imported-thermal-representation.technical: The GNS representation of $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ in the I-state $\omega_{I}$ is the Araki-Wyss representation. It acts on a doubled Fock space carrying two commuting copies of the CAR, the GNS vector entangles the two copies pairwise, and the modular operator of that vector implements exactly the flow $\tau$ at inverse temperature $\beta$.
hawking.imported-thermal-representation.lay: A thermal state of fermions can be represented as a single pure state of two copies of the system, entangled pair by pair. In that representation the state's natural internal time evolution is exactly the physical time evolution at the given temperature. This is a standard result of quantum statistical mechanics.

obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-window.formal: Fix a countable mode set $J$ with Schwarzschild frequencies $\omega_j > 0$ ($j \in J$), the frequencies the geometry assigns to the boundary modes (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation}). \emph{Provenance of $J$:} the boundary modes are the ladder pairs of the blown-up singular boundary, one per point, aggregated over the s-wave channels into the countable array of Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}, an identification the singularity paper makes and flags. By convention here (it is in neither the singularity paper nor the thermality paper, and reconciles the array's weights $\kappa k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, with $\omega_j > 0$), the modes below the level enter $J$ through their particle-hole conjugates, so that every frequency is positive, and the one zero-frequency mode of the array lies outside $J$; the bookkeeping is filed alongside (synthesis.s-wave-array-is-a-boundary-mode-set). The tower of iterated completions is the algebra's model, not the source of its countability: its limit is the CAR algebra with the adjoined null pairs as modes (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}), while on the physical closure one ascent completes the description and further rungs lie on shadow walls outside the physical region (Corollary \claimref{tower.answers-iteration-question}). The \emph{boundary-mode algebra} $\mathfrak{A}$ is the CAR algebra over $\ell^2(J)$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}), the C*-inductive limit of the \emph{window algebras} $\mathfrak{A}_F$, $F \subset J$ finite, each $\mathfrak{A}_F \cong \End(\Lambda^\bullet \C^F)$ of dimension $4^{|F|}$. The \emph{boost dynamics} is the one-parameter group $\tau_t$ acting on generators by $\tau_t(a_j) = e^{-i\omega_j t}\,a_j$, with $t$ Schwarzschild time: the quasi-free flow whose one-particle Hamiltonian is $h = \mathrm{diag}(\omega_j)$; it preserves every window. In rapidity $\lambda = \kappa t$ the same flow has boost weights $\omega_j/\kappa$ and modular temperature $2\pi$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation}); in Schwarzschild time the inverse temperature is $\beta = 1/\TH = 2\pi/\kappa$, and this normalisation is used throughout.
obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-window.technical:
Fix a countable mode set $J$ with Schwarzschild frequencies $\omega_{j} > 0$. The set $J$ indexes the s-wave aggregate of the ladder pairs of the blown-up singular boundary, one pair per point, as the singularity paper identifies them, with, by this definition's own convention, the modes below the level entering through their particle-hole conjugates and the single zero-frequency mode left outside; the tower of iterated completions supplies the algebra's form, not the count, since the physical closure needs one ascent only. The boundary-mode algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ is the CAR algebra over $\ell^{2}(J)$, the C*-inductive limit of the window algebras $\mathfrak{A}_{F} \cong \End(\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{F})$ for finite $F \subset J$, each of dimension $4^{|F|}$. The boost dynamics is the quasi-free flow $\tau_{t}(a_{j}) = e^{-i\omega_{j}t}a_{j}$ in Schwarzschild time $t$, with one-particle Hamiltonian $h = \mathrm{diag}(\omega_{j})$; it preserves every window.

In rapidity $\lambda = \kappa t$ the same flow has boost weights $\omega_{j}/\kappa$ and modular temperature $2\pi$; in Schwarzschild time the inverse temperature is $\beta = 1/\TH = 2\pi/\kappa$, the normalisation used throughout.
obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-window.lay: This definition sets up the algebra describing a black hole's horizon modes: a collection of fermion modes, each with a frequency fixed by the geometry, built up from finite groups of modes. The modes come from the singularity's boundary, one pair per point, gathered into a countable list by keeping the spherically symmetric part; the tower of repeated completions is used only as a mathematical model of the algebra they form, not as the reason there are countably many. It also fixes how the modes evolve in time, each rotating at its own frequency, and the temperature scale that goes with that evolution.

obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space.formal: Let $\mathfrak{h}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space (the one-particle space; for the Schwarzschild s-wave sector, $L^2(\R_+, d\omega)$; with angular channels, a direct sum of copies indexed by $(\ell, m)$ and species), and let $h$ be self-adjoint on $\mathfrak{h}$ (the one-particle Hamiltonian of Schwarzschild time; for the s-wave sector, multiplication by the frequency $\omega$; self-adjointness, not positivity, is what the theorems below use, and the section “The finite boundary mode space, and the $\ell_P^2/A$ correction”'s bilateral ladder is an instance with spectrum unbounded below). The \emph{continuum mode space} is the CAR algebra $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ with the quasi-free (Bogoliubov) dynamics $\tau_t(a(f)) = a(e^{ith}f)$. The countable mode space of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} is the case $\mathfrak{h} = \ell^2(J)$; the CAR functor turns isometric inclusions of one-particle spaces into unital embeddings of algebras, so refining the tower's mode set into a dense subset of the continuum realises $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ as the completed union of tower-type subalgebras: the continuum is the tower's limit re-parametrised, not a new object.
obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space.technical:
Given a separable complex Hilbert space $\mathfrak{h}$ (the one-particle space; for the Schwarzschild s-wave sector $L^2(\R_+, d\omega)$, and with angular channels a direct sum of copies indexed by $(\ell, m)$ and species) and a self-adjoint one-particle Hamiltonian $h$ on it, the continuum mode space is the CAR algebra $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ with the quasi-free dynamics $\tau_t(a(f)) = a(e^{ith}f)$. Only self-adjointness of $h$ is required, not positivity, so a spectrum unbounded below is allowed.

The countable mode space of the boundary-mode algebra is the case $\mathfrak{h} = \ell^2(J)$. Because the CAR functor turns isometric inclusions of one-particle spaces into unital embeddings of algebras, refining the tower's mode set into a dense subset of the continuum realises $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ as the completed union of tower-type subalgebras: the continuum is the tower's limit re-parametrised, not a new object.
obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space.lay: The boundary modes of a black hole can be labelled either by a countable list or by a continuous range of frequencies. This definition sets up the continuous version: the standard algebra of fermion operators built on a space of one-particle wavefunctions, with time evolution given by a one-particle energy operator. The countable version is a special case, and refining it fills out the continuous one, so nothing new is being introduced.

obj.pairing.pairing-class-transport.formal: The pairing class of the transport along $X$, relative to the vacuum field, is $\pv(\Omega(X)) = \ip{\Omega(X)\cdot\ell}{m}$. The transport preserves the vacuum ray along $X$ if and only if $\pv(\Omega(X)) = 0$ (Proposition \claimref{pairing.stabiliser-parabolic-algebra-null-direction}), and by Proposition \claimref{pairing.pairing-functional-pair-creation-amplitude} the spin transport $\exp(s\,\Omega(X))$ carries the vacuum, to first order in $s$ and up to a scalar, to $\ket{0} - s\,\pv(\Omega(X))\,\ket{12}$: the class is the Thouless amplitude of the mismatch. (Comparing the vacuum field against the transported frame instead reverses the sign; nothing below depends on the convention.)
obj.pairing.pairing-class-transport.technical:
Along a direction $X$ the Levi-Civita connection acts on the Clifford fibre by a bivector $\Omega(X)$, in the sense that $\nabla_X v = \tfrac12[\Omega(X), v]$ for vectors of constant frame components. Relative to a vacuum field with null direction $\ell$ and transverse complex null vector $m$, the pairing class of the transport along $X$ is $\pv(\Omega(X)) = \ip{\Omega(X)\cdot\ell}{m}$.

The transport preserves the vacuum ray along $X$ exactly when $\pv(\Omega(X)) = 0$, and to first order in $s$ the spin transport $\exp(s\,\Omega(X))$ carries the vacuum, up to a scalar, to $\ket{0} - s\,\pv(\Omega(X))\,\ket{12}$: the class is the Thouless amplitude of the mismatch. Comparing against the transported frame instead reverses the sign, and nothing depends on that convention.
obj.pairing.pairing-class-transport.lay: A vacuum state of the fermion fields can be pictured as a choice of light-like direction at each point. Carrying that choice along a path using the geometry of spacetime may tilt it away from where the vacuum field says it should be. The pairing class measures that tilt, and it is the amplitude for the move to create a pair of particles out of the vacuum.

obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condit.formal: Let $K_{\mathrm{geo}} := \sum_k \omega_k K_k$ generate the Killing boost flow of the boundary modes, the flow whose bivector at each point of $E$ is the curvature-selected $\sigma_r$ of Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling} and Corollary \claimref{singularity.matching-steps-4b-4c-join-equation}, with $\omega_k$ the mode's weight. A \emph{faithful} state satisfies the \emph{geometric modular condition} (G) if its modular automorphism group is the phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK_{\mathrm{geo}}})$ generated by $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$, not its real rotor flow, up to a single constant reparametrisation. Faithfulness is part of the condition, not a consequence of it: a state has a modular automorphism group only if it is faithful, so (G) presupposes hypothesis (iii) of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} and cannot be used to derive it.
obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condit.technical:

A faithful state satisfies the geometric modular condition (G) if its modular automorphism group is the phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK_{\mathrm{geo}}})$ generated by $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$, up to a single constant reparametrisation.

Faithfulness is part of the condition: only a faithful state has a modular automorphism group, so (G) presupposes the cyclic-and-separating hypothesis of modular descent and cannot be used to derive it.
obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condit.lay: Every faithful quantum state comes with its own internal clock, its modular flow. It only makes sense for states that are faithful in the technical sense, so it cannot be used to prove that a state is faithful.

obj.synthesis.cosmological-horizon-bound.formal:
Let $\Lambda > 0$, fix a static observer, and let $(v_{\Lambda}, v_{\Lambda}^{*})$ be the completed pair of the cosmological horizon in the plane $\Pi_{\Lambda} = \mathrm{span}\{e_{0}, e_{W}\}$ of the static Killing generator (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cosmological-horizon-completed-pair}). For a finite set $J$, the \emph{boundary modes of the cosmological horizon} on $J$ are pairs $(v_{j}, v_{j}^{*})$, $j \in J$, each a copy of $(v_{\Lambda}, v_{\Lambda}^{*})$ in its own copy $\Pi_{j} = \mathrm{span}\{a_{j}, b_{j}\}$ of $\Pi_{\Lambda}$ ($Q(a_{j}) = 1$, $Q(b_{j}) = -1$, $v_{j} = \tfrac12(a_{j} + b_{j})$, $v_{j}^{*} = \tfrac12(a_{j} - b_{j})$), the copies mutually orthogonal, so that the $v_{j}, v_{j}^{*}$ generate $\Cl(|J|, |J|)$ and satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations
\[
v_{i}v_{j}^{*} + v_{j}^{*}v_{i} = \delta_{ij}, \qquad v_{i}v_{j} + v_{j}v_{i} = 0 ,
\]
the construction of the tower (Definition \claimref{obj.tower.tower}) with one plane per mode. The \emph{boundary-mode algebra} $\mathfrak{B}_{\Lambda}(J)$ is its complexification, with occupation boosts $\sigma_{j} = v_{j}^{*}v_{j} - v_{j}v_{j}^{*}$, boost generators $K_{j} = \sigma_{j}/2 = N_{j} - \tfrac12$, and the static Killing flow
\[
\alpha_{t} \;=\; \operatorname{Ad}\exp\Bigl(it\sum_{j \in J}\omega_{j}K_{j}\Bigr), \qquad \alpha_{t}(v_{j}) = e^{-it\omega_{j}}v_{j},
\]
$\omega_{j} > 0$ the Killing frequency of mode $j$. The geometry supplies one such plane, $\Pi_{\Lambda}$; the further copies are tower planes isometric to it, not realised in the ambient space, and the definition fixes neither $|J|$, the cell calibration on which the horizon's entropy count depends, nor the $\omega_{j}$.
obj.synthesis.cosmological-horizon-bound.technical: The boundary modes of the cosmological horizon are copies of one building block: the completed pair that the static observer's boost plane carries. Each mode gets its own copy of the plane, the copies are orthogonal, and the resulting creation and annihilation operators obey the canonical anticommutation relations, exactly as the tower builds its modes, one plane per rung. The algebra is the complexification, each mode's occupation boost $\sigma_{j}$ gives its boost generator $K_{j} = N_{j} - \tfrac12$, and the static Killing flow turns each mode's annihilator by the phase $e^{-it\omega_{j}}$. How many modes there are, which the horizon's entropy count needs, is not part of the definition.
obj.synthesis.cosmological-horizon-bound.lay: This defines the quantum modes that the cosmological horizon carries in the series' language. Each mode is one copy of the pair of operators that the horizon's geometry supplies, one that removes an excitation and one that adds it, and different modes are kept independent in the standard way for fermions. The observer's clock turns each mode at its own frequency. The definition does not say how many modes there are; that number is what a count of the horizon's entropy would need.
