proofs.main: Every automorphism of a matrix factor is inner, $\theta = \operatorname{Ad}(U)$. (1) Commutation gives $Ue^{itK}U^{*} = c(t)e^{itK}$ with $|c(t)| = 1$; taking determinants, $c(t)^{2} = 1$, and $c$ is continuous with $c(0) = 1$, so $c \equiv 1$ and $U$ commutes with $K$. As $K = \operatorname{diag}(-\tfrac12, \tfrac12)$ is nondegenerate, $U$ is diagonal and $\operatorname{Ad}(U)$ fixes every diagonal matrix, in particular $e^{-\beta K}/Z$. (2) Flow reversal gives $UKU^{*} = -K$, so $U$ exchanges the spectral projectors of $K$ and $Ue^{-\beta K}U^{*} = e^{+\beta K}$. (3) The reparametrised flow is $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{it(cK)})$, generated by $cK$, and by Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} its $\beta'$-KMS state is $e^{-\beta' cK}/Z$, which equals $e^{-\beta K}/Z$ exactly when $\beta' = \beta/c$. (4) By Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} the KMS states are exactly the Gibbs states, and an automorphism intertwining the flow either commutes with it or reverses it (it conjugates $K$ to $\pm K$ up to a constant, the spectrum $\{-\tfrac12, \tfrac12\}$ of $K$ leaving no other option), so by (1) and (2) it acts on the parameter through $\{\pm 1\}$ only. That is the whole mathematical content of the clause; the sentence about what a selecting condition must refer to is its reading, and clause (3) is the reason the reading is exact: $\beta$ is the ratio of the state's modular parameter to the flow's parameter, and the second of these is a choice the algebra does not make. The script verifies clauses (1) to (3) on rational data.

singularity.universality-temperature-und.formal: A state satisfying (G) has $\beta_k = \beta$ independent of $k$ over the modes of nonzero weight: one temperature for all the boundary modes. Conversely a state with per-mode marginals $\mathrm{Gibbs}(\beta_k\omega_k)$ and no inter-mode correlation satisfies (G) only if the $\beta_k$ of the modes of nonzero weight coincide.
singularity.universality-temperature-und.technical:
By KMS uniqueness on the factor, a state satisfying (G) is $\varrho \propto e^{-\beta K_{\mathrm{geo}}} = \bigotimes_k e^{-\beta\omega_k K_k}$, whose marginal at mode $k$ is $\mathrm{Gibbs}(\beta\omega_k)$: the same inverse temperature $\beta_k = \beta$ at every mode of nonzero weight.

Conversely, a product state with marginals $\mathrm{Gibbs}(\beta_k\omega_k)$ has modular generator $-\sum_k \beta_k\omega_k N_k$ up to a constant, which is proportional to $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ only if $\beta_k\omega_k = \lambda\omega_k$ for a single $\lambda$; so it satisfies (G) only if the $\beta_k$ of the modes of nonzero weight coincide. A mode of zero weight constrains nothing.
singularity.universality-temperature-und.lay: If the boundary modes' internal clock runs exactly along the black hole's time symmetry, every mode has the same temperature. Conversely, independent modes at different temperatures cannot have such a clock. Modes that carry no energy are left out, since for them the temperature makes no difference.

Conversely the modular generator of a product state is $\log\varrho = -\sum_k \beta_k\omega_k N_k + \mathrm{const}$, proportional to $K_{\mathrm{geo}} = \sum_k \omega_k N_k + \mathrm{const}$ if and only if $\beta_k\omega_k = \lambda\omega_k$ for a single $\lambda$ and every $k$ of nonzero weight (under Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}'s linear assignment the $k = 0$ mode is excluded from this clause and from the converse: at $\omega_0 = 0$ the marginal is $\tfrac12\,\mathrm{id}$ for every $\beta_0$ and constrains nothing).

singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-in.formal:
The only finite rate the Schwarzschild gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) supplies to the boost flow is the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/4M$, a horizon quantity: on the singular side the connection rate diverges as $\sqrt{M/2r^{3}}$ (Proposition \claimref{singularity.connection-bivector-computed}(3)) and offers no finite period to be identified with $2\pi$. (R) (Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) applies across the horizon locus in the chart: the Euclidean section is regular at its tip, which fixes the period $2\pi/\kappa$; for a state that is KMS for the Killing flow, this is also the period at which it is regular across the horizon locus in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart. The horizon locus is met in a cross-section $\Sigma_{t_0} = \{t = t_0,\ r = 2M\}$ of the horizon locus in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart, of area $16\pi M^{2}$, on which the Killing field $K = \hb^{-1}(e_t)$ is null and normal to the horizon, with $(K \cdot D)K = \kappa K$, $\kappa = 1/4M$; the boost flow is the flow of $K$, which carries cross-sections to cross-sections. There, by Propositions \claimref{singularity.unipotent-ray} and \claimref{singularity.solution-where-divergence-lies}(3), the gauge field is invertible and unimodular and division does not fail. Hence the transport principle, being a theory of the loci where division fails, makes no statement at the locus where the temperature is calibrated, and no strengthening of the framework's statements at the singular boundary can supply (R).

The bifurcation surface itself, where the boost flow has its fixed points, lies beyond one flat chart (it is the meeting of the four regions of the maximal extension); the chart contains the future horizon, on whose cross-sections the area, the surface gravity and the boost flow are those stated.
singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-in.technical:

Premise (R) applies across the horizon locus $r = 2M$ of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart, where the Euclidean section is regular at its tip, fixing the period $2\pi/\kappa$ (for a state that is KMS for the Killing flow, this is also the period at which it is regular across the horizon locus in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart); on each cross-section of that locus the Killing field $K = \hb^{-1}(e_t)$ is null with $(K \cdot D)K = \kappa K$, the gauge field is invertible and unimodular, and division does not fail.

Since the transport principle is a theory of the loci where division fails, it makes no statement at the locus where the temperature is calibrated, and no strengthening of the framework's statements at the singular boundary can supply (R). The bifurcation surface itself lies beyond one flat chart; the chart's horizon cross-sections carry the same area, surface gravity and boost flow.
singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-in.lay: The framework's machinery acts only where division in its algebra breaks down, which for a black hole is at the singularity. The temperature, though, is set at the horizon, where nothing breaks down and the only finite rate on offer is the surface gravity. So the condition that fixes the temperature cannot come from the framework itself and has to be brought in from outside.

state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvat.technical:
With $\sigma_r$ the unit boost bivector of the radial plane and $I$ the pseudoscalar, $(I\sigma_r)^2 = I^2\sigma_r^2 = -1$, and $\{\sigma_r, I\sigma_r\}$ is exactly the doubled eigenplane pair of the shape operator, $S(B) = -2B$. The rotor $R_\theta = \exp(\theta I\sigma_r/2) = \cos(\theta/2) + I\sigma_r\sin(\theta/2)$ has $R_{2\pi} = -1$ and $R_{4\pi} = +1$, so the rotor has period $4\pi$ while its conjugation action has period $2\pi$.

$R_\theta$ is the continuation of the boost rotor $\exp(\lambda\sigma_r/2)$ under $\lambda \mapsto i\theta$ in the sense that both are one-parameter rotor flows in the same eigenplane pair, the hyperbolic one generated by the member of square $+1$ and the elliptic one by the member of square $-1$. With the continuation's unit read as the conformal spinors' unit $I_{6} = I_{4}E$, the continued boost acts on each chiral half of the conformal spinors as $R_{\pm\theta}$, the sense set by the chirality (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.wick-rotor-chiral-angular-rotor}). In that action on spinors the Euclidean rotation carrying the periodicity is the second member of the curvature-selected pair, distinguished from the boost by the sign of its square. On vectors it is not: $R_\theta$ rotates along the bifurcation sphere, not around it, and no real rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$ realises the Euclidean rotation there (Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}(3)).
state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvat.lay: The curvature of a black hole picks out a pair of planes. One carries the boost of the horizon's time symmetry; this result shows that the other carries an ordinary rotation, which returns to itself after a full turn when acting on geometric quantities. Read as the imaginary-time partner of the boost, that rotation is the one whose period thermal arguments demand when it acts on spinors, the quantities that describe fermions, so there it is supplied by the curvature rather than brought in from outside. Acting on ordinary directions in spacetime it is not that rotation: it turns along the horizon sphere, not around it.

proofs.main: (1) $I$ commutes with every even element and $I^{2} = -1$ in $\Cl(1,3)$, so $(I\sigma_r)^{2} = I^{2}\sigma_r^{2} = -1$ using $\sigma_r^{2} = +1$. The eigenplane statement is \cite[Thm.~6.1]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling}), whose spectrum is $(-2,-2,1,1,1,1)$ with the doubled eigenvalue attained exactly on $\operatorname{span}\{\sigma_r, I\sigma_r\}$. (2) With $(I\sigma_r)^{2} = -1$ the exponential series splits into the cosine and sine series, giving the displayed rotor; $R_{2\pi} = \cos\pi + I\sigma_r\sin\pi = -1$, and conjugation by $-1$ is the identity, so the conjugation action closes at $2\pi$ while the rotor itself closes at $4\pi$. (3) The two flows are the two real one-parameter subgroups of the rotor group of the plane pair, related by the substitution $\lambda = i\theta$ in the exponential; the substitution exchanges $\cosh, \sinh$ with $\cos, \sin$ exactly because the two generators differ by the factor $I$ with $I^{2} = -1$. (4) Read with the conformal spinors' unit $I_{6} = I_{4}E$ as the unit of the continuation, the continued boost is $\exp(\theta I_{6}\sigma_r/2) = \tfrac12(1+E)R_\theta + \tfrac12(1-E)R_{-\theta}$, which is Proposition \claimref{synthesis.wick-rotor-chiral-angular-rotor}(ii): on the chiral half $E = +1$ it is $R_\theta$ and on $E = -1$ it is $R_{-\theta}$, so on spinors the Euclidean rotation is carried by the second member, with the sense fixed by the chirality. The restriction to spinors is forced: by Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}(3) the rotor $R_\theta$ fixes $e_0$, $e_1$ and rotates $e_2$ into $e_3$, along the bifurcation sphere, and no real rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$ realises the rotation around it, while the continued element is no rotor on vectors (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.wick-rotor-chiral-angular-rotor}(iii)).

state-selection.rate-discharge-hypothesi.formal:
Assume (P) and (R), the latter in T05's form (\claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}: on each mode the two orderings of every ladder correlator meet after one period of the regular Euclidean section), and that the state satisfies the GMC of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condition-g}. Then the modular period in rapidity is exactly $2\pi$, so by Corollary \claimref{singularity.universality-temperature-under-g} and the calibration of \cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT5},
\[
\beta \;=\; \frac{2\pi}{\kappa} \;=\; 8\pi M , \qquad T \;=\; \frac{\kappa}{2\pi} \;=\; \frac{1}{8\pi M} \;=\; \TH ,
\]
Hypothesis (iii) of \cite[Thm.~7.3]{ButlerT5}, that the state be faithful, that is cyclic and separating for the one-sided algebra, is presupposed here and not derived: a state has a modular automorphism group only if it is faithful, so the GMC contains it. Its discharge without the GMC is T05's Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, from T05's (R) on each mode.
state-selection.rate-discharge-hypothesi.technical:
Assume (P), the regularity premise (R) in the form the main paper states it, mode by mode, and that the state satisfies the geometric modular condition. By KMS uniqueness the state is the Gibbs state of the boost's phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK})$ at some $\beta$, and regularity of the continued correlation functions at the fixed locus forces the modular period in rapidity to be exactly $2\pi$, the angle at which the conjugation action of the curvature-selected Euclidean rotor closes, that rotor carrying the continued boost on each chiral half of the spinors. With the universality of the temperature and the calibration of rapidity against Schwarzschild time, $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa = 8\pi M$ and $T = \kappa/2\pi = 1/8\pi M = \TH$.

The cyclic-and-separating hypothesis of modular descent is not derived here. The geometric modular condition speaks of the state's modular automorphism group, which exists only for a faithful state, so the condition already contains that hypothesis; the full-rank Gibbs matrix at finite nonzero $\beta$ is consistent with it but cannot discharge it. The main paper discharges it from its own form of (R), mode by mode, without the modular condition.
state-selection.rate-discharge-hypothesi.lay: Given the univalence and regularity premises (P) and (R), and the condition that the modes' internal clock runs along the black hole's time symmetry, smoothness at the horizon forces the clock's period to be exactly one full turn. Converting that turn into ordinary time gives the Hawking temperature. A technical condition, that the state be faithful, is built into the modular condition and so is assumed here, not derived; the main paper derives it separately.
state-selection.rate-discharge-hypothesi.typing_note: Added the universality corollary the statement invokes and the hypotheses (P) and (R) as assumes; the cited modular descent theorem is the target of the discharge, not a premise. Levels pass: lay now names premises (P) and (R).

proofs.main: By the GMC the state is KMS for the boost's phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK})$ at some $\beta$, one for all modes (\claimref{singularity.universality-temperature-under-g}), and by Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} it is the corresponding Gibbs state; the KMS condition says its correlation functions are analytic in the strip of width $\beta$ and periodic, with the graded sign (the state being even by (P), \claimref{singularity.p-univalence}), under translation by $i\beta$ in the flow parameter. Under the continuation $\lambda \mapsto i\theta$ of Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected}(3), read on spinors as in its clause (4), that translation acts on each chiral half as the rotor of the second member of the curvature-selected pair, by the angle $\theta = \beta$, in one sense on one half and the opposite sense on the other; on vectors it is no real rotation, so the period is read in this action on spinors. By Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected}(2) the conjugation action of the rotation closes at $2\pi$ and at no smaller angle, so a continuation that is single valued and regular at the fixed locus of the flow, which is premise (R) in the form T05 states it (\claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}: on each mode the two orderings of every ladder correlator are glued after one period of the regular Euclidean section), forces $\beta = 2\pi$ in rapidity: a value $\beta \neq 2\pi$ makes the continued correlation function multivalued around the fixed locus, equivalently gives the Euclidean section a conical excess or deficit there. The conversion to Killing time is \cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.plane-rate}). Faithfulness: the GMC presupposes it, since a state has a modular automorphism group only if it is faithful, so hypothesis (iii) is an input of this argument and not an output. That $\beta = 2\pi$ is finite and nonzero, so that the Gibbs matrix has full rank, is consistent with it but derives nothing, the argument having started from the modular group. Hypothesis (iii) is discharged without the GMC by Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, from T05's (R) on each mode. The note's own wording of (R), regularity of the continued two-point functions at the fixed locus, is satisfiable and contentful on the boundary-mode algebra only when the two orderings are glued, and then on the whole window it adds vanishing inter-mode two-point functions, which this argument does not use (\claimref{synthesis.state-selection-r-and-le-against-t05}, (i), (ii) and (iv)); T05's (R) is the premise assumed here.

state-selection.where-fermi-dirac-comes.formal: The rotor implementing one Euclidean period is $R_{2\pi} = -1$, which acts as $+1$ on the even sector $\Aev$ and as $-1$ on the odd sector $\Aod$. The ladder's own generators are odd, so their correlation functions are antiperiodic around the modular period while the metric-level observables are periodic. This is the structural origin of the Fermi-Dirac denominator $e^{\omega/T} + 1$ rather than the Bose-Einstein $e^{\omega/T} - 1$, and hence of the first wrinkle recorded in \cite[Rem.~7.5]{ButlerT5}: the statistics of the directly produced spectrum is fixed by the double cover, and the bosonic sector has to be reached by bosonisation, as Step 4e does.
state-selection.where-fermi-dirac-comes.technical:
The rotor implementing one Euclidean period on spinors, where the curvature-selected Euclidean rotor carries the continued boost on each chiral half, is $R_{2\pi} = -1$, which acts as $+1$ on the even sector $\Aev$ and as $-1$ on the odd sector $\Aod$. The ladder's generators are odd, so their correlation functions are antiperiodic around the modular period, while the metric-level observables, which live in the even sector, are periodic.

Read through the standard Matsubara correspondence, this antiperiodicity is the structural origin of the Fermi-Dirac denominator $e^{\omega/T} + 1$ rather than the Bose-Einstein $e^{\omega/T} - 1$: the statistics of the directly produced spectrum is fixed by the double cover, and the bosonic sector has to be reached by bosonisation.
state-selection.where-fermi-dirac-comes.lay: A full turn of the Euclidean rotation leaves ordinary geometric quantities unchanged but flips the sign of fermion operators. Through a standard correspondence, quoted rather than proved here, that sign flip is why the directly produced radiation follows Fermi-Dirac rather than Bose-Einstein statistics. Reaching photon-like Bose-Einstein radiation therefore needs a separate step, bosonisation.
state-selection.where-fermi-dirac-comes.typing_note: Kept both edges; the Matsubara step is quoted as the standard reading and is not in the store as an imported claim, so no standard route was added.

proofs.main: The value $R_{2\pi} = -1$ is Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected}(2). Conjugation by $-1$ is trivial, so the even sector, which is where the metric-level observables live by Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average}, is periodic. The odd sector is acted on by the rotor in the spinor module, where $-1$ acts as $-1$; the antiperiodicity of odd correlation functions around the modular period is the standard consequence, and the Matsubara reading of that antiperiodicity is the Fermi-Dirac factor. The last step is the standard reading and is flagged as such rather than proved here.

synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-with.formal:
On one generator of a Killing horizon of surface gravity $\kappa$ with affine parameter $U > 0$, let the one-particle space be $L^{2}(\R_{+}, dU)$ (half-densities) and let the boost at Killing time $t$ act as the unitary dilation $(D_{t}f)(U) = e^{-\kappa t/2}f(e^{-\kappa t}U)$, the action of the modular flow on null translations of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}; on the CAR algebra over this space (a continuum mode space in the sense of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}) it is the quasi-free real-time flow $a(f) \mapsto a(D_{t}f)$, a phase flow in the sense of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}. Let $\chi_{j}$ be the normalised indicator of the affine cell $[j\delta, (j+1)\delta)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Support grows at rate $\kappa$.)} If $e^{\kappa t} = m$ is an integer, $D_{t}\chi_{j} = m^{-1/2}\sum_{l=0}^{m-1}\chi_{mj+l}$: one cell is spread uniformly over $e^{\kappa t}$ cells with amplitude $e^{-\kappa t/2}$ and norm one. The mode operator $a(\chi_{j})$ therefore covers $N$ cells at real Killing time $t = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Local anticommutators decay.)} For every fixed cell $k$, $\{a(D_{t}\chi_{j}), a^{*}(\chi_{k})\} = \langle\chi_{k}, D_{t}\chi_{j}\rangle \in \{0, e^{-\kappa t/2}\}$; every anticommutator of the evolved mode operator with a fixed cell operator is bounded by $e^{-\kappa t/2}$, and the squares over all cells sum to one.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Basis dependence.)} On log cells $[m^{i}\delta, m^{i+1}\delta)$ the same flow at $e^{\kappa t} = m$ maps the normalised indicator of cell $i$ to that of cell $i+1$: it displaces without spreading.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(It hops.)} In the affine-cell basis the generator is not diagonal: it moves one-particle weight from cell $j$ to cells $mj, \dots, mj + m - 1$.
\end{enumerate}
So, in the affine-cell basis, the count $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$ of Assumption \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} has a real-time reading under the phase flow, as the number of affine cells one cell is spread over by the boost, with amplitudes falling as $e^{-\kappa t/2}$ rather than growing; it is free dilation, with no growth of local anticommutators, so it is not the out-of-time-order growth the chaos bound concerns, and on boost-adapted (log) cells it disappears.
synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-with.technical: On a horizon generator the boost is a dilation of the affine parameter. Acting on modes localised in equal affine cells, it spreads one cell over $e^{\kappa t}$ cells in real time, unitarily and quadratically, with amplitude $e^{-\kappa t/2}$ in each. A single mode thus covers $N$ cells after $\kappa^{-1}\ln N$, the fast-scrambling count, but its overlap with any fixed cell decays, so every local anticommutator decays: one-particle support grows (the evolved operator stays linear in the modes) while no local anticommutator grows. On cells equally spaced in the logarithm of the affine parameter, which are adapted to the boost, the same flow merely shifts each cell to the next. The spreading generator moves occupation between affine cells, the kind of generator boundary-mode locality excludes on the exceptional set.
synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-with.lay: A black hole's horizon stretches what falls along it. A quantum mode confined to one small stretch of the horizon is smeared, as time passes, over exponentially many stretches, reaching N of them after a time proportional to the logarithm of N, the famous fast-scrambling time. But it is smeared thinner as it spreads, so its influence on any one stretch fades: this is spreading, not the scrambling that the chaos bound is about.

proofs.main:
Unitarity: $\|D_{t}f\|^{2} = e^{-\kappa t}\int|f(e^{-\kappa t}U)|^{2}dU = \int|f|^{2}$, and $D_{s}D_{t} = D_{s+t}$, so $t \mapsto D_{t}$ is a strongly continuous unitary group; by the CAR functor (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}) $a(f) \mapsto a(D_{t}f)$ is a quasi-free one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms, a time evolution in the sense of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}. That it is the boost is the relation $\Delta^{it}U(a)\Delta^{-it} = U(e^{-2\pi t}a)$ of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}: with modular parameter $s$ corresponding to Killing time $t = -2\pi s/\kappa$ (rapidity $\kappa t$), the boost rescales null translations of the affine parameter by $e^{\kappa t}$, and on functions of $U$ this is $D_{t}$ (the sign of $t$ selects which of the two null directions is stretched; the statement is for the stretched one).

(i) Take $\delta = 1$ (the general case by scaling $U$). For $e^{\kappa t} = m$, $(D_{t}\chi_{j})(U) = m^{-1/2}\chi_{j}(U/m)$, which is $m^{-1/2}$ on $[mj, mj + m)$ and zero elsewhere, i.e.\ $m^{-1/2}\sum_{l=0}^{m-1}\chi_{mj+l}$. Iterating, at $e^{\kappa t} = m^{n}$ the support is $m^{n}$ consecutive cells with amplitude $m^{-n/2}$ each; setting $m^{n} = N$ gives $\kappa t = \ln N$. The script checks this exactly for $m = 4$ (amplitude $1/2$), $n = 1, \dots, 4$, two starting cells, and the flow property $D_{\ln 4}D_{\ln 4} = D_{\ln 16}$, on functions constant on unit cells, together with isometry on a generic cell-constant vector.

(ii) The CAR give $\{a(f), a^{*}(g)\} = \langle g, f\rangle$. By (i), $\langle\chi_{k}, D_{t}\chi_{j}\rangle$ is $e^{-\kappa t/2}$ for the $e^{\kappa t}$ cells in the support and zero otherwise, and the sum of squares is $\|D_{t}\chi_{j}\|^{2} = 1$. For even observables the same overlaps bound the commutators, for example $[a^{*}(D_{t}\chi_{j})a(D_{t}\chi_{j}), a^{*}(\chi_{k})] = \langle\chi_{k}, D_{t}\chi_{j}\rangle\,a^{*}(D_{t}\chi_{j})$, of norm at most $e^{-\kappa t/2}$. The script checks that every overlap with a fixed cell is $0$ or $2^{-n}$.

(iii) For $e^{\kappa t} = m$ and the indicator $1_{i}$ of $[m^{i}, m^{i+1})$, $D_{t}1_{i} = m^{-1/2}1_{i+1}$, and $\|1_{i+1}\|^{2} = m\|1_{i}\|^{2}$, so the normalised indicators satisfy $D_{t}\hat{1}_{i} = \hat{1}_{i+1}$. Checked for $m = 4$, $i = 0, \dots, 3$.

(iv) For $j \ge 1$ the cell $j$ is not among $mj, \dots, mj + m - 1$, so $\langle\chi_{j}, D_{t}\chi_{j}\rangle = 0$: the flow is not diagonal in the cell basis, and its generator moves occupation between cells (a hopping generator in the sense of Premise \claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality}, which excludes such generators for the ladders at points of $E$, not on a horizon generator). Checked for three cells.

Comparison with the stored results. Assumption \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} derives $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$ from amplitudes growing as $e^{\kappa t}$, and Theorem \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation} shows that on boost-eigenmode windows that growth is the rotor flow's, an imaginary-time rate. Here the real-time phase flow reaches the same count by spreading amplitudes that shrink. Both readings agree that no local anticommutator grows under quadratic dynamics, so neither supplies chaos-bound saturation; what (i) adds is that the count itself is available in real time, in the affine-cell basis of the horizon.

synthesis.array-ln2-is-zero-mode-doublet.technical: The boson-fermion correspondence splits the series' s-wave array into two independent parts: a charge sector, labelled by the number of fermions added to or removed from the sea, and one tower of bosonic oscillators, which is what the currents create. With the (Q) weights, the lowest energy at charge $Q$ is $Q(Q-1)/2$ in units of $\kappa$, so charges $0$ and $1$ are degenerate at zero energy: the zero mode can be empty or filled for free. That two-fold degeneracy is where the $\ln 2$ per array lives; with the sea placed between sites instead, the other particle-hole symmetric choice, there is no zero mode, no degeneracy, and the array carries half as much. The currents conserve charge: the charge current reads which of the two states the array is in, and no other current can move between them. The oscillators, which become the s-wave photons under Joint J3, carry only the tower's entropy, a small fraction of $\ln 2$ at the Hawking temperature. Since the current sector has one oscillator per frequency, an array supplies one helicity channel; the two helicities of a partial wave need two towers, whose state counts differ already at the first level. The capacity per array is a charge-sector quantity, so no reading of J3 can change it, and a residue built from helicity channels of the current would be far from both registered values.
synthesis.array-ln2-is-zero-mode-doublet.lay: The series models the boundary modes as a single row of fermion slots, and shows that their collective ripples behave like particles of light. Assuming, as the series does for this step, that the modes are jointly in the simplest thermal state (Premise (Q)), this result separates the row's information into two parts. Almost all of it, one bit, sits in a single question: whether the slot exactly at the zero level is filled. The ripples, which are the light, cannot change that answer, and they carry only a small fraction of the information. The row also turns out to contain exactly one kind of ripple at each frequency, which is enough for one polarisation of light but not for both. So the earlier question of whether one boundary mode holds one polarisation or two does not affect the count that fixes the series' calibration, and one row of modes supplies one polarisation.

proofs.main:
Throughout, (Q) is assumed as in Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}: weights $\omega_{k} = \kappa k$, sea level at $k = 0$, Gibbs state of $\sum_{k}\kappa k:N_{k}:$ at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$. A configuration with finitely many particles above the sea and holes in it has charge $Q = \#\{\text{occupied } k \ge 0\} - \#\{\text{empty } k < 0\}$ and energy $E = \sum_{\text{occupied } k \ge 0}k + \sum_{\text{empty } k < 0}|k|$, which is the eigenvalue of $\sum_{k}k:N_{k}:$; its Gibbs weight is $q^{E}$ with $q = e^{-\beta\kappa} = e^{-2\pi}$.

(i) Lowest energy at fixed charge: for $Q > 0$ fill $k = 0, \ldots, Q - 1$, energy $\sum_{k=0}^{Q-1}k = Q(Q-1)/2$; for $Q < 0$ empty $k = -1, \ldots, Q$, energy $\sum_{j=1}^{|Q|}j = |Q|(|Q| + 1)/2 = Q(Q-1)/2$. The generating function of all configurations is $(1 + z)\prod_{k \ge 1}(1 + zq^{k})(1 + z^{-1}q^{k})$, with $z$ counting charge; by the Jacobi triple product identity (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobi-triple-product}, its second rewritten form; the script also verifies it on windows) it equals $\sum_{Q \in \Z}z^{Q}q^{Q(Q-1)/2}\prod_{m \ge 1}(1 - q^{m})^{-1}$. Reading off the coefficient of $z^{Q}q^{E}$ gives $p(E - Q(Q-1)/2)$. This is the charge decomposition of the boson-fermion correspondence that the bridge cites for its charge-zero isomorphism (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}): the factor $\prod(1 - q^{m})^{-1}$ is the partition function of one oscillator tower, one oscillator of energy $m$ per $m \ge 1$, created by the $a_{-m}$. The script checks the count exactly on the window $k = -6, \ldots, 6$ for every $E \le 6$, where no configuration of energy $E \le 6$ is cut off by the window, against $p$ computed from $\prod(1 - q^{m})^{-1}$. Since the Gibbs weight $q^{E} = q^{Q(Q-1)/2}\cdot q^{E - Q(Q-1)/2}$ factorises over the decomposition, the Gibbs state is the product of $P(Q) \propto q^{Q(Q-1)/2}$ and the Gibbs state of the tower, and entropy is additive over a product: $S_{\mathrm{array}} = S_{\mathrm{charge}} + S_{\mathrm{osc}}$, where each oscillator of energy $m\kappa$ contributes the Bose entropy $s_{\mathrm{B}}(2\pi m)$.

(ii) $Q(Q-1)/2 = 0$ exactly for $Q \in \{0, 1\}$ and is at least $1$ otherwise, so the zero-energy configurations are the sea and the sea with $k = 0$ filled; the script lists them. $P(0) = P(1)$ is the largest charge probability and is below $\tfrac12$, so $S_{\mathrm{charge}} \ge -\ln P(0) > \ln 2$. In Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(vi) the array's $\ln 2$ is the entropy of the zero-weight mode $k = 0$, whose two occupations are exactly these two charge sectors. With weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ the lowest energy at charge $Q$ is $\sum_{k=0}^{Q-1}(k + \tfrac12) = Q^{2}/2$ for $Q > 0$ and likewise for $Q < 0$, the generating function becomes $\sum_{Q}z^{Q}q^{Q^{2}/2}\prod_{m}(1 - q^{m})^{-1}$ (the first rewritten form of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jacobi-triple-product}), the tower factor is unchanged, and $Q^{2}/2 = 0$ only at $Q = 0$; the script checks these counts on the window $k = -6, \ldots, 5$ in units of $\kappa/2$.

(iii) Each $\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{l}$ changes $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ by zero, so $[N_{\mathrm{tot}}, a_{m}] = 0$ and every current preserves $Q$; $a_{0}$, normal ordered at the sea, is $Q$ itself, diagonal on the doublet with eigenvalues $0$ and $1$; on the finite window this is the operator identity checked on Jordan-Wigner matrices for five sites, and it is consistent with the exact edge identity of Proposition \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split}, all of whose terms are number operators. The doublet states have charges $0$ and $1$, so every current, and every element of the algebra the currents generate, has zero matrix element between them, and for $m \neq 0$ the current acts on the tower factor only; the script checks this for $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}$ and their adjoints, checks that the charge separates the two states without connecting them, and shows that $\psi_{0}^{\dagger}$ connects them. Hence any state or flux built from the currents (the Bose-Einstein occupancy of the bridge's clause (3), and the current boson that Joint J3 of Proposition \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised} lifts to the field) sees only the tower factor and its entropy $S_{\mathrm{osc}}$.

(iv) At charge $0$ the level counts are $p(E)$, the dimension of the tower's energy-$E$ subspace; $p(1) = 1$ means one oscillator at weight $\kappa$, and by (i) one at each weight $m\kappa$. A massless field's partial wave at fixed $(\ell, m)$ with both helicities has two independent oscillators at each frequency (standard free-field Fock structure, imported, not proved in the series), so its level counts are the coefficients of $\prod(1 - q^{m})^{-2}$, namely $1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 36, 65$, which exceed $p(E)$ at every $E \ge 1$, already at $E = 1$. A single array's current sector therefore cannot carry both helicities of one partial wave; under J3 it carries one channel. This is consistent with Theorem \claimref{synthesis.capacity-per-mode-independent-of-helicity}, which fixes the capacity per ladder pair without J3; here the capacity per array is located in the charge sector, which J3 does not touch.

Numerics (floating point, proof text only): $s_{\mathrm{B}}(2\pi) = 0.0136246$, $s_{\mathrm{B}}(4\pi) = 4.73 \times 10^{-5}$, the remaining terms below $2 \times 10^{-7}$ in total, so $S_{\mathrm{osc}} = 0.0136721$; the charge distribution, with $P(0) = P(1) = 0.499068$, gives $S_{\mathrm{charge}} = 0.7067246$, and the sum $0.7203967$ equals $\ln 2 + \varepsilon$ computed mode by mode in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(vi) ($\varepsilon = 0.0272495$), as additivity requires. At the other offset the charge distribution, with $P(0) = 0.920442$, gives $S_{\mathrm{charge}} = 0.3329015$, and $S_{\mathrm{charge}} + S_{\mathrm{osc}} = 0.3465736$, consistent with the value $\tfrac12\ln 2$ proved in the proposal filed alongside, synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2. All values in this paragraph are computed in floating point and reproducible; none is used in the statement. So the charge sector at (Q)'s offset carries $\ln 2 + 0.0136$, the doublet's $\ln 2$ plus the excess from higher charges. The residue under a count of $h$ helicity channels of the current per array, each carrying $S_{\mathrm{osc}}$, would be $1/(4hS_{\mathrm{osc}}) = 18.29/h$.

synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-.formal:
Work in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ of the flat background with the store's signature, on a local Rindler horizon of a region of vanishing field strength (for the Killing horizons see (vi)). Let $k$ be a future null vector, $m$ the null vector with $\ip{k}{m} = 1$ in the plane of $k$ and $e_{0}$, $N_{k} = \{x : \ip{x}{k} = 0\} = \{u\,k + x_{\perp}\}$ the null plane with generators along $k$ and affine parameter $u$, edge $u = 0$. Let $\Lambda(a) = a\gamma_{0}/(2a_{0})$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1)), $x^{*}$ the frame $*$-structure (Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}), and $B_{\lambda} = \exp(\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,k\wedge m)$ normalised so that $B_{\lambda}kB_{\lambda}^{\sim} = e^{\lambda}k$ and $B_{\lambda}mB_{\lambda}^{\sim} = e^{-\lambda}m$ (for $k = e_{0} + e_{1}$: $B_{\lambda} = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2} + e_{1}e_{0}\sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}$), the boost of the horizon, with rapidity $\lambda = \kappa t$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The canonical component.)} $\Lambda(m)\,a\gamma_{0}\,\Lambda(m) = 0$ for $a = k$ and for $a \perp k, m$, and $\Lambda(m)\,m\gamma_{0}\,\Lambda(m) = \Lambda(m)$. With $\nabla = k\,(m\cdot\nabla) + m\,(k\cdot\nabla) + \nabla_{\perp}$, the stored anticommutator $\chi(\nabla D)\gamma_{0}$ compressed to $\Lambda(m)$ is $\chi\,(k\cdot\nabla D)\,\Lambda(m)$: it involves only the derivative along the generators, so $\psi_{m} = \Lambda(m)\psi$ is the canonical component on $N_{k}$, with kernel a multiple of $\delta(u - v)\delta^{2}(x_{\perp} - y_{\perp})\Lambda(m)$, and on each generator its algebra is the continuum mode space $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes\Lambda(m)S)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}. The other component $\Lambda(k)\psi$ keeps only the $m\cdot\nabla$ part, a derivative off the plane.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Two factors, one automorphism.)} The covariant action $\psi(x) \mapsto B_{\lambda}\psi(B_{\lambda}^{\sim}xB_{\lambda})$ is, on $\psi_{m}$ along a generator, the product of two factors: the rotor on values, $B_{\lambda}\Lambda(m) = e^{-\lambda/2}\Lambda(m)$, with $B_{\lambda}^{*} = B_{\lambda}$ and $B_{\lambda}\Lambda(m)B_{\lambda}^{*} = e^{-\lambda}\Lambda(m)$; and the transport of the affine parameter, $B_{\lambda}^{\sim}(uk)B_{\lambda} = e^{-\lambda}u\,k$, which multiplies the delta kernel by $e^{\lambda}$. Their product is
\[
\alpha_{\lambda}(\psi_{m}(u)) = e^{-\lambda/2}\psi_{m}(e^{-\lambda}u), \qquad \alpha_{\lambda}(a(f)) = a(D_{\lambda}f),\quad (D_{\lambda}f)(u) = e^{-\lambda/2}f(e^{-\lambda}u),
\]
with $D_{\lambda}$ unitary and $D_{\lambda}D_{\mu} = D_{\lambda+\mu}$, so $\alpha$ is a one-parameter group of quasi-free $*$-automorphisms; it is the dilation of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-without-scrambling}. Neither factor alone preserves the anticommutator (they rescale it by $e^{\mp\lambda}$), so neither is a $*$-automorphism, and among weights $e^{-w\lambda}$ only $w = \tfrac12$ makes the product unitary. On $\Lambda(k)\psi$ the rotor weight is $e^{+\lambda/2}$ and the two factors do not cancel.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The phase flow.)} On each half-generator the half-density monomials $f_{w}(u) = |u|^{-1/2 + iw}$ satisfy $D_{\lambda}f_{w} = e^{-iw\lambda}f_{w}$, and a weight $e^{-\lambda(1/2 + s)}$ on $|u|^{s}$ is a phase exactly when $\mathrm{Re}\,s = -\tfrac12$. So in the Mellin basis $\alpha_{\kappa t}$ is the phase flow $a(f_{w}) \mapsto e^{-i\kappa wt}a(f_{w})$ of one-particle Hamiltonian $\kappa w$, spectrum all of $\R$: the boost dynamics of the windows (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}) with its point spectrum refined to the continuum.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Imaginary rapidity.)} Continued to $\lambda = i\theta$ the two factors are the Euclidean rotor $B_{i\theta} = \cos\tfrac{\theta}{2} + i\,e_{1}e_{0}\sin\tfrac{\theta}{2}$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies} on values, $B_{i\theta}\Lambda(m) = e^{-i\theta/2}\Lambda(m)$, and the rotation $u \mapsto e^{-i\theta}u$ of the affine parameter into the complex plane. At $\theta = \pi$ it carries the half-generator $u > 0$ to $u < 0$ with factor $-i$; at $\theta = 2\pi$ it returns with factor $-1$, at $4\pi$ with $+1$. On Mellin modes the continued phase is the real factor $e^{w\theta}$: the rotor flow, which rescales the modes, is this group's continuation into the strip, and under (N$_{+}$) the restriction of the ground state to a half-generator is KMS for $\alpha$ at $\theta = 2\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}).
\item[(v)] \emph{(Real time.)} For all $f, g$ and all real $\lambda$, $|\{a(D_{\lambda}f), a^{*}(g)\}| = |\ip{g}{D_{\lambda}f}| \le \|f\|\,\|g\|$, and for two fixed affine cells it falls as $e^{-\lambda/2}$. The anticommutator of linear elements is a scalar, so in every state the out-of-time-order correlators built from them are bounded: the real-time Lyapunov exponent of the quasi-free dynamics $\alpha$ on linear elements is $0$. Nothing here bears on non-quadratic dynamics. What grows at rate $\kappa$ in real time is the support, which covers $e^{\kappa t}$ affine cells (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-without-scrambling}); what grows in imaginary time is the Mellin factor $e^{w\theta}$.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Killing horizons.)} At the eternal hole's horizon and at the de Sitter cosmological horizon the Killing flow acts on the affine parameter of the generators as $u \mapsto e^{\pm\kappa t}u$ (the boost $\beta_{t}$ of the setup of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}); by (ii) the anticommutator then forces the weight $\tfrac12$, so the boost time evolution there is the same group $\alpha_{\kappa t}$, and (iii) to (v) hold unchanged. That its value factor is the boost of the frame along the generator, relative to frames parallel along the generators, is derived for every Killing horizon with nonzero surface gravity, off its bifurcation surface and whatever the field strength, in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.killing-horizon-value-factor-is-the-generator-boost}, which builds on (i) and (ii) here.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the two boost flows of the series are one $*$-automorphism group of the continuum read in real and imaginary rapidity: the time evolution is $\alpha_{\kappa t}$, and the rotor flow is its continuation into the KMS strip, as on the windows, with the continuum adding that the real rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$ and the transport of the affine parameter are the two factors of the one unitary evolution. The chaos-bound comparison of Assumption \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} restated on this basis: one unitary group has real-time support-dilation rate $\kappa$ and, under (N$_{+}$), KMS period $2\pi/\kappa$, so the equality of the rate with $2\pi T$ is the identity $\kappa\beta = 2\pi$ of that group, derived from (N$_{+}$) on the continuum and holding on the windows only under (R); the real-time Lyapunov exponent of this quasi-free dynamics is $0$, so the chaos bound is met, not saturated, which contradicts the earlier sentence of Assumption \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} that the window saturates it by construction, at the level of the free continuum dynamics, and $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N = (\beta/2\pi)\ln N$ is the time for one affine cell to cover $N$ cells, $\ln N$ units of rapidity. The comparison does not need two distinct evolutions. The equality is a property of the state, not of the group: a stationary state of the half-generator that is KMS for $\alpha$ at rapidity period $2\pi c$ (the continuum I-state at that period exists for every $c > 0$) sees the same real-time rate $\kappa$ and the KMS period $2\pi c/\kappa$, so the identity holds exactly when $c = 1$, which (N$_{+}$) supplies.
synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-.technical:
The series names two boost flows with one generator: the real rotor flow, which rescales the modes and drives the scrambling law, and the phase flow, which carries the KMS analysis. On the windows the stored result shows that only the phase flow is a time evolution. On the continuum of a horizon generator the question can be answered more fully, because there both flows are visible inside one unitary map.

The spinor field restricted to the null plane of a horizon has one canonical component, picked out by the projector onto the kernel of the dual null vector $m$: on it the stored anticommutator keeps only the derivative along the generators. The boost rotor acts on that component's values by the weight $e^{-\lambda/2}$, and the same rotor moves the points of each generator by $u \mapsto e^{-\lambda}u$ in the argument. The weight alone shrinks the anticommutator, the transport alone stretches it, and together they preserve it: the product is the unitary dilation that the stored affine-cell result uses. In the Mellin basis of half-density powers of $u$ it is the phase flow with continuous spectrum; continued to imaginary rapidity it is the Euclidean rotor on values times a rotation of $u$ into the complex plane, which at half a turn reaches the other half of the generator and at a full turn gives the spinor sign. So the rotor flow is the same group's imaginary-time continuation.

In real time the anticommutators of linear elements stay bounded and fall off for fixed cells, so the Lyapunov exponent of this quasi-free dynamics is zero, and the stored statement that the window saturates the chaos bound by construction does not hold for it: the bound is met, not saturated; the rate $\kappa$ shows up as the dilation of support, not as growth. The chaos-bound sentence then compares a single group's dilation rate with its own KMS period under (N$_{+}$), whose product $2\pi$ is the rapidity period that premise gives. The claim's checks verify the Clifford identities, the kernel factors, the Mellin exponents, the Euclidean factors and the cell bounds exactly; the light-front normalisation of the kernel and the Mellin-Plancherel theorem are cited from memory, and the value factor at Killing horizons of nonvanishing field strength is argued.
synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-.lay: Near a horizon the series uses two descriptions of "letting time run": one that stretches things and one that turns phases. They looked like two different motions. Along a single light ray of a horizon they turn out to be one motion seen two ways. Running time does two things at once to the field on the ray: it shrinks the field's value and slides its profile further out along the ray. Either on its own would spoil the basic rule fermions obey; together they keep it. Written in the right basis this one motion just turns phases, and run in imaginary time it stretches, which is the other description. Nothing grows exponentially in real time for this free motion: the field only spreads out thinly, so the earlier statement that the horizon reaches the maximal rate of chaos does not hold for it, and, given the series' premise that the modes on each light ray are in their lowest-energy state, the rate at which it spreads matches the temperature because both come from the same motion.

proofs.main:
Conventions. $a(f) = \int \overline{f(u)}\,\psi_{m}(u)\,du$ on one generator (antilinear in $f$), $a^{*}(f) = a(f)^{*}$; a flow is a $*$-automorphism group when it preserves the anticommutator and the $*$-operation. Take $k = e_{0} + e_{1}$ and $m = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{1})$ (every other pair is carried to this one by a rotor, which leaves every statement below covariant); then $\ip{k}{m} = 1$, $k \wedge m = e_{1}e_{0}$ and $B_{\lambda} = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2} + e_{1}e_{0}\sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}$. The check sets $e^{\lambda/2} = r$ rational, so $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ of $\lambda/2$ are rational and every identity in (i), (ii) and (iv) is an exact identity of multivectors.

\emph{(i)} $\Lambda(m) = m\gamma_{0}/(2m_{0}) = \tfrac12(1 + e_{0}e_{1})$ is idempotent and self-adjoint for the frame $*$-structure of Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}, $m\Lambda(m) = 0$ since $Q(m) = 0$, and $\Lambda(k) + \Lambda(m) = 1$. Every vector is $a = \ip{a}{m}k + \ip{a}{k}m + a_{\perp}$ with $a_{\perp}$ orthogonal to $k$ and $m$, hence $\nabla = k\,(m\cdot\nabla) + m\,(k\cdot\nabla) + \nabla_{\perp}$. Direct multiplication gives $\Lambda(m)k\gamma_{0}\Lambda(m) = 0$, $\Lambda(m)e_{j}\gamma_{0}\Lambda(m) = 0$ for $j = 2, 3$ and $\Lambda(m)m\gamma_{0}\Lambda(m) = \Lambda(m)$. The field is that of Definition \claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}. Compressing the anticommutator $\chi(\nabla D)\gamma_{0}$ of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(2) to $\Lambda(m)$ therefore leaves $\chi\,(k\cdot\nabla D)\,\Lambda(m)$: only the derivative along the generators of $N_{k}$ survives. On the null plane that derivative of the Pauli-Jordan function is a constant multiple of $\delta(u - v)\delta^{2}(x_{\perp} - y_{\perp})$ (the light-front restriction, cited from memory; only the constant depends on it), so the canonical component $\psi_{m}$ has a delta kernel in the affine parameter and, generator by generator, its algebra is $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes\Lambda(m)S)$, a continuum mode space in the sense of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}. The same multiplication gives $\Lambda(k)m\gamma_{0}\Lambda(k) = 0$ and $\Lambda(k)k\gamma_{0}\Lambda(k) = 2\Lambda(k)$, so $\Lambda(k)\psi$ keeps only $m\cdot\nabla$, the derivative off the plane: it is not an independent canonical datum on $N_{k}$.

\emph{(ii)} With $r = e^{\lambda/2}$: $B_{\lambda}kB_{\lambda}^{\sim} = r^{2}k$, $B_{\lambda}mB_{\lambda}^{\sim} = r^{-2}m$, $B_{\lambda}^{\sim}kB_{\lambda} = r^{-2}k$, $B_{\lambda}^{*} = B_{\lambda}$, $B_{\lambda}\Lambda(m) = r^{-1}\Lambda(m)$ (because $e_{1}e_{0}\Lambda(m) = -\Lambda(m)$), and so $B_{\lambda}\Lambda(m)B_{\lambda}^{*} = r^{-2}\Lambda(m)$. Under the covariant action $\psi(x) \mapsto B_{\lambda}\psi(B_{\lambda}^{\sim}xB_{\lambda})$ the canonical component along a generator becomes $\psi'_{m}(u) = r^{-1}\psi_{m}(r^{-2}u)$. Its anticommutator is the product of the rotor factor $r^{-2}$ (from $B_{\lambda}\Lambda(m)B_{\lambda}^{*}$) and the transport factor: $\delta(r^{-2}(u - v)) = r^{2}\delta(u - v)$, equivalently the ratio of a cell's length to that of its image under $u \mapsto r^{-2}u$. The product is $1$ and each factor alone is $r^{\mp 2} \neq 1$ for $\lambda \neq 0$; a map that rescales the anticommutator by a constant other than $1$ is not a $*$-automorphism. For a weight $r^{-2w}$ the product is $r^{2 - 4w}$, which is $1$ for all $r$ only at $w = \tfrac12$. In smeared form $\alpha_{\lambda}(a(f)) = a(D_{\lambda}f)$ with $(D_{\lambda}f)(u) = e^{-\lambda/2}f(e^{-\lambda}u)$; $\|D_{\lambda}f\|^{2} = e^{-\lambda}\int|f(e^{-\lambda}u)|^{2}du = \|f\|^{2}$, $D_{\lambda}$ is onto with inverse $D_{-\lambda}$, and $D_{\lambda}D_{\mu} = D_{\lambda + \mu}$; a unitary one-particle group defines a group of quasi-free $*$-automorphisms of the CAR algebra (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}). The same weight-1/2 dilation, as the scaling about the edge, is clause (i) of the edge-scaling result filed alongside (synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit); here it is obtained with its two factors. This is the flow $D_{t}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-without-scrambling} at $\lambda = \kappa t$, up to the direction of the time parameter. On $\Lambda(k)$, $e_{1}e_{0}\Lambda(k) = \Lambda(k)$ gives $B_{\lambda}\Lambda(k) = r\Lambda(k)$ and $B_{\lambda}\Lambda(k)B_{\lambda}^{*} = r^{2}\Lambda(k)$; with the transport factor $r^{2}$ the kernel gains $r^{4}$.

\emph{(iii)} For $u > 0$ and complex $s$, $D_{\lambda}u^{s} = e^{-\lambda/2}e^{-\lambda s}u^{s} = e^{-\lambda(1/2 + s)}u^{s}$; the exponent $-(1/2 + s)$ is purely imaginary exactly when $\mathrm{Re}\,s = -\tfrac12$, and then equals $-iw$ for $s = -\tfrac12 + iw$. The same holds on $u < 0$ with $|u|$. By the Mellin-Plancherel theorem (cited from memory) the transform $f \mapsto \int_{0}^{\infty}u^{-1/2 - iw}f(u)\,du/\sqrt{2\pi}$ is unitary from $L^{2}(\R_{+}, du)$ onto $L^{2}(\R, dw)$, and it carries $D_{\lambda}$ to multiplication by $e^{-iw\lambda}$. So $\alpha_{\kappa t}$ is, in this basis, $a(f_{w}) \mapsto e^{-i\kappa wt}a(f_{w})$: the quasi-free dynamics of the one-particle Hamiltonian $\kappa w$, self-adjoint with spectrum $\R$, the boost dynamics $a_{j} \mapsto e^{-i\omega_{j}t}a_{j}$ of the windows with the frequencies $\omega_{j}$ refined to a continuum, which Proposition \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation} identifies as the windows' time evolution.

\emph{(iv)} Put $\lambda = i\theta$. The value factor is $B_{i\theta} = \cos\tfrac{\theta}{2} + i\,e_{1}e_{0}\sin\tfrac{\theta}{2}$, the continuation of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}(1) (there written with $\sigma = e_{0}e_{1} = -e_{1}e_{0}$, so the sign of the sine flips with the orientation), and $e_{1}e_{0}\Lambda(m) = -\Lambda(m)$ gives $B_{i\theta}\Lambda(m) = e^{-i\theta/2}\Lambda(m)$; the check verifies this at rational points of the unit circle. The transport factor becomes $u \mapsto e^{-i\theta}u$, a rotation of the affine parameter into the complex plane, the contour rotation that the stored ground-state theorem uses. At $\theta = \pi$ the factor is $-i$ and $e^{-i\pi}u = -u$: the half-generator $u > 0$ is carried to $u < 0$. At $\theta = 2\pi$ the factor is $-1$, the spinor sign, and at $4\pi$ it is $+1$, the rotor period $4\pi$ with conjugation period $2\pi$ of the stored Euclidean rotor. On a Mellin mode the continued multiplier is $e^{-iw(i\theta)} = e^{w\theta}$, real: the continuation rescales the modes, which is the defining property of the rotor flow (the series' note on its two boost flows), so the rotor flow is the imaginary-rapidity continuation of $\alpha$. Under (N$_{+}$) Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii) shows the restriction of the ground state to each half-generator is the continuum I-state for this boost at rapidity period $2\pi$, so the strip of this continuation closes at $\theta = 2\pi$ and nowhere before.

\emph{(v)} $\{a(D_{\lambda}f), a^{*}(g)\} = \ip{g}{D_{\lambda}f}$ by the CAR, and Cauchy-Schwarz with unitarity gives $|\ip{g}{D_{\lambda}f}| \le \|f\|\,\|g\|$ for every real $\lambda$. For normalised indicators of cells $[a, b)$ and $[c, d)$ in $u > 0$ the overlap is $e^{-\lambda/2}|[e^{\lambda}a, e^{\lambda}b)\cap[c, d)|/\sqrt{(b - a)(d - c)}$; the check verifies the bound at every tested pair and rapidity and, for two fixed unit cells at the edge, the exact value $e^{-\lambda/2}$, which falls to $0$. For linear elements the anticommutator is a scalar, so for $A = a(f)$, $B = a^{*}(g)$ and any state $\omega$, $\omega(\{A(\lambda), B\}^{*}\{A(\lambda), B\}) = |\ip{g}{D_{\lambda}f}|^{2} \le \|f\|^{2}\|g\|^{2}$: no out-of-time-order growth, real-time exponent $\limsup_{t\to\infty} t^{-1}\ln|\{A(\kappa t), B\}| \le 0$, and it is $0$ for pairs with $\ip{g}{D_{\lambda}f}$ not decaying exponentially, for instance a Mellin packet whose density in $w$ is the indicator of an interval, whose overlap with itself is the Fourier transform of that indicator and falls only as $1/\lambda$. The general quasi-free statement is Proposition \claimref{synthesis.number-diagonal-dynamics-spreads-nothing}'s conclusion transferred from the windows. What does grow at rate $\kappa$ is support: at $e^{\lambda} = N$ the unit cell at the edge covers exactly $N$ unit cells (checked for several $N$), Proposition \claimref{synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-without-scrambling}(i).

\emph{(vi)} The setup of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises} (the boost $\beta_{t}$, with the Killing field $\kappa u\,\partial_{u}$ on the generators) shows that the Schwarzschild Killing flow and the de Sitter static flow act on the affine parameter of their horizon generators as $u \mapsto e^{\pm\kappa t}u$. A quasi-free automorphism of $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ that acts on the argument by this dilation and on values by a constant factor is unitary only with the weight $e^{\mp\kappa t/2}$, by the computation of (ii); so the time evolution there is $\alpha_{\pm\kappa t}$ and (iii) to (v) hold as stated. That the constant factor is the boost of a frame carried along the generator is the reading of (ii) in that frame; for every Killing horizon with nonzero surface gravity, off its bifurcation surface and whatever the field strength, it is derived in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.killing-horizon-value-factor-is-the-generator-boost}, which rests on (i) and (ii) here and is cited, not used as a premise.

The conclusion. By (ii) and (iii) the time evolution of the continuum is the single group $\alpha_{\kappa t}$, and by (iv) the rotor flow is its continuation in the rapidity. The statement of Assumption \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} that ``every intrinsic clock runs at the modular rate and the expansion rate is exactly $2\pi T$'' becomes: the one group $\alpha$ has real-time support-dilation rate $\kappa$ by (v), and its KMS period in Killing time is $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$ under (N$_{+}$) by (iv), so $\kappa = 2\pi/\beta$ is one identity of one group (for Schwarzschild $\kappa = 1/4M$, $\beta = 8\pi M$; the check also confirms that the doubled period of the stored independence model breaks it). On the windows the same identity is premise (R), as the stored phase-flow result shows. The real-time Lyapunov exponent of this quasi-free dynamics on linear elements is $0 < 2\pi T$, so the chaos bound is met with room, not saturated, contrary to the earlier sentence of that assumption, since corrected, and $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N = (\beta/2\pi)\ln N$ counts $\ln N$ units of rapidity: the time for one affine cell to spread over $N$. Nothing in the comparison needs a second evolution. The rate in (v) is fixed by $\alpha$ alone, whatever the state; the period is fixed by the state. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii) and the continuum I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}, the quasi-free state of symbol $(1 + e^{2\pi c\,w})^{-1}$ on the Mellin modes of a half-generator is KMS for $\alpha$ at rapidity period $2\pi c$ for every $c > 0$, so the same group with the same rate $\kappa$ has KMS period $2\pi c/\kappa$ in that state, and $\kappa\beta = 2\pi$ holds exactly when $c = 1$, the value (N$_{+}$) forces. $\square$

synthesis.boundary-mode-locality-is-desc.technical:
The series' descent on a window of boundary modes is the pinching onto the joint-number-diagonal algebra: it keeps occupation data and erases every coherence. A generator commutes with this pinching exactly when it is itself number-diagonal: if it commutes, it must commute with every joint-number projector, since the pinching of a commutator with such a projector is zero; and a number-diagonal generator is a combination of the projectors, which the pinching fixes. On three modes the script finds the space of covariant generators to be exactly the eight-dimensional diagonal algebra inside the sixty-four-dimensional window algebra. Covariance at a single time is weaker: a unitary that permutes the joint-number basis (times phases) commutes with the pinching, and the hop flow reaches such a permutation, the full swap, at one time. So (T) is a statement about the continuous flow, for all $t$, and the equivalence holds on finite windows only; continuum windows, and the differential dynamics (L$_{E}$) mentions there, are not covered.

The locality premise (L$_{E}$) says precisely that the boundary-mode dynamics is generated by number-diagonal elements. So (L$_{E}$) is equivalent to the requirement that the dynamics commute with the descent. Hopping and pairing, which earlier work had to exclude by two different arguments (a theorem within the supplied class for hopping, the premise itself for pairing), now fail one condition in the same way.

For channels the same covariance allows partial transmission: a beam splitter against a vacuum in-channel commutes with the descent and carries occupation $N \mapsto \Gamma N$. That is the occupancy content of the interface identification (I), which suggests reading (L$_{E}$) and (I) as one covariance condition on the inside and the outside of the horizon, the label correspondence of (I) remaining an input.
synthesis.boundary-mode-locality-is-desc.lay: The series assumes that a black hole's boundary quantum bits evolve without moving anything from one bit to another, a locality assumption it could not derive. It also has a standard operation, the descent, that reads off how full each bit is and forgets everything else. This result shows that, for a finite set of bits, the locality assumption says exactly that the evolution and this reading-off can be done in either order with the same result, at every moment of the evolution. This is a restatement of the assumption in terms of an operation the series already has, not a derivation of it. Two exclusions the series stated separately become one, and the same condition, applied to the escape of radiation from the black hole, allows the familiar partial transmission while forbidding mixing between channels.
