synthesis.boundary-mode-premises-finite-.formal:
A \emph{finite boundary-mode model} is a set of $n$ modes with ladders $\{v_k, v_k^{*}\}$ generating $\CAR \cong \Mat_{2^{n}}(\C)$, real weights $\omega_k$ with Killing generator $K_{\mathrm{geo}} = \sum_k \omega_k K_k$ (the constants in $K_k = v_k^{*}v_k - \tfrac12$ drop out of every flow), a state $\omega = \tr(\varrho\,\cdot\,)$, and an even self-adjoint generator $H$ of the dynamics with $\omega \circ \Ad(e^{itH}) = \omega$ (stationarity). Read on such a model: (P) is $\omega \circ \alpha = \omega$ for the grading $\alpha = \Ad(\Gamma)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.grading-parity-automorphism}; (R) is the KMS condition of Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus} for each single-mode marginal at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, in the full reading (the marginal is the Gibbs state of $\omega_k K_k$, so also $\omega(v_k) = 0$), which contains the literal reading on ladder pairs; (L$_E$) is that $H$ lies in the algebra generated by the $v_k^{*}v_k$ (Premise \claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality}); (Q) is Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}: $\omega$ is the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with diagonal symbol, KMS at $\beta$ for $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ with $\omega_k = \kappa k$. Write $u = e^{-2\pi}$, the Boltzmann factor of one unit of weight. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Q) implies (P) and (R). The geometric modular condition (G) of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.geometric-modular-condition-g} also implies (P) on finitely many modes, at any weights.
\item[(ii)] (odd resonance) Every state stationary under the Killing flow $\Ad(e^{itK_{\mathrm{geo}}})$ is even if and only if the weights have no odd signed resonance, that is no odd-size set $T$ of modes and signs $\epsilon_k = \pm 1$ with $\sum_{k \in T}\epsilon_k\omega_k = 0$. A zero-weight mode is such a resonance, as is any relation $\omega_a + \omega_b = \omega_c$. When there is one and $n \geq 2$, there are Killing-stationary odd states whose every single-mode marginal is the Gibbs state at $\beta$.
\item[(iii)] (not (P)) On the (Q) modes $k = 0, 1$ the state $\varrho_{A} = \tfrac12\id \otimes \operatorname{diag}(1, u)/(1 + u) + \tfrac{u}{4(1 + u)}\,X_0 Z_1$ (Jordan-Wigner, $X_0 = v_0 + v_0^{*}$, $Z_1 = 1 - 2v_1^{*}v_1$) is positive, stationary under $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$, satisfies (R) and (L$_E$) with $H = K_{\mathrm{geo}}$, and has $\omega(X_0 Z_1) = u/(1 + u) \neq 0$ for the odd element $X_0Z_1$. On positive weights $1, 2, 3$ the Gibbs state plus half its population times $|110\rangle\langle 001| + |001\rangle\langle 110|$ does the same, with $\omega(v_3^{*}v_2v_1) \neq 0$. So (P) does not follow from (R), (L$_E$) and stationarity.
\item[(iv)] (not (R)) On the (Q) window $k = -1, 0, 1$ the gauge-invariant quasi-free state at the doubled period, occupations $u^{2k}/(1 + u^{2k})$, is even, stationary under $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ and violates (R) at $k = \pm 1$. So (R) does not follow from (P), (L$_E$), stationarity and quasi-freeness with (Q)'s weights.
\item[(v)] (not (L$_E$)) On the (Q) window the pairing generator $G = v_{1}v_{-1} + v_{-1}^{*}v_{1}^{*}$ is even, commutes with $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ and with the (Q) state, and does not commute with $v_1^{*}v_1$; on the window $k = -1, 0, 1, 2$ so does the weight-conserving quartic hop $v_2^{*}v_{-1}^{*}v_1v_0 + \text{h.c.}$, which conserves number. So (L$_E$) does not follow from (P), (R), (Q) and stationarity. On the window $k = -j, \ldots, j$ the quadratic generators that leave the (Q) state stationary are exactly the span of the $v_k^{*}v_k$ and of the pairings $v_kv_{-k}$, $v_{-k}^{*}v_{k}^{*}$, $1 \leq k \leq j$: (Q) with stationarity excludes quadratic hopping, not pairing.
\item[(vi)] (not (Q)) On weights $1, 2$ the Gibbs state plus $c\,Z_0Z_1$, $c$ half the population of $|11\rangle$, is even, diagonal (so stationary under every (L$_E$) generator), satisfies (R), and has connected density correlation $c \neq 0$. So (Q) does not follow from (P), (R), (L$_E$) and stationarity.
\item[(vii)] Clause (2) of Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability} needs the pairing exclusion of (L$_E$): the pairing rotation $\exp\theta(v_1^{*}v_{-1}^{*} - v_{-1}v_1)$ at $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) = (\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$ fixes the (Q) state but maps an even state with Gibbs marginals (the (Q) state plus a pairing coherence) to one whose $k = 1$ marginal is not Gibbs.
\end{enumerate}
So in the block $\{$(P), (R), (L$_E$), (Q)$\}$ the only implications are (Q) $\Rightarrow$ (P) and (Q) $\Rightarrow$ (R): $\{$(P), (R), (L$_E$)$\}$ is an independent set, (Q) is an independent strengthening of (P) and (R), and in any derivation that assumes (Q) the premises (P) and (R) are redundant.
synthesis.boundary-mode-premises-finite-.technical:
The four premises that govern the boundary-mode state and dynamics are tested on finite models: finitely many fermion modes with weights, a density matrix, and a dynamics under which that density matrix is stationary. Requiring stationarity links state and dynamics, so the models are not vacuous.

The store words (Q) on top of (P) and (R), as the quasi-free state with the marginal data they fix, so the first two implications are expected; read as a self-contained condition on the state, quasi-freeness with the s-wave weights, (Q), implies both univalence (P) (a gauge-invariant state is invariant under the gauge rotation by $\pi$, which is the grading) and the regularity premise (R) (the marginals of the product Gibbs state are Gibbs states). The geometric modular condition implies (P) as well, since its state is the Gibbs state of an even generator. Stationarity under the Killing flow gives (P) for free exactly when the weights have no odd signed resonance; (Q)'s weights have one (the zero mode, and relations such as $1 + 2 = 3$), and explicit odd states then satisfy (R), (L$_E$) and stationarity. A state at twice the period violates (R) and nothing else. A pairing of the modes $\pm k$ commutes with (Q)'s Killing generator, because their weights cancel, so it preserves the (Q) state while violating (L$_E$); a weight-conserving quartic hop does the same. A correlated state with Gibbs marginals violates (Q) alone. The pairing rotation that preserves the (Q) state still moves other states of the premises' class, so the stability corollary does need (L$_E$)'s pairing clause.
synthesis.boundary-mode-premises-finite-.lay: The series assumes four separate things about the quantum bits at a black hole's boundary: that their state never mixes even and odd particle numbers, that each bit on its own looks thermal at the Hawking temperature, that the bits evolve only by phase changes, and (for one step) that the bits are as uncorrelated as possible with a fixed energy ladder. This result asks whether any of these follows from the others. It builds small, exactly computable examples, each obeying all but one assumption, and finds that the last assumption implies the first two, while otherwise none can be dropped. One example shows that pairs of bits with opposite energies can be created and destroyed without disturbing the steady thermal state, so the ban on such pair creation is a genuine extra assumption.

proofs.main:
Throughout, $\CAR$ on $n$ modes is realised on $\C^{2^{n}}$ by the Jordan-Wigner matrices $v_k = Z \otimes \cdots \otimes Z \otimes \sigma^{-} \otimes 1 \otimes \cdots \otimes 1$ in the occupation basis $|b_1 \cdots b_n\rangle$, $N_k = v_k^{*}v_k$, and the grading is $\alpha = \Ad(\Gamma)$ with $\Gamma = \prod_k (1 - 2N_k)$, as in Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.grading-parity-automorphism}; a state $\tr(\varrho\,\cdot\,)$ is even if and only if $[\varrho, \Gamma] = 0$. The Killing generator $K_{\mathrm{geo}} = \sum_k\omega_kK_k$ differs from $H_0 := \sum_k\omega_kN_k$ by a constant, so the two generate the same flow. Every configuration $b$ is an eigenvector of $H_0$ with energy $E(b) = \sum_k\omega_kb_k$. The single-mode subalgebra generated by $v_k$ is a copy of $\Mat_2(\C)$; by Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} its unique KMS state for $\Ad(e^{it\omega_kK_k})$ at $\beta \neq 0$ is the Gibbs state, which has $\omega(v_k) = \omega(v_k^{*}) = 0$ and $\omega(v_k^{*}v_k) = e^{-\beta\omega_k}\omega(v_kv_k^{*})$, and conversely these three relations fix the marginal. At $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$ and $\omega_k = \kappa k$ the factor is $e^{-2\pi k} = u^{k}$. This is the full reading of (R); the literal reading of Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}, with $a, b$ in the ladder, imposes only the third relation, so a model satisfying the full reading satisfies the literal one, and a model violating the third relation violates both.

\textbf{(i).} Under (Q) the state is the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with diagonal symbol $n_k$; by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra} on a finite window it is the product $\bigotimes_k\operatorname{diag}(1 - n_k, n_k)$, and since (Q) makes it KMS for $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ at $\beta$, Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} gives $\varrho_Q = e^{-\beta H_0}/Z$, so $n_k = u^{k}/(1 + u^{k})$. Gauge invariance means invariance under $v_k \mapsto e^{i\theta}v_k$ for all $\theta$; at $\theta = \pi$ this map is $\alpha$, so (P) holds. The restriction of $\varrho_Q$ to the mode-$k$ subalgebra has $\omega(v_k) = 0$ (an odd monomial in a diagonal state) and $\omega(v_k^{*}v_k) = n_k = u^{k}(1 - n_k)$, the three relations above, so (R) holds at each mode. Under (G) the state is faithful and its modular group is $\Ad(e^{itcK_{\mathrm{geo}}})$ for a constant $c \neq 0$; a faithful state is KMS for its modular group at $\beta = -1$, so it is KMS for $\Ad(e^{itK_{\mathrm{geo}}})$ at $\beta' = -c \neq 0$, and by Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor} $\varrho = e^{-\beta' K_{\mathrm{geo}}}/Z$. Since $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is a polynomial in the $N_k$ it commutes with $\Gamma$, hence so does $\varrho$: (P). The check confirms the (Q) case on the window $k = -1, 0, 1$ (evenness, stationarity, the three relations at each mode, the occupations, Wick factorisation of $\langle N_iN_j\rangle$ and vanishing hopping and pairing two-point data) and the Gibbs case at the nonresonant weights $(1, 2, 4)$ and $(2, 3, 7)$.

\textbf{(ii).} A state is stationary under the Killing flow if and only if $[\varrho, H_0] = 0$, that is, $\varrho$ preserves every eigenspace $V_E = \operatorname{span}\{|b\rangle : E(b) = E\}$. If no $V_E$ contains configurations of both parities, $\Gamma$ is a scalar $\pm 1$ on each $V_E$, so every $\varrho$ commuting with $H_0$ commutes with $\Gamma$ and the state is even. Two configurations $b, b'$ of equal energy and opposite parity give, with $T = \{k : b_k \neq b'_k\}$ and $\epsilon_k = b_k - b'_k$ on $T$, $\sum_{T}\epsilon_k\omega_k = E(b) - E(b') = 0$ with $|T| \equiv \sum_k b_k - \sum_k b'_k$ odd; conversely an odd signed resonance $(T, \epsilon)$ gives such a pair by putting $b_k = 1, b'_k = 0$ where $\epsilon_k = 1$, the opposite where $\epsilon_k = -1$, and $b = b'$ arbitrary off $T$. So stationarity forces evenness exactly when there is no odd signed resonance (for the converse direction see the constructions next). A zero weight is the resonance $T = \{k\}$; $\omega_a + \omega_b = \omega_c$ is $T = \{a, b, c\}$. Construction with Gibbs marginals, for $0 < u < 1$ and the Gibbs state $\varrho_G = e^{-\beta H_0}/Z$, which has full rank: if $|T| \geq 3$, $\varrho = \varrho_G + c(|b\rangle\langle b'| + |b'\rangle\langle b|)$ with $0 < c \leq p_b = p_{b'}$ (equal populations since equal energies) is positive (it differs from $\varrho_G$ only in the $2 \times 2$ block $\left(\begin{smallmatrix} p & c \\ c & p\end{smallmatrix}\right)$), commutes with $H_0$, is odd, and has the marginals of $\varrho_G$, since the partial trace of $|b\rangle\langle b'|$ onto one mode vanishes when $b$ and $b'$ differ at two or more modes. If $T = \{k\}$ ($\omega_k = 0$) and $m \neq k$ is another mode, $\varrho = \varrho_G + c\,X_kZ_m$ with $X_k = v_k + v_k^{*}$, $Z_m = 1 - 2N_m$: $X_kZ_m$ is odd, commutes with $H_0$ (it changes only $b_k$, at zero energy cost), and its partial trace onto any single mode vanishes ($\tr Z = \tr X = 0$ on the mode it is traced over, with the Jordan-Wigner string contributing further factors $Z$); positivity holds for $|c|$ at most the smallest population, as the explicit instance in (iii) shows. The check computes, for each weight set, the dimension of the commutant of $H_0$, $\sum_E (d_E^{+} + d_E^{-})^{2}$, against that of its even part, $\sum_E ((d_E^{+})^{2} + (d_E^{-})^{2})$, with $d_E^{\pm}$ the numbers of even and odd configurations of energy $E$: $(1,2,4)$: $8, 8$; $(1,2,3)$: $10, 8$; $(-1,0,1)$: $24, 12$; $(-2,\ldots,2)$: $176, 88$; $(1,3,5,7)$: $18, 18$ (its resonance $1 + 7 = 3 + 5$ is even); and it confirms that the two differ exactly when an odd signed resonance exists, on all $35$ three-element weight sets from $\{-3, \ldots, 3\}$ and all $15$ four-element sets from $\{1, \ldots, 6\}$ ($39$ of these $50$ are resonant).

\textbf{(iii).} Model A: weights $0, 1$, $\varrho_G = \tfrac12\id \otimes \operatorname{diag}(1, u)/(1 + u)$, $c = u/(4(1 + u))$. The vectors $(|0\rangle \pm |1\rangle) \otimes |m\rangle$, $m = 0, 1$, are eigenvectors with eigenvalues $(2 + u)/(4(1 + u))$, $u/(4(1 + u))$, $(2 - u)/(4(1 + u))$, $3u/(4(1 + u))$, all positive for $0 < u < 1$, so $\varrho_A > 0$; $\tr\varrho_A = 1$; $[\varrho_A, H_0] = 0$ with $H_0 = N_1$; the three relations hold at both modes ($u^{0} = 1$ at the zero mode, where the marginal is tracial); $\tr(\varrho_A X_0Z_1) = u/(1 + u)$; $[\varrho_A, \Gamma] \neq 0$. The dynamics $H = K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is number-diagonal, so (L$_E$) holds, and $\varrho_A$ is stationary under it. Model B: weights $1, 2, 3$, $b = 110$, $b' = 001$, both of energy $3$ and population $p = u^{3}/Z$, $c = p/2$; the check confirms trace, stationarity, the relations at the three modes, $\tr(\varrho_B v_3^{*}v_2v_1) \neq 0$, oddness, and positivity by exhibiting $8$ independent eigenvectors with eigenvalues positive on $(0, 1)$. Model B shows that the zero mode is not needed: one three-term relation suffices.

\textbf{(iv).} The state $e^{-2\beta H_0}/Z$ on weights $-1, 0, 1$ is diagonal, hence even and stationary, with diagonal symbol and vanishing pairing data (gauge-invariant quasi-free, Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}), and its marginals satisfy $\omega(v_k^{*}v_k) = u^{2k}\omega(v_kv_k^{*})$; at $k = \pm 1$ this differs from $u^{k}\omega(v_kv_k^{*})$ since $u \neq 1$, so (R) fails there, in both readings, while the zero mode is tracial at every period. The check confirms the pattern $[\text{fail}, \text{hold}, \text{fail}]$ at the period $p$ and $[\text{hold}, \text{hold}, \text{hold}]$ at $2p$.

\textbf{(v).} For distinct modes $[H_0, v_i^{*}v_j] = (\omega_i - \omega_j)v_i^{*}v_j$, $[H_0, v_iv_j] = -(\omega_i + \omega_j)v_iv_j$, $[H_0, v_i^{*}v_j^{*}] = (\omega_i + \omega_j)v_i^{*}v_j^{*}$, and $[H_0, N_i] = 0$; the quadratic monomials are linearly independent, so the kernel of $\Ad H_0$ on their span is spanned by the monomials of eigenvalue zero. Because $u \neq 1$ the function $E \mapsto u^{E}$ is injective, so $\varrho_Q = u^{H_0}/Z$ and $H_0$ have the same spectral projections and an operator commutes with $\varrho_Q$ if and only if it commutes with $H_0$. With $\omega_k = \kappa k$ distinct, $\omega_i - \omega_j = 0$ only for $i = j$ and $\omega_i + \omega_j = 0$ only for $\{i, j\} = \{k, -k\}$, $k \neq 0$ ($v_0v_0 = 0$): the stationary quadratic generators are the span of the $N_k$ and of $v_kv_{-k}$, $v_{-k}^{*}v_k^{*}$, as stated. In particular $G$ is stationary, even (quadratic), Hermitian, and $[G, N_1] = -v_1v_{-1} + v_{-1}^{*}v_1^{*} \neq 0$, so it is not in the algebra generated by the $N_k$: it is exactly a pairing term of the kind (L$_E$) excludes (compare Proposition \claimref{singularity.l-stabiliser-tangent}, where such terms are the tangent of the vacuum orbit). The quartic $v_2^{*}v_{-1}^{*}v_1v_0$ has eigenvalue $\kappa(2 - 1 - 1 - 0) = 0$; with its adjoint it commutes with $H_0$, with $\varrho_Q$ and with $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$, and not with $N_2$: a number-conserving hop that moves occupation from the modes $0, 1$ to the modes $-1, 2$ without disturbing the (Q) state. The check verifies these commutators as matrices, the zero-eigenvalue lists on the window $-2, \ldots, 2$, and the eigenvalue rule on three pair monomials of that window.

\textbf{(vi).} $Z_0Z_1 = \operatorname{diag}(1, -1, -1, 1)$ has vanishing partial traces onto either mode, so $\varrho = \varrho_G + cZ_0Z_1$ has the Gibbs marginals; it is diagonal, so even and stationary under every element of the algebra generated by the $N_k$; with $c = u^{3}/(2Z)$, $Z = (1 + u)(1 + u^{2})$, every diagonal entry is positive on $(0, 1)$ (the two lowered ones are $u^{2}(2 - u)/(2Z)$ and $u(2 - u^{2})/(2Z)$). Its connected correlation is $\omega(N_0N_1) - \omega(N_0)\omega(N_1) = c \neq 0$, while a quasi-free gauge-invariant state with diagonal symbol has $\omega(N_0N_1) = n_0n_1$ by Wick's theorem (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}). So (Q) fails. This is an explicit instance of the freedom recorded in Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}(3).

\textbf{(vii).} Let $A = v_1^{*}v_{-1}^{*}$ and $\Theta = A - A^{*}$, real and anti-Hermitian. On $\operatorname{span}\{|0_{-1}0_1\rangle, |1_{-1}1_1\rangle\}$ (at either occupation of the zero mode) $\Theta$ acts as a rotation generator and it annihilates the singly occupied pairs, so $\Theta^{3} = -\Theta$ and $e^{\theta\Theta} = 1 + \sin\theta\,\Theta + (1 - \cos\theta)\Theta^{2}$; at $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) = (\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$ this is a rational orthogonal matrix $U_\theta$. The two configurations it mixes have equal energy $-1 + 1 = 0$ and so equal populations in $\varrho_Q$; hence $[U_\theta, \varrho_Q] = 0$. Let $\varrho_c = \varrho_Q + \tfrac{p}{2}(|1_{-1}0_01_1\rangle\langle 0_{-1}0_00_1| + \text{h.c.})$ with $p$ the common population of the two configurations: it is even, and its single-mode marginals are those of $\varrho_Q$ (the coherence connects configurations differing at two modes), so it lies in the class $\mathcal{C}$ of Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}. Conjugating the $2 \times 2$ block $\left(\begin{smallmatrix} p & p/2 \\ p/2 & p\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ by a rotation of angle $\theta$ moves $\mp\tfrac{p}{2}\sin 2\theta$ of population between the two configurations; the check computes $U_\theta\varrho_cU_\theta^{*}$ exactly and finds $\omega(N_1)$ shifted by $-\tfrac{6}{25}\,u/(1 + u)^{2} \neq 0$ (with $p = u/(2(1 + u)^{2})$ and $\sin 2\theta = \tfrac{24}{25}$) and the third relation at $k = 1$ violated. (Coherences of the same sign in both zero-mode blocks would cancel in $\omega(N_1)$ through the Jordan-Wigner string of $v_1$; one block suffices.) So the pairing dynamics leaves $\mathcal{C}$, and the stability clause (2) of that corollary uses (L$_E$)'s pairing exclusion, not only its hopping exclusion.

\textbf{Consequence for the block.} By (i), (Q) implies (P) and (R). By (iii), (P) does not follow from $\{$(R), (L$_E$)$\}$ even with stationarity, and since every model of (Q) is even, the models of (iii) violate (Q). By (iv), (R) does not follow from $\{$(P), (L$_E$)$\}$ with stationarity and quasi-freeness. By (v), (L$_E$) does not follow from $\{$(P), (R), (Q)$\}$ with stationarity. By (vi), (Q) does not follow from $\{$(P), (R), (L$_E$)$\}$ with stationarity. Hence no premise of the block follows from the others except through (Q) $\Rightarrow$ (P), (R), and $\{$(P), (R), (L$_E$)$\}$ is independent. The models are finite and every relation used is verified in exact rational-function arithmetic in $u$; positivity on $0 < u < 1$ (where $u = e^{-2\pi}$ lies) is certified by eigenvectors whose eigenvalues have numerator and denominator polynomials with nonnegative Bernstein coefficients on $[0, 1]$, not all zero.

synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On the flat gravitational field ($\hb = 1$, $\Omega = 0$; Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) let $N = \{x_{0} + \lambda k + y\}$ be a null plane with generators along $k = e_{0} + e_{3}$, $y$ in the span of $e_{1}, e_{2}$, $m = e_{0} - e_{3}$, and $\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12(1 + e_{0}e_{3})$ the projector onto the canonical part on $N$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}), with two-channel image $V_{\Lambda}$. For the free Dirac field of mass $m_{0} \ge 0$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}) put $\psi_{N}(\lambda, y) = \sqrt{2}\,\Lambda(m)\psi(x_{0} + \lambda k + y)$ and $K = L^{2}(\R^{2}, d^{2}y)\otimes V_{\Lambda}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The plane carries the generator CAR; computed.)} $\{\psi_{N}(\lambda, y), \psi_{N}^{*}(\lambda', y')\} = \delta(\lambda - \lambda')\,\delta^{2}(y - y')\,\Lambda(m)$: the continuum mode space $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, d\lambda)\otimes K)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, with $u = \lambda$ an affine parameter on each generator.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Every vacuum restricts to the null vacuum; computed exactly.)} $\Lambda(m)(p \pm m_{0})e_{0}\Lambda(m) = \ip{p}{k}\Lambda(m)$ for every vector $p$ and mass $m_{0}$, the positive-energy shell has $\ip{p}{k} > 0$, and in the variables $(\ip{p}{k}, p_{\perp})$ the compressed shell density is $\tfrac12$ for every $m_{0}$ and $p_{\perp}$. Hence for every $m_{0} \ge 0$ the bulk vacuum restricts (the restriction defined by this momentum-space computation with transverse smearing, not as a pullback of distributions, since the wave-front set of the vacuum kernel meets the conormal of $N\times N$ along the generators) to $\omega_{m_{0}}(\psi_{N}^{*}(v)\psi_{N}(u)) = W_{0}(u, v)\otimes\id_{K}$, $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$: the null vacuum $\omega_{0}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i) on every generator, in every affine parameter.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Hadamard states give the generator condition; proved, given the imported fact.)} If $\omega$ is a gauge-invariant quasi-free state of the mass-$m_{0}$ field whose two-point kernel differs from $\omega_{m_{0}}$'s by a smooth kernel (a Hadamard state; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}), its restriction to $N$ has smooth remainder $R = W_{\omega} - W_{0}\otimes\id_{K}$ on $J\times J$ for every interval $J$ of every generator, in each $K$-component with compactly supported transverse profiles. So it satisfies the microlocal spectrum condition on every such $J$ and, by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}(ii), its scaling limit at every point of $N$ is $\omega_{0}$: the local form of (N$_{+}$) holds at every point of every local Rindler horizon of the flat field, with no stationarity, temperature or symmetry assumed.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What it does not give.)} Not the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$) (every Hadamard state passes, the stored affine-KMS states included), not (Loc), and not the statement on a field with nonzero field strength.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Note (nonzero field strength; added 1 November).} At points of a gravitational field with nonzero field strength the conclusion of (iii) is carried by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}, (HS) (adopted as a premise on 1 November, proved on 2 November): a gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard Dirac state there scales to the massless vacuum of the flat field, also on the generators of every local Rindler horizon through the point, and by (ii) at $m_{0} = 0$ that vacuum restricts to the null vacuum; so, by (HS), such states have the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point of every local Rindler horizon. This result does not use (HS); it is proved on the flat field only. The mass independence in (ii) is the standard light-front statement (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-null-plane-restriction-of-free-fields-is-mass-independent}), here computed in the store's generator conventions.
synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-.technical:
The stored horizon results pose, on a single horizon generator, the analogue of the Hadamard condition, the standard requirement that physical states look like the vacuum at short distances, and show that it gives the local form of the null ground-state premise (N$_{+}$) at every point. What was missing is the link to the field theory: whether the field theory's own states, the Hadamard states of a four-dimensional Dirac field, satisfy the generator condition.

On the flat gravitational field this link is computed. On a null plane the canonical part of the Dirac field, its image under $\Lambda(m)$, carries the generator algebra with the transverse directions as multiplicity labels. The projector removes the mass term from the vacuum kernels, and in the null momentum the shell density is exactly one half for every mass and transverse momentum, so the vacuum of every mass restricts to the null vacuum on every generator (a standard light-front result, here in the store's generator conventions). A gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state differs from that vacuum by a smooth kernel, which stays smooth when restricted to the plane; so it satisfies the generator condition on every interval and has the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point of every local Rindler horizon.

It does not give the ground-state clause, since every Hadamard state passes, nor (Loc), and it is proved only where the gravitational field strength vanishes; at points of nonzero field strength the same conclusion follows from the scaling-limit theorem (HS), formerly a premise, which this result does not use. Transport-absent.
synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-.lay: The series' account of horizon temperature rests on an assumption that, very close to any point of a horizon, the quantum field looks like empty space. This result checks that assumption against the field theory in empty flat space. On any light-like plane, the field's vacuum, whatever the particle's mass, looks exactly like the empty state that the assumption names, and every state that physicists regard as reasonable, one that differs from the vacuum only smoothly, looks like it at short distances too. So in flat space the assumption's short-distance part is a consequence of the field theory, though not the part that says the state is the vacuum everywhere, and not yet in a gravitational field.

transverse profiles of compact support: the K-components are taken for compactly supported transverse profiles

proofs.main:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Work in $\Cl(1,3)$ on the flat gravitational field, $\hb = 1$, $\Omega = 0$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}); the free Dirac field of mass $m_{0} \ge 0$ is the one of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}. Matrix forms below are parenthetical readings of left multiplication in $\Cl(1,3)$.

\emph{The plane and its canonical part.} With $k = e_{0} + e_{3}$, $m = e_{0} - e_{3}$, $\ip{k}{m} = 2$, the canonical part of a spinor on $N$ is $\Lambda(m)\psi$, $\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12(1 + e_{0}e_{3}) = \tfrac14 mk$ (Theorems \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}, \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(i)). It is idempotent and self-adjoint for the Dirac adjoint ($e_{0}\tilde\Lambda e_{0} = \Lambda$), its image is two complex channels, and the check verifies $\Lambda e_{0}\Lambda = 0$ and $\Lambda e_{\mu}e_{0}\Lambda = \ip{e_{\mu}}{k}\Lambda$ for $\mu = 0, \dots, 3$. By linearity
\[
\Lambda(m)\,(p \pm m_{0})\,e_{0}\,\Lambda(m) \;=\; \ip{p}{k}\,\Lambda(m)
\]
for every vector $p$ and every mass: the mass term drops out of the compressed kernels. (Algebraically: $e_{0}\Lambda = \tfrac12 k$ and $\Lambda k = 0$.)

\emph{(ii) The vacuum.} The restriction to $N$ is not a pullback of distributions in H\"ormander's sense: the wave-front set of the vacuum kernel contains the null covectors along the generators, which meet the conormal of $N\times N$. It is defined here by the momentum-space (light-front) computation below, with transverse smearing; the outcome, that the null-plane vacuum does not depend on the mass, is the standard light-front result (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-null-plane-restriction-of-free-fields-is-mass-independent}), reproduced in the store's generator conventions. The bulk vacuum kernels are (standard, matrix reading) $\omega_{m_{0}}(\psi(x)\psi^{\dagger}(x')) = \int\frac{d^{3}p}{(2\pi)^{3}2p_{0}}(p + m_{0})e_{0}\,e^{-ip\cdot(x - x')}$ and $\omega_{m_{0}}(\psi^{\dagger}(x')\psi(x)) = \int\frac{d^{3}p}{(2\pi)^{3}2p_{0}}(p - m_{0})e_{0}\,e^{+ip\cdot(x - x')}$, over the positive-energy shell. Parametrise the shell by $p_{+} = \ip{p}{k}$ and $p_{\perp}$, with $s = p_{\perp}^{2} + m_{0}^{2}$ (Euclidean square): $p_{0} = \tfrac12(p_{+} + s/p_{+})$, $p_{3} = \tfrac12(s/p_{+} - p_{+})$, so $dp_{3}/dp_{+} = -p_{0}/p_{+}$ and $d^{3}p/(2p_{0}) = dp_{+}\,d^{2}p_{\perp}/(2p_{+})$; for $s > 0$, $p_{0} > |p_{3}|$, so $p_{+} > 0$ on the whole positive-energy shell and $p_{+}$ runs over $(0, \infty)$ (for $s = 0$ the set $p_{\perp} = 0$, $m_{0} = 0$ has measure zero). On $N$, $x - x' = (\lambda - \lambda')k + (y - y')$ and $p\cdot(x - x') = (\lambda - \lambda')p_{+} - p_{\perp}\cdot(y - y')$. Compressing by $\Lambda(m)$, the integrand becomes $\tfrac{1}{2p_{+}}\,p_{+}\Lambda = \tfrac12\Lambda$, independent of $m_{0}$ and $p_{\perp}$ (the check verifies the density $\tfrac12$ on rational shell points with and without mass). Hence, with the standard Fourier integrals $\int d^{2}p_{\perp}e^{ip_{\perp}\cdot y} = (2\pi)^{2}\delta^{2}(y)$ and $\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-i\lambda p}dp = -i(\lambda - i0)^{-1}$,
\[
\omega_{m_{0}}\big(\Lambda\psi(x)\,(\Lambda\psi(x'))^{\dagger}\big) = \tfrac12\,\delta^{2}(y - y')\Lambda\cdot\Big(-\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\Big)(\lambda - \lambda' - i0)^{-1},
\]
and the other ordering is $\tfrac12\delta^{2}(y - y')\Lambda\cdot\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(\lambda - \lambda' + i0)^{-1}$. In the stored conventions (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)) $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$ and $\delta - W_{0} = -\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v - i0)^{-1}$. So with $\psi_{N} = \sqrt{2}\,\Lambda(m)\psi$ and $u = \lambda$: (i) the anticommutator is $\delta(u - v)\,\delta^{2}(y - y')\Lambda$, the CAR of $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ with $K = L^{2}(\R^{2}, d^{2}y)\otimes V_{\Lambda}$, $V_{\Lambda}$ the two-channel image of $\Lambda(m)$ on spinors, and (ii) $\omega_{m_{0}}(\psi_{N}^{*}(v)\psi_{N}(u)) = W_{0}(u, v)\otimes\id_{K}$ for every $m_{0} \ge 0$. Equivalently, for each $p_{\perp}$ the occupation symbol in $p_{+}$ is $\theta(p_{+})$, the null vacuum's. A rescaling $\lambda = cu$ multiplies both $\delta$ and $(\lambda - \lambda' \mp i0)^{-1}$ by $1/c$, absorbed by the weight $\tfrac12$ of $\psi_{N}$, so the statement holds in every affine parameter.

\emph{(iii) Hadamard states.} By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}, quasi-free Dirac Hadamard states differ by smooth kernels, and on Minkowski space the vacuum of mass $m_{0}$ is one; so a quasi-free Hadamard state $\omega$ of the mass-$m_{0}$ field has $\omega(\psi(x)\psi^{\dagger}(x')) = \omega_{m_{0}}(\psi(x)\psi^{\dagger}(x')) + S(x, x')$ with $S$ smooth, and the other ordering differs by $-S$ (the anticommutator is state independent). Restricting to $N$ and compressing, $\omega(\psi_{N}^{*}(v)\psi_{N}(u))$ has matrix elements $\ip{f}{\,\cdot\,g}_{K}$, for transverse profiles $f, g$ of compact support, equal to those of $W_{0}(u, v)\otimes\id_{K}$ plus $2\int\!\!\int \bar f(y)\Lambda S(\cdot)\Lambda g(y')$, a smooth function of $(u, v)$ (differentiation under the integral over a compact set). So the remainder $R$ is smooth on $J\times J$ for every interval $J$ of every generator, in each $K$-component, and by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}(i) the restricted state satisfies the generator's microlocal spectrum condition there; by its (ii) its scaling limit at every point of $N$ is $\omega_{0}$, the local form of (N$_{+}$), with no stationarity, temperature or symmetry used. The restricted state is gauge-invariant and quasi-free because $\omega$ is and the restricted fields are linear in $\psi$. For translation-invariant states the same follows on the symbol side: on the shell $p_{0} = \tfrac12 p_{+} + s/(2p_{+}) \ge p_{+}/2$ (checked), so a bulk occupation remainder decaying faster than every power of $p_{0}$ gives a remainder symbol decaying faster than every power of $p_{+}$ (and, for $s > 0$, also as $p_{+} \to 0^{+}$).

\emph{(iv) Limits.} The ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$) is not reached: the result holds for every Hadamard state, and the stored theorem's affine-KMS states pass the same condition; the thermal states of the bulk field, which are Hadamard (argued, standard), restrict to states that are not the null vacuum. The plane is the local Rindler horizon of the flat field; on a field with nonzero field strength the restriction of the Hadamard parametrix to a null surface is not computed here, and Kay and Wald's analysis of horizon restrictions on Killing horizons is cited from memory only. The light-front reading of the canonical part on a null plane and the mass independence of the restriction are standard (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-null-plane-restriction-of-free-fields-is-mass-independent}); at points of nonzero field strength the conclusion of (iii) is carried by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}, (HS) (formerly a premise), which this proof does not use; the new content is the link to the horizon premises: the field theory's gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard states, not a choice of vacuum, give the local form of (N$_{+}$). Transport-absent.

synthesis.collapse-in-vacuum-regular-at-.formal:
Work on flat spacetime with gravity the gauge fields $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). The collapse field is the null-shell (Vaidya) field: vanishing field strength for advanced time $v < v_{0}$, and for $v > v_{0}$ the Schwarzschild field of mass $M$ in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge $\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta^{2} = 2M/r$, with the rotation-gauge field of Proposition \claimref{singularity.connection-bivector-computed}, $\Omega(e_{t}) = -\beta\beta'\sigma_{r}$, $\Omega(e_{r}) = -\beta'\sigma_{r}$; $\kappa = 1/4M$, $m := 2M$, $T_{H} = \kappa/2\pi$. On each radial light ray the modes are the continuum mode space of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}: a complex chiral CAR field of weight $\tfrac12$ in a parameter $\lambda$ of the ray, with null vacuum kernel $\omega(\psi^{*}(\lambda_{2})\psi(\lambda_{1})) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(\lambda_{1} - \lambda_{2} + i0)^{-1}$; a reparametrisation $\lambda = f(\mu)$ acts by $\psi_{\mu}(\mu) = f'(\mu)^{1/2}\psi_{\lambda}(f(\mu))$. Say a state of the outgoing modes on an ingoing ray is in the short-distance class at a point $\lambda = 0$ if its kernel is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}[(\lambda_{1} - \lambda_{2} + i0)^{-1} + R(\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2})]$ with $R$ continuous near $(0,0)$. Write $\{f, x\} = f'''/f' - \tfrac32(f''/f')^{2}$ for the Schwarzian; the null energy flux of the state is $-\tfrac{1}{24\pi}$ times the Schwarzian of the map from its vacuum's parameter to the observer's (normal ordered at the observer's vacuum).
Two facts of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand field are used and recomputed here from the stored rotation-gauge field (they are clauses (i) and (ii) of the result filed alongside, synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet, which states the short-distance condition and derives the late-time I-state from it): on the ingoing radial null worldlines the physical tangent $k = (\gamma_{0} - \gamma_{1})/(1 + \beta)$ is parallel, so $r$ is affine there; and on such a worldline $U := -\rho\,e^{\rho/2M}$, $\rho = r - 2M$, satisfies $dU/du = -\kappa U$ for the outgoing worldlines' Killing label $u$, with $dU/dr = -1$ at the crossing.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The collapse state is in the class.)} The ray that entered from past null infinity at advanced time $v < v_{H} := v_{0} - 4M$ and leaves the centre outgoing in the flat region leaves the shell at radius $s = (v_{0} - v)/2 > m$; its retarded Killing time is $u = v_{0} - 2s - 2m\ln(s/m - 1)$ and its Kruskal label is an analytic function of $v$ with nonzero derivative at $v_{H}$, of the form $C\,e^{z}z$, $z = s/m - 1$. If the ingoing modes at past null infinity are in the null vacuum for the affine translations of $v$ (the vacuum of the region before the shell), then on every ingoing ray crossing the future horizon the outgoing modes are in the short-distance class at the crossing in the affine parameter $r$, with remainder $R(\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2}) = \tfrac{1}{12}\{f, \lambda\}(\lambda_{1} - \lambda_{2}) + O(|\lambda|^{2})$ vanishing at the crossing ($\{z e^{z}, z\}_{z=0} = -3$, $\{U, v\}_{v_{H}} = -3/(4m^{2})$, finite).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The flux, exactly, and its limit.)} At future null infinity the outgoing flux per complex chiral field per ray is $-\tfrac{1}{24\pi}\{v, u\}$ with
\[
\{v, u\} = -\frac{m(4s - 3m)}{8s^{4}}\qquad\text{exactly}, \qquad \lim_{u\to\infty}\{v, u\} = -\frac{1}{8m^{2}} = -\frac{\kappa^{2}}{2},
\]
approached as $O(s - m) = O(e^{-\kappa u})$, so the late flux is $\kappa^{2}/48\pi = \tfrac{\pi}{12}T_{H}^{2}$, that of a complex chiral fermion at $T_{H}$. The late-time two-point function in $u$ is the pull-back of the null vacuum by $U = -e^{-\kappa u}/\kappa$, which is exactly $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\tfrac{\kappa}{2}\sinh(\tfrac{\kappa}{2}(u_{1} - u_{2}) + i0)^{-1}$, the continuum I-state at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}), unique by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness}; the remainder contributes $O(e^{-2\kappa t})$ to the kernel at shift $t$ (for this state; the result filed alongside shows the limit for every state of the class).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Regularity selects $T_{H}$.)} Let a state of the outgoing modes have late-time flux $\tfrac{\pi}{12}(\theta T_{H})^{2}$, $\theta \ge 0$. Its flux in the frame of the $U$-vacuum is $F_{U} = (\theta^{2} - 1)/(48\pi U^{2})$ at leading order as $U \to 0^{-}$, bounded across the future horizon if and only if $\theta = 1$. The Boulware state (the $u$-vacuum, $\theta = 0$) has $\{u, U\} = 1/(2U^{2})$ and diverges there. So, among states that are KMS for the Killing translations at late times, finite null energy across the future horizon holds only at temperature $\kappa/2\pi$. Only the flux is used: bounded $F_{U}$ is a necessary condition, and it is neither the short-distance class nor sufficient for it. (Filed alongside, synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet, shows that the Boulware-type state is outside the class and that no exact null-translation ground state can be posed on the collapse geometry's half-line rays.)
\end{enumerate}
Hypotheses: the in-region state (a ground state for the affine advanced time, the Minkowski vacuum of the region before the shell); the per-light-ray chiral reduction, which is the s-wave reduction of the postulate J3 (\claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction}) in its geometric-optics form, with no greybody factors; and the transformation law of the null energy of a chiral field (the coefficient of the linear remainder, cited from memory).

\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The glued field across the shell and the null infinities, read on the conformal compactification, are not carried by one gravitational field on one chart; the preliminaries and statement (iii) hold in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart, which covers both sides of the future horizon.
synthesis.collapse-in-vacuum-regular-at-.technical:
The result filed alongside (synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet) states the condition for a collapsing hole as the short-distance ground-state condition on the ingoing light rays at the future horizon, and derives the Hawking state from it, since the Killing translation dilates the Kruskal parameter about the crossing. Two questions remain: does a hole formed by collapse satisfy the condition, and is the condition forced? This result answers both for the null-shell collapse, exactly, under the per-light-ray chiral reduction (the s-wave reduction of the postulate J3). The physical state is the vacuum of the region before the collapse, a ground state for the affine advanced time $v$ of the incoming light rays. Through the shell, the ray-tracing map from $v$ to the Kruskal label $U$ is analytic with nonzero derivative at the last ray that escapes, so the state on the future horizon's ingoing rays is the ground-state kernel plus a remainder that vanishes at the crossing. The flux at infinity is the Schwarzian $\{v, u\} = -m(4s - 3m)/8s^{4}$, exact at all times, tending to the value of a thermal chiral fermion at $\kappa/2\pi$. Conversely, a state KMS at late times at any other temperature has a flux in the horizon-regular frame that diverges as $U^{-2}$ at the future horizon; the Boulware state is the case $\theta = 0$. So the condition is realised by collapse, and among late-time KMS states only the Hawking temperature has finite null energy at the future horizon. The result filed alongside states the condition, proves that the late-time limit of every state in the class is the I-state, and excludes the Boulware-type state and an exact ground state; this result does not repeat those clauses.

The computations are exact: the parallel transport of the ingoing tangent with the stored Painlev\'e-Gullstrand rotation gauge field; the dilation identity $dU/du = -\kappa U$, whose exponential factor cancels; the pull-back identities of the weight-$\tfrac12$ kernel (M\"obius invariance; thermal kernel in $x = e^{\kappa u/2}$); the remainder series of the map $z e^{z}$ to sixth order; the Schwarzian along the shell exit radius from exact Taylor coefficients of $u'(s) = -2s/(s - m)$; and the regularity dichotomy. The Fermi integral behind $\tfrac{\pi}{12}T^{2}$ and the four-dimensional statement (Fredenhagen and Haag) are cited from memory.
synthesis.collapse-in-vacuum-regular-at-.lay: A real black hole forms when matter collapses; it was never an eternal hole in equilibrium. The series' premise that fixes the Hawking temperature covered only the eternal hole. A result filed alongside says what the condition should be for a collapsing hole: near the horizon, at very short distances, the quantum field looks like empty space. This result checks that a collapse really produces such a state, in the simplest exact model, a thin shell of light falling inward. The field starts in empty space before the collapse; its light rays pass through the centre and out past the forming horizon, and the stretching they suffer is computed exactly. The outgoing energy flow tends to that of a thermal glow at exactly the Hawking temperature. It also shows that no other temperature is possible: any other late-time thermal state would make the field's energy blow up at the horizon. The calculation treats each light ray separately, as the series' standard reduction does.
flags: beyond one flat chart: the collapse field is the vanishing field for v < v0 and the Painleve-Gullstrand field for v > v0, glued across the null shell with the radial label continuous; past and future null infinity are read on the conformal compactification

proofs.main:
\emph{(Preliminaries: the two facts of the field.)} In the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge the physical coframe is $\theta^{0} = dt$, $\theta^{1} = \beta\,dt + dr$ (Proposition \claimref{singularity.connection-bivector-computed}), so the background direction $e_{t} + w e_{r}$ has physical image $\gamma_{0} + (\beta + w)\gamma_{1}$, null for $w = 1 - \beta$ (outgoing) and $w = -(1 + \beta)$ (ingoing). For the ingoing tangent $a = e_{t}/(1 + \beta) - e_{r}$ the image is $k = (\gamma_{0} - \gamma_{1})/(1 + \beta)$ and $dr/d\lambda = -1$. Then $a\cdot\nabla k = \beta'(1 + \beta)^{-2}(\gamma_{0} - \gamma_{1})$, $\Omega(a) = (1+\beta)^{-1}\Omega(e_{t}) - \Omega(e_{r}) = \beta'(1 + \beta)^{-1}\sigma_{r}$, and with $\sigma_{r} = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{0}$ one has $\sigma_{r}\times(\gamma_{0} - \gamma_{1}) = -(\gamma_{0} - \gamma_{1})$, so $a\cdot\nabla k + \Omega(a)\times k = 0$: $k$ is parallel and $r$ is affine (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(iii)). The background time translation is a symmetry of the field ($\beta$ depends on $r$ only) and moves the outgoing worldlines; label them by $u = t - r_{*}$ with $dr_{*}/dr = 1/(1 - \beta)$. Along an ingoing worldline $dt/dr = -1/(1 + \beta)$, so $du/dr = -2/(1 - \beta^{2}) = -2r/(r - 2M)$. For $U = -\rho e^{\rho/2M}$, $dU/du = -(1 + \rho/2M)e^{\rho/2M}\,dr/du = \tfrac{2M + \rho}{2M}e^{\rho/2M}\cdot\tfrac{\rho}{2(2M + \rho)} = \tfrac{1}{4M}\rho e^{\rho/2M} = -\kappa U$. Hence $U(u + t) = e^{-\kappa t}U(u)$ on each ingoing ray, and $dU/dr = -(1 + \rho/2M)e^{\rho/2M} = -1$ at $\rho = 0$. The check verifies the null directions, the parallel transport (with a control in which $\Omega$ is reversed), $dr/du$ and $dU/du = -\kappa U$ exactly at $(M, \beta)$ and $(M, r)$ samples, horizon and interior included.

\emph{(i)} Throughout, the modes are the per-light-ray chiral fields of the s-wave reduction of the postulate J3 (\claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction}) in its geometric-optics form; this is a hypothesis of the result. Inside the shell the field vanishes: an ingoing ray of advanced time $v$ reaches the centre and leaves as the outgoing ray of flat retarded time $v$, which meets the shell $v = v_{0}$ at $r = s = (v_{0} - v)/2$. The radial label is continuous across the shell, so in the Schwarzschild region the ray is the outgoing ray through $(v_{0}, s)$; in the derived-metric reading its retarded time is $u = v_{0} - 2r_{*}(s)$, $r_{*}(s) = s + m\ln(s/m - 1)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}), and its Kruskal label is $-4M e^{-v_{0}/4M}e^{s/m}(s/m - 1) = C\,z e^{z}$ with $z = s/m - 1$, $C = -4Me^{1 - v_{0}/4M}$; the escaping rays are $s > m$, the horizon ray $s = m$ ($v = v_{H}$), and the formula continues analytically to $s < m$. On the outgoing modes of an ingoing ray crossing the future horizon the label $U$ is the analytic coordinate of (i), and by the preliminaries $U$ is an analytic function of $r$ with $dU/dr = -1$ there; so the parameter $v$ of the in-vacuum is an analytic function $f$ of the affine parameter $\lambda$ of the ray with $f' \ne 0$ at the crossing. The in-vacuum's kernel in $v$ is the null vacuum (hypothesis), and its pull-back to $\lambda$ is $f'(\lambda_{1})^{1/2}f'(\lambda_{2})^{1/2}/(f(\lambda_{1}) - f(\lambda_{2}))$. For any analytic $f$ with $f'(0) \ne 0$ this equals $(\lambda_{1} - \lambda_{2})^{-1} + \tfrac{1}{12}\{f, \lambda\}(\lambda_{1} - \lambda_{2}) + \dots$, the remainder analytic and zero on the diagonal (the weight-$\tfrac12$ kernel is exactly M\"obius invariant, so only the Schwarzian enters at the first order). The check computes the series exactly for $f(\lambda) = \lambda e^{\lambda}$, the common form of the ray's Kruskal map and the ray-tracing map after affine changes (which the kernel ignores up to the M\"obius invariance it verifies), along the lines $(\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2}) = (p\epsilon, q\epsilon)$ for three $(p, q)$, to order six: the $\epsilon^{0}$ term of $\epsilon R$ vanishes, the $\epsilon^{1}$ term vanishes, and the $\epsilon^{2}$ term is $-\tfrac{3}{12}(p - q)$, with $\{\lambda e^{\lambda}, \lambda\}_{0} = -3$; a control with $\lambda e^{2\lambda}$ gives another coefficient. Composition of analytic maps with nonzero derivative keeps the class, so the in-vacuum is in the short-distance class at the crossing. In closed form $\{U, y\} = (y + 2)/y - \tfrac32((y + 1)/y)^{2}$ with $y = s/m$, singular only at $s = 0$, the ray that reaches the shell at the centre, which is inside the horizon; at the horizon ray $\{U, v\} = \{U, y\}/(4m^{2}) = -3/(4m^{2})$ (checked).

\emph{(ii)} For a chiral field the vacuum-subtracted null energy in the parameter $u$ of a state that is the vacuum in the parameter $v$ is $-\tfrac{c}{24\pi}\{v, u\}$, with $c = 1$ for a complex chiral fermion; this is the coefficient of the linear remainder in (ii) under point splitting (cited from memory: Davies and Fulling 1977, the moving mirror; the same law for every two-dimensional conformal field). With $v = v_{0} - 2s$ and $u'(s) = -2s/(s - m)$, $\{v, u\} = -\{u, s\}/u'(s)^{2}$, and $\{u, s\} = m(4s - 3m)/(2s^{2}(s - m)^{2})$, so $\{v, u\} = -m(4s - 3m)/(8s^{4})$. The check obtains $u''$ and $u'''$ as exact Taylor coefficients of the rational function $u'$ at twelve sample $(m, s)$ and compares. At $s = m$ the closed form is $-1/(8m^{2}) = -\kappa^{2}/2$; as $u \to \infty$, $s/m - 1 \sim C'e^{-\kappa u}$, and the deviation is $O(s - m)$ (checked at $s - m = m/10, m/1000$). So the late flux is $\kappa^{2}/48\pi$. A complex chiral fermion at temperature $T$ carries $2\int_{0}^{\infty}\varpi(1 + e^{\varpi/T})^{-1}d\varpi/2\pi = \pi T^{2}/12$ (the Fermi integral $\pi^{2}/12$, cited); at $T = T_{H}$ this is $\kappa^{2}/48\pi$. For the two-point function: with $x = e^{\kappa u/2}$, $U = -1/(\kappa x^{2})$, $U' = x^{-2}$, and $(U_{1}'U_{2}')^{1/2}/(U_{1} - U_{2}) = \kappa/(x_{1}/x_{2} - x_{2}/x_{1}) = \tfrac{\kappa}{2}\sinh(\tfrac{\kappa}{2}(u_{1} - u_{2}))^{-1}$ exactly; continuation by $-i\beta$, $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, sends $x_{1} \mapsto -x_{1}$ and the kernel to minus itself, with no pole on the strip, the fermionic KMS boundary value. By Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} this quasi-free state is the continuum I-state for the Killing translation at $\beta$, and it is the unique $\beta$-KMS state by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness}. Equivalently, the half-line algebra $U < 0$ of the null vacuum carries the translations $U \mapsto U + a$, $a \ge 0$, as a half-sided inclusion with positive generator, and the abstract theorem of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses} makes its modular group the dilations, which by (i) are the Killing translations at rate $\kappa$. The remainder: at Killing shift $t$ the kernel in $u$ is $e^{-\kappa t}$ times the $U$-kernel at points scaled by $\mu = e^{-\kappa t}$; the vacuum part is exactly scale invariant and the remainder contributes $\mu R(\mu\lambda_{1}, \mu\lambda_{2}) = O(\mu^{2})$ (checked at $\mu = 1/10, 1/100$).

\emph{(iii)} The transformation law gives $F_{u} = U_{u}^{2}F_{U} - \tfrac{1}{24\pi}\{U, u\}$, and for $U = -e^{-\kappa u}/\kappa$, $\{U, u\} = -\kappa^{2}/2$ ($(\log U')' = -\kappa$), $U_{u} = -\kappa U$. A state of the outgoing modes that is KMS for the Killing translations at late times at temperature $\theta T_{H}$ has late flux $\tfrac{\pi}{12}\theta^{2}T_{H}^{2}$ per complex chiral field (the Fermi integral above). A late flux $\tfrac{\pi}{12}\theta^{2}T_{H}^{2} = \theta^{2}\kappa^{2}/48\pi$ therefore needs $F_{U} = (\theta^{2} - 1)/(48\pi U^{2})$ to leading order, bounded as $U \to 0^{-}$ only at $\theta = 1$; in Schwarzian units ($F = -S/24\pi$) the check verifies the closure of the chain rule and the dichotomy at four $\theta$, two $\kappa$, three $U$. The Boulware state, the vacuum for $u$, has $u = -\kappa^{-1}\ln(-\kappa U)$, $(\log|u'|)' = -1/U$, and $\{u, U\} = 1/(2U^{2})$: its energy in the horizon-regular frame diverges at the future horizon. This is the Candelas / Christensen-Fulling regularity criterion on the series' carrier. The same formula, with $\theta = 1/c$, is the flux of a state that is stationary for a boost at period $2\pi c$ near the edge of a horizon generator (filed alongside, synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit); the late value $\kappa^{2}/48\pi$ is the Robinson-Wilczek anomaly flux (cited from memory).

\emph{(Remark, from the result filed alongside, synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet.)} In the collapse field the future horizon is, inside the shell, the outgoing light cone of a point of the centre, so its generators begin there; an ingoing radial ray ends at $r = 0$ at finite affine parameter. On $L^{2}((0, \infty))$ the solutions of $i f' = \pm i f$ are $e^{\lambda}$ and $e^{-\lambda}$, of which only $e^{-\lambda}$ is square integrable: deficiency indices $(1, 0)$, so $i\,d/d\lambda$ has no self-adjoint extension and generates no unitary translation group (von Neumann; cited). An exact ground-state condition of the form of (N$_{+}$) has nothing to be a ground state for, and only the short-distance form survives. Combining (i), (ii) and (iii): the collapse realises the short-distance class, and among states KMS for the Killing translations at late times finite null energy across the future horizon holds only at $T = T_{H}$; bounded $F_{U}$ is necessary for the class and not sufficient, so (iii) does not characterise the class. What is not shown: the four-dimensional statement with greybody factors and angular modes (Fredenhagen and Haag 1990, cited from memory, not imported), and other collapse geometries (argued: any collapse in which the ray tracing is $C^{3}$ with nonzero derivative at the horizon ray gives the same limit, since only $\{U, v\}$ bounded is used).
