synthesis.imported-null-plane-modular-ha.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a null plane of Minkowski space, with affine parameter $u$ along its generators and transverse coordinates $y \in \R^{2}$, let $\omega$ be the vacuum of a free quantum field, and for $u_{0} \in \R$ let $\mathcal{A}(u_{0})$ be the algebra of the field restricted to the half $\{u > u_{0}\}$ of $\mathcal{N}$ (the horizon algebra of Wall). Write
\[
K(u_{0}) \;=\; \int d^{2}y\int_{u_{0}}^{\infty}(u - u_{0})\,T_{uu}(u, y)\,du
\]
for the boost energy on the generators beyond the cut $u = u_{0}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Null-plane modular Hamiltonian.)} The restriction of $\omega$ to $\mathcal{A}(u_{0})$ is KMS at temperature $1/2\pi$ for the null dilations about $u_{0}$ generated by $K(u_{0})$: its modular Hamiltonian is $2\pi K(u_{0})$, local on $\mathcal{N}$ and a sum over the generators with no cross terms. For a cut $u = \gamma(y)$ the same holds with $u_{0}$ replaced by $\gamma(y)$ under the transverse integral. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Wall2011}, Sec. 2.4, eqs. (28) to (31), from Sewell's form of the Bisognano-Wichmann theorem with positivity of the null translations in place of the spectrum condition, the hypotheses verified explicitly for the free scalar (Sec. 3) and stated for free fields of spin $\tfrac12$, $1$ and $2$ (Sec. 4); \cite{CasiniTesteTorroba2017}, eqs. (1.5), (3.6), which record it as proved for free fields by \cite{Wall2011} and derive it for conformal field theories; \cite{FLPW2016} for the first-order deformation of a planar cut.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Araki's relative entropy.)} For normal states $\rho$, $\sigma$ of a von Neumann algebra the relative entropy $S(\rho\,\|\,\sigma) \in [0, \infty]$ is defined, vanishes only for $\rho = \sigma$, and does not increase under restriction to a subalgebra; for density matrices it is $\Tr\rho(\ln\rho - \ln\sigma)$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Araki1975}; \cite{Wall2011}, Sec. 2.5, eq. (38) and its monotonicity.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(First law for entropy differences.)} Let $\sigma$ be a faithful normal state of a von Neumann algebra with modular Hamiltonian $H_{\sigma}$ (its modular operator is $\Delta_{\sigma} = e^{-H_{\sigma}}$). For a normal state $\rho$ with $S(\rho\,\|\,\sigma) < \infty$ and finite $\Delta\langle H_{\sigma}\rangle = \rho(H_{\sigma}) - \sigma(H_{\sigma})$, the entropy difference
\[
\Delta S \;:=\; \Delta\langle H_{\sigma}\rangle - S(\rho\,\|\,\sigma)
\]
is the von Neumann entropy difference whenever both entropies are finite (for density matrices, $S(\rho\,\|\,\sigma) = \Delta\langle H_{\sigma}\rangle - \Delta S$ with $H_{\sigma} = -\ln\sigma$), and on a type III algebra, where the entropies themselves are infinite, $\Delta S$ is defined in this way. Hence $\Delta S \le \Delta\langle H_{\sigma}\rangle$, with equality only for $\rho = \sigma$, and along a family $\rho_{\epsilon}$ with $\rho_{0} = \sigma$ on which $S(\rho_{\epsilon}\,\|\,\sigma)$ is differentiable, $\Delta S = \Delta\langle H_{\sigma}\rangle$ at first order in $\epsilon$: the first law of entanglement. For the vacuum on $\mathcal{A}(u_{0})$, by (i), $H_{\omega} = 2\pi K(u_{0})$ and $\Delta S = 2\pi\,\Delta\langle K\rangle - S(\rho\,\|\,\omega)$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{CasiniTesteTorroba2017}, eqs. (1.1) to (1.3); \cite{Wall2011}, Sec. 2.5.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.imported-null-plane-modular-ha.technical: These are known results of quantum field theory on a null plane. For a free field in its vacuum, the algebra of the field on the part of a null plane beyond a cut is thermal at temperature $1/2\pi$ for the dilations of the light rays about the cut, so its modular Hamiltonian is $2\pi$ times the boost energy $\int(u - u_{0})T_{uu}$ on the generators, ray by ray. Wall proved this from axioms of the horizon algebra, via Sewell's form of the Bisognano-Wichmann theorem with the positivity of null translations in place of the spectrum condition, and verified the axioms for the free scalar, stating them for higher spins; Casini, Teste and Torroba record the formula as proved for free fields and derive it for conformal theories, and Faulkner, Leigh, Parrikar and Wang give its first-order form for deformed cuts. Araki's relative entropy, defined for any pair of normal states of a von Neumann algebra, is nonnegative, zero only for equal states and monotone under restriction. With the modular Hamiltonian it defines the entropy difference of an excited state, $\Delta S = 2\pi\Delta\langle K\rangle - S(\rho\,\|\,\omega)$, the only meaning entropy has on these type III algebras; at first order in a perturbation the relative entropy drops out and $\Delta S = 2\pi\Delta\langle K\rangle$, the first law of entanglement. In the store the KMS property of (i) for the chiral fermion on one generator, in the store's conventions, is the computation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii).
synthesis.imported-null-plane-modular-ha.lay: A quantum field in empty space, looked at only on the part of a light-like surface beyond some cut, looks thermal: it has a temperature with respect to stretching the light rays away from the cut. The quantity that generates this stretching is a weighted total of the field's energy flowing along the rays, and it plays the role that energy plays for an ordinary hot system. A standard measure of distance between quantum states, Araki's relative entropy, then gives the entropy change of any disturbance of the field, and for small disturbances the entropy change equals that energy change divided by the temperature. These are established results of quantum field theory, imported here as facts.

synthesis.imported-null-plane-restrictio.technical: Light-front quantisation sets up a free field on a null plane instead of on a spacelike surface. Leutwyler, Klauder and Streit showed in 1970 that on such a plane the fields of different masses become unitarily equivalent, unlike on spacelike surfaces, and that they generate an irreducible algebra. Wall used the same structure on horizons: restricted to a null surface, a free scalar's algebra and null energy do not see the mass apart from zero modes, and for the Dirac field only one half of the spinor is free data on the surface, the mass appearing in the constraint that fixes the other half. The vacuum restricted to the surface is the ground state of the null energy.
synthesis.imported-null-plane-restrictio.lay: A quantum field can be described by its values on a surface moving at the speed of light rather than on an instant of time. On such a surface, fields of particles of different masses look the same: the mass drops out of the description, apart from a few special modes. This is the standard light-front picture, taken from the literature.

synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesa.formal:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] (Powers-Stormer.) For operators $0 \le A, B \le 1$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{K}$, the gauge-invariant quasi-free states $\omega_{A}$, $\omega_{B}$ of the CAR algebra over $\mathcal{K}$ are factor states, and they are quasi-equivalent if and only if $A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}$ and $(1 - A)^{1/2} - (1 - B)^{1/2}$ are Hilbert-Schmidt; being factor states, they are disjoint whenever they are not quasi-equivalent.
\item[(b)] (Takesaki.) Let $\alpha$ be a one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms of a C*-algebra and let $\omega$, $\omega'$ be $(\alpha, \beta)$- and $(\alpha, \beta')$-KMS states with $\beta \neq \beta'$. If the von Neumann algebra generated in the GNS representation of one of them is of type III, then $\omega$ and $\omega'$ are disjoint.
\item[(c)] (The Powers-Stormer inequality.) For bounded positive operators $A$, $B$ on a Hilbert space, $\|A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}\|_{2}^{2} \le \|A - B\|_{1}$, with $\|\cdot\|_{2}$ the Hilbert-Schmidt norm and $\|\cdot\|_{1}$ the trace norm, either side possibly infinite; in particular, if $A - B$ is trace class then $A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}$ is Hilbert-Schmidt. In the form for a von Neumann algebra in standard form, for normal positive functionals $\varphi$, $\psi$ with representing vectors $\xi_{\varphi}$, $\xi_{\psi}$ in the natural cone, $\|\xi_{\varphi} - \xi_{\psi}\|^{2} \le \|\varphi - \psi\| \le \|\xi_{\varphi} - \xi_{\psi}\|\,\|\xi_{\varphi} + \xi_{\psi}\|$.
\item[(d)] (Purity; Araki.) For an operator $0 \le A \le 1$ on $\mathcal{K}$, the gauge-invariant quasi-free state $\omega_{A}$ of the CAR algebra over $\mathcal{K}$ is pure if and only if $A$ is a projection; it is then a Fock state.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Provenance:} \cite{PowersStormer1970, Takesaki1970}; clause (d) \cite{Araki1970}.
synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesa.technical: Results on when thermal states of an infinite system belong to different sectors. Powers and Størmer showed that the gauge-invariant quasi-free states of the fermion (CAR) algebra are factor states, and that two of them, with one-particle density operators $A$ and $B$, are quasi-equivalent exactly when $A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}$ and $(1 - A)^{1/2} - (1 - B)^{1/2}$ are Hilbert-Schmidt; otherwise they are disjoint. Araki's criterion says that such a state is pure exactly when its one-particle density operator is a projection. Takesaki showed that KMS states of the same dynamics at different temperatures are disjoint when the von Neumann algebra induced by one of them is of type III. The Powers-Størmer inequality bounds the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of the square roots of two positive operators by the trace distance of the operators, so that states close in norm have close square roots; for one-particle operators between $0$ and $1$ whose difference is trace class it gives the Hilbert-Schmidt condition on the square roots in (a).
synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesa.lay: For a system with infinitely many parts, two states can be so different that no measurement on finitely many parts relates them: they live in separate sectors. A further classical result says when such a state is pure, as sharp as quantum mechanics allows: exactly when every one-particle level is either fully occupied or empty. These two classical theorems say when that happens for fermions in thermal-like states, through a condition on how much their occupations differ in total (with an inequality that turns a small total difference into a small difference of square roots), and that equilibrium states at different temperatures are separated in this way in the typical infinite case. They are taken from the literature.

imported_from.citation: R. T. Powers and E. Stormer, Free states of the canonical anticommutation relations, Commun. Math. Phys. 16 (1970), 1--33.
M. Takesaki, Disjointness of the KMS-states of different temperatures, Commun. Math. Phys. 17 (1970), 33--41.
H. Araki, On quasifree states of CAR and Bogoliubov automorphisms, Publ. Res. Inst. Math. Sci. 6 (1970/71), 385--442.

synthesis.imported-propagation-of-hadama.formal: Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose derived metric is globally hyperbolic, and let $G(x, x')$ be the anticommutator (symmetrised two-point) function of a state of the free scalar field. If $G$ has the Hadamard singularity structure in an open neighbourhood of one Cauchy surface, it has the Hadamard singularity structure everywhere: Cauchy evolution preserves the Hadamard form. In particular, for a gravitational field whose field strength vanishes below some Cauchy surface, the "in" vacuum is of Hadamard form everywhere. A micro-local proof of the preservation, by propagation of singularities, is in Radzikowski's work (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}(a)). \emph{Provenance:} \cite{FullingSweenyWald1978}.
synthesis.imported-propagation-of-hadama.technical: Fulling, Sweeny and Wald showed that the short-distance requirement on physical states of a free scalar field, the Hadamard form of the two-point function, does not have to be imposed everywhere: if it holds near one instant of time (an open neighbourhood of a Cauchy surface), the field equation carries it to the whole spacetime. So a field that starts in the vacuum of a flat region, before a star collapses for example, stays Hadamard throughout. Radzikowski later gave the same result a micro-local proof. The Dirac-field analogue is not part of this Fact.
synthesis.imported-propagation-of-hadama.lay: If a quantum field looks like empty space up close at one moment, the laws of motion keep it that way at every later and earlier moment. Fulling, Sweeny and Wald proved this for the simplest fields in a gravitational field, so the requirement only has to be checked once, for instance before a black hole forms. This is taken from the literature.

imported_from.citation: S. A. Fulling, M. Sweeny and R. M. Wald, Singularity structure of the two-point function in quantum field theory in curved spacetime, Commun. Math. Phys. 63 (1978), 257--264.

synthesis.incidence-vacua-entanglement-l.technical: At each point of spacetime the series attaches a line of vacuum states, spanned by two distinguished ones in which the added ascent mode is entangled with spacetime's own boost qubit. That entanglement depends on the point only through the null coordinates: it is $s(u) = \ln(1 + u^{2}) - \frac{u^{2}}{1 + u^{2}}\ln u^{2}$ for one vacuum and $s(v)$ for the other. Because each marginal is a Gibbs state of one fixed number operator, it obeys the Gibbs identity $ds = \beta\,dn$, with $\beta = -\ln u^{2}$ the inverse temperature of the thermofield double, and it is maximal, one bit, exactly where $\beta = 0$: for the first vacuum on the future light cones, for the second on the past light cones, of the two events one unit of time before and after the origin. The partner mode changes with the spatial direction of the point. Those cones bound the causal diamond of the unit ball, and on the ball itself the entanglement grows from zero at the centre to its maximum on the bounding sphere. The unit of length and the time direction are fixed by the module's Hermitian structure, since boosts and dilations are not unitary for it. The picture echoes Jacobson's entanglement-equilibrium setting, a small ball in a chosen rest frame with its entanglement at the edge, but it has one size, one frame and no metric, so it cannot by itself yield field equations.
synthesis.incidence-vacua-entanglement-l.lay: The series attaches to every point of spacetime a small family of quantum states. In the two special members of that family, an extra quantum mode is entangled with a mode that belongs to spacetime itself, by an amount that depends on where the point is. Working this out exactly, the entanglement is largest, one full bit, precisely on the light cones of two events, one unit of time before and after the origin. Those light cones are the edges of the region a signal can cross inside a ball of unit size, and across that ball the entanglement grows from nothing at the centre to its maximum at the edge. This echoes a known derivation of Einstein's equations from entanglement in small balls, but here the ball has one fixed size and orientation and no geometry can bend it, so the echo does not yet give those equations.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} The two vectors span the incidence line $L_{x}$ of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.spacetime-manifold-vacuum-lines}, and by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.incidence-vacua-thermofield-real-capacity}(ii), in the occupation basis of the pair $(a, b)$, $\Omega_{x}/\|\Omega_{x}\| = (\ket{00} - u\ket{11})/\sqrt{1 + u^{2}}$ and $\Psi_{x}/\|\Psi_{x}\| = (\ket{01} - v\ket{10})/\sqrt{1 + v^{2}}$, each tensored with a definite spectator state, so the $(a, b)$ state is pure and the entanglement entropy of $a$ with $b$ is the von Neumann entropy of the ascent marginal, $\operatorname{diag}(1, w^{2})/(1 + w^{2})$ with $w = u$ or $w = v$ (the check rebuilds both vectors in a two-mode Jordan-Wigner representation and computes the marginal). With $n = w^{2}/(1 + w^{2})$ and $1 - n = 1/(1 + w^{2})$,
\[
s(w) = -n\ln n - (1 - n)\ln(1 - n) = \ln(1 + w^{2}) - n\ln w^{2} .
\]
For $w \neq 0$ the marginal is faithful and, by Theorem \claimref{state-selection.partner-purification-are-canonical}, the vector is the thermofield double of the Gibbs state with $e^{-\beta} = w^{2}$, modular Hamiltonian $\beta N$. Differentiating, $ds/dw = \frac{2w}{1 + w^{2}} - \frac{dn}{dw}\ln w^{2} - n\cdot\frac{2}{w}$, and the first and third terms cancel since $n\cdot 2/w = 2w/(1 + w^{2})$; so $ds/dw = -\ln w^{2}\,\frac{dn}{dw} = \beta\,\frac{dn}{dw}$, with $dn/dw = 2w/(1 + w^{2})^{2}$. This is the Gibbs identity $dS = \beta\,d\langle N\rangle$ for the one-parameter family of Gibbs states of the fixed operator $N$, and holds for any such family. As a function on the chart, $S_{\Omega}$ depends on $x$ only through $u$; the partner $b(x)$ is defined after the spatial rotation taking $x$ into the $(e_{1}, e_{2})$ plane, so it varies with the spatial direction of $x$. The sign of $ds/dw$ is the sign of $(1 - w^{2})\,w$ (as $\beta > 0$ exactly when $w^{2} < 1$, and $dn/dw$ has the sign of $w$), so the critical points are $w = 0$, where $n = 0$ and $s = 0$ by continuity ($n\ln w^{2} \to 0$), and $w = \pm 1$, where $n = \tfrac12$, $\beta = 0$ and $s = \ln 2$; $s$ increases with $|w|$ on $[0, 1]$ and decreases beyond. The check verifies the cancellation as an identity of rational functions and the signs at forty rational points.

\emph{(ii).} With $r \geq 0$, $u = t - r = 1$ is $r = t - 1$, $t \geq 1$, the future light cone of the event $(t, r) = (1, 0)$, that is of $e_{1}$; $u = -1$ is the future light cone of $-e_{1}$; $v = 1$ is the past light cone of $e_{1}$; $v = -1$ the past light cone of $-e_{1}$. So $\{|u| = 1\}\cup\{|v| = 1\}$ is the union of the light cones of $\pm e_{1}$, which is $\{(t - 1)^{2} = r^{2}\}\cup\{(t + 1)^{2} = r^{2}\}$ (checked on a grid of rational points). The causal diamond of the unit ball $\{t = 0, r \leq 1\}$ is $\{u \geq -1,\ v \leq 1\}$, with tips $\pm e_{1}$; its past null boundary $u = -1$ is where $\Omega_{x}$ is maximal, its future null boundary $v = 1$ where $\Psi_{x}$ is maximal. On $t = 0$, $u = -r$ and $v = r$, so both entropies are $s(r)$, and (i) gives the monotonicity.

\emph{(iii).} A boost of the $(t, r)$ plane by rapidity $\eta$ sends $(u, v) \mapsto (e^{-\eta}u, e^{\eta}v)$, and a dilation by $\lambda$ sends $(u, v) \mapsto (\lambda u, \lambda v)$; neither preserves $\{|u| = 1\}$ unless $\eta = 0$, $\lambda = 1$. In the Hermitian structure of the theorem, $g^{*} = g^{-1}$ on generators, so $e_{1}^{*} = e_{1}$, $e_{2}^{*} = -e_{2}$, $e_{\pm}^{*} = \pm e_{\pm}$; hence $(e_{1}e_{2})^{*} = e_{2}^{*}e_{1}^{*} = -e_{2}e_{1} = e_{1}e_{2}$ and likewise $(e_{+}e_{-})^{*} = e_{+}e_{-}$. Both square to one, so $\exp(\sigma g) = \cosh\sigma + g\sinh\sigma$ is self-adjoint and $\exp(\sigma g)^{*}\exp(\sigma g) = \exp(2\sigma g) \neq 1$ for $\sigma \neq 0$: neither group is unitary, as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.incidence-vacua-thermofield-real-capacity}(iv) records for dilations. The check verifies the adjoints, the squares, and the non-unitarity at a rational point of the hyperbola. So the maximal set, and with it the diamond's radius and rest frame, are fixed by the Hermitian structure; and by (i) the profile is a function of $u$ and $v$ alone.

synthesis.killing-horizon-value-factor-i.formal:
Work on flat spacetime with gravity the gauge fields $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), with the store's signature. Let $K$ be a Killing vector field of $(\hb, \Omega)$ in the sense of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(vi), with Killing bivector $F_{K} = \tfrac12 D \wedge K$, so that $(A\cdot D)K = A\cdot F_{K}$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Killing horizon of $K$: a null hypersurface on which $K$ is normal, $Q(K) = 0$, with surface gravity $\kappa \ne 0$, $(K\cdot D)K = \kappa K$. At a point of $\mathcal{H}$ off its bifurcation surface write $K = \phi\,k$ with $k$ the physical generator direction, let $m$ be the null vector with $\ip{k}{m} = 1$ in the plane of $k$ and the frame vector $\gamma_{0}$, and $\Lambda(a) = a\gamma_{0}/(2a_{0})$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1)), so that $\Lambda(m)$ projects onto the canonical light-ray component of a spinor field on the generator's null plane and $\Lambda(k) = 1 - \Lambda(m)$ onto the constrained one (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group}(i)).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Shape of the Killing bivector.)} For all physical vectors $X, Y$ tangent to $\mathcal{H}$, $Y\cdot(X\cdot F_{K}) = 0$. The bivectors with this property are exactly $\mathrm{span}\{k\wedge m,\ k\wedge a,\ k\wedge b\}$ ($a, b$ spanning the plane orthogonal to $k$ and $m$), and the surface-gravity condition fixes the first coefficient: on $\mathcal{H}$
\[
F_{K} = -\kappa\,k\wedge m + k\wedge\omega, \qquad \omega \perp k, m ,
\]
with $\omega$ the horizon's rotation one-form (zero for the static spherically symmetric class). No transverse rotation $a\wedge b$ and no $m\wedge a$, $m\wedge b$ occur. $F_{K}^{2} = \kappa^{2}$, so $F_{K}/\kappa$ is the unit boost bivector of a plane through $k$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The value factor.)} $F_{K}$ is parallel along the orbits of $K$, and relative to frames parallel along a generator, a field invariant under the Killing flow has values $\psi(t) = R_{t}\psi(0)$ with $R_{t} = \exp(-tF_{K}/2) = \cosh\tfrac{\kappa t}{2} - \sinh\tfrac{\kappa t}{2}\,F_{K}/\kappa$, the flow advancing the generator's affine parameter as $u \mapsto e^{\kappa t}u$ ($R_{t}kR_{t}^{\sim} = e^{\kappa t}k$). Since $\Lambda(m)k = 0$ and $\Lambda(m)(k\wedge m) = -\Lambda(m)$,
\[
\Lambda(m)F_{K} = \kappa\,\Lambda(m), \qquad \Lambda(m)R_{t} = e^{-\kappa t/2}\Lambda(m), \qquad kR_{t} = e^{-\kappa t/2}k ,
\]
for every rotation one-form $\omega$: on the canonical component the value factor is exactly the boost $B_{\kappa t}$ of the generator plane of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group}(ii), and the intrinsic canonical data $k\psi$ (which do not depend on the choice of $m$) scale the same way. The null-rotation part $k\wedge\omega$ maps the canonical range into the constrained one and never back.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Composition.)} With the transport $u \mapsto e^{\kappa t}u$ the value factor $e^{-\kappa t/2}$ preserves the canonical delta kernel, so the Killing flow on the generators' continuum is the unitary dilation group $\alpha_{\kappa t}$ of that theorem, for either sign of $\kappa$ (the eternal hole's horizon and the cosmological horizon), with no additional phase on the two chirality channels; the argued step of its clause (vi) holds as stated.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The static spherically symmetric class.)} For $\hb(a) = a - \beta\,(a\cdot e_{t})\,e_{r}$ with $\beta(r)^{2} = 1 - f(r)$ (Painleve-Gullstrand gauge), the rotation-gauge field along the Killing vector $K = \hb^{-1}(e_{t})$ is $\Omega(e_{t}) = -\beta\beta'\,\sigma_{r} = \tfrac{f'}{2}\sigma_{r}$, $\sigma_{r} = e_{r}e_{t}$, with no angular part, at every radius; at a horizon $f(r_{h}) = 0$ the $t$-line is a null generator with $k = e_{t} + \beta e_{r}$, $\sigma_{r} = k\wedge m$, $\omega = 0$ and $\kappa = f'(r_{h})/2$: $1/4M$ for Schwarzschild (the stored rate of Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate}), $-H$ for de Sitter, and $\tfrac27$, $-\tfrac{5}{28}$ for the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field with horizons at $r = 1, 2$ ($H^{2} = \tfrac17$, $M = \tfrac37$).
\end{enumerate}
So the boost time evolution of a Killing horizon's generators is one unitary dilation group in every field strength: its value factor is a theorem, not an identification, and rotation of the horizon does not change it on the canonical component.
synthesis.killing-horizon-value-factor-i.technical:
The stored result on the continuum of a horizon's generators found that the boost time evolution is one unitary dilation: the boost rotor acts on the canonical component of the spinor field with weight $e^{-\lambda/2}$ and the same rotor moves the points of the generator, and only the product preserves the anticommutator. At a Killing horizon in a gravitational field of nonzero field strength the transport of the affine parameter was known, but that the factor on values is the boost of the generator plane was argued.

This proves it. On a Killing horizon the covariant derivative of the Killing vector, the Killing bivector, is antisymmetric (the Killing property) and, restricted to the horizon, symmetric (it is the derivative of a normal field of a hypersurface); so it vanishes on pairs of tangent vectors, which leaves only three bivectors: the boost of the generator plane, with coefficient fixed by the surface gravity, and two null rotations about the generator, whose coefficients form the horizon's rotation one-form. Relative to frames parallel along the generator, the Killing flow turns the field's values by the rotor generated by this bivector. The canonical projector annihilates the generator from the right, so it sees the boost with weight $e^{-\kappa t/2}$ and does not see the null rotations at all. Combined with the stretching of the affine parameter this is again the unitary dilation. The Painleve-Gullstrand form of the static fields gives the rotation-gauge field along the Killing line as $f'/2$ times the radial boost, $\kappa$ at the horizon, computed exactly from Cartan's structure equations.
synthesis.killing-horizon-value-factor-i.lay: On a black hole's horizon, or the horizon of an expanding universe, the flow of time slides each light ray along itself and, at the same time, turns the values of matter fields riding on it. An earlier result showed that these two effects together make one well-behaved time evolution, provided the turning is a particular stretch, the one that matches the sliding; that was shown where gravity is absent and only argued at real horizons. Here it is shown at every horizon of this type, including those of spinning holes: the spin adds a twist, but the twist touches only the part of the field that is not free data on the light ray, so the free part evolves exactly as before.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Off the bifurcation surface write $\mathcal{H} = \{S = 0\}$ locally, with physical gradient $n = DS \ne 0$; since $K$ is normal to $\mathcal{H}$ and nonzero there, $K = \phi\,n$ on $\mathcal{H}$ with $\phi \ne 0$. For physical vectors $X, Y$ tangent to $\mathcal{H}$ (so $Y\cdot n = 0$, and the derivative of $K$ along $X$ only involves $K$ on $\mathcal{H}$),
\[
Y\cdot\bigl((X\cdot D)K\bigr) = \phi\,Y\cdot\bigl((X\cdot D)n\bigr) + (X\cdot D\phi)\,(Y\cdot n) = \phi\,Y\cdot\bigl((X\cdot D)DS\bigr),
\]
which is symmetric in $X, Y$ because $\Omega$ is torsion-free (the covariant Hessian of a scalar is symmetric). By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(vi) the same quantity is $Y\cdot(X\cdot F_{K})$, antisymmetric in $X, Y$. Hence $Y\cdot(X\cdot F_{K}) = 0$ for all tangent $X, Y$. The tangent space of $\mathcal{H}$ is $k^{\perp} = \mathrm{span}\{k, a, b\}$ (it contains $k$, which is null). Expand $F_{K}$ in the basis $k\wedge m$, $k\wedge a$, $k\wedge b$, $m\wedge a$, $m\wedge b$, $a\wedge b$: with $X\cdot(u\wedge v) = (X\cdot u)v - (X\cdot v)u$ one finds that $k\wedge m$, $k\wedge a$, $k\wedge b$ satisfy the condition (for $X \in k^{\perp}$, $X\cdot(k\wedge v) = -(X\cdot v)k$, a multiple of $k$, orthogonal to every $Y \in k^{\perp}$), while the pairs $(X, Y) = (a, b)$, $(b, a)$ and $(a, k)$, $(b, k)$ detect the coefficients of $a\wedge b$, $m\wedge a$ and $m\wedge b$ respectively ($k\cdot(a\cdot(m\wedge a)) = -Q(a)\,\ip{k}{m} \ne 0$, $b\cdot(a\cdot(a\wedge b)) = Q(a)Q(b) \ne 0$, and so on). So the solution space is exactly $\mathrm{span}\{k\wedge m, k\wedge a, k\wedge b\}$; the check confirms the rank $3$ of the nine-by-six constraint matrix and the independence of the three bivectors exactly, for $k = e_{0} + e_{1}$ and for the tilted null vector $k = 5e_{0} + 3e_{1} + 4e_{2}$, and that $a\wedge b$, $m\wedge a$, $m\wedge b$ violate the condition. Write $F_{K} = c\,k\wedge m + k\wedge\omega$ with $\omega \in \mathrm{span}\{a, b\}$. Since $k\cdot(k\wedge m) = Q(k)m - \ip{k}{m}k = -k$ and $k\cdot(k\wedge\omega) = Q(k)\omega - \ip{k}{\omega}k = 0$, the surface-gravity condition $(K\cdot D)K = K\cdot F_{K} = \kappa K$ with $K = \phi k$ gives $-c\phi k = \kappa\phi k$, so $c = -\kappa$. Finally $(k\wedge m)^{2} = \ip{k}{m}^{2} - Q(k)Q(m) = 1$; with $k\wedge m = km - 1$ one has $(k\wedge m)k\omega = k\omega$ and $k\omega(k\wedge m) = -k\omega$ (since $k\omega k = -kk\omega = 0$), so the two anticommute; and $(k\omega)^{2} = -kk\omega\omega = 0$. Hence $F_{K}^{2} = \kappa^{2}$. All identities are checked exactly for $\kappa = \tfrac14, -\tfrac27, 3$, two rotation one-forms and both null frames.

\emph{(ii)} Choose near the generator a frame $\{d_{a}\}$ dragged by the Killing flow, $[K, d_{a}] = 0$; it stays orthonormal since $K$ is Killing. For a dragged vector field $A$, torsion-freeness gives $(K\cdot D)A = (A\cdot D)K = A\cdot F_{K} = -F_{K}\times A$, and the components of $F_{K}$ in the dragged frame are constant along the orbit (the Killing flow preserves $D\wedge K$). A vector $P$ parallel along the orbit, $(K\cdot D)P = 0$, has dragged components obeying $\dot P = F_{K}\times P$, so $P(t) = S_{t}P(0)S_{t}^{\sim}$ with $S_{t} = \exp(tF_{K}/2)$: parallel frames are the dragged frames turned by $S_{t}$, and since $S_{t}$ commutes with $F_{K}$ the components of $F_{K}$ are constant in the parallel frame as well ($F_{K}$ is parallel along the orbit). A spinor field invariant under the flow has constant dragged components; relative to the parallel spin frame (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii), $dU/dt = -\tfrac12\Omega U$) its values are $\psi(t) = S_{t}^{\sim}\psi(0) = R_{t}\psi(0)$, $R_{t} = \exp(-tF_{K}/2)$. As $F_{K}^{2} = \kappa^{2}$, $R_{t} = \cosh\tfrac{\kappa t}{2} - \sinh\tfrac{\kappa t}{2}F_{K}/\kappa$, and $R_{t}R_{s} = R_{t+s}$, $R_{t}R_{t}^{\sim} = 1$. With $\Lambda(a) = a\gamma_{0}/(2a_{0})$ of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1), writing $\gamma_{0} = \alpha k + \beta m$ (it lies in the plane of $k$ and $m$), $\Lambda(m)k = m\gamma_{0}k/(2m_{0}) = (\alpha\,mkk + \beta\,mmk)/(2m_{0}) = 0$; with $k\wedge m = km - 1$ this gives $\Lambda(m)(k\wedge m) = -\Lambda(m)$, $\Lambda(m)k\omega = 0$, hence $\Lambda(m)F_{K} = \kappa\Lambda(m)$ and $\Lambda(m)R_{t} = (\cosh\tfrac{\kappa t}{2} - \sinh\tfrac{\kappa t}{2})\Lambda(m) = e^{-\kappa t/2}\Lambda(m)$. Likewise $kF_{K} = -\kappa k(km - 1) + kk\omega = \kappa k$ and $kR_{t} = e^{-\kappa t/2}k$; a null rotation $1 + \tfrac12 ks$ about $k$ (an element of the abelian group of null rotations fixing $k$, Proposition \claimref{transport.group-null-rotations}; it changes $m$) leaves $k$ fixed from the left, so the data $k\psi$ do not depend on the choice of $m$. On the vectors, $R_{t}kR_{t}^{\sim} = e^{\kappa t}k$: relative to parallel frames the invariant vector $K$ grows as $e^{\kappa t}$, which is the statement $K = \kappa u\,k_{\mathrm{aff}}$ with $u \mapsto e^{\kappa t}u$ of the boost $\beta_{t}$ of the setup of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}. The null-rotation part maps the canonical range into the constrained one: $\Lambda(m)$ is a left eigen-element of $F_{K}$ ($\Lambda(m)F_{K} = \kappa\Lambda(m)$), so the canonical component of $R_{t}\psi$ is $e^{-\kappa t/2}\Lambda(m)\psi$ whatever $\Lambda(k)\psi$ is, while $F_{K}\Lambda(m) \ne \kappa\Lambda(m)$ when $\omega \ne 0$. A transverse rotation $\exp(\theta\,a\wedge b/2)$ would commute with $\Lambda(m)$ without being a scalar on its range (a phase on the two chirality channels, checked as a control); (i) excludes it. The check verifies all of this exactly at $e^{\kappa t/2} = \tfrac32, \tfrac25, \tfrac73$, for boosts composed with null rotations in either order, and on the closed form.

\emph{(iii)} Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group}(ii): a value factor $e^{-\kappa t/2}$ rescales the canonical kernel by $e^{-\kappa t}$, and the transport $u \mapsto e^{\kappa t}u$ rescales the delta kernel by $e^{\kappa t}$, so the composite preserves it and is the dilation $D_{\kappa t}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.affine-cell-boost-spreads-without-scrambling}; for $\kappa < 0$ (the cosmological orientation, $u \mapsto e^{-|\kappa|t}u$) the same holds with $t \mapsto -t$. The check verifies the kernel identity on affine cells at three rapidities, with each factor alone failing. Since (ii) shows the value factor is exactly the boost $B_{\kappa t}$ on $\Lambda(m)$, with no phase, the identification argued in that theorem's (vi) is derived.

\emph{(iv)} For $\hb(a) = a - \beta(a\cdot e_{t})e_{r}$ the derived metric (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}(d)) has the orthonormal coframe $\theta^{0} = dt$, $\theta^{1} = dr + \beta\,dt$, $\theta^{2} = r\,d\vartheta$, $\theta^{3} = r\sin\vartheta\,d\varphi$, with $Q(\beta) = 1 - f$. Its torsion-free metric connection, the rotation-gauge field read as connection forms (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii)), is $\omega^{1}{}_{0} = -\beta'\theta^{1}$, $\omega^{2}{}_{0} = -(\beta/r)\theta^{2}$, $\omega^{3}{}_{0} = -(\beta/r)\theta^{3}$, $\omega^{2}{}_{1} = \theta^{2}/r$, $\omega^{3}{}_{1} = \theta^{3}/r$, $\omega^{3}{}_{2} = (\cot\vartheta/r)\theta^{3}$: by hand from $d\theta^{1} = \beta'\theta^{1}\wedge\theta^{0}$, $d\theta^{2} = (\theta^{1} - \beta\theta^{0})\wedge\theta^{2}/r$, $d\theta^{3} = (\theta^{1} - \beta\theta^{0})\wedge\theta^{3}/r + (\cot\vartheta/r)\theta^{2}\wedge\theta^{3}$, and confirmed in the check by Cartan's first structure equation $d\theta^{a} = -\omega^{a}{}_{b}\wedge\theta^{b}$ and metric compatibility at three sample points with independent rational $\beta, \beta', r, \cot\vartheta$ (a connection with a perturbed radial coefficient fails). Contracting with $K = \partial_{t} = E_{0} + \beta E_{1}$ kills every form except $\omega^{1}{}_{0}$, which gives $-\beta\beta' = f'/2$: $\Omega(e_{t}) = \tfrac{f'}{2}\sigma_{r}$ with no angular part, at every radius, as Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate} found for Schwarzschild. The frame is $t$-independent, so it is dragged by $K$ and $\Omega(e_{t}) = -F_{K}$ by (ii). At a horizon, $f = 0$ and $Q(\beta) = 1$; the radial null rays have $dr/dt = \pm1 - \beta$, so for $\beta = 1$ the $t$-line is the outgoing generator, $K = e_{t} + e_{r} = k$ is null, $m = \tfrac12(e_{t} - e_{r})$, $k\wedge m = e_{r}e_{t} = \sigma_{r}$, and $(K\cdot D)K = \Omega(e_{t})\times K = \tfrac{f'}{2}K$, so $\kappa = f'(r_{h})/2$ and $\omega = 0$. Instances checked exactly: Schwarzschild $\beta = \sqrt{2M/r}$, $\beta(2M) = 1$, $\beta'(2M) = -1/4M$, $\kappa = 1/4M$ for $M = 1, \tfrac32, \tfrac17$; de Sitter $\beta = Hr$, $\kappa = -H$ at $r = 1/H$ for $H = 1, \tfrac23$; Schwarzschild-de Sitter $f = 1 - 2M/r - H^{2}r^{2}$ with $H^{2} = \tfrac17$, $M = \tfrac37$, whose horizons are $r = 1$ and $r = 2$ ($f$ vanishes there exactly), with $\beta' = -f'/2$ at $\beta = 1$ and $\kappa = \tfrac27$, $-\tfrac{5}{28}$. Rotating horizons are covered by (i) to (iii) without a gauge computation (the same block-triangular mechanism applies to any null rotation about the generator, whose canonical block is the identity): their Killing bivector has $\omega \ne 0$ off the bifurcation surface, which (ii) shows does not reach the canonical component.

Scope: the statement is local on the horizon off the bifurcation surface (where $K = 0$ and the generator parameter degenerates; there $F_{K}$ is $-\kappa$ times the binormal). It assumes a Killing horizon with $\kappa \ne 0$ and excludes degenerate (extremal) horizons; it says nothing about horizons without a Killing field (a collapsing hole's horizon), for which the stored local-horizon results apply instead.

synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gi.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a generator of a horizon, with a regular parameter $u$ and the continuum mode space $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, let $\omega$ be a gauge-invariant quasi-free state with two-point kernel $W_{\omega}(u, v) = \omega(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u))$, $\omega_{0}$ the null vacuum with $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}\otimes\id_{K}$ (the state that (N$_{+}$) selects, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)), and $R = W_{\omega} - W_{0}$. For an interval $J$ say that $\omega$ is \emph{locally normal to $\omega_{0}$ on $J$} if the restrictions of $\omega$ and $\omega_{0}$ to $\CAR(L^{2}(J)\otimes K)$ are quasi-equivalent, and that $\omega$ satisfies the \emph{local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on $J$} if $R$ restricted to $J \times J$ is a square-integrable kernel (in each $K$-component). Scaling limits and the local form of (N$_{+}$) are as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The scaling preserves local Hilbert-Schmidt norms; proved.)} For the scaling about $u_{0}$ with weight $p$ per leg, $(S_{\lambda}R)(x, y) = \lambda^{2p}R(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda y)$, and any interval $I$, $\|S_{\lambda}R\|^{2}_{L^{2}(I \times I)} = \lambda^{4p - 2}\|R\|^{2}_{L^{2}((u_{0} + \lambda I)^{2})}$. The norm is carried over unchanged exactly for $p = \tfrac12$, the weight of the boost and of the anticommutator.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Local normality gives the local form; proved, given Powers-Stormer.)} Local normality to $\omega_{0}$ on $J$ implies the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on $J$. If the condition holds on an interval $J$ containing $u_{0}$, then the scaled kernels $\lambda W_{\omega}(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda y)$ converge to $W_{0}$ in Hilbert-Schmidt norm on every bounded interval, so every $n$-point function converges: the scaling limit of $\omega$ at $u_{0}$ exists and is $\omega_{0}$, that is, $\omega$ is locally the null vacuum at $u_{0}$. No bound on $R$ near the point and no reference to the field strength enters.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Parametrisation independence; proved.)} For a regular reparametrisation $f$ ($C^{3}$, $f' > 0$) the vacuum of the parameter $f$ differs from $\omega_{0}$ by a kernel continuous across the diagonal (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet}(iii)), hence square integrable on bounded intervals; so the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition relative to the vacuum of any regular parameter is one condition, and (ii) holds in the affine parameter of a generator whatever the field strength. Example (exact): $f(u) = u + \tfrac23 u^{3} + \tfrac15 u^{5}$, $f' = (1 + u^{2})^{2}$, gives the difference $(u - v)\big(\tfrac13 - \tfrac15(u^{2} + 3uv + v^{2})\big)/Q(u, v)$ with $Q = (f(u) - f(v))/(u - v) > 0$, leading term $S_{f}(0)(u - v)/12$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Stationarity plus local normality at the edge is (N$_{+}$); proved.)} Let the horizon be in the scope of (N$_{+}$), $u$ the affine parameter with the edge at $u = 0$, and $\omega$ stationary for the boost, which acts as the weight-$\tfrac12$ dilation about the edge (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}(i)). If $\omega$ satisfies the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on an interval containing the edge, in particular if it is locally normal to $\omega_{0}$ there, then $\omega = \omega_{0}$: it satisfies (N$_{+}$), and its affine null translations are positive. This strengthens (ii) of that theorem, where $R$ is assumed bounded near $(0, 0)$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Local disjointness of the thermal products; proved.)} A kernel homogeneous of degree $-1$ and nonzero on a set of positive measure is not square integrable on any neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$: its integral over each dyadic shell is the same positive number. Hence every stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free state other than $\omega_{0}$, in particular each product $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ of half-generator KMS states at rapidity period $2\pi c$, $c \in (0, \infty]$, including $c = 1$ where both halves are the I-state at $2\pi$, fails the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on every interval containing the edge, and by Powers-Stormer it is disjoint from $\omega_{0}$ on the algebra of every such interval. For the cross-edge block, common to all $c$, the shell value is $\ln\tfrac98$ on every square $[s, 2s]^{2}$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} Within the stationary class, (N$_{+}$) is equivalent to local normality to the null vacuum at the bifurcation surface, an operator-algebraic condition with no temperature in it and no chart beyond a regular parameter of the generator through its edge point (by (iii) the vacuum of any regular parameter gives the same local Hilbert-Schmidt condition). On the eternal hole this gives item (ii) of the positivity problem, the positivity of the affine null translations, from stationarity plus local normality at the bifurcation surface, where the half-generators of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart do not reach. At any point of a local Rindler horizon in a gravitational field of nonvanishing field strength, (ii) and (iii) give the local form of (N$_{+}$) from local normality at that point, in place of the null-surface form of a Hadamard condition. The condition is the analogue, for the CAR algebra of an interval of one generator relative to $\omega_{0}$, of the local normality principle of algebraic quantum field theory, which asks physical states to lie locally in the vacuum folium of the algebras of spacetime regions (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haag-local-normality}(a)); it is not a theorem of the series, and (N$_{+}$) remains the premise, with this condition its equivalent form within stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free states. The scaling-limit route to the horizon temperature goes back to Haag, Narnhofer and Stein (1984; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haag-local-normality}(b)). Without stationarity the local condition does not give (N$_{+}$) (argued): a state KMS for the affine translations at any temperature has a remainder bounded on bounded sets, so it satisfies the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition and, by (ii), has the null vacuum as scaling limit at every point, and it is not a ground state (that such a state is also locally normal is known for free fields, cited from memory, and not derived here). Transport-absent.
synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gi.technical:
On a horizon generator the boost is the dilation about the edge with weight one half, and that weight is exactly the one for which rescaling a two-point kernel onto a shrinking neighbourhood preserves its Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Two consequences follow, for gauge-invariant quasi-free states. A state whose kernel differs from the null vacuum's by a square-integrable kernel near a point has the null vacuum as its scaling limit there, since the scaled difference has the norm of the original on a shrinking set, which tends to zero. And a stationary state, being its own scaling limit at the edge, with a square-integrable difference near the edge has difference zero, so it is the null vacuum of (N$_{+}$).

By the Powers-Stormer criterion, quasi-equivalence of quasi-free fermion states on the algebra of an interval implies the square-integrable difference. So the condition is local normality on the algebra of an interval of the generator, the analogue of the locality requirement of algebraic quantum field theory, stated without temperature and without reference to a chart beyond a regular parameter: a regular reparametrisation moves the vacuum by a bounded kernel, as an exact non-Moebius example shows, so the square-integrability condition does not depend on the parameter. Conversely, a nonzero kernel homogeneous of degree $-1$, which is what every stationary state other than the vacuum differs by, contributes the same positive amount on every dyadic shell around the edge and is not square integrable; so the stationary products of half-generator thermal states are locally disjoint from the vacuum at the edge, at every temperature, the right one included. The checks are exact: polynomial kernels integrated over rational rectangles, the finite-dimensional Powers-Stormer inequality, the rational arguments of the shell logarithms, and the reparametrisation identity on a rational grid.
synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gi.lay: A black hole's horizon is made of light rays, and the series' premise says that the quantum field on those rays is in its lowest-energy state for sliding along them. This result shows that, for a field that does not change in time, that premise is the same as a standard locality requirement of quantum field theory: close to the point where the horizon's light rays begin, the state must look like the vacuum in the strong sense that the two cannot be told apart by measurements in a small enough region. The reason is a scaling property: zooming in by the horizon's own time evolution keeps a measure of the difference from the vacuum exactly unchanged, so a time-independent state that differs from the vacuum at all differs equally at every scale and is distinguishable at the starting point. States that are thermal on each half of the light ray fail at that point, even at the Hawking temperature. The locality requirement is borrowed from the literature, not derived in the series.
flags: beyond one flat chart: on the eternal hole and de Sitter space the edge, where (iv) is posed, is not on the Painleve-Gullstrand or static chart; the condition is stated on the algebra of an interval of the generator through the edge point, with any regular parameter there

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Substitute $u = u_{0} + \lambda x$, $v = u_{0} + \lambda y$: $\int_{I}\int_{I}\lambda^{4p}|R(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda y)|^{2}\,dx\,dy = \lambda^{4p - 2}\int_{u_{0} + \lambda I}\int_{u_{0} + \lambda I}|R(u, v)|^{2}\,du\,dv$. The factor is $1$ for all $\lambda$ exactly when $p = \tfrac12$; this is the weight of the boost on a generator and the only weight preserving the anticommutator (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}(i)). The check confirms the identity with exact integrals of polynomial kernels over rational rectangles at $\lambda = t^{2}$ and $p = k/4$, equality for $k = 2$ and the factor $t^{2k}/\lambda^{2}$ otherwise, and that the boost rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$ dilates the generator about its edge.

\emph{(ii)} By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(a), applied to the CAR algebra over $L^{2}(J)\otimes K$ with the compressed symbols $A$, $B$ ($0 \le A, B \le 1$, kernels the restrictions of $W_{\omega}$ and $W_{0}$, up to the convention of which of $S$ and $1 - S$ carries the two-point function, which does not affect the differences), local normality on $J$ makes $A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}$ Hilbert-Schmidt; then $A - B = A^{1/2}(A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}) + (A^{1/2} - B^{1/2})B^{1/2}$ with $\|A^{1/2}\|, \|B^{1/2}\| \le 1$ gives $\|A - B\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le 2\|A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}$ (the identity and the inequality are checked exactly on rational contractions), so $R$ is square integrable on $J \times J$. Now $W_{0}$ is invariant under translations and under the weight-$\tfrac12$ dilations, so $\lambda W_{\omega}(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda y) - W_{0}(x, y) = (S_{\lambda}R)(x, y)$ with $p = \tfrac12$. For a bounded interval $I$ and $\lambda$ small, $u_{0} + \lambda I \subset J$, and by (i) $\|S_{\lambda}R\|_{L^{2}(I \times I)} = \|R\|_{L^{2}((u_{0} + \lambda I)^{2})}$, which tends to $0$ by dominated convergence, the sets shrinking to the point $(u_{0}, u_{0})$. Hilbert-Schmidt convergence implies operator-norm convergence of the compressed symbols, and the $n$-point functions of a gauge-invariant quasi-free state are determinants of matrix elements of its symbol, so they converge on test functions supported in $I$. Hence the scaling limit at $u_{0}$ exists and is $\omega_{0}$, in the sense of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}. For a bounded remainder the shrunk norm is $O(\lambda)$ (checked: $\le \lambda^{2}|I|^{2}\max|R|^{2}$ for the squared norm on polynomial samples), which is the case of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet}(iv).

\emph{(iii)} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet}(iii), the vacuum kernels of two regular parameters differ, at weight $\tfrac12$, by a kernel continuous across the diagonal, hence bounded and square integrable on bounded intervals, and the weight-$\tfrac12$ change of variables is unitary on $L^{2}$; so the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition relative to one regular vacuum is equivalent to it relative to any other. The exact example: with $f' = (1 + u^{2})^{2}$, $(1 + u^{2})(1 + v^{2}) - Q(u, v) = (u - v)^{2}\big(\tfrac13 - \tfrac15(u^{2} + 3uv + v^{2})\big)$, checked on a rational grid; the leading coefficient $\tfrac13$ is $S_{f}(0)/12$ with $S_{f}(0) = 4$ computed from the polynomial derivatives.

\emph{(iv)} Stationarity and the dilation form of the boost give $R(u, v) = sR(su, sv)$ for all $s > 0$. Let $R$ be square integrable on $(-a, a)^{2}$. By (i) with $u_{0} = 0$, $\|R\|_{L^{2}((-a, a)^{2})} = \|R\|_{L^{2}((-sa, sa)^{2})}$ for every $s \in (0, 1]$, and the right side tends to $0$ as $s \to 0$ by dominated convergence. So $R = 0$ almost everywhere on $(-a, a)^{2}$, and by the homogeneity, which maps any point into $(-a, a)^{2}$, everywhere. A gauge-invariant quasi-free state is fixed by its two-point function, so $\omega = \omega_{0}$, which satisfies (N$_{+}$) (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)); in its GNS representation the affine translations have nonnegative generator.

\emph{(v)} If $R$ is homogeneous of degree $-1$, $|R|^{2}$ is homogeneous of degree $-2$, and the substitution $(u, v) \mapsto (2u, 2v)$ maps the shell $\{2^{-k-1}a \le \max(|u|, |v|) < 2^{-k}a\}$ onto the next with the same integral of $|R|^{2}$; if $R$ is nonzero on a set of positive measure, some shell, hence every shell, has a positive integral, and the sum over shells diverges. For the cross-edge block $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v)^{-1}$, $u > 0 > v$, $w = -v$: $\int_{a}^{b}\int_{c}^{d}(u + w)^{-2}\,dw\,du = \ln\frac{(a + d)(b + c)}{(a + c)(b + d)}$, and on the squares $[s, 2s]^{2}$ the argument is $\tfrac98$ for every $s$ (checked exactly, with the multiplicativity of the arguments over adjacent rectangles, which is the additivity of the integral). The cross-edge block of every $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ is $0$, so its difference from $\omega_{0}$ there is minus this block, whatever $c$; on a half at $c = \tfrac12$, with $u = a^{2}$, $v = b^{2}$, the difference is $-\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(a - b)/((a + b)(a^{2} + b^{2}))$, homogeneous of degree $-1$ in $(u, v)$ and nonzero off the diagonal (checked). More generally, for any stationary $\omega \neq \omega_{0}$ the difference $R$ is homogeneous of degree $-1$ by stationarity and nonzero, so by (iv) it is not square integrable near the edge; by (ii) the restrictions to the algebra of any interval containing the edge are not quasi-equivalent, and by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(a) (gauge-invariant quasi-free states are factor states) they are disjoint.

\emph{Reading.} The equivalence within the stationary class is (iv) with the trivial converse ($\omega_{0}$ is locally normal to itself). That a state KMS at temperature $T$ for the affine translations has a remainder bounded on bounded sets follows from its kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\pi T/\sinh(\pi T(u - v + i0))$, whose difference from $W_{0}$ is analytic across the diagonal (argued; it is not in the check), so the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition holds at every point and (ii) applies; local normality of that state is not derived here. The equivalence is stated for the generator-algebra analogue of local normality; that the vacua of two regular parameters are locally quasi-equivalent, not only within a bounded kernel of each other, would need the implementability of the reparametrisation (known for the free chiral fermion, cited from memory) and is not used. The principle whose generator-algebra analogue is adopted, local normality of physical states with respect to the vacuum for the algebras of spacetime regions, and its antecedent, the Hawking temperature from a scaling-limit condition at the horizon, are Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haag-local-normality} (Haag; Haag, Narnhofer and Stein 1984); the transfer to the algebra of an interval of one generator is the analogue, not part of that Fact. Literature from memory: K. Fredenhagen and R. Haag, Commun. Math. Phys. 127 (1990) 273.

synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-gene.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a generator of a horizon, with a regular parameter $u$ and the continuum mode space $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, let $\omega$ be a gauge-invariant quasi-free state with the two orderings of its two-point kernel $W_{\omega}(u, v) = \omega(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u))$ and $\tilde W_{\omega}(u, v) = \omega(\psi(u)\psi^{*}(v)) = \delta(u - v)\otimes\id_{K} - W_{\omega}(u, v)$, let $\omega_{0}$ be the null vacuum, $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}\otimes\id_{K}$ (the state that (N$_{+}$) selects, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)), and $R = W_{\omega} - W_{0}$. For a distribution $D$ on $J \times J$, $J$ an open interval, write $\mathrm{WF}(D)$ for its wave-front set, and let $\Gamma_{\pm} = \{(u, u; \xi, -\xi) : u \in J,\ \pm\xi > 0\}$, with the sign convention in which $\mathrm{WF}(W_{0}) = \Gamma_{+}$. Say that $\omega$ satisfies the \emph{microlocal spectrum condition on $J$} (the generator analogue of the microlocal form of the Hadamard condition) if $\mathrm{WF}(W_{\omega}) \subset \Gamma_{+}$ and $\mathrm{WF}(\tilde W_{\omega}) \subset \Gamma_{-}$ on $J \times J$, in each $K$-component. It names no temperature, no period and no symmetry of the state. The local Hilbert-Schmidt condition, scaling limits and the local form of (N$_{+}$) are as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Equivalence; proved.)} $\omega$ satisfies the microlocal spectrum condition on $J$ if and only if $R$ is smooth on $J \times J$. The condition is the same in every smooth regular parameter.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Consequences; proved, a corollary of the stored theorem.)} If $\omega$ satisfies the condition on $J$, it satisfies the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on every closed bounded subinterval of $J$, so by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}(ii) its scaling limit at every point of $J$ is $\omega_{0}$: the local form of (N$_{+}$) holds at every point of $J$, with no stationarity and no temperature assumed. With that theorem's (iv): if the horizon is in the scope of (N$_{+}$), $J$ contains the edge and $\omega$ is stationary for the boost, then $\omega = \omega_{0}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Examples; computed exactly.)} (a) Every state KMS for the affine translations at inverse temperature $\beta$, $W_{\beta}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\beta}\sinh\!\big(\pi(u - v + i0)/\beta\big)^{-1}$, satisfies the condition on every interval: $R$ is real-analytic on the whole plane, with leading term $-\tfrac{i\pi}{12\beta^{2}}(u - v)$. (b) For $0 \le t < 1$ the states with occupation symbol $t\,\theta(p) + (1 - t)\,\theta(-p)$, gauge-invariant, quasi-free and invariant under the affine translations, have $R = -(1 - t)\tfrac{i}{\pi}\,\mathrm{PV}(u - v)^{-1}$ and fail the condition and the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition at every point. (c) The stationary half-thermal products $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit} satisfy the condition on every interval not containing the edge and fail it on every interval that contains it. (d) The state with occupation symbol $\theta(p) - \mathrm{sign}(p)\,c/(1 + |p|)$, $0 < c \le \tfrac12$, has a bounded, square-integrable remainder with a jump across the diagonal, $R(u, v) \to -\tfrac{ic}{2}\,\mathrm{sign}(u - v)$ as $u - v \to 0$; it satisfies the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition and the bounded-remainder condition and fails the microlocal spectrum condition at every point. So the microlocal condition is strictly stronger than both.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(No selection; proved, from (iii)(a).)} The microlocal spectrum condition, and with it the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition, holds at every point for every affine-KMS state with $\beta < \infty$, which is not a ground state; neither selects the state of (N$_{+}$) without a global datum, such as boost stationarity at the edge in (ii).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Note (the bulk link; added 1 November).} The restriction of bulk Hadamard states to the generator algebra, recorded in the technical level as not in the store, is now computed on the flat field for the Dirac field on every null plane, with the transverse labels as $K$ and no s-wave reduction: every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state restricts to a state satisfying the condition of (i) on every interval of every generator (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(iii)). Where the field strength is nonzero, the consequence (ii), the local form of (N$_{+}$) at each point, follows for such states by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}, (HS) (formerly a premise); the condition of (i) on intervals is not derived there. So the open premise that the series' states satisfy this condition reduces, for the use the store makes of it, to their being Hadamard plus (HS). Statement and proof unchanged.
synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-gene.technical: The Hadamard condition is the standard requirement on physical states of a quantum field in a gravitational background: at short distances every physical state looks like the vacuum. In its microlocal form it says that the singularities of the two-point function carry only positive frequency, a pointwise condition with no reference to any symmetry. This result poses the generator analogue of that condition on one generator of a horizon, for the two orderings of the continuum modes' two-point kernel, and proves the generator analogue of the statement that Hadamard states differ by smooth kernels: the condition holds exactly when the kernel differs from the null vacuum's by a smooth function. The proof is two lines: the difference inherits positive frequency from one ordering and negative frequency from the other, and a distribution singular in neither direction is smooth. So the condition gives the square-integrable remainder from which the store already derives the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point; for a state stationary under the boost the stored theorem then gives (N$_{+}$), which is the Kay-Wald mechanism on the generator algebra. Thermal states for the affine translations meet the condition at every point, so it cannot select the ground state by itself (the stored theorem states this as argued; here it is proved): a global datum is still needed. Translation-invariant mixtures of the vacuum and the anti-vacuum fail it everywhere, the stored half-thermal products fail it at the edge only, and a state whose remainder jumps across the diagonal shows that it is stronger than both square integrability and boundedness of the remainder. It is complementary to normality at the point at infinity of the closed generator: neither condition implies the other, and together they still do not give (N$_{+}$) without stationarity. What op.derive-loc-and-r-loc still needs (the series' states satisfy local normality at every point of the generators) would follow from this condition, which in turn would follow from the bulk Hadamard condition given a restriction of bulk Hadamard states to the generator algebra, which is not in the store (for the Dirac field it needs the s-wave reduction J3), and the propagation of the bulk condition from one Cauchy surface. (Added 1 November: on the flat field that restriction is now computed, for the Dirac field on every null plane with no s-wave reduction, and where the field strength is nonzero the local form at each point follows for Hadamard states by the scaling-limit theorem (HS), formerly a premise; so for that use the open premise reduces to the series' states being Hadamard.)
synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-gene.lay: Physicists usually require that any reasonable quantum state, looked at closely enough, resembles empty space. The precise version of this requirement says that the very fine-grained structure of the state carries only positive energy. This result writes a version of that requirement for the quantum modes running along a single light ray of a horizon and shows that it is the same as saying the state differs from the vacuum only by something smooth. From there the store's earlier results give the horizon temperature at every point, without assuming that anything is static. It does not single out the vacuum, though: a gas of modes at any temperature also passes, so to get the full premise one still needs the state to be static near the point where the two halves of the horizon meet. Whether the series' states obey the requirement is still an open assumption.

proofs.main:
\emph{Facts used about wave-front sets} (standard distribution theory; Hormander, The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators I, Ch. 8, cited from memory): $\mathrm{WF}(D_{1} + D_{2}) \subset \mathrm{WF}(D_{1}) \cup \mathrm{WF}(D_{2})$; $\mathrm{WF}(D)$ is empty over an open set exactly when $D$ is smooth there; the pullback by a diffeomorphism maps wave-front sets by the transposed derivative.

\emph{The vacuum's sets.} From $(x + i0)^{-1} = -i\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{ipx}\,dp$ one has $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{ip(u - v)}\,dp$ and $\tilde W_{0} = \delta - W_{0} = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{0}e^{ip(u - v)}\,dp$. Each is smooth off the diagonal, and on the diagonal its singular directions are $(\xi, \eta) = (p, -p)$ with $p$ of one sign only: $\mathrm{WF}(W_{0}) = \Gamma_{+}$ and $\mathrm{WF}(\tilde W_{0}) = \Gamma_{-}$ (sign convention fixed by the first). So $\omega_{0}$ satisfies the condition on every interval.

\emph{(i)} Suppose the condition holds on $J$. Then $R = W_{\omega} - W_{0}$ has $\mathrm{WF}(R) \subset \mathrm{WF}(W_{\omega}) \cup \mathrm{WF}(W_{0}) \subset \Gamma_{+}$. The anticommutator is the same for every state, $W + \tilde W = \delta\otimes\id_{K}$, so also $R = -(\tilde W_{\omega} - \tilde W_{0})$ and $\mathrm{WF}(R) \subset \Gamma_{-}$. As $\Gamma_{+} \cap \Gamma_{-} = \emptyset$, $\mathrm{WF}(R)$ is empty over $J \times J$ and $R$ is smooth there. Conversely, if $R$ is smooth then $\mathrm{WF}(W_{\omega}) = \mathrm{WF}(W_{0} + R) = \Gamma_{+}$ and $\mathrm{WF}(\tilde W_{\omega}) = \mathrm{WF}(\tilde W_{0} - R) = \Gamma_{-}$. This is the generator analogue of the bulk argument by which Hadamard states differ by smooth kernels (Radzikowski 1996 for the scalar field; for the Dirac field on both orderings, Hollands 2001, where the conditions on the two orderings are imposed separately and the smooth difference is stated: Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}). Parameter independence: a smooth regular reparametrisation $f$ ($f' > 0$) acts at weight $\tfrac12$ by $W \mapsto f'(u)^{1/2}f'(v)^{1/2}W(f(u), f(v))$; the smooth factor does not enlarge wave-front sets, and the pullback by $(u, v) \mapsto (f(u), f(v))$ maps $(u, u; \xi, -\xi)$ to $(u, u; f'(u)\xi, -f'(u)\xi)$, preserving the sign of $\xi$; so $\Gamma_{\pm}$ go to $\Gamma_{\pm}$ and the condition is the same in every smooth regular parameter (consistent with Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}(iii), where the vacua of two regular parameters differ by a continuous kernel).

\emph{(ii)} A smooth $R$ is bounded on every compact $I \times I \subset J \times J$, hence square integrable there: the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition holds on every closed bounded subinterval of $J$. The rest is a corollary of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}: by its (ii) the scaling limit at every point of $J$ exists and is $\omega_{0}$, which is the local form of (N$_{+}$) there; nothing in that step uses a symmetry of $\omega$ or a temperature. If $J$ contains the edge and $\omega$ is stationary for the boost (the weight-$\tfrac12$ dilation about the edge, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}(i)), its (iv) gives $\omega = \omega_{0}$, which satisfies (N$_{+}$) (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)). Nothing new is claimed for the stationary clause beyond the stronger hypothesis.

\emph{(iii)(a)} With $y = \pi x/\beta$, $x = u - v$, $\tfrac{2\beta}{i}(W_{\beta} - W_{0}) = \sinh(y)^{-1} - y^{-1} = y^{-1}(g(y^{2}) - 1)$, where $g$ is the inverse of the power series $\sinh(y)/y = \sum_{k}y^{2k}/(2k + 1)!$, which has constant term $1$; the $i0$ prescriptions of the two poles at $y = 0$ coincide and cancel. The check inverts the series exactly to order $y^{18}$ and confirms $g_{n} = 2(1 - 2^{2n - 1})B_{2n}/(2n)!$ with the Bernoulli numbers from their recurrence, $g_{0} = 1$, $g_{1} = -\tfrac16$, $g_{2} = \tfrac{7}{360}$; so the remainder is $y$ times a power series, with leading term $-\tfrac{y}{6}$, that is $R = -\tfrac{i\pi}{12\beta^{2}}x + O(x^{3})$. On the real line every Taylor coefficient of $\sinh(y)/y$ is positive, so $\sinh(y)/y \ge 1$ (checked on partial sums at rational points) and $\sinh(y)^{-1} - y^{-1}$ is real-analytic on all of $\R$; hence $R$ is smooth on the whole plane and, by (i), the condition holds on every interval. In symbols: the occupation $f = (1 + e^{-\beta p})^{-1}$ has $|f - \theta| \le e^{-\beta|p|}$ at both ends (checked at rational $q = e^{-\beta}$ and integer $p$), the translation-invariant form of the two-ordering condition: $f$ decays rapidly as $p \to -\infty$ and $1 - f$ as $p \to +\infty$.

\emph{(iii)(b)} The symbol $f_{t} = t\,\theta + (1 - t)(1 - \theta)$ lies in $[0, 1]$, so it defines a gauge-invariant quasi-free state, invariant under the translations. Its remainder symbol is $(1 - t)(1 - 2\theta) = -(1 - t)\,\mathrm{sign}(p)$, which does not decay at either end, and $W_{t} - W_{0} = (1 - t)(\delta - 2W_{0})$; since $2W_{0} = \tfrac{i}{\pi}\mathrm{PV}(x^{-1}) + \delta$, $R = -(1 - t)\tfrac{i}{\pi}\mathrm{PV}(x^{-1})$. For a translation-invariant kernel $k$ on $[0, L]^{2}$, $\|k\|^{2} = 2\int_{0}^{L}(L - x)|k(x)|^{2}\,dx$; for $k = x^{-1}$ restricted to $x > \varepsilon$ this exceeds $\tfrac{L}{2}\int_{\varepsilon}^{L/2}x^{-2}\,dx = \tfrac{L}{2\varepsilon} - 1$, unbounded as $\varepsilon \to 0$ (checked at $\varepsilon = L/2^{k + 1}$: the bound is $2^{k} - 1$). So the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition, and by (ii) the microlocal one, fail on every interval. For $t = \tfrac12$ this is the tracial state.

\emph{(iii)(c)} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit} the kernels of $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ differ from $W_{0}$ by a function analytic off the edge (exact example at $c = \tfrac12$ on a half: $-\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(a - b)/((a + b)(a^{2} + b^{2}))$ at $u = a^{2}$, $v = b^{2}$, a rational function with positive denominator for $a, b > 0$), and on the cross-edge block by $-\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v)^{-1}$, whose value at $(s, -s)$ is $-\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(2s)^{-1}$; both are homogeneous of degree $-1$ about the edge (checked), hence unbounded on every neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$ and not smooth there. By (i) the condition holds on intervals avoiding the edge and fails on intervals containing it. The check also confirms that the boost rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$ dilates the generator about its edge, which turns stationarity into this homogeneity.

\emph{(iii)(d)} The symbol $f = 1 - c/(1 + p)$ for $p > 0$ and $c/(1 + |p|)$ for $p < 0$ lies in $[0, 1]$ for $0 < c \le \tfrac12$. Its remainder symbol $r(p) = -\mathrm{sign}(p)\,c/(1 + |p|)$ is odd and square integrable ($\int r^{2} = 2c^{2}\int_{0}^{\infty}(1 + p)^{-2}dp = 2c^{2}$; the check bounds the integer partial sums and confirms the oddness), so the translation-invariant remainder kernel is square integrable and the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition holds on every bounded interval. By oddness, $R(x) = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\int e^{ipx}r(p)\,dp = -\tfrac{ic}{\pi}\int_{0}^{\infty}\tfrac{\sin(px)}{1 + p}\,dp$, and for $x > 0$ the substitution $s = px$ gives $\int_{0}^{\infty}\tfrac{\sin s}{x + s}\,ds$, which is bounded by $\int_{0}^{\pi}\tfrac{\sin s}{s}\,ds$ (the lobes alternate in sign with decreasing size) and tends to $\int_{0}^{\infty}\tfrac{\sin s}{s}\,ds = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$ as $x \to 0^{+}$. So $R$ is bounded and $R(x) \to -\tfrac{ic}{2}\,\mathrm{sign}(x)$ as $x \to 0$: a jump across the diagonal, so $R$ is not smooth (not even continuous) there, and by (i) the microlocal condition fails at every point although the remainder is bounded and square integrable. Equivalently, $|p\,r(p)| \ge c/2$ for $|p| \ge 1$ (checked), so $r$ is not rapidly decreasing.

\emph{(iv)} Immediate from (iii)(a) and (ii): the affine-KMS states are not ground states for $\beta < \infty$ (their symbol is not $\theta$), yet satisfy the condition, hence the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition, at every point. The Reading of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state} states the second half as argued; (iii)(a) proves it.

\emph{Reading (argued, not part of the statement).} What the outside results bring, and what they assume. Radzikowski's microlocal form of the Hadamard condition, and Hollands' version for the Dirac field on both orderings (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}), are the bulk conditions of which the condition here is the generator analogue. No theorem restricting a four-dimensional Hadamard state to the algebra of one null generator is in the store, and for a four-dimensional Dirac field the restriction to one null line is not defined without transverse smearing; the series reaches one chiral field per light ray only through the s-wave reduction J3 (Kay and Wald, Phys. Rep. 207 (1991) 49, analyse restrictions to a horizon, from memory). Verch's theorem (for the scalar field) and its Dirac analogue (D'Antoni and Hollands), Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-local-quasi-equivalence-of-hadamard-states}, make local quasi-equivalence of quasi-free Hadamard states a theorem in the bulk, the principle that Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haag-local-normality}(b) states; on a generator, a smooth remainder is trace class on bounded intervals, and with the Powers-Stormer inequality $\|A^{1/2} - B^{1/2}\|_{2}^{2} \le \|A - B\|_{1}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(c)) the condition here would give local normality itself, not only the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition. The bulk condition is propagated by the field equation from a neighbourhood of one Cauchy surface (Fulling, Sweeny and Wald 1978, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-propagation-of-hadamard-form}, for the scalar field; the Dirac analogue is not imported), so for a hole formed by collapse whose state is Hadamard before the collapse, and given a restriction theorem, the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point of every generator, the future horizon included, would follow from one initial condition rather than from a premise posed at every point. On the eternal hole the condition cannot select the state: by (iv) the global datum is still needed, which is the stationarity of the Kay-Wald uniqueness theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kay-wald-uniqueness-and-no-go}(a)). Kay and Wald also give a no-go result for the extended Schwarzschild-de Sitter field (no stationary Hadamard state; a gap in the Kay-Wald proofs was later filled by Kay and Lupo, App. B; Kerr is the case described as argued in Kay's review): Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kay-wald-uniqueness-and-no-go}(b), (c); with a positive cosmological constant the stationary-class route to (N$_{+}$) at a black-hole horizon then has no state to describe, and the stationarity-free local route is the one that applies there.

\emph{Relation to the condition at infinity (\claimref{synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state}).} The condition here is ultraviolet and posed at finite points; normality at the point at infinity of the closed generator is infrared. Neither implies the other: the affine-KMS states, and the vacua of parameters whose affine slopes differ at the two ends with a $C^{\infty}$ transition, satisfy the condition here on every bounded interval and fail the one at infinity; the rank-one excitation $P_{0} + |g\rangle\langle g|$ of the vacuum projection $P_{0}$, with $g$ a unit vector orthogonal to its range and not smooth, satisfies the one at infinity and fails this one; and with $g$ a Schwartz function it satisfies both and is not a ground state, so even together they do not give (N$_{+}$) without stationarity. The slope-jump states and the half-thermal products of (iii)(c) share one obstruction, a remainder homogeneous of degree $-1$, at infinity for the former and at the edge for the latter. Since the condition here holds in every smooth regular parameter, and the closed generator makes infinity a regular point with the spinor weight, the condition imposed on every arc of the closed generator is well posed and implies normality at infinity (argued). Imposed at every point of a local horizon, either condition would also fix the period that the Clausius relation on the action shell leaves free in matter-free regions (\claimref{synthesis.clausius-on-the-action-shell-ties-entropy-density-to-period}): the period-$2\pi c$ model there fails the condition here at the patch edge by (iii)(c). That would be a new premise, not a derivation. The result is transport-absent: it uses only the continuum mode space and the stored local-normality results.
