synthesis.modular-data-on-a-generator-fi.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On one horizon generator with affine parameter $u \in \R$, let $\mathfrak{h} = L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K$, $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ the continuum mode space (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}), $\mathfrak{A}(O)$ its subalgebra over $L^{2}(O)\otimes K$ for an interval or half-line $O$, $\tau_{t}(a(f)) = a(f(\cdot - t))$ the field translations, $P = i\,d/du$, and $\omega_{0}$ the null vacuum, the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with symbol $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$ (convention $\omega(a^{*}(f)a(g)) = \ip{g}{Ef}$), the unique gauge-invariant quasi-free state of (N$_{+}$) (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)). For a measurable $m : \R \to U(K)$ let $\alpha_{m}(a(f)) = a(mf)$, and let $r_{a}(u) = 2a - u$. $\Theta$ is the grading unitary, normalised by $\Theta\Omega = \Omega$; the vacuum's half-line conjugations act on the fields as $J_{a}\,a(f)\,J_{a} = \Theta\,a^{*}(c\,f\circ r_{a})$, $f$ supported in $(a, \infty)$, with a constant phase $c$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-modular-conjugation-of-the-chiral-fermi-field-is-the-twisted-reflection}(c); $c = i\eta$ in the notation $J_{a}\psi(f)J_{a} = \eta Z\psi^{*}(\rho_{a}f)Z^{*}$ with the Klein twist $Z$; $c = -i$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Net-level identity.)} For every $m$, the state $\omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}$ has the GNS triple $(\mathcal{H}_{0}, \pi_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}, \Omega_{0})$ and the same von Neumann algebra $\pi_{0}(\mathfrak{A}(O))''$ for every interval and half-line $O$ as $\omega_{0}$. Its modular operators and conjugations for every such algebra are the vacuum's, so every condition on the net $O \mapsto \pi(\mathfrak{A}(O))''$ and the vector holds for it exactly when it holds for $\omega_{0}$: the generator form of the Condition of Geometric Modular Action ($J_{a}$ maps the algebra of each $O \subset (a, \infty)$ onto the twisted algebra of $r_{a}O$, every cut $a$), geometric modular groups on the net, modular stability, twisted Haag duality, and the existence of a unitary group with positive generator implementing the net translations and fixing the vector.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Fermi seas.)} For $m(u) = e^{iu\kappa}$, $\kappa$ a constant Hermitian operator on $K$, $\omega_{\kappa} = \omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}$ is the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with symbol $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P - \kappa)$: pure, $\tau$-invariant, locally normal to $\omega_{0}$ on every bounded interval (the symbols differ there by $\pm$ a positive trace-class operator), and its two-point kernel differs from the vacuum's by a smooth kernel, so it satisfies the generator microlocal condition of \claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state} at every point. For $\kappa \neq 0$ it is not a ground state for $\tau$: the excitations at momenta between $0$ and an eigenvalue of $\kappa$ (holes for a positive eigenvalue, particles for a negative one) have negative energy, and the generator is unbounded below. Its charge density is $\tr\kappa/2\pi$ and its energy density $\tr\kappa^{2}/4\pi$. It is the ground state of the other lift $\alpha_{m}^{-1}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}$, $a(f) \mapsto a(e^{-it\kappa}f(\cdot - t))$, $\tau_{t}$ followed by the internal rotation $e^{-it\kappa}$, with one-particle generator $P - \kappa$. For $\kappa = k\,\id_{K}$, on the gauge-invariant subalgebra it is a ground state for $\tau$ (there $\alpha_{m}$ commutes with $\tau$ and the vacuum's positive implementer serves), distinct from $\omega_{0}$ by its charge density; with $K$ two-dimensional and $\kappa$ of eigenvalues $\pm k$ the charge density vanishes. Elementwise, its modular conjugations act as $J_{a}\,a(f)\,J_{a} = \Theta\,a^{*}(c\,e^{2i\kappa(a - u)}f\circ r_{a})$: a reflection with a position-dependent phase, constant only for $\kappa = 0$; so the elementwise action does see the lift.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The sign.)} The filled positive-energy sea $\bar\omega_{0}$, symbol $\chi_{(0,\infty)}(P)$, equals $\omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{R}$ for the reflection $R : u \mapsto -u$, and equals $x \mapsto \overline{\omega_{0}(\theta(x))}$ for the antilinear automorphism $\theta$ fixing every Majorana field $a(f) + a^{*}(f)$; $\theta$ commutes with $\tau$, the grading and the gauge group and maps each real local subalgebra onto itself. Its half-line modular conjugations act as the reflections about the cuts with the conjugate phase $\bar c = +i$, with the same half-line inclusions (the conjugation of the twisted complement algebra is $\Theta J$). The vacuum's $c = -i$ is fixed by natural-cone positivity in the companion field-level result \claimref{synthesis.geometric-modular-conjugations-on-a-generator-give-the-null-ground-state} (its Step 4, $\eta = -1$); the reflected cross-cut kernels $\mp i/(2\pi t)$ of the two states agree with it (argued, through the continuum form of (vi)). So net-level data do not see the sign, and the elementwise phase records it.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Independence.)} Let $G_{1}$ be the automorphisms of $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ mapping each $\mathfrak{A}(O)$ onto itself and commuting with the gauge group and grading, and $G_{2}$ the linear or antilinear automorphisms commuting with $\tau$, the gauge group and the grading and mapping each real local subalgebra onto itself. A property of states invariant under $G_{1}$ (under $G_{2}$) that $\omega_{0}$ has is shared by every $\omega_{\kappa}$ (by $\bar\omega_{0}$), and none of these is a ground state for $\tau$. So no principle invariant under $G_{1}$ or $G_{2}$ implies the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$); $\omega_{\kappa}$ is the ground state of the lift $\alpha_{m}^{-1}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}$. The two data these groups cannot see are: the lift of the affine translations to the fields (which of the automorphisms $\alpha_{m}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}^{-1}$, all mapping $\mathfrak{A}(O)$ onto $\mathfrak{A}(O + t)$, is the translation; for $m(u) = e^{iu\kappa}$ the lift $\alpha_{m}^{-1}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}$ is $\tau_{t}$ followed by $e^{-it\kappa}$, transport along the generator with a flat connection; parallel transport, the zero connection, gives $\tau$), and the orientation of the imaginary unit relative to the time orientation, which the series does not fix and (N$_{+}$) assumes. In $\Cl(1,3)$, with $n = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$, $B = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{3}$ and $J = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, exactly: $I_{4}B = J$, $J^{2} = -1$, the transverse rotor $\exp(\varphi J/2)$ fixes $n$ and $B$, and the transverse reflection fixes $n$ and $B$ and reverses $J$ and $I_{4}$. Reading (argued, not proved): if the field's $i$ is read as $J = I_{4}B$, the lift datum is a transverse rotation rate invisible to the generator's null direction and boost, and the sign datum is the orientation $I_{4}$ relative to $B$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One cut; affine structure.)} For $m(u) = e^{i\vartheta(|u|)}$, any measurable $\vartheta$, $J_{0}$ acts elementwise as the vacuum's reflection about $0$ with the constant phase $c$, while the modular group of $\mathfrak{A}((0,\infty))$ acts elementwise as the boost about $0$ followed by the local phase $e^{i(\vartheta(e^{s}|u|) - \vartheta(|u|))}$, which is geometric only if $e^{i\vartheta(x)} = e^{i\mu}x^{i\lambda_{0}}$ for constants $\lambda_{0}$, $\mu$. The slope-jump vacuum of \claimref{synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state}(vi) has modular conjugations acting by the reflections of its own regular parameter $\lambda$, $u \mapsto \lambda^{-1}(2\lambda(a) - \lambda(u))$, and by no affine reflection, at every cut.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(The modular conjugation from the one-particle operator; two finite cases.)} For the Slater states on $1 + 1$ and $2 + 2$ modes of Step 6 (basis projection $E$ of rank $r$, $\Omega$ cyclic and separating for the CAR algebra $M$ of the first block of modes), $J\,a(f)\,J = \Gamma_{\Omega}\,a^{*}(Wf)$, with $\Gamma_{\Omega} = (-1)^{r}\Gamma$ the parity normalised to fix $\Omega$ and $W$ the polar part of the block of $E$ crossing from $M$'s modes to the others; so elementwise geometric action of $J$ at a cut is a statement about the polar part of the cross-cut block. (The general finite case, by factorising the Slater state over Schmidt pairs, is argued.)
\end{enumerate}
Status: (i) to (v) proved (the vacuum's modular data imported, Facts \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses} and \claimref{synthesis.imported-modular-conjugation-of-the-chiral-fermi-field-is-the-twisted-reflection}; the vacuum's phase $c = -i$ from \claimref{synthesis.geometric-modular-conjugations-on-a-generator-give-the-null-ground-state}; the Hankel-kernel route to it argued); the $\Cl(1,3)$ identities in (iv) proved, their reading argued; (vi) proved for the two finite cases by exact computation, with uniqueness of the polar decomposition. Comparison (literature, verified): for wedges in Minkowski space the Condition of Geometric Modular Action gives translations, and with Modular Stability positivity only up to sign (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-buchholz-florig-summers-geometric-modular-action-and-modular-stability}(c), (d) \cite{BuchholzFlorigSummers1999}); (i) and (iii) are the generator forms of those two gaps. Transport-absent.
synthesis.modular-data-on-a-generator-fi.technical: The open problem asks whether the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$), that the generator modes are in their lowest-energy state for sliding along the light ray, follows from a principle of the series with no thermal input. A natural candidate is geometric modular action of the modular conjugations alone: no modular group and no temperature enter it. This result bounds what such a principle can do when it is stated at the level of the net. Every condition stated in terms of the algebras of regions and the state vector (the condition in the form Buchholz and Summers use, modular stability, Haag duality, and positive energy for some implementation of the net translations) is satisfied identically by the null vacuum and by every local gauge transform of it, because a local gauge transformation maps each region's algebra onto itself. Among these are the translation-invariant Fermi seas, filled up to a nonzero null momentum: they satisfy the generator microlocal condition and are locally normal everywhere, yet the field translations have negative-energy excitations in them; they are ground states of a different lift of the translations, and on the gauge-invariant observables, for a scalar shift, ground states of the translations themselves with a constant charge density. Complex conjugation of the real Majorana algebra carries the vacuum to the filled positive-energy sea. So no principle invariant under these groups implies the ground-state clause; the two data they cannot see are (1) which automorphism lifts the affine translations to the fields, equivalently a flat connection along the generator (parallel transport gives the zero connection), and (2) the orientation of the imaginary unit relative to time, which the series does not fix. The action of the same modular conjugations on the fields themselves sees both: it fixes the lift and records the orientation as its phase, which is what the companion field-level result uses (\claimref{synthesis.geometric-modular-conjugations-on-a-generator-give-the-null-ground-state}). Read in $\Cl(1,3)$ with the field's $i$ taken as $J = I_{4}B$ (\claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}), the first datum would be a transverse rotation rate that the boost does not see and the second the orientation $I_{4}$; this reading is argued, not proved. At a single cut even the field-level conjugation says nothing about the modular group.
synthesis.modular-data-on-a-generator-fi.lay: The series assumes that the quantum modes along a horizon's light rays sit in their lowest-energy state. One hoped-for justification uses a mirror symmetry that quantum theory attaches to each half of a ray. This result shows what that justification cannot reach when it looks only at which observables belong to which stretch of the ray. The same mirror data are shared by states filled with particles up to some momentum, which have the same local algebras and mirror data region by region and are locally indistinguishable from the empty state in the sense of local normality, and by the state in which every positive-energy level is filled, which differs in the orientation of the square root of minus one relative to the direction of time. So two pieces of information must be supplied separately: how a slide along the ray is carried over to the field, and that orientation. The mirror data acting on the fields themselves fix the first, and record the second as a sign that is not fixed by anything else in the series and must be assumed.

proofs.main:
\emph{Set-up.} Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On one generator, $\mathfrak{h} = L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K$, $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ the continuum mode space (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}) with $a(f)$ antilinear in $f$, $\mathfrak{A}(O) = \CAR(L^{2}(O)\otimes K)$ for an interval or half-line $O$, $\tau_{t}(a(f)) = a(f(\cdot - t))$, $P = i\,d/du$ (so $e^{-ipu}$ has $P$-eigenvalue $p$ and $\tau_{t}$ acts on it by $e^{itp}$), and a gauge-invariant quasi-free state $\omega_{E}$ is fixed by its symbol $E$, $\omega_{E}(a^{*}(f)a(g)) = \ip{g}{Ef}$. The null vacuum is $\omega_{0} = \omega_{E_{0}}$, $E_{0} = \chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$, kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$; it is the unique gauge-invariant quasi-free state of (N$_{+}$), whose ground-state clause asks that $\tau$ be implemented in the GNS representation by a unitary group with nonnegative generator fixing the GNS vector (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)). Its half-line modular data are geometric: the modular group of $\mathfrak{A}((a, \infty))$ is the boost about $a$ at rapidity $2\pi t$, and the modular conjugation $J^{0}_{a}$ acts as the reflection $r_{a}(u) = 2a - u$ composed with charge conjugation: $J^{0}_{a}\pi_{0}(a(f))J^{0}_{a} = \Theta\,\pi_{0}(a^{*}(c\,f\circ r_{a}))$ for $f$ supported in $(a, \infty)$, with $\Theta$ the grading unitary normalised by $\Theta\Omega_{0} = \Omega_{0}$ and $c$ a constant phase (Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}: Bisognano-Wichmann and the conformal-net form, the modular conjugation being CPT composed with the turn by $\pi$; its action on the fields as the twisted reflection, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-modular-conjugation-of-the-chiral-fermi-field-is-the-twisted-reflection}(c)). In the Klein-twist form $J^{0}_{a}\psi(f)J^{0}_{a} = \eta Z\psi^{*}(\rho_{a}f)Z^{*}$, $Z = (1 + i\Theta)/(1 + i)$, one has $Z\psi^{*}Z^{*} = i\Theta\psi^{*}$, so $c = i\eta$; the companion field-level result \claimref{synthesis.geometric-modular-conjugations-on-a-generator-give-the-null-ground-state} (Step 4, natural-cone positivity, proved and checked there) fixes $\eta = -1$ for the null vacuum, so $c = -i$. Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 use only that $c$ does not depend on $f$. For an automorphism $\alpha$ the state $\omega\circ\alpha$; for an antilinear automorphism $\theta$ the state $x \mapsto \overline{\omega(\theta(x))}$.

\emph{Step 1: net-level identity, (i).} Let $m : \R \to U(K)$ be measurable and $\alpha_{m}(a(f)) = a(mf)$; multiplication by $m$ is unitary and preserves the anticommutator, so $\alpha_{m}$ is an automorphism, and since multiplication by $m$ and by $m^{-1}$ maps $L^{2}(O)\otimes K$ onto itself, $\alpha_{m}(\mathfrak{A}(O)) = \mathfrak{A}(O)$ for every $O$. The triple $(\mathcal{H}_{0}, \pi_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}, \Omega_{0})$ represents $\omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}$, and $\Omega_{0}$ is cyclic for it because $\alpha_{m}$ is onto; by uniqueness of the GNS representation it is the GNS triple. Hence $\pi_{0}(\alpha_{m}(\mathfrak{A}(O)))'' = \pi_{0}(\mathfrak{A}(O))''$ for every $O$: the two states define the same Hilbert space, vector and von Neumann algebra for every region. The modular operator and conjugation of a pair (von Neumann algebra, cyclic separating vector) depend on nothing else, so they coincide region by region, and so does every property of the net and the vector built from them: the generator form of the Condition of Geometric Modular Action (in the Buchholz-Summers form, a condition on the algebras as sets, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-buchholz-florig-summers-geometric-modular-action-and-modular-stability}(a) \cite{BuchholzFlorigSummers1999, BuchholzSummers1993}), geometric action of the modular groups on the net, modular stability, twisted Haag duality, and the vacuum's translation unitaries $U_{0}(t)$, with nonnegative generator, which map $\pi_{0}(\mathfrak{A}(O))''$ onto $\pi_{0}(\mathfrak{A}(O + t))''$ and fix $\Omega_{0}$.

\emph{Step 2: the Fermi seas, (ii).} Take $m(u) = e^{iu\kappa}$, $\kappa = \kappa^{*}$ on $K$. Then $\omega_{0}(\alpha_{m}(a^{*}(f)a(g))) = \ip{mg}{E_{0}mf} = \ip{g}{m^{-1}E_{0}mf}$, and $m^{-1}$ followed by $P$ and then $m$ is $P - \kappa$ on plane waves ($m$ sends the eigenvalue $p$ to $p - \kappa$), so the symbol is $E_{\kappa} = \chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P - \kappa)$, a projection: $\omega_{\kappa}$ is pure, and it is $\tau$-invariant since $E_{\kappa}$ commutes with $P$. On a bounded interval $O$ of length $L$, for $\kappa = k\,\id_{K}$ with $k > 0$ (the general case is the sum over eigenvectors of $\kappa$, with the sign of each eigenvalue), $\chi_{O}(E_{k} - E_{0})\chi_{O} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{k}\chi_{O}\ket{e_{p}}\bra{e_{p}}\chi_{O}\,dp$, $e_{p}(u) = e^{-ipu}$, a positive operator of trace $kL\dim K/2\pi$: trace class, so by the Powers-Stormer inequality and criterion (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(a), (c)) the restrictions to $\mathfrak{A}(O)$ are quasi-equivalent, the same argument as in the stored local-normality theorem. The kernel difference $\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{k}e^{-ip(u - v)}\,dp$ is entire in $u - v$, so the generator microlocal condition holds at every point (\claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}, which characterises it by a smooth kernel difference).
Not a ground state: since $\omega_{\kappa}$ is $\tau$-invariant, $\tau$ has a canonical implementer $U_{\kappa}(t)$ fixing $\Omega$, and $U_{\kappa}(t)\pi_{\kappa}(a^{*}(f))\Omega = \pi_{\kappa}(a^{*}(e^{itP}f))\Omega$, $U_{\kappa}(t)\pi_{\kappa}(a(g))\Omega = \pi_{\kappa}(a(e^{itP}g))\Omega$. For $f$ in the range of $1 - E_{\kappa}$ (a particle at momentum $p > k$) the energy is $+p$; for $g$ in the range of $E_{\kappa}$ (a hole at $p < k$), $a$ being antilinear, it is $-p$. With $k > 0$, holes at $p \in (0, k)$ have negative energy, and $n$ holes in disjoint momentum windows inside $(k/2, k)$ have energy below $-nk/2$; for $k < 0$ the particles at $p \in (k, 0)$ do the same. In an irreducible representation any other implementer differs by a character $e^{i\lambda t}$, so no implementer has a generator bounded below.
On the gauge-invariant subalgebra $\mathfrak{A}^{G}$: $\alpha_{m}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}^{-1}(a(f)) = a(e^{iu\kappa}e^{-i(u - t)\kappa}f(u - t)) = a(e^{it\kappa}f(\cdot - t))$, $\tau_{t}$ followed by the internal rotation $e^{it\kappa}$; inversely $\alpha_{m}^{-1}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}(a(f)) = a(e^{-it\kappa}f(\cdot - t))$, whose one-particle generator on $e^{-ipu}$ is $p - \kappa$, and $\omega_{\kappa} = \omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}$ is the ground state of this lift ($\omega_{\kappa}\circ\alpha_{m}^{-1}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m} = \omega_{0}\circ\tau_{t}\circ\alpha_{m}$, implemented by $U_{0}$). The rotation $e^{it\kappa}$ commutes with every gauge rotation; for $\kappa = k\,\id$ it is a gauge rotation and acts trivially on $\mathfrak{A}^{G}$, so $\alpha_{m}$ and $\tau_{t}$ commute there. Then $U_{0}(t)\pi_{0}(\alpha_{m}(x))U_{0}(t)^{*} = \pi_{0}(\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}(x)) = \pi_{0}(\alpha_{m}(\tau_{t}x))$ for $x \in \mathfrak{A}^{G}$: on the cyclic subspace $\overline{\pi_{0}(\mathfrak{A}^{G})\Omega_{0}}$, which $U_{0}$ preserves, $U_{0}$ implements $\tau$ for $\omega_{\kappa}$ with nonnegative generator and fixes the vector, so $\omega_{\kappa}$ restricted to $\mathfrak{A}^{G}$ is a ground state for $\tau$. It differs from $\omega_{0}$ there: $\omega_{k}(a^{*}(f)a(f)) - \omega_{0}(a^{*}(f)a(f)) = \ip{f}{(E_{k} - E_{0})f}$, a charge density $k/2\pi$, and the energy density is $\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{k}p\,dp = k^{2}/4\pi$ per dimension of $K$. With $K$ two-dimensional and $\kappa$ of eigenvalues $\pm k$ the charges cancel and the energies add; this state is not a ground state for $\tau$ (the eigenvalue $k$ gives negative-energy holes as above), and it is the ground state of the lift $\alpha_{m}^{-1}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}$, $\tau_{t}$ followed by $e^{-it\kappa}$ (one-particle generator $P - \kappa$).
Elementwise conjugation: with $\pi_{\kappa} = \pi_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}$ and $J_{a} = J^{0}_{a}$ (Step 1), $J_{a}\pi_{\kappa}(a(f))J_{a} = J^{0}_{a}\pi_{0}(a(mf))J^{0}_{a} = \Theta\,\pi_{0}(a^{*}(c\,(mf)\circ r_{a})) = \Theta\,\pi_{\kappa}(a^{*}(c\,m^{-1}\,(mf)\circ r_{a}))$, and $m(u)^{-1}m(2a - u) = e^{2i\kappa(a - u)}$, constant in $u$ only for $\kappa = 0$.

\emph{Step 3: the sign, (iii).} $R : u \mapsto -u$ is unitary on $\mathfrak{h}$ with $RPR = -P$, so $\omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{R}$ has symbol $RE_{0}R = \chi_{(0,\infty)}(P)$ (the point $0$ is null), the filled sea $\bar\omega_{0}$. With $\phi(f) = a(f) + a^{*}(f)$, real-linear in $f$, $a(f) = \tfrac12(\phi(f) + i\phi(if))$; the antilinear automorphism $\theta$ fixing every $\phi(f)$ has $\theta(a(f)) = \tfrac12(\phi(f) - i\phi(if)) = a^{*}(f)$, and $x \mapsto \overline{\omega_{0}(\theta(x))}$ has $\overline{\omega_{0}(a(f)a^{*}(g))} = \overline{\ip{f}{(1 - E_{0})g}} = \ip{g}{(1 - E_{0})f}$: symbol $1 - E_{0} = \chi_{(0,\infty)}(P)$ again. $\theta$ commutes with $\tau$ ($\tau_{t}\phi(f) = \phi(f(\cdot - t))$), with the grading, and with the gauge rotations ($\gamma_{\vartheta}\phi(f) = \phi(e^{i\vartheta}f)$), and maps the real algebra generated by $\{\phi(f) : f \in L^{2}(O)\otimes K\}$ onto itself. The GNS triple of $\bar\omega_{0}$ is $(\mathcal{H}_{0}, \pi_{0}\circ\alpha_{R}, \Omega_{0})$, and the algebra of $(a, \infty)$ is $\pi_{0}(\mathfrak{A}((-\infty, -a)))''$, the twisted commutant $Z\mathcal{R}'Z^{*}$ of the vacuum's algebra $\mathcal{R}$ of $(-a, \infty)$; since $Z\Omega_{0} = \Omega_{0}$, $J^{0}_{-a}ZJ^{0}_{-a} = Z^{*}$ and $Z^{2} = \Theta$, its modular conjugation is $ZJ^{0}_{-a}Z^{*} = Z^{2}J^{0}_{-a} = \Theta J^{0}_{-a}$. Inverting the vacuum relation $J a(f) J = \Theta a^{*}(c\,f\circ r)$ ($J = J^{0}_{-a}$, $r = r_{-a}$, $J\Theta J = \Theta$): applying $J$ gives $Ja^{*}(c\,f\circ r)J = \Theta a(f)$; for $g$ supported in $(-\infty, -a)$ and $f = \bar c\,g\circ r$, $Ja^{*}(g)J = \Theta a(\bar c\,g\circ r) = c\,\Theta a(g\circ r)$, and the adjoint is $J a(g) J = \bar c\,a^{*}(g\circ r)\Theta = -\bar c\,\Theta a^{*}(g\circ r)$. Hence $(\Theta J)a(g)(\Theta J)^{-1} = \Theta(-\bar c\,\Theta a^{*}(g\circ r))\Theta = \bar c\,\Theta a^{*}(g\circ r)$. Transporting by $R$ ($R\,r_{-a}R = r_{a}$): the filled sea's conjugations act as the reflections about the cuts with the phase $\bar c$, on the same half-line algebras with the same inclusions; with $c = -i$ (set-up) this is $+i$. Consistency of the phases (argued): by (vi) in its continuum form ($\Gamma_{\Omega} \to \Theta$; the continuum one-particle polar decomposition exists since the cross-cut block is injective with dense range), $J_{0}$ acts through the polar part of $X = \chi_{(-\infty,0)}E\chi_{(0,\infty)}$; $(XF)(-x) = \int_{0}^{\infty}h(x + y)F(y)\,dy$ with $h(t) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S}e^{ipt}\,dp$ for $E = \chi_{S}(P)$, which is $-\frac{i}{2\pi t}$ for $S = (-\infty, 0)$ and $+\frac{i}{2\pi t}$ for $S = (0, \infty)$; $\bar c\,h \geq 0$ (the Carleman kernel $1/(x + y)$ is a positive operator) gives $c = -i$ for $\omega_{0}$ and $c = +i$ for $\bar\omega_{0}$, in agreement.

\emph{Step 4: independence, (iv).} $\alpha_{m} \in G_{1}$ by Step 1 and it commutes with the gauge rotations and the grading; $\theta \in G_{2}$ by Step 3. If a property is $G_{1}$-invariant and $\omega_{0}$ has it, $\omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}$ has it, in particular every $\omega_{\kappa}$, which for $\kappa \neq 0$ is not a ground state for $\tau$ (Step 2). If it is $G_{2}$-invariant, $\bar\omega_{0}$ has it, and in the GNS space of $\bar\omega_{0}$ the implementer of $\tau$ is $U_{0}(-t)$ transported by $R$, with nonpositive, nonzero generator, so $\bar\omega_{0}$ is not a ground state for $\tau$. The ground-state clause is not $G_{1}$-invariant because $G_{1}$ does not normalise $\{\tau_{t}\}$: $\alpha_{m}\tau_{t}\alpha_{m}^{-1}$ maps $\mathfrak{A}(O)$ onto $\mathfrak{A}(O + t)$ for every $m$, and for $m = e^{iu\kappa}$ it is $\tau_{t}$ followed by $e^{it\kappa}$ (Step 2), so fixing which lift is the translation is fixing $\kappa$, the flat connection $\kappa\,du$ along the generator. It is not $G_{2}$-invariant because positivity of a generator $A$ with $U(t) = e^{itA}$ refers to $i$: under $\theta$ the implementer's generator changes sign. Geometric algebra (identities exact; their reading argued, not proved): in $\Cl(1,3)$ with $n = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$, $B = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{3}$, $J = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$: $I_{4}B = J$, $J^{2} = -1$, $B^{2} = 1$, $JB = BJ$. The rotor $R_{\varphi} = \cos\tfrac{\varphi}{2} + \sin\tfrac{\varphi}{2}J$ (checked at $\cos\tfrac{\varphi}{2} = \tfrac35$) has $R_{\varphi}nR_{\varphi}^{-1} = n$, $R_{\varphi}BR_{\varphi}^{-1} = B$ and turns $\gamma_{1}$: a transverse rotation at a rate along the generator is invisible to $n$ and the boost, and if the field's $i$ is read as $J$, a transverse rotation at a rate along the generator acts on the spinor values as a $u$-dependent phase of the kind $\alpha_{m}$ (a reading). The transverse reflection $v \mapsto -\gamma_{1}v\gamma_{1}^{-1}$ fixes $n$ and $B$ and sends $J \mapsto -J$, $I_{4} \mapsto -I_{4}$: under the same reading, $i = J = I_{4}B$, the sign of $i$ relative to the time orientation (fixed by $n$ and $B$) is the orientation $I_{4}$ (compare \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}, which writes the Klein twist with $i = I_{4}$). The series does not fix this orientation; (N$_{+}$) assumes it.

\emph{Step 5: one cut and the affine structure, (v).} For $m(u) = e^{i\vartheta(|u|)}$, $m(-u) = m(u)$, so by Step 2's computation the phase of $J_{0}$ is $c\,m(u)^{-1}m(-u) = c$: elementwise geometric with the vacuum's constant phase. The modular group of $\mathfrak{A}((0, \infty))$ for $\omega_{0}\circ\alpha_{m}$ is the vacuum's $\Delta^{is}$ (Step 1), and $\Delta^{is}\pi_{m}(a(f))\Delta^{-is} = \pi_{0}(a(\beta_{s}(mf))) = \pi_{m}(a(m^{-1}\beta_{s}(mf)))$ with $\beta_{s}$ the boost about $0$ (weight $\tfrac12$, rapidity proportional to $s$): $m(u)^{-1}m(e^{s}u) = e^{i(\vartheta(e^{s}|u|) - \vartheta(|u|))}$, which is independent of $u$ for every $s$ exactly when $h = e^{i\vartheta}$ satisfies $h(\lambda x) = \chi(\lambda)h(x)$ for almost every $x > 0$; then $\chi$ is a measurable character of the multiplicative group, $\chi(\lambda) = \lambda^{i\lambda_{0}}$, and $h(x)x^{-i\lambda_{0}}$ is dilation invariant, hence constant: $h(x) = e^{i\mu}x^{i\lambda_{0}}$. So at one cut the elementwise conjugation carries no information on the modular group beyond the vacuum's. The slope-jump vacuum is $\omega_{0}$ transported by the weight-$\tfrac12$ unitary of a regular increasing $\lambda : \R \to \R$ whose slopes at the two ends differ, $\lambda'(u) \to s_{\pm}$ as $u \to \pm\infty$, $s_{-} \neq s_{+}$ (\claimref{synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state}(vi)); its algebra of $O$ is the vacuum's of $\lambda(O)$, so its $J_{a}$ maps the algebra of $O$ to that of $\lambda^{-1}r_{\lambda(a)}\lambda(O)$. This is $r_{a}O$ for every interval $O \subset (a, \infty)$ only if $\lambda(2a - u) = 2\lambda(a) - \lambda(u)$ for all $u > a$; differentiating, $\lambda'(2a - u) = \lambda'(u)$, and letting $u \to \infty$ gives $s_{-} = s_{+}$, a contradiction, at every cut $a$. So at every cut it acts by its own parameter's reflection and by no affine one.

\emph{Step 6: the finite formula, (vi).} On $n_{0} + n_{1}$ modes let $\Omega = a^{*}(\phi_{1})\cdots a^{*}(\phi_{r})\ket{0}$, $E = \sum\ket{\phi_{j}}\bra{\phi_{j}}$, $M$ the CAR algebra of the first $n_{0}$ modes with $\Omega$ cyclic and separating, $X$ the block of $E$ from the first $n_{0}$ modes to the others, $W$ its polar part, $\Gamma_{\Omega} = (-1)^{r}\Gamma$ the parity normalised by $\Gamma_{\Omega}\Omega = \Omega$, and $J_{c}$ the antilinear map $x\Omega \mapsto \varphi(x)\Omega$ for the antilinear multiplicative $*$-map $\varphi$ with $\varphi(a(e_{j})) = \Gamma_{\Omega}\,a^{*}(We_{j})$ (cyclic and separating on the full space forces $n_{0} = n_{1} = r$, so $(-1)^{r} = (-1)^{n_{0}}$ here). The exact check verifies, for $1 + 1$ modes ($\phi = \tfrac35e_{0} + \tfrac{4i}{5}e_{1}$, $W = i$) and $2 + 2$ modes (two Schmidt pairs rotated in each block, $W = i\ket{l_{a}}\bra{r_{a}} + \ket{l_{b}}\bra{r_{b}}$, with $X = W|X|$ checked): the two-point function equals $E$; $\Gamma_{\Omega}\Omega = \Omega$; $J_{c}$ is antiunitary, an involution, and fixes $\Omega$; $J_{c}S$ ($S$ the Tomita operator on the cyclic basis of monomials) is Hermitian with positive leading principal minors, hence positive definite. By uniqueness of the polar decomposition $S = J\Delta^{1/2}$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-theory-matrix-factor-proved-outright} for the finite case) $J = J_{c}$ and $\Delta^{1/2} = J_{c}S$, and $J_{c}a(e_{j})J_{c} = \varphi(a(e_{j}))$ is checked as an operator identity. The general finite case (factorising the Slater state over Schmidt pairs, each a $1 + 1$ case) is argued, not checked.

synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state.formal:
\emph{Premise (N$_{+}$).} Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be one of: (a) the future event horizon of the eternal (Kruskal-extended) Schwarzschild solution; (b) the future cosmological horizon of the static patch of de Sitter space; (c) a local Rindler horizon $\mathcal{H}_{p,\ell}$ of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} in Minkowski space, flat spacetime with vanishing gravitational field ($\hb = 1$, $\Omega = 0$; Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). On each generator of $\mathcal{H}$ let $u$ be the affine parameter, with $u = 0$ on the bifurcation (edge) surface and $u \in \R$ the whole generator of the extended solution. The modes of $\mathcal{H}$ are the continuum mode space of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, one carrier per light ray: $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$, $K$ the transverse and internal labels, generated by fields $\psi(u)$ with $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)\otimes\id_{K}$, carrying the affine null translations $\nu_{a}(\psi(u)) = \psi(u + a)$, which act on the fields by parallel transport along the generator, the zero flat connection on $K$: no internal rotation accompanies the translation. Then the state $\omega$ of these modes is gauge-invariant and quasi-free, it is invariant under $\nu$, and the generator of $\nu$ in its GNS representation is positive: $\omega$ is a ground state for the affine null translations along the generators. It contains no temperature, period or Euclidean section.

\emph{The two data the premise supplies.} (1) The lift. The clause names the lift of the affine translations to the fields, by parallel transport. This excludes the translation-invariant Fermi seas $\chi_{(-\infty, 0)}(P - \kappa)$, $\kappa \ne 0$ a constant Hermitian operator on $K$: they are local gauge transforms of the null vacuum, with its local algebras and modular objects, locally normal to it and generator-Hadamard, and they are ground states only of the lift with flat connection $\kappa\,du$, not of $\nu$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.modular-data-on-a-generator-fix-neither-the-translation-lift-nor-the-sign-of-i}(ii), (iv)). (2) The orientation of $i$. The positivity clause refers to the imaginary unit of the field algebra: the filled positive-energy sea $\chi_{(0, \infty)}(P)$, the time reverse of the null vacuum and the image of it under complex conjugation of the Majorana fields, has the same local algebras and the same net-level modular data and is a ground state only for the reversed translations (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.modular-data-on-a-generator-fix-neither-the-translation-lift-nor-the-sign-of-i}(iii), (iv)). Which of the two is the state of the light rays, the orientation of the imaginary unit relative to the time orientation, is a datum that (N$_{+}$) assumes; the series does not fix it.

\emph{Local form.} On a local Rindler horizon $\mathcal{H}_{p,\ell}$ of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime with nonvanishing field strength, the premise is read at leading order in the size of the patch: in a gauge with $\hb(x_0) = 1$ and $\Omega(x_0) = 0$ at the point $x_0$ of $p$ (the reading of a normal neighbourhood), the state of the modes on the generators is a ground state for the null translations of the background along $\ell$, a physically null direction at $x_0$. That this is the leading-order form of (c) is argued, not derived.

\emph{Scope.} In case (a) the premise is a Hartle-Hawking-type regularity condition on the whole Kruskal generator: it describes the eternal hole in equilibrium. A hole formed by collapse is not covered by case (a): its horizon generators have no $u < 0$ half, and its physical state is not a ground state for $\nu$ on the horizon. It is covered by the premise's local form read on the other sheet, given the reduction of the outgoing sector to one chiral CAR field per light ray (the postulate J3, Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction}): posed in its short-distance form (on a generator, the ground-state singularity plus a remainder bounded near the point, a class the same in every regular parameter for the weight-$\tfrac12$ kernel) on the ingoing sheet through each point of the future horizon, whose generator has both halves, it gives the late-time state of the near-horizon exterior outgoing modes as the continuum I-state at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$; the condition is sufficient, and states outside the class can have the same limit (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet}). In the collapse of a null shell the vacuum before the collapse is in that class, and among states KMS for the Killing translations at late times finite null energy across the future horizon holds only at $\kappa/2\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collapse-in-vacuum-regular-at-future-horizon-selects-hawking-temperature}). Hawking's flux at infinity follows from that late-time state under Premise \claimref{hawking.premise-i-interface-identification} with the greybody passage; the greybody factors themselves and collapse geometries other than the spherical null shell are not covered. Not part of this premise: the weight clause of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}, $\omega_{k} = \kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ in its version 3, which stays a separate hypothesis (the half-integer offset is read from the modes being spinor fields of boost weight $\tfrac12$ in the state (N$_{+}$) selects, a reading and not a consequence). \emph{Scope note (local normality).} Within stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free states, (N$_{+}$) is equivalent to local normality of the state to the null vacuum on the algebra of an interval of each generator containing the bifurcation surface (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}(iv)), the analogue for that generator algebra of the local normality principle of algebraic quantum field theory, which is stated for the algebras of spacetime regions (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haag-local-normality}). (N$_{+}$) remains the premise; local normality at the edge is its equivalent form within that class, and adopting it would not derive (N$_{+}$) from the series. \emph{Scope note (stationarity-free forms).} Without stationarity two forms are known, neither of which is (N$_{+}$). The folium form: local normality to the null vacuum on every interval of the generator closed by its Moebius covariance, the arcs through the point at infinity included, puts a pure gauge-invariant quasi-free state in the null vacuum's folium, where the affine translations are positive, and excludes the affine-KMS states (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-generator-gives-the-vacuum-folium-not-the-ground-state}). The local form at every point: the generator analogue of the microlocal (Hadamard) condition, on both orderings of the two-point kernel, holds exactly when the kernel differs from the null vacuum's by a smooth kernel, and gives the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point of the interval, with no stationarity and no temperature; the affine-KMS states satisfy it (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}). Neither condition, nor both together, gives the ground-state clause without stationarity: a normal excitation of the vacuum by a one-particle vector that is a Schwartz function satisfies both and is not a ground state. \emph{Scope note (the eternal hole when $\Lambda > 0$).} Case (a) is an idealisation in a universe with a positive cosmological constant. On a spacetime with a bifurcate Killing horizon the stationary quasi-free Hadamard state is unique, but on the extended Schwarzschild-de Sitter field, whose two horizons have different temperatures, Kay and Wald give a no-go result: no such state exists (a gap in their proofs was corrected by Kay and Lupo 2016, App. B; on Kerr the corresponding result is argued, from superradiance) (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kay-wald-uniqueness-and-no-go}). The series' universe has $\Lambda > 0$, carried by its frozen point ($Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$, the square of the cosmological horizon's surface gravity, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-static-boost-frozen-point}), so its holes are Schwarzschild-de Sitter holes and the equilibrium state of case (a) has no stationary counterpart there; the physics is carried by the local reading (the local form at points of the generators, and for holes formed by collapse its short-distance form on the ingoing sheet). The passage from the bulk no-go to the state of the generators is argued, since no theorem restricting a four-dimensional Hadamard state to the algebra of one generator is imported. \emph{Scope note (the open premise).} That the series' states satisfy the Hadamard (microlocal) condition on horizon generators is recorded as an open premise, not adopted as a postulate: it would give the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point of every generator, and with the bulk theorems imported as Facts (Facts \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}, \claimref{synthesis.imported-local-quasi-equivalence-of-hadamard-states}, \claimref{synthesis.imported-propagation-of-hadamard-form}) it would follow from the bulk Hadamard condition only given a restriction of bulk Hadamard states to the generator algebra, which is not in the store (for the Dirac field it needs the s-wave reduction J3). \emph{Scope note (the reduction of the open premise; added 1 November).} The restriction named above as missing is computed on the flat field for the Dirac field on every null plane, with the transverse labels as multiplicity space and no s-wave reduction: every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state restricts to a state satisfying the generator condition, hence the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point of every local Rindler horizon of the flat field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}). Where the field strength is nonzero the same local form follows for such states by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}, (HS) (adopted as a premise on 1 November, proved on 2 November). So, for its use here (the local form at every point of every local Rindler horizon), the open premise is reduced to the statement that the series' states are gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard states, (HS) being a theorem; given that statement, the local form is a consequence rather than only argued, while the passage from it to the period of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) stays argued at leading order. Neither reaches the ground-state clause. These scope notes record what is known; what the premise asserts is unchanged.

\emph{What it delivers.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}, (N$_{+}$) fixes $\omega$ as the filled sea $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$, $P = i\,d/du$, and its restriction to either side of the edge is the continuum I-state at rapidity period $2\pi$ for the boost future-directed on that side. Hence the continuum restatements of (R) (Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) for the eternal hole, of (R$_{\Lambda}$) (Premise \claimref{synthesis.r-lambda-regularity-cosmological-horizon}) and of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) (clause of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}) in Minkowski space, with the joint KMS part of (Q), follow from (N$_{+}$); where the field strength is nonzero the continuum form of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) follows from the local form, argued at leading order. (N$_{+}$) cannot be posed on point-spectrum mode sets with phase-acting flows (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.point-spectrum-boost-admits-no-half-sided-translations}): the stored wordings of (R), (R$_{\Lambda}$) and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) are its discretisations, recovered only for modes of vanishing Mellin width. For case (c) the positivity and the invariance follow, not assumed, from a unitary representation of $\mathrm{Spin}^{+}(2,4)$ with nonnegative conformal energy on the state's GNS space whose GNS vector is translation invariant (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-gives-positive-null-translations}). For case (b) with conformally invariant fields the positivity follows in the same way from nonnegative conformal energy: the uniform affine translation along a de Sitter cosmological horizon's generators is the background conformal null rotation generated by $\tfrac12 nI = P_{n} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{12}n\nO$, a nonnegative generator, with the identification of the horizon modes argued (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation}). The series' modes carry such a representation: the twistor attachment's conformal energy $|s| + 1 + n$ is the nonnegative generator of $Z = e_{0}\nu$, and the attachment's Fock vacuum satisfies the positivity and invariance clause on the horizons of case (c) and, for conformally invariant fields, of case (b), where it is the conformal vacuum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is-generated-by-z}; exact at the one-particle level, the Fock level by the standard second-quantisation functor). The state the clause admits is unique, so on those horizons (N$_{+}$) is the choice of that vacuum as the state of the light rays: a restatement of the premise and not a derivation of it, in which positivity is no longer assumed but the state is still chosen. Positivity remains part of the premise only in case (a), the eternal hole (and, in case (b), for fields that are not conformally invariant, which these results do not reach).

\emph{What it costs.} The thermal input is relocated, not removed: at a Killing horizon (N$_{+}$) is the regularity of the state across the bifurcation surface of Kay-Wald and Sewell (Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}), the import every derivation of the Hawking temperature makes. Within the stationary class this relocation is proved rather than cited: on each generator the boost is the anticommutator-preserving scaling about the edge, so a stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free state is its own scaling limit there and satisfies (N$_{+}$) exactly when it is locally the null vacuum at the bifurcation surface, while stationary states thermal on each half at any period, with or without cross-edge correlation, are locally the null vacuum at every other point, so no condition at points off the edge gives (N$_{+}$) or (R) (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}). Within the stationary class (N$_{+}$) is therefore stationarity plus its local form at the bifurcation surface, which on the eternal hole lies off the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart. It is strictly stronger than (R): it forces the exact joint product form over boost modes, which by Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} removes the inter-mode correlations the series' later steps need, so those correlations are departures from (N$_{+}$), as they are from (Q).

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if any of the following is established: (a) a result showing that the series' other premises force, on a horizon in its scope, a state that is not a ground state for the affine null translations, for example one that is singular across the bifurcation surface of the eternal hole or of de Sitter space; (b) a confirmed departure from the temperatures it delivers, $\kappa/2\pi$ at the horizons of (a) and (b) and $a/2\pi$ for uniformly accelerated observers in the Minkowski vacuum; (c) a proof that the horizon modes must be a point-spectrum mode set, so that no continuum carrier exists on which (N$_{+}$) can be posed; (d) a proof that the inter-mode correlations the series' later steps need belong to the state of the horizon modes itself rather than to a departure from equilibrium, which the joint product form forbids.

\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The whole generator of the eternal horizon (case (a)) and of the de Sitter cosmological horizon (case (b)), through its bifurcation surface, is global and is not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region are in GTG, and the whole generator, through its bifurcation surface, is read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.

\emph{Note (a modular form of the ground-state clause, 2 November 2026).} For the fermionic (CAR) modes of one generator the ground-state clause has an equivalent form without a temperature: a state is the null vacuum of this premise exactly when, for every point $a$ of a set unbounded below, its restriction to the modes beyond $a$ is KMS, at some period, for the boost about $a$; two points already force the period $2\pi$, and no stationarity, quasi-freeness or gauge invariance is assumed (\claimref{synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-half-generator-fixes-the-period-and-the-null-ground-state}). This is the generator form of geometric modular action. It is available where every point of a generator is the edge of a Killing wedge, on the null planes of Minkowski space and, argued, on de Sitter horizons (given geometric modular action and that the horizon modes generate the wedge algebras), not on the eternal hole, where only the bifurcation surface carries a Killing boost. It is recorded as an equivalent form of the clause, not as a further premise; what (N$_{+}$) asserts is unchanged.

\emph{Note (a field-level modular form of the ground-state clause, 6 November 2026).} Within gauge-invariant quasi-free states on the modes of one generator the ground-state clause has a second equivalent form, free of stationarity, of any modular group and of any temperature: for a set of cuts whose differences generate a dense subgroup of $\R$ (three cuts $0$, $1$, $c$ with $c$ irrational suffice), the modular conjugation of the algebra of the modes beyond each cut acts on the fields as the twisted charge-conjugating reflection about the cut, with the sign $\eta = -1$ (field-level geometric modular action; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.geometric-modular-conjugations-on-a-generator-give-the-null-ground-state}(iv), (v), the converse imported). In this form the lift of (1) above is fixed by the reflections, whose products are the field translations, and the orientation of (2) is the sign $\eta$: $\eta = +1$ gives the filled positive-energy sea, so $\eta = -1$ is assumed, as (N$_{+}$) assumes the orientation. It needs only the generator algebra, so it can be posed in every case of the scope, the eternal hole included, where it is posed and not derived. Forms of the same condition on the net of local algebras only cannot give the clause: every local gauge transform of the null vacuum, the Fermi seas included, satisfies them (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.modular-data-on-a-generator-fix-neither-the-translation-lift-nor-the-sign-of-i}(i), (iv)). It is recorded as an equivalent form of the clause within that class, as the KMS form of 2 November was, not as a further premise; (N$_{+}$) remains the premise and what it asserts is unchanged.
synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state.technical:
The series has three thermal premises of one shape: (R) at the black-hole horizon, (R$_{\Lambda}$) at the cosmological horizon and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) on every local Rindler horizon, each asserting that boundary modes are thermal for a boost at the period where the boost's Euclidean section is smooth. This premise replaces their thermal content with one statement that has no temperature in it. Place the modes continuously along each light ray of the horizon, with the affine translations along the rays. (N$_{+}$) asks that the state of these modes be gauge-invariant and quasi-free and a ground state for those translations: invariant, with positive generator. The store proves that such a state is the filled sea of every generator and that, seen from either side of the edge, it is exactly thermal at rapidity period $2\pi$; so the continuum forms of (R) for the eternal hole, of (R$_{\Lambda}$) and of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) in Minkowski space, with the joint thermal part of (Q), follow from it. Where the gravitational field strength is nonzero the local horizons need its leading-order local form, which is argued. The premise supplies two data that the structure of the light rays alone does not: the translations act on the fields by parallel transport along the rays, which excludes the translation-invariant states filled up to a nonzero null momentum (they have the vacuum's local algebras and modular objects), and the orientation of the imaginary unit relative to time, which separates the vacuum from the filled positive-energy sea and which the series does not fix.

The scope is the eternal hole (a Hartle-Hawking-type state), de Sitter space and the local horizons. A hole formed by collapse is reached through the premise's short-distance form read on the ingoing sheet through each point of the future horizon: given the reduction J3 of the outgoing sector to one chiral field per light ray, it gives the late-time outgoing state near the horizon at temperature $\kappa/2\pi$ (a sufficient condition); the vacuum before a null-shell collapse satisfies it, and among late-time thermal states only $\kappa/2\pi$ has finite energy across the future horizon; greybody factors and other collapse geometries are not covered. On local Rindler horizons of Minkowski space, and on de Sitter horizons for conformally invariant fields, the positivity follows from positive conformal energy, and the twistor attachment's vacuum satisfies the positivity and invariance clause there, so on those horizons the premise is the choice of that vacuum, a restatement rather than a derivation; only at the eternal hole (and for fields that are not conformally invariant in de Sitter space) is positivity still assumed. The counted point-spectrum mode sets on which (R), (R$_{\Lambda}$) and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) are worded become discretisations. The thermal input is moved, not removed: it is now the regularity of the state across the bifurcation surface (Kay-Wald, Sewell), and within the stationary class this is proved: a stationary state satisfies the premise exactly when it is locally the null vacuum at the bifurcation surface, and no condition at other points implies it. Equivalently, within stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free states the premise is local normality to the null vacuum at the bifurcation surface, the analogue on one generator of Haag's local normality; the premise stays the premise, with this as its equivalent form there. Without stationarity, local normality on the generator closed at infinity gives only the vacuum's folium, and the generator analogue of the Hadamard condition only the local form at every point; neither, nor both, gives the ground state. The eternal hole of case (a) is an idealisation when $\Lambda > 0$, as in the series' universe: by Kay and Wald no stationary Hadamard state exists on a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, so the local reading carries the physics. Whether the series' states satisfy the Hadamard condition on horizon generators is an open premise, not a postulate; for the local form at every point of every local Rindler horizon it now reduces to the series' states being Hadamard, by the flat-field restriction result and, where the field strength is nonzero, the scaling-limit theorem (HS). The premise forces the exact joint product form, stronger than (R) on single modes, so the correlations the chain needs are departures from it. It is a Tier C premise, taken as given, refuted if the other premises force a horizon state in its scope that is not such a ground state, by a confirmed departure from the temperatures it gives, by a proof that the modes cannot live on a continuum, or by a proof that the needed correlations belong to the state itself. The whole generator of the eternal and de Sitter horizons, through the bifurcation surface, is global and is not carried by the store's one-chart fields, so it is read on several charts of flat spacetime, each carrying its own gravitational field, glued on overlaps by displacement and rotation gauge transformations.

(Note, 2 November 2026: for fermionic modes the ground-state clause is equivalent to thermality, at an unspecified temperature, of the future half beyond each point of a set of points reaching arbitrarily far into the past, for the boost about that point; the period $2\pi$ is then forced. This holds on Minkowski null planes and, argued, on de Sitter horizons, not on the eternal hole, \claimref{synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-half-generator-fixes-the-period-and-the-null-ground-state}.)

(Note, 6 November 2026: within gauge-invariant quasi-free states the ground-state clause is also equivalent to field-level geometric modular action: at cuts whose differences generate a dense subgroup, the modular conjugation of the modes beyond each cut acts on the fields as the twisted charge-conjugating reflection about the cut, with sign $\eta = -1$, the sign being the assumed orientation of $i$; no stationarity, temperature or modular group enters, so it can be posed on the eternal hole, where it is not derived, \claimref{synthesis.geometric-modular-conjugations-on-a-generator-give-the-null-ground-state}. The same condition stated on the local algebras alone cannot give the clause, \claimref{synthesis.modular-data-on-a-generator-fix-neither-the-translation-lift-nor-the-sign-of-i}.)
synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state.lay: Black holes, the horizon of an expanding universe and the horizon an accelerating observer sees all have a temperature. The series used to assume each temperature with its own premise. This premise replaces them with one assumption that mentions no temperature: the quantum modes running along each horizon's light rays are in their lowest-energy state for sliding along the rays. The store proves that this state, seen from one side of the horizon, is exactly thermal at the expected temperature. The assumption describes a black hole that has always existed in equilibrium; read on the light rays falling into the horizon, its short-distance form also covers a hole formed by collapse, given a simplification of the radiating fields to one direction per light ray. For the horizon an accelerating observer sees, and for the cosmological horizon with fields that keep their form under rescalings of lengths, it amounts to choosing the standard vacuum of the field theory. It still carries an input: that the state is smooth where the two halves of the horizon meet, the condition every derivation of black-hole temperature uses in some form. A black hole that has always existed in equilibrium is an idealisation in a universe with a positive cosmological constant, where no such equilibrium state exists, so the local form of the assumption is the one that matters there; whether the series' states are smooth enough at short distances to give that local form everywhere is still open, though it now comes down to the usual short-distance requirement on states: how such states look at very short distances where gravity is present, assumed before, is now proved. The assumption also supplies two things the light rays alone do not: that sliding along a ray carries the fields along with no internal rotation, which rules out states filled up to some nonzero momentum, and which way round the square root of minus one points relative to the direction of time, which the series does not otherwise fix. For the simplest class of states it can be restated as a mirror condition at a few points of each ray, with no reference to time evolution or temperature.

synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-genera.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a generator with affine parameter $u$ and the continuum mode space $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, let $\omega$ be a gauge-invariant quasi-free state with two-point kernel $W_{\omega}$, $\omega_{0}$ the null vacuum, $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}\otimes\id_{K}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)), $R = W_{\omega} - W_{0}$, and the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on a set $A$ as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state} ($R$ square integrable on $A \times A$). The \emph{closed generator} is $\R \cup \{\infty\}$; its intervals are the bounded intervals and the complements of bounded intervals (the arcs through $\infty$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The attachment closes the generator; proved.)} In $\Cl(2,4)$ with $\nInf = \nu + e_{-}$, $\nO = \tfrac12(\nu - e_{-})$ and the points $X(s) = \nO + s n$ of the null line of $n = e_{0} + e_{1}$ ($Q(X(s)) = 0$), the rotors $1 + \tfrac{t}{2}n\nInf$, $1 + \tfrac{c}{2}m\nO$ ($m = e_{0} - e_{1}$) and $\cosh\theta + \sinh\theta\,\nu e_{-}$ act on the line by $s \mapsto s + t$, $s \mapsto s/(1 - 2cs)$ and $s \mapsto e^{-2\theta}s$; the composite $J$ of a translation by $-1$, a special conformal map with $c = -\tfrac12$ and a translation by $-1$ acts by $s \mapsto -1/s$ and sends $\nO$ to a multiple of $n$, the point at infinity of the line. The null vacuum kernel with the spinor weight is invariant under every $g(s) = (as + b)/(cs + d)$, $ad - bc = 1$: $(cu + d)^{-1}(cv + d)^{-1}\,(g(u) - g(v))^{-1} = (u - v)^{-1}$. So $\infty$ is a regular point of the closed generator for $\omega_{0}$, and the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on an arc through it is posed as on any other interval. The property used is the $SL(2, \R)$ covariance of the chiral vacuum, which holds on every generator; the conformal rotors are its realisation on null lines of Minkowski space, and on the eternal hole only the abstract covariance is available.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Local on the closed generator is global; proved.)} If $\omega$ satisfies the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on every interval of the closed generator, in particular if it is locally normal to $\omega_{0}$ on each (Powers-Stormer, as in the theorem cited above), then $R$ is square integrable on $\R \times \R$: with $E_{1} = \{|u| > L\}$ and two disjoint bounded intervals $E_{2}, E_{3} \subset [-L, L]$, every pair of points avoids some $E_{k}$, and the complements $A_{k}$ are intervals of the closed generator. For a pure state ($W_{\omega}$ a projection) this is equivalent to quasi-equivalence, hence unitary equivalence, with $\omega_{0}$ on the whole generator algebra (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-powers-stormer-takesaki-disjointness}(a)): on the closed generator the condition is global normality restated. For mixed states it gives the square-integrable difference only, not quasi-equivalence.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Stationary states; proved, the boost case a corollary of the stored theorem.)} If $R$ is square integrable on a far end and $\omega$ is stationary for the affine translations, then $\omega = \omega_{0}$; if instead $\omega$ is stationary for the boost about a point, $\omega = \omega_{0}$ already by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}(iv), of which this is a corollary. So the condition gives (N$_{+}$) itself only together with one of the two stationarities.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The folium form of (N$_{+}$); proved for pure states, standard once (ii) holds.)} A pure $\omega$ with the condition of (ii) is a vector state of the null vacuum's representation, in which the affine translations are implemented with nonnegative generator $P$; so the positivity clause of (N$_{+}$) holds in the representation of $\omega$, and the averaged null energy along the complete generator relative to $\omega_{0}$, $\omega(P)$, is nonnegative wherever defined. The ground-state clause, $\omega = \omega_{0}$, is not implied: no condition depending only on the folium can single out $\omega_{0}$, since its normal excitations share it (the state with projection $P_{0} + |g\rangle\langle g|$).
\item[(v)] \emph{(Affine-KMS states; proved.)} A state KMS for the affine translations at temperature $T > 0$ differs from $\omega_{0}$ by the nonzero translation-invariant kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\big(\pi T/\sinh(\pi T s) - 1/s\big)$, $s = u - v$, with expansion $-\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\big(\tfrac{(\pi T)^{2}s}{6} - \tfrac{7(\pi T)^{4}s^{3}}{360} + \dots\big)$; a nonzero translation-invariant kernel is not square integrable on $(L, \infty)^{2}$ for any $L$. So these states, which satisfy the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition at every finite point, fail it on a single far end.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(The far ends must be joined; proved, given Powers-Stormer.)} Let $f$ be the regular reparametrisation with $f(u) = u$ for $u \le -1$, $f(u) = u/4$ for $u \ge 1$ and $f' = 1 - \tfrac34 S(\tfrac{u + 1}{2})$ on $[-1, 1]$, $S(t) = 6t^{5} - 15t^{4} + 10t^{3}$ ($C^{3}$, $f' \in [\tfrac14, 1]$), and $\omega_{f}$ the vacuum of the parameter $f$, $W_{f}(u, v) = \sqrt{f'(u)f'(v)}\,W_{0}(f(u), f(v))$, a pure state. Then: $W_{f} = W_{0}$ on $(-\infty, -1)^{2}$ and on $(1, \infty)^{2}$, so $\omega_{f}$ is the null vacuum on each far end; $\omega_{f}$ satisfies the local Hilbert-Schmidt condition on every bounded interval (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet}(iii)), so it is locally the null vacuum at every finite point; for every affine map $\alpha$ (translations, and boosts about every point) $\omega_{f}\circ\alpha$ is quasi-equivalent to $\omega_{f}$; and on $(1, \infty)\times(-\infty, -1)$, $W_{f} - W_{0} = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u + 2v)/((u - 4v)(u - v))$, homogeneous of degree $-1$ and not square integrable, so $\omega_{f}$ is disjoint from $\omega_{0}$ and fails the condition of (ii) on the arcs through $\infty$. With slope $1/\mu$ at $+\infty$ in place of $\tfrac14$ the cross-block difference is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\big(\sqrt{\mu}/(u - \mu v) - 1/(u - v)\big)$, and the states are mutually disjoint for different $\mu$ (slopes $\tfrac14$ and $\tfrac19$, $\mu = 4, 9$, differ by $-\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u + 6v)/((u - 4v)(u - 9v))$ on the cross block). In the coordinate $w = -1/u$ the reparametrisation has slope $1$ for $w > 0$ and $4$ for $w < 0$: $\omega_{f}$ is a kink at the point at infinity, the degree $-1$ obstruction of the stored half-thermal products at the edge (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}(v)) moved to infinity.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} The stationarity-free output is the folium form of (N$_{+}$), not (N$_{+}$): local normality to the null vacuum on every interval of the Moebius-closed generator, the point at infinity included, which for pure states is global quasi-equivalence with $\omega_{0}$ restated, and in which positivity of the affine translations is standard. It holds for $\omega_{0}$ and its normal excitations, gives (N$_{+}$) only with translation or boost stationarity, and excludes the affine-KMS states and the half-thermal products. The new content is the three-arc lemma, the failure of the affine-KMS states on one far end, and the slope-jump vacua: the far-away clause has to be posed on the arcs through $\infty$, which join the two ends, since the vacuum on each end separately, local normality at every finite point and implementability of the boosts about every point are all satisfied by the disjoint states $\omega_{f}$ (with a $C^{\infty}$ transition in place of the quintic, $\omega_{f}$ also has a smooth remainder on bounded intervals; argued). The condition is complementary to the microlocal condition on a generator (\claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}): that one is a short-distance condition at finite points, this one a condition at the point at infinity, and neither implies the other (the affine-KMS states and a smooth slope-jump vacuum pass the first and fail the second; $P_{0} + |g\rangle\langle g|$ with $g$ not smooth passes the second and fails the first). Even together they do not give (N$_{+}$) without stationarity: with $g$ a Schwartz function that state passes both and is not a ground state. The principle is the generator-algebra analogue of local normality (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haag-local-normality}), imported, not derived. Transport-absent; the closing of the generator is the standard Moebius covariance of the chiral vacuum, which the twistor attachment realises on null lines of Minkowski space.
synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-genera.technical: On a horizon generator the earlier local-normality result needs stationarity to turn a local condition into the premise (N$_{+}$). Without stationarity, local conditions at points cannot do it: states thermal for the affine translations look like the vacuum near every point. The remedy examined here is to impose the condition also far away, and the result shows exactly what that gives. On a single far end the thermal states already fail, since a translation-invariant difference accumulates without bound along the end. The vacuum on each end separately is not enough: the vacuum of a parameter whose slope at one end differs from the slope at the other is the vacuum on each end and near every finite point, admits every translation and boost as a symmetry of its folium, and is still disjoint from the vacuum, through a scale-invariant correlation between the two ends; seen from the point at infinity it is a kink, the same obstruction that the half-thermal products present at the edge. The chiral vacuum is covariant under Moebius maps of the generator, which the twistor attachment realises on null lines of Minkowski space, so the two ends meet at a regular point of a circle. Imposing local normality on every arc of that circle makes the difference square integrable globally, by a covering with three arcs. For pure states this is just global equivalence with the vacuum representation, in which the null energy is positive: the folium form of (N$_{+}$). Being the vacuum itself, the ground-state clause, still needs invariance under the boost or the translations; no condition on the folium can do more, because excitations of the vacuum share its folium. Checks: the conformal rotors in $\Cl(2,4)$ acting on the points of a null line, the Moebius invariance of the vacuum kernel, the arc cover, the series of $x/\sinh x$, and the slope-jump kernel identities with exact lower bounds on dilated rectangles.
synthesis.normality-on-the-closed-genera.lay: The series assumes that the quantum field on the light rays of a horizon is in its lowest-energy state. Earlier work showed that for a field that does not change in time this is the same as a standard locality requirement at the point where the horizon's light rays begin. Here the time-independence is dropped. Looking like the vacuum near every point of a light ray is not enough, since a warm state does so too; asking for the vacuum far along the ray rules out the warm state, but a subtler state still passes if the two far ends are tested separately. Joining the two ends of a light ray at one point, as the symmetries of the vacuum allow, and requiring the vacuum's local behaviour there as well puts the state in the vacuum's family, where energy along the ray is never negative; being the vacuum itself still needs time-independence.
flags: beyond one flat chart: the closing at infinity is the abstract Moebius covariance of the one-generator algebra and its vacuum; on null lines of Minkowski space (and on de Sitter horizons) the attachment realises it by conformal rotors, while on the eternal hole the point at infinity of a Kruskal generator is not a spacetime point joined by the attachment and only the abstract covariance is available

Implementability. For an affine map $\alpha$, $\omega_{f}\circ\alpha$ is the vacuum of the parameter $f\circ\alpha$; transporting by the unitary of $f^{-1}$, which maps $\omega_{f}$ to $\omega_{0}$, it is quasi-equivalent to $\omega_{f}$ exactly when the vacuum of $h = f\circ\alpha\circ f^{-1}$ is quasi-equivalent to $\omega_{0}$, that is (pure states, (ii)), when $W_{h} - W_{0}$ is square integrable on $\R^{2}$. So $W_{h} - W_{0}$ is square integrable and every translation and every dilation about $0$ is implementable in the representation of $\omega_{f}$; the boosts about other points are their composites. The slope jump between the two ends is what no affine map of the generator changes and what the arcs through $\infty$ detect.

\emph{Reading.} Statement (ii) uses the Hilbert-Schmidt form of local normality throughout; that the vacuum of a regular parameter is locally normal to $\omega_{0}$ on bounded intervals in the stronger sense of quasi-equivalence would follow from the implementability of smooth circle diffeomorphisms for the free chiral fermion (Segal; cited from memory, not used). The principle of local normality is Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haag-local-normality}, applied to the algebras of intervals of the closed generator; the closing itself is (i).
