synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a half-generator of a horizon with surface gravity $\kappa$ let $u = e^{\kappa\tau}$, $\tau$ the Killing time. Call the \emph{null ordering} the normal ordering at the null ground state of Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}, in which that state has $\langle T_{uu}\rangle = 0$, and the \emph{boost ordering} the normal ordering at the boost ground state (the Mellin vacuum). An evenly spaced array with weights $\omega_{k} = \kappa(k + \delta)$, $k \in \Z$, $0 \le \delta < 1$, has the single-particle spectrum of one chiral complex component on a Killing-time interval of length $2\pi/\kappa$ with a twisted condition (its real-time recurrence window; that the array is that component on a window of the continuum is part of the window reading of (iv)), the offset $\delta = \tfrac12$ being the antiperiodic condition of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} version 3. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The boost ground state on one window.)} The Schwarzian of $u = e^{\kappa\tau}$ is $\{u, \tau\} = -\kappa^{2}/2$, so the null ground state carries the Killing-frame energy density $\kappa^{2}/(48\pi)$ per complex component in the boost ordering, and the boost ground state $-\kappa^{2}/(48\pi)$ in the null ordering, the value of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit} at $c \to \infty$. Over one window of Killing time $2\pi/\kappa$ the boost ground state carries $-\kappa/24$ in the null ordering.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The array's sea selects the offset.)} The zeta-regularised energy of the filled sea of the array in the symmetric ordering (half of each mode below and above, $\sum_{k}\omega_{k}(\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{k} - \tfrac12)$) is $\tfrac{\kappa}{2}B_{2}(\delta)$ for $0 < \delta < 1$, with $B_{2}(a) = a^{2} - a + \tfrac16$, and $+\kappa/12$ at $\delta = 0$. Since
\[
\tfrac{\kappa}{2}B_{2}(\delta) + \tfrac{\kappa}{24} = \tfrac{\kappa}{2}\bigl(\delta - \tfrac12\bigr)^{2},
\]
the array's sea in its symmetric ordering carries the boost ground state's null-ordered window energy $-\kappa/24$ exactly when $\delta = \tfrac12$, a double root, and at no other offset.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The thermal state.)} At $\delta = \tfrac12$ and $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$ the array's energy above its sea is $\kappa/24$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}(i)), equal to the null ground state's energy over one window in the boost ordering; in the symmetric ordering of (ii), which at this offset gives the null ground state's window value (the identification of the two orderings is the hypothesis of (iv)), it is $0$, the null ground state's value in every window. At $\delta = 0$ the energy above the sea is $\beta E \in (0.0235, 0.0236)$, not $\pi/12$, and the symmetric value is not $0$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The counted units, under the window reading.)} Suppose (the window reading, Premise \claimref{synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-energy}) the Killing energy of an array is the continuum's Killing energy over its recurrence window (the discretisation reading of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(iv) applied to energy), measured, as (N$_{+}$) measures null energy, from the null ground state. Then at the weights of (Q) version 3 the physical ordering of the sea's energy is the zeta-regularised symmetric one; a counted unit of two arrays carries mean Killing energy $0$, the equality case of clause (v) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}; in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hole-mass-is-ground-energy-label}(iii) the constant of the hole's Hamiltonian is exactly $M$, and the label carries all of $M$, the counted units none. At the zero offset no ordering of the array is consistent with the null ordering window by window, since its symmetric sea is $+\kappa/12$, not $-\kappa/24$.
\end{enumerate}
So (N$_{+}$) decides the ordering question left open by the counted-unit energy result, given the window reading: the counted units carry no mean Killing energy, and the half offset of (Q) version 3 is the only offset at which the array's own zeta-regularised sea takes the continuum's null-ordered window value. Without the window reading, (i) to (iii) are equalities of numbers and the ordering is not decided.
synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units.technical:
The stored counted-unit result found that a counted unit at the weights of (Q) version 3 carries Killing energy $\kappa/12$ above its filled sea, and none in the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering, and left open which ordering is physical. (N$_{+}$) supplies the zero: the state of the horizon's light rays is the ground state of the affine null translations, and null energy is measured from it.

On one light ray, with Killing time $\tau$ and affine parameter $u = e^{\kappa\tau}$, the ground state of the affine translations and the ground state of the boost differ by the Schwarzian of the exponential map, $\{u, \tau\} = -\kappa^{2}/2$: measured from the null ground state the boost ground state has Killing-frame energy density $-\kappa^{2}/(48\pi)$, as the stored edge-scaling result found. An array with Killing-frequency spacing $\kappa$ has the spectrum of one chiral component on a Killing-time window of length $2\pi/\kappa$, and over that window the boost ground state carries $-\kappa/24$. The array's own boost ground state, its filled sea, has zeta-regularised symmetric energy $\tfrac{\kappa}{2}B_{2}(\delta)$, which equals $-\kappa/24$ exactly at the half offset: $\tfrac{\kappa}{2}B_{2}(\delta) + \tfrac{\kappa}{24} = \tfrac{\kappa}{2}(\delta - \tfrac12)^{2}$. At the half offset the array's thermal energy above its sea is also $\kappa/24$, so in the symmetric ordering the thermal array has energy zero, which is what the null ground state has on every window. The match is the standard modular relation between a chiral fermion's thermal state at temperature $\kappa/2\pi$ on the line and its antiperiodic vacuum on a circle of length $2\pi/\kappa$, whose Casimir energy is $-\tfrac{1}{24}\cdot\tfrac{2\pi}{L}$ (cited from memory); what is used here is that the antiperiodic, half-offset case is the only one where the array's zeta sea meets the continuum's null-ordered value. Under the window reading, which identifies the array's energy with the continuum's on its window as the continuum's on its window, the symmetric ordering is the physical one, the counted units carry no mean Killing energy, and the whole of $M$ sits in the constant of the hole's Hamiltonian.
synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units.lay: The series counts the black hole's entropy in small units on its horizon, and an earlier result found that whether those units carry any energy depended on a bookkeeping choice: where to put the zero of energy. The series' own premise about the state on the horizon's light rays fixes that zero: energy is measured from the lowest state for motion along the light rays. Measured that way, a stretch of light ray as long as one unit's natural cycle carries exactly the amount of energy that the zero-point bookkeeping of a unit assigns, but only if the unit's energy levels sit halfway between whole steps, which is the choice the series made. If a unit's energy is taken to be the energy of that stretch of light ray, then with that zero the units carry no energy on average, and the hole's mass sits entirely in one overall constant rather than in the counted units.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} For $u = e^{\kappa\tau}$ every derivative is a multiple of $u$: $u' = \kappa u$, $u'' = \kappa^{2}u$, $u''' = \kappa^{3}u$, so $\{u, \tau\} = u'''/u' - \tfrac32(u''/u')^{2} = \kappa^{2} - \tfrac32\kappa^{2} = -\kappa^{2}/2$. By the flux rule of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.collapse-in-vacuum-regular-at-future-horizon-selects-hawking-temperature} (the null energy flux of a chiral component's vacuum, normal ordered at an observer's vacuum, is $-\tfrac{1}{24\pi}$ times the Schwarzian of the map from its parameter to the observer's), the vacuum of $u$, which is the null ground state of (N$_{+}$) on the generator (Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}), normal ordered at the vacuum of $\tau$, which is the boost ground state, has Killing-frame energy density $-\tfrac{1}{24\pi}\cdot(-\tfrac{\kappa^{2}}{2}) = \kappa^{2}/(48\pi)$ per complex component. Independently, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit} gives the Killing-frame density $\kappa^{2}u^{2}\langle T_{uu}\rangle = \kappa^{2}(c^{-2} - 1)/(48\pi)$ of the period-$2\pi c$ state in the null ordering, which is $0$ for the null ground state ($c = 1$) and $-\kappa^{2}/(48\pi)$ for the boost ground state ($c \to \infty$): the two routes give the same difference with opposite orderings. (A third route: the null ground state's Mellin modes are Fermi-Dirac at rapidity period $2\pi$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(iii), so in the boost ordering a complex component has, per unit rapidity, $\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\cdot 2\int_{0}^{\infty}w\,dw/(e^{2\pi w} + 1) = \tfrac{1}{\pi}\cdot\tfrac{1}{4\pi^{2}}\cdot\tfrac{\pi^{2}}{12} = \tfrac{1}{48\pi}$, using $\int_{0}^{\infty}x\,dx/(e^{x} + 1) = \pi^{2}/12$, cited from memory and not in the check.) A Killing-time interval of length $2\pi/\kappa$ then carries $\tfrac{\kappa^{2}}{48\pi}\cdot\tfrac{2\pi}{\kappa} = \tfrac{\kappa}{24}$, the factors of $\pi$ cancelling, so the boost ground state carries $-\kappa/24$ per window in the null ordering. The check verifies the Schwarzian, the flux coefficient, the agreement with the stored density at $c^{-2} = 0$ and $1$, and the window product exactly at $\kappa = \tfrac14, \tfrac27, 3, \tfrac12$, with affine and M\"obius maps (Schwarzian $0$, no shift of the zero) as controls.

The array as a window (the spectral identity is exact; reading the array as that component on a window of the continuum is part of the window reading): a chiral complex component on a Killing-time interval of length $L$ with the condition $\psi(\tau + L) = e^{2\pi i\delta}\psi(\tau)$ has single-particle Killing frequencies $\tfrac{2\pi}{L}(k + \delta)$, $k \in \Z$; the array's spacing $\kappa$ is $L = 2\pi/\kappa$, its real-time recurrence period (the remark of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}), and $\delta = \tfrac12$ is the antiperiodic condition, the parity automorphism at one period noted for (Q) version 3 (Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}).

\emph{(ii)} For $0 < a \le 1$ put $h_{a}(\epsilon) = \sum_{n \ge 0}e^{-\epsilon(n + a)} = e^{-\epsilon a}/(1 - e^{-\epsilon})$, so $\sum_{n \ge 0}(n + a)e^{-\epsilon(n + a)} = -h_{a}'(\epsilon)$. Since $\epsilon h_{a}(\epsilon) = e^{-\epsilon a}\cdot\epsilon/(1 - e^{-\epsilon}) = \sum_{j}c_{j}\epsilon^{j}$ is a power series, $-h_{a}' = -\sum_{j}(j - 1)c_{j}\epsilon^{j - 2}$, whose finite part is $-c_{2}$; the generating function of the Bernoulli polynomials gives $c_{2} = B_{2}(1 - a)/2 = B_{2}(a)/2$, so the finite part is $-B_{2}(a)/2$, the Hurwitz value $\zeta(-1, a)$, with the rule of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}(ii) (finite part of the exponentially regulated sum). The check computes $c_{2}$ by exact power-series inversion for $a = \tfrac12, \tfrac14, \tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac15, 1$. In the symmetric ordering each mode contributes $-\tfrac12|\omega_{k}|$ to the sea: the particle tower $\kappa(n + \delta)$ and the hole tower $\kappa(n + 1 - \delta)$, $n \ge 0$, give $-\tfrac{\kappa}{2}\bigl(\zeta(-1, \delta) + \zeta(-1, 1 - \delta)\bigr) = \tfrac{\kappa}{4}\bigl(B_{2}(\delta) + B_{2}(1 - \delta)\bigr) = \tfrac{\kappa}{2}B_{2}(\delta)$ ($B_{2}$ is symmetric about $\tfrac12$). At $\delta = \tfrac12$ this is $-\kappa/24$, the value of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}(ii); at $\delta = 0$ the zero mode contributes nothing and the towers $\kappa n$, $n \ge 1$, give $-\kappa\zeta(-1, 1) = +\kappa/12$. Finally $\tfrac12B_{2}(\delta) + \tfrac1{24} = \tfrac12(\delta^{2} - \delta + \tfrac14) = \tfrac12(\delta - \tfrac12)^{2}$, which vanishes only at $\delta = \tfrac12$; the check verifies the identity at five offsets and four values of $\kappa$, and that equality with $-\kappa/24$ holds exactly when $\delta = \tfrac12$.

\emph{(iii)} At $\delta = \tfrac12$ and $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}(i) gives $\beta E = \pi/12$ above the sea, exactly by the theta-function identities of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-theta-function-identities}; the check confirms it to $10^{-15}$ with rigorous rational bounds (Machin's $\pi$, exponentials by halving and squaring with outward rounding, a geometric tail). By (i), $\beta\cdot\kappa/24 = \tfrac{2\pi}{\kappa}\cdot\tfrac{\kappa}{24} = \pi/12$: the array's thermal energy above its sea equals the null ground state's energy over one window in the boost ordering. Shifting by the sea's symmetric energy $-\kappa/24$ of (ii), $\beta E_{\mathrm{sym}} = \pi/12 - \pi/12 = 0$, and by (i) and (ii) this shift equals the change from the boost ordering to the null ordering on one window of the continuum (that the array's shift is that change is the window reading of (iv)); in the null ordering the null ground state has $\langle T_{uu}\rangle = 0$ (the stored density at $c = 1$), hence zero energy on every window. At $\delta = 0$, $\beta E \in (0.0235, 0.0236)$ (checked; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}(i) gives $(0.02351, 0.02352)$), which is not $\pi/12$, and $\beta E_{\mathrm{sym}} = \beta E + \pi/6 > 0$.

\emph{(iv)} Under the window reading (Premise \claimref{synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-energy}) the array's Killing energy in the physical zero of (N$_{+}$) is its energy in the null ordering on its window, which by (ii) and (iii) is the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering, with mean value $0$ in the thermal state. Two arrays, a counted unit, then carry $0$, so $E = 0 < TS$ realises the equality case $E = 0$ of clause (v) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}. In Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hole-mass-is-ground-energy-label}(iii) write the hole's Hamiltonian as $c + H_{\mathrm{sym}}$; the stored split (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}(iii)) has $c = E_{0}(M) + N\kappa/12$ with $E_{0}(M) = M - N\kappa/12$, so $c = M$ for every number $N$ of counted units, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{sym}}\rangle = 0$: the label carries all of $M$. At $\delta = 0$ the symmetric sea is $+\kappa/12$, while the boost ground state carries $-\kappa/24$ per window in the null ordering, so the array's symmetric ordering is not the null ordering, and no constant shift fixed by the array alone makes both its sea and its thermal state agree with the continuum window by window.

Scope and status: (i) to (iii) are proved (exact checks; the thermal value at the half offset rests on the imported theta identities, as stored). (iv) is conditional on the reading that an array's Killing energy is the continuum's over one recurrence window, the discretisation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(iv) applied to energy rather than to occupation; it is not derived here. Nothing here fixes the count unit (two arrays per registered mode) or derives the label's energy function.

synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-.formal:
Let $\Cl(p,q)$, $p + q \ge 2$, carry the frame $*$-structure of Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms} ($x^{*} = x$ for a frame generator with $Q(x) = 1$, $x^{*} = -x$ for one with $Q(x) = -1$, extended as an antiautomorphism, conjugate-linear on the complexification), let $V$ be its vectors, $E(x,y) := \br{x\,y^{*}}_{0}$, positive definite on $V$ with the frame orthonormal, and $h$ the same expression on $V_{\C}$, a positive Hermitian form. Write $\operatorname{ad}_{B}x = Bx - xB$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every bivector $B$, $\operatorname{ad}_{B}$ preserves $V$ and its $E$-adjoint is $\operatorname{ad}_{B^{*}}$. Every bivector splits uniquely as $B = B_{c} + B_{b}$ with $B_{c}^{*} = -B_{c}$ (spanned by $e_{i}e_{j}$ with $Q(e_{i}) = Q(e_{j})$) and $B_{b}^{*} = B_{b}$ (spanned by $e_{i}e_{j}$ with $Q(e_{i}) = -Q(e_{j})$, the boosts). The rotor flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda B})$ is a $*$-automorphism for all $\lambda$ if and only if $B_{b} = 0$, and then it acts on $V$ by $E$-orthogonal maps, with $\operatorname{ad}_{B}$ of purely imaginary spectrum.
\item[(ii)] No clock in the sense of Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}(ii) (adjoint action semisimple with a nonzero real eigenvalue) generates a $*$-automorphic flow, for any frame $*$-structure. The atom boost $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*}$ is $*$-symmetric, $\operatorname{ad}_{\sigma}$ has weights $-2, +2$ on $v, v^{*}$, and its rotor flow $v \mapsto e^{-\lambda}v$, $v^{*} \mapsto e^{\lambda}v^{*}$ is not a $*$-map.
\item[(iii)] Let $H = H^{*}$ be a quadratic element of a complexified window (for instance $K = \sigma/2$, $\sum_{j}\omega_{j}K_{j}$, or these plus any hop or pairing coupling). Then $\operatorname{ad}_{H}$ is $h$-Hermitian on $V_{\C}$, $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itH})$ is a $*$-automorphism acting on $V_{\C}$ by $h$-unitary maps (the compact Bogoliubov group, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}), and $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda H})$ with $\lambda$ real and nonzero is not a $*$-map unless $H$ is a scalar. If $H = \kappa K_{\mathrm{tot}} + W$ with $K_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{j}(N_{j} - \tfrac12)$ and $W$ gauge-invariant, the boost multiplies every evolved mode operator by the common phase $e^{-i\kappa t}$ and the moduli of its coefficients do not depend on $\kappa$. If $W = g(a_{1}^{*}a_{2}^{*} + a_{2}a_{1})$ on two modes, $\operatorname{ad}_{H}$ on $(a_{1}, a_{2}^{*})$ is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-\kappa & -g\\ -g & \kappa\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with square $\Omega^{2} = \kappa^{2} + g^{2}$: the unitary flow is trigonometric at frequency $\Omega$ and moves at most $g^{2}/(\kappa^{2} + g^{2})$ of the weight of $a_{1}$ onto $a_{2}^{*}$, so in real time the boost detunes, while the real-parameter flow grows as $\cosh(\Omega\lambda)$.
\item[(iv)] The common-rapidity rotor flow $\alpha_{\lambda}(a_{j}) = e^{-\lambda}a_{j}$ does not map states to states: for every $\lambda \neq 0$ there are an even pure two-mode state $\omega = c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ (a thermofield pair, $c\cosh 2\lambda > 1$) and $X = a_{1}a_{2} - t$ with $\omega(\alpha_{\lambda}(X^{*}X)) = s^{2}(1 - c^{2}\cosh^{2}2\lambda) < 0$.
\item[(v)] The rotor flow is the phase flow $\tau_{t} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK})$ at imaginary parameter, $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda K}) = \tau_{-i\lambda}$, and at rapidity $\beta$ it is the KMS swap of the Gibbs state $\omega_{\beta}$ of $K$: $\omega_{\beta}(A\,\operatorname{Ad}(e^{-\beta K})(B)) = \omega_{\beta}(BA)$ for all $A, B$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence, taking a physical time evolution to be a one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms that preserves the state space, the time evolution of a window is the phase flow, the boost dynamics of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}, and the rotor flow is its continuation into the KMS strip; by (i), (ii), (iv) and (v) this holds for every bivector and every clock, not only for quadratic dynamics. On the CAR windows, the growth step of Assumption \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated}, that a quadratic generator containing the boost scales the ladder operators by $e^{\pm\kappa t}$, holds for the rotor flow only: under any quadratic time evolution of the windows the $h$-norm of an evolved mode operator is conserved (the fermionic Bogoliubov group is compact) and the boost contributes a phase or a detuning, so for the quadratic dynamics that law assumes the rate $\kappa$ of $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$ is an imaginary-time rate, and the chaos-bound comparison of that rate with $2\pi T$ is the identity $\kappa = 2\pi/\beta$ of (R), not a statement about real-time spreading on the windows. This restriction is to the CAR windows: bosonic or geometric boosts, such as the real-time blueshift $p_{U} \mapsto e^{\kappa t}p_{U}$ of Kruskal momenta in shock-wave scrambling arguments, are unitary and grow exponentially in real time, and nothing here bears on them or on non-quadratic generators.
synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-.technical:
In the real Clifford algebra with the tower's frame $*$-structure, the bivectors split into a compact part ($*$-antisymmetric: rotations among generators of equal square) and a boost part ($*$-symmetric: mixed planes). The $E$-adjoint of $\operatorname{ad}_{B}$ on vectors is $\operatorname{ad}_{B^{*}}$, so a bivector flow preserves the $*$-structure exactly when it has no boost part, and such flows act on vectors orthogonally, with imaginary spectrum. A clock, whose adjoint action has a real nonzero eigenvalue, is therefore never a $*$-automorphism, and the atom's boost rotor, which scales $v$ and $v^{*}$ by $e^{\mp\lambda}$, is not one.

On the complexified windows every self-adjoint quadratic generator $H$ gives the unitary flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itH})$, acting on the mode operators through the compact Bogoliubov group; the same generator at a real parameter is not a $*$-map. For a gauge-invariant coupling the boost only multiplies every mode operator by a common phase; for a pairing coupling it detunes, capping the transferred weight at $g^{2}/(\kappa^{2} + g^{2})$, while the real-parameter flow of the same generator grows as $\cosh$. The rotor flow at common rapidity sends a thermofield pair to a functional that is negative on a positive element, so it is not an evolution of states. It is the phase flow at imaginary time, and at rapidity $\beta$ it is the KMS swap of the Gibbs state.

So, taking a time evolution to be a group of $*$-automorphisms preserving the states, the phase flow is the window's time evolution and the rotor flow its KMS-strip continuation. On the CAR windows the spreading law's exponential growth $e^{\kappa t}$ is the rotor flow's: under any quadratic time evolution of the windows the norm of an evolved mode operator is conserved and the boost supplies a phase or a detuning, so for the quadratic dynamics the law assumes, the chaos-bound comparison reduces to $\kappa = 2\pi/\beta$, which is (R). Bosonic or geometric boosts, such as the real-time blueshift of Kruskal momenta, do grow exponentially in real time and are outside this statement.
synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-.lay: The papers used one name for two motions built from the same ingredient: a stretching that makes some quantities grow exponentially, and a turning that rotates each quantum mode's phase like a clock hand. This result decides which one is the real passage of time. Only the turning respects the rules of quantum theory: the stretching would turn some legitimate quantum states into impossible ones with negative probabilities. The stretching is the turning run in imaginary time, the device behind black-hole temperature, and at one full thermal period it is exactly the swap that defines thermal equilibrium. The series' fast-scrambling argument for the boundary modes relied on the stretching's exponential growth. For the simple (quadratic) dynamics of those fermionic modes, that growth belongs to imaginary time, not to the actual evolution, and the claimed match with the quantum chaos bound reduces to the definition of the temperature. This is a statement about the series' fermionic boundary modes only: in standard treatments of black-hole scrambling, other ingredients (gravitational blueshift, interactions) do grow exponentially in real time.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} For a bivector $B$ and a vector $x$, $Bx - xB = 2\,B \cdot x$ is a vector, so $\operatorname{ad}_{B}$ preserves $V$. The $*$-operation of Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms} is an antiautomorphism with $(B^{*})^{*} = B$, and the scalar part is cyclic, $\br{XY}_{0} = \br{YX}_{0}$. Hence
\[
E(\operatorname{ad}_{B}x, y) = \br{Bxy^{*}}_{0} - \br{xBy^{*}}_{0} = \br{xy^{*}B}_{0} - \br{xBy^{*}}_{0} = \br{x\,(B^{*}y - yB^{*})^{*}}_{0} = E(x, \operatorname{ad}_{B^{*}}y),
\]
using $(B^{*}y)^{*} = y^{*}B$ and $(yB^{*})^{*} = By^{*}$. On a frame generator $\br{e_{i}e_{i}^{*}}_{0} = Q(e_{i})\cdot Q(e_{i}) = 1$ and distinct frame generators give $0$, so $E$ is positive definite with the frame orthonormal. For $i < j$, $(e_{i}e_{j})^{*} = e_{j}^{*}e_{i}^{*} = Q(e_{i})Q(e_{j})\,e_{j}e_{i} = -Q(e_{i})Q(e_{j})\,e_{i}e_{j}$, which is $-e_{i}e_{j}$ when the squares agree and $+e_{i}e_{j}$ when they differ; this gives the unique splitting $B = B_{c} + B_{b}$. If $B_{b} = 0$ then $(e^{\lambda B})^{*} = e^{\lambda B^{*}} = e^{-\lambda B}$, so $e^{\lambda B}$ is unitary and $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda B})$ commutes with $*$; by the adjoint formula $\operatorname{ad}_{B}$ is $E$-antisymmetric, so its spectrum is imaginary and $e^{\lambda\operatorname{ad}_{B}}$ is $E$-orthogonal. Conversely, if $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda B})$ commutes with $*$ for all $\lambda$, differentiating at $\lambda = 0$ gives $(\operatorname{ad}_{B}X)^{*} = \operatorname{ad}_{B}(X^{*})$, that is $X^{*}(B + B^{*}) = (B + B^{*})X^{*}$ for all $X$, so $B + B^{*} = 2B_{b}$ is central; the centre of $\Cl(p,q)$ is spanned by $1$ and, for $p + q$ odd, the volume element of grade $p + q \ge 3$, so it contains no nonzero bivector and $B_{b} = 0$.

\emph{(ii)} Let $X$ be a clock in the sense of Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}(ii), so $\operatorname{ad}_{X}$ is semisimple with a real eigenvalue $c \neq 0$ and real eigenvector $x \in V$. If $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda X})$ were $*$-automorphic for some frame $*$-structure, (i) would make $\operatorname{ad}_{X}$ antisymmetric for that frame's $E$, and $cE(x,x) = E(\operatorname{ad}_{X}x, x) = -E(x, \operatorname{ad}_{X}x) = -cE(x,x)$ with $E(x,x) > 0$ forces $c = 0$, a contradiction. For the atom of $\Cl(1,1)$ with $v = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{+} - e_{-})$ the CAR hold and $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*} = e_{+}e_{-}$, $\sigma^{2} = 1$, $\sigma^{*} = \sigma$, $\operatorname{ad}_{\sigma}v = -2v$, $\operatorname{ad}_{\sigma}v^{*} = 2v^{*}$; the rotor $R_{\lambda} = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2} + \sigma\sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}$ gives $v \mapsto e^{-\lambda}v$, $v^{*} \mapsto e^{\lambda}v^{*}$, and since $(e^{-\lambda}v)^{*} = e^{-\lambda}v^{*} \neq e^{\lambda}v^{*}$ for $\lambda \neq 0$ it is not a $*$-map (this is the single-plane clause of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.boost-modes}). The script also checks (ii) for clocks obtained by conjugating an atom boost of $\Cl(2,2)$ with boost and rotation rotors (the real eigenvalue survives, the boost part is nonzero, and $\operatorname{ad}_{X}$ is not $E$-antisymmetric), and it checks (i) and (ii) on random rational bivectors of $\Cl(1,1)$, $\Cl(2,2)$, $\Cl(3,3)$, $\Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl(3,1)$, $\Cl(2,4)$ and on the atom at $e^{\lambda/2} = 2$.

\emph{(iii)} The adjoint formula of (i) holds verbatim for $h$ on $V_{\C}$ with $*$ conjugate-linear. For $H = H^{*}$, $\operatorname{ad}_{H}$ is $h$-Hermitian, so $i\operatorname{ad}_{H}$ is $h$-anti-Hermitian and $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itH}) = e^{it\operatorname{ad}_{H}}$ is $h$-unitary on $V_{\C}$; $e^{itH}$ is unitary, so the flow is a $*$-automorphism. On the Majorana generators the unitary maps preserving the CAR form the compact group of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}. For real $\lambda$, $(\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda H})X)^{*} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{-\lambda H})(X^{*})$, which equals $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda H})(X^{*})$ for all $X$ only if $e^{2\lambda H}$ is central in the window, a matrix factor, hence a positive scalar, hence $H$ a scalar. If $W$ is gauge-invariant, $[K_{\mathrm{tot}}, W] = 0$, so $e^{it(\kappa K_{\mathrm{tot}} + W)} = e^{it\kappa K_{\mathrm{tot}}}e^{itW}$, and $[K_{\mathrm{tot}}, a_{j}] = -a_{j}$ gives $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{it\kappa K_{\mathrm{tot}}})a_{j} = e^{-i\kappa t}a_{j}$ for every $j$, a common phase. For the pairing generator, $[N_{1}, a_{1}] = -a_{1}$, $[N_{2}, a_{2}^{*}] = a_{2}^{*}$, $[a_{1}^{*}a_{2}^{*}, a_{1}] = -a_{2}^{*}$, $[a_{2}a_{1}, a_{2}^{*}] = -a_{1}$ and the other brackets vanish, so $\operatorname{ad}_{H}$ on $(a_{1}, a_{2}^{*})$ is the matrix $M$ stated, with $M^{2} = \Omega^{2}$. Hence $e^{itM} = \cos\Omega t + i\,(\sin\Omega t)\,M/\Omega$, which sends $a_{1}$ to $(\cos\Omega t - i\tfrac{\kappa}{\Omega}\sin\Omega t)\,a_{1} - i\tfrac{g}{\Omega}(\sin\Omega t)\,a_{2}^{*}$, of conserved weight $1$ and transferred weight $\tfrac{g^{2}}{\Omega^{2}}\sin^{2}\Omega t \le g^{2}/(\kappa^{2} + g^{2})$, while $e^{\lambda M} = \cosh\Omega\lambda + (\sinh\Omega\lambda)\,M/\Omega$. On the Fock space $H$ vanishes on the odd sector and $H^{2} = \Omega^{2}$ on the even sector, so $e^{itH} = \cos\Omega t\,P_{\mathrm{even}} + i\sin\Omega t\,H/\Omega + P_{\mathrm{odd}}$; the script builds it over $\Q(i)$ at rational points of the circle, checks unitarity and the group law, and compares $e^{itH}a_{1}e^{-itH}$ with the stated combination. It also verifies the brackets, $M^{2} = \Omega^{2}$ and the weights in Jordan-Wigner matrices at $(\kappa, g, \Omega) = (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (0,1,1)$, and $[K_{\mathrm{tot}}, a_{1}^{*}a_{2} + a_{2}^{*}a_{1}] = 0$.

\emph{(iv)} $\alpha_{\lambda}$ is an algebra automorphism with $\alpha_{\lambda}(a_{1}a_{2}) = e^{-2\lambda}a_{1}a_{2}$, $\alpha_{\lambda}(a_{2}^{*}a_{1}^{*}) = e^{2\lambda}a_{2}^{*}a_{1}^{*}$ and $\alpha_{\lambda}(N_{1}N_{2}) = N_{1}N_{2}$. For $X = a_{1}a_{2} - t$, $X^{*}X = N_{1}N_{2} - t\,a_{2}^{*}a_{1}^{*} - t\,a_{1}a_{2} + t^{2}$ is positive and $\alpha_{\lambda}(X^{*}X) = N_{1}N_{2} - te^{2\lambda}a_{2}^{*}a_{1}^{*} - te^{-2\lambda}a_{1}a_{2} + t^{2}$. In $\omega = c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ ($c^{2} + s^{2} = 1$, $c, s > 0$), $\omega(N_{1}N_{2}) = s^{2}$ and $\omega(a_{1}a_{2}) = \omega(a_{2}^{*}a_{1}^{*}) = \epsilon cs$ with $\epsilon = \pm 1$ fixed by the ordering, so $\omega(\alpha_{\lambda}(X^{*}X)) = s^{2} - 2t\epsilon cs\cosh 2\lambda + t^{2}$, which at $t = \epsilon cs\cosh 2\lambda$ equals $s^{2}(1 - c^{2}\cosh^{2}2\lambda)$. For $\lambda \neq 0$ choose $c \in (1/\cosh 2\lambda, 1)$; the value is negative while $\omega(X^{*}X) \ge 0$. The script evaluates it exactly at $e^{2\lambda} = 4, 2, \tfrac{11}{10}$ with $(c,s) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35), (\tfrac{12}{13}, \tfrac{5}{13}), (\tfrac{899}{901}, \tfrac{60}{901})$.

\emph{(v)} $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{\lambda K}) = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{i(-i\lambda)K}) = \tau_{-i\lambda}$ is the definition of the continuation (Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}). With $\varrho = e^{-\beta K}/\Tr e^{-\beta K}$, the unique KMS state of the phase flow on the factor (Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}), $\omega_{\beta}(A\,e^{-\beta K}Be^{\beta K}) = \Tr(e^{-\beta K}Ae^{-\beta K}Be^{\beta K})/\Tr e^{-\beta K} = \Tr(Ae^{-\beta K}B)/\Tr e^{-\beta K} = \omega_{\beta}(BA)$ by cyclicity of the trace. The script checks it on all matrix units of the mode for $e^{\beta/2} = 2, \tfrac32, \tfrac75$.

\emph{The reading.} Take a physical time evolution to be a one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms preserving the state space (the hypothesis of the concluding paragraph). By (i), (ii) and (iv) the rotor flow is not a $*$-automorphism and does not preserve the state space, so it is not the evolution of any state; by (iii) the phase flow and every quadratic perturbation of it are $*$-automorphisms, and the phase flow is the boost dynamics of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}; by (v) the rotor flow is its imaginary-parameter continuation and implements the KMS condition at rapidity $\beta$. The growth step of Assumption \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} exponentiates the real weights $\mp 1$ of the boost with a real parameter, which by (ii) is the rotor flow; by (iii) the same generator in real time conserves the $h$-norm of every evolved mode operator and contributes a phase (gauge-invariant couplings) or a detuning (pairing couplings). The rate $\kappa$ in $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$ is therefore the rotor flow's, and its equality with $2\pi T$ is $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, the content of (R). The conservation of the $h$-norm is a property of the compact fermionic Bogoliubov group of the CAR windows; nothing here bears on non-quadratic generators, or on bosonic and geometric boosts (for instance the real-time blueshift of Kruskal momenta), which are unitary and grow exponentially in real time.

synthesis.point-spectrum-boost-admits-no.technical: The series' best candidate for supplying the Hawking temperature from a principle stated in its own algebra is the Bisognano-Wichmann and Borchers mechanism: if the boost acts on a group of positive-energy translations by dilating them, the modular flow of the vacuum is that boost at exactly the rate $2\pi$, so the temperature would follow from positivity of energy instead of from the thermal premise (R). The store had already noted that a finite window cannot carry such translations. This result extends that to every setting the series uses for the boundary modes before the continuum: the whole countable mode space (with any real weights, including those of (Q)) and the Hilbert space of any boost-invariant state on it. The reason is that the boost there acts by phases on the modes, so it has pure point spectrum: every vector in a dense set moves on a compact orbit, and a translation group that the boost dilates is then forced to act trivially, by squeezing the translation parameter to zero along the orbit. So the half-sided translations that would fix $2\pi$ are trivial on these spaces, and a derivation of (R) along this route must use the continuum mode space, where the boost has continuous spectrum. Under (Q)'s weights the flow is even periodic, returning to the identity after exactly one modular period.
synthesis.point-spectrum-boost-admits-no.lay: One hope for explaining the black-hole temperature without simply assuming it uses a celebrated theorem: if the time-stretching symmetry at a horizon acts on a family of positive-energy shifts by rescaling them, the temperature comes out automatically with the right value. This result shows that the discrete models the series uses for the horizon's quantum modes cannot host that mechanism: their time evolution only ever returns close to where it started, and a rescaling that never escapes a bounded region can only rescale shifts that do nothing. The mechanism needs a genuinely continuous spectrum of mode energies, so any derivation of the temperature along these lines has to be built on the series' continuum description of the modes.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} By Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} the dynamics multiplies each generator $a_{j}$ by a phase, so it maps each window algebra $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$, the algebra generated by $\{a_{j}\}_{j \in F}$, onto itself; on $\mathfrak{A}_{F} \cong \End(\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{F})$ it is $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK})$ with $K = \sum_{j \in F}\omega_{j}N_{j}$ (in the Fock basis of the window each monomial in the $a_{j}, a_{j}^{\dagger}$ picks up the phase of its net weight, the same as under $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{itK})$). The orbit $\{\tau_{t}(x)\}_{t}$ of $x \in \mathfrak{A}_{F}$ is a bounded subset of the finite-dimensional space $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$, since each $\tau_{t}$ is isometric, so its closure $K_{x}$ is compact. Since $K$ is self-adjoint, $\operatorname{ad}K$ is diagonalisable on $\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ with real eigenvalues, the differences of eigenvalues of $K$; so $[K, P] = icP$ with $c$ real and nonzero has only $P = 0$. This is the finite-window obstruction (an element scaled by a real exponential cannot be an eigenvector of a unitary flow) in exact form; Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2) shows the real scaling $v \mapsto e^{-\lambda}v$ is carried by the rotor flow, which is not a $*$-automorphism. The script verifies it on a three-mode window for the weights $(-1, 0, 1)$ and $(1, 2, 3)$: the real form of the equation, $[K, X] = -cY$ and $[K, Y] = cX$ for $P = X + iY$, has full rank for $c = 1, 2, 7$, while at $c = 0$ its solution space has dimension twice the dimension of the commutant of $K$ ($24$ and $10$, the sums of squared multiplicities of the two spectra).

\emph{(ii)} Fix $a \in \R$ and $x \in \mathfrak{A}_{F}$. The covariance gives $\gamma_{a} = \tau_{t}\circ\gamma_{e^{-ct}a}\circ\tau_{-t}$ for every $t$, so, with $s = e^{-ct}a$ and $y_{t} = \tau_{-t}(x) \in K_{x}$,
\[
\|\gamma_{a}(x) - x\| \;=\; \bigl\|\tau_{t}\bigl(\gamma_{s}(y_{t}) - y_{t}\bigr)\bigr\| \;=\; \|\gamma_{s}(y_{t}) - y_{t}\| .
\]
Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and cover the compact set $K_{x}$ by finitely many balls $B(y_{i}, \varepsilon)$. By strong continuity there is $\delta > 0$ with $\|\gamma_{s}(y_{i}) - y_{i}\| < \varepsilon$ for all $i$ whenever $|s| < \delta$, and since each $\gamma_{s}$ is isometric, $\|\gamma_{s}(y) - y\| \le \|\gamma_{s}(y - y_{i})\| + \|\gamma_{s}(y_{i}) - y_{i}\| + \|y_{i} - y\| < 3\varepsilon$ for every $y \in K_{x}$ and $|s| < \delta$. Choosing $t$ with $ct$ so large that $e^{-ct}|a| < \delta$ gives $\|\gamma_{a}(x) - x\| < 3\varepsilon$. Hence $\gamma_{a}(x) = x$ on the dense subalgebra $\bigcup_{F}\mathfrak{A}_{F}$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}: the CAR algebra is the closure of the union of the windows), and $\gamma_{a} = \id$ by continuity.

\emph{(iii)} Invariance of $\omega$ makes $V_{t}$ well defined and unitary. For $x \in \mathfrak{A}_{F}$ the orbit $V_{t}\pi(x)\Omega = \pi(\tau_{t}(x))\Omega$ is the image of the orbit of $x$ under the bounded map $y \mapsto \pi(y)\Omega$, so its closure is compact. The argument of (ii), with $U(a)$ unitary in place of $\gamma_{a}$ and vectors in place of elements, gives $U(a)\pi(x)\Omega = \pi(x)\Omega$ for every $x$ in the union of the windows; these vectors are dense because $\Omega$ is cyclic, so $U(a) = 1$. If $\Delta^{is} = V_{-\beta s}$, the conclusion of the abstract theorem of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}, $\Delta^{is}U(a)\Delta^{-is} = U(e^{-2\pi s}a)$, reads $V_{t}U(a)V_{-t} = U(e^{2\pi t/\beta}a)$ with $t = -\beta s$, the hypothesis of (iii) with $c = 2\pi/\beta \neq 0$, so any $U$ satisfying that theorem's hypotheses is trivial. For a faithful $(\tau, \beta)$-KMS state the modular group is $\sigma_{s} = \tau_{-\beta s}$ by the correspondence between the KMS condition and modular theory (Takesaki, cited from memory; on a matrix factor it is the explicit computation of Proposition \claimref{singularity.modular-theory-matrix-factor-proved-outright}, $\sigma_{s}(a) = \rho^{is}a\rho^{-is}$ with $\rho \propto e^{-\beta K}$), and $\Delta^{is}\pi(x)\Omega = \pi(\sigma_{s}(x))\Omega = V_{-\beta s}\pi(x)\Omega$ on a dense set, which is the case named in the statement.

\emph{(iv)} For $\omega_{k} = \kappa k$, $\tau_{2\pi/\kappa}(a_{k}) = e^{-2\pi ik}a_{k} = a_{k}$; for $\omega_{k} = \kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, $\tau_{2\pi/\kappa}(a_{k}) = e^{-i\pi(2k+1)}a_{k} = -a_{k}$. The script checks the integrality behind both on a three-mode window: for the weights $(-1, 0, 1)$ every eigenvalue of $\operatorname{ad}K$ is an integer (the set is $\{-2, \ldots, 2\}$); for $(\tfrac12, \tfrac32, \tfrac52)$ the eigenvalues lie in $\tfrac12\Z$, are integers exactly on even matrix units, and reach $\tfrac92$.

For the consequence: the theorem of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses} produces $2\pi$ only from a nontrivial $U$; by (ii) and (iii) none exists on the spaces named, for any $\beta$ and any real weights. On the continuum mode space with a Hamiltonian of continuous spectrum the compactness used in (ii) fails, and the imported free-field examples realise the mechanism there; whether the boundary modes of the series satisfy the remaining hypotheses on that space is not addressed.

synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-p.formal:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be one of: (a) the future event horizon of the eternal (Kruskal-extended) Schwarzschild solution of mass $M$; (b) the future cosmological horizon of the static patch of de Sitter space with $\Lambda = 3H^{2}$; (c) a local Rindler horizon $\mathcal{H}_{p,\ell}$ of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} in Minkowski space, flat spacetime with vanishing gravitational field ($\hb = 1$, $\Omega = 0$; Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). Let $\xi$ be its boost (the Killing flow in (a), (b); the local boost in (c), with time measured in rapidity) and $\kappa$ its surface gravity: $\kappa = 1/(4M)$, $H$, $1$. On each generator let $u$ be the affine parameter with $u = 0$ on the bifurcation (edge) surface, defined on the whole generator $u \in \R$ of the extended solution, and normalised so that $\xi = \kappa u\,\partial_{u}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. Let $\mathfrak{h} = L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K$ ($K$ the transverse and internal labels) and $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ the continuum mode space of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, generated by the fields $\psi(u)$ with $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)\otimes\id_{K}$, carrying the null translations $\nu_{a}(\psi(u)) = \psi(u + a)$ and the boost $\beta_{t}(\psi(u)) = e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$ (the weight $\tfrac12$ is the one for which $\beta_{t}$ preserves the anticommutator). Hypothesis (N$_{+}$), Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}: the state $\omega$ is gauge-invariant and quasi-free (assumed, not derived), invariant under $\nu$, and the generator of $\nu$ in its GNS representation is positive.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The null vacuum.)} Under (N$_{+}$) the symbol of $\omega$ is $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$, where $P = i\,d/du$ is the one-particle generator of $\nu$, $\nu_{a}(a(f)) = a(e^{iaP}f)$: $\omega(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u)) = \dfrac{i}{2\pi}\dfrac{1}{u - v + i0}\otimes\id_{K}$. No other gauge-invariant quasi-free state satisfies (N$_{+}$).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The factor $2\pi$.)} The subalgebra $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{+}, du)\otimes K)$ of the modes beyond the edge is $\beta$-invariant, and the restriction of $\omega$ to it is the continuum I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} for the one-particle boost generator $h$ at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$: on $u^{-1/2 + iw}$, $h$ acts as $-\kappa w$ and the symbol is $(1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1} = (1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$. It is jointly KMS on the whole subalgebra and even, and it is the unique $\beta$-KMS state there. The same holds on the past half $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{-}, du)\otimes K)$ for the boost that is future-directed there, $\beta_{-t}$, with symbol $(1 + e^{2\pi w})^{-1}$ on $|u|^{-1/2 + iw}$; the reflection $u \mapsto -u$ exchanges the two statements. Positivity fixes the sign (the opposite sign gives $-2\pi/\kappa$), and the one-sided support is needed (on the full generator the boost-continued two-point function has a pole at imaginary rapidity $\pi$, and the restriction of $\omega$ there is pure); the period $2\pi$ is the first return of the rotated half-generator $e^{i\theta}\R_{+}$ to itself.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The continuum restatements follow.)} Hence: on (a), the modes of the generators are jointly KMS for the Killing flow at $\beta = 8\pi M$, Fermi-Dirac with density $(1 + e^{2\pi\varpi/\kappa})^{-1}$ in Killing frequency $\varpi$: the continuum restatement of (R) (Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) for the eternal hole, (N$_{+}$) being there a Hartle-Hawking-type regularity condition on the whole Kruskal generator; a hole formed by collapse is not covered (its horizon generators have no $u < 0$ half, and its physical state is not a ground state for $\nu$ on the horizon). On (b), the same at $\beta = 2\pi/H$: the continuum restatement of (R$_{\Lambda}$) (Premise \claimref{synthesis.r-lambda-regularity-cosmological-horizon}). On (c), on the past half of the generators, which is the half the premise's patch uses, joint KMS for the future-directed local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$ on the patch's whole mode algebra: the continuum restatement of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$). In each case the state is jointly KMS and even: the joint KMS part of (Q) (Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}); its quasi-freeness is a hypothesis of (N$_{+}$), and its weight clause ($\omega_{k} = \kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ in version 3 of (Q), $\kappa k$ in version 2) is not given.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Only on the continuum.)} (N$_{+}$) needs a nontrivial strongly continuous translation group dilated by the boost at rate $\kappa$; by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.point-spectrum-boost-admits-no-half-sided-translations} there is none when the boost acts by phases on a generating set of modes, so (N$_{+}$) cannot be posed on the windows, the countable mode space or the array of (Q). The stored wordings of (R), (R$_{\Lambda}$) and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), on point-spectrum mode sets with phase-acting flows, are discretisations of the statements in (iii): the boost has no eigenvectors on the continuum, a normalisable mode $f$ has occupation $\int|\hat f(w)|^{2}m(w)\,dw$, and the ladder values $m(w_{j})$ are recovered only for modes of vanishing Mellin width.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Positivity from the spectrum condition.)} If a representation of the spacetime translations has spectrum in the closed forward cone, every future null translation has a positive generator: $\ip{\ell}{p} \ge 0$ for $p$ in the closed forward cone and $\ell$ future null, with equality only on the ray of $\ell$. In the conformal model $\Cl(2,4)$ the null translation $1 + \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\ell\nInf$ along a generator, the boost and the dilation (both unit boosts) satisfy the $ax{+}b$ relation of the Borchers form of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}, the boost and the dilation agreeing on the generator and differing off it.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The whole generator of the eternal horizon (case (a)) and of the de Sitter cosmological horizon (case (b)), through its bifurcation surface, is global and is not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region are in GTG, and the whole generator, through its bifurcation surface, is read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-p.technical:
The series carries three thermal premises of one shape: (R) at the black-hole horizon, (R$_{\Lambda}$) at the cosmological horizon, and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) on every local Rindler horizon. Each asserts that boundary modes are KMS for a boost at the period where the boost's Euclidean section is smooth. This result restates them on the continuum of a horizon's null generators and derives that restated content from one premise with no temperature in it. Place the modes on the generators, with the affine null translations along them. Premise (N$_{+}$) asks that a gauge-invariant quasi-free state be a ground state for those translations: invariant, with positive generator. That fixes the state as the filled sea of every generator. Restricted to either side of the edge, it is the continuum I-state at rapidity period exactly $2\pi$ for the boost that is future-directed on that side. The local-horizon premise and the Einstein derivation use the past side, the generators ending on the edge.

The computation is one line in the Mellin basis $u^{-1/2 + iw}$, which diagonalises the boost: the compressed sea projection has symbol $(1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1}$. Equivalently, the boost-continued two-point function is analytic across the strip of width $2\pi$ in imaginary rapidity, with the KMS boundary values. Positivity fixes the sign of the period, and restriction to one side of the edge is needed (on the whole generator the state is pure). The weight $\tfrac12$ of the field is forced by the anticommutator, not chosen; integer-weight (bosonic) fields give the same $2\pi$. Every horizon of the three kinds acts on its generators' affine parameter as the dilation $u \mapsto e^{\kappa t}u$. This is the null-plane form of the results of Bisognano-Wichmann, Hislop-Longo, Sewell and Kay-Wald (Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}), transport-absent in its analytic core. What is new for the store is its execution on the continuum mode space with the store's conventions, where the point-spectrum no-go left the route open.

What the restatement costs, and what it does not cover. First, the carrier is the continuum: (N$_{+}$) cannot be posed on the point-spectrum mode sets, and the stored wordings become discretisations, recovered only for modes of vanishing Mellin width. The carrier must change in any case. On point-spectrum mode sets with phase-acting flows, (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) as worded is satisfiable at nonzero weight only if no mode is shared by two local horizons whose boosts act by inverse flows (filed alongside, synthesis.r-loc-needs-sheet-labelled-modes). The continuum carrier meets this automatically: the past halves of the two sheets of one edge are different null half-planes, the past and future halves of one generator are disjoint half-line algebras, and the edge is a null set that carries no mode. Second, at a Killing horizon (N$_{+}$) is the regularity of the state across the bifurcation surface, posed on the whole generator of the extended solution: the Hartle-Hawking-type state of the eternal hole. A hole formed by collapse has no $u < 0$ half, and its physical state is not a null-translation ground state on the horizon, so it is not covered. Third, the thermal input is relocated, not removed: the regularity condition is the one the stored remark on the cost of (R) lists as the import every derivation of the Hawking temperature makes. Fourth, (N$_{+}$) is strictly stronger than (R): it forces the exact joint product form over boost modes. Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} shows that this form removes the inter-mode correlations the chain's later steps need, which is why (R) was imposed on marginals; those correlations become deviations from (N$_{+}$), as they are from (Q). Where the gravitational field strength is nonzero, case (c) needs a local form of (N$_{+}$): at leading order about the point $x_0$, in a gauge with $\hb(x_0) = 1$ and $\Omega(x_0) = 0$, the state is a ground state for the null translations of the background along the generator. That is a premise, argued and not derived here. The whole generator of the eternal and de Sitter horizons, through the bifurcation surface, which cases (a) and (b) use, is global and is not carried by the store's one-chart fields, so it is read on several charts of flat spacetime, each carrying its own gravitational field, glued on overlaps by displacement and rotation gauge transformations.

Remarks (argued). On this continuum the edges at different $u_{0}$ give nested half-generator algebras $\CAR(L^{2}((u_{0}, \infty))\otimes K)$, which the translations $\nu_{a}$, $a \ge 0$, move properly into one another. This is the half-sided structure that Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-nested-patch} shows impossible on point spectrum. (N$_{+}$) is a condition on the state, not a choice of the windows' dynamics: the null translations shift the Mellin weight, so they lie outside the number-diagonal class (L$_{E}$) admits. The stored exclusion of (R) by a unique ground state under (L$_{E}$) concerns ground states of the boost dynamics, not of the translations. Along the imaginary boost, the strip $0 < \theta < \pi$ on which the twistor form is definite (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.twistor-form-states-only-off-the-real-slice}(iii), reflection at $\theta = \pi$) is the $\Delta^{1/2}$ half of the two-point KMS strip $0 < \theta < 2\pi$, with midpoint $\theta = \pi/2$ the $\Delta^{1/4}$ point; the Mellin contour rotation by $e^{-i\pi}$ used in the proof is the imaginary rapidity $\pi$ of that reflection.
synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-p.lay: Black holes, the horizon of an expanding universe, and the small horizons an accelerating observer sees all have a temperature. The series has so far assumed each of these temperatures with a separate premise of the same kind, each fixing a period of $2\pi$ by hand. This result shows that a single assumption with no temperature in it gives all three, once the quantum modes are taken to run continuously along each horizon's light rays. The assumption is that these modes are in their lowest-energy state with respect to sliding along the rays. Looked at from one side of the horizon, that state is exactly thermal, and the $2\pi$ comes out of the calculation, because energy is positive and the observer sees only half of each ray. There are costs. The finite lists of modes the series counts become an approximation. For a black hole the assumption describes an eternal hole in equilibrium, not one formed by collapse. And the assumption is still an input: it says the state is smooth across the point where the horizon's two halves meet, which is what every derivation of black-hole temperature assumes in some form.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, the Christoffel symbols of clause (iii) below are those of the covariant derivative $D$ in the frame of the stated gauge, and $\nabla_{\partial_v}\partial_v = \kappa\,\partial_v$ is $(K \cdot D)K = \kappa K$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (ii) and (vi)). Conventions. $a(f) = \int \overline{f(u)}\,\psi(u)\,du$ (antilinear in $f$), $a^{*}(f) = a(f)^{*}$; a gauge-invariant quasi-free state has symbol $A$, $\omega(a^{*}(f)a(g)) = \ip{g}{Af}$, so that its kernel is $A(u, v) = \omega(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u))$; a flow $\tau$ is written $\tau_{t}(a(f)) = a(e^{ith}f)$, the convention of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}, in which the I-state at $\beta$ has symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$. Since $\nu_{a}(a(f)) = \int\overline{f(u)}\,\psi(u + a)\,du = a(f(\cdot - a))$, the one-particle generator of $\nu$ is $P = i\,d/du$ ($e^{iaP}f = f(\cdot - a)$). Since $\beta_{t}(a(g)) = \int\overline{g(u)}\,e^{\lambda/2}\psi(e^{\lambda}u)\,du = a\bigl(e^{-\lambda/2}g(e^{-\lambda}\,\cdot)\bigr)$ with $\lambda = \kappa t$, on $\varphi_{w}(u) = u^{-1/2 + iw}$ ($u > 0$) one has $e^{-\lambda/2}\varphi_{w}(e^{-\lambda}u) = e^{-iw\lambda}\varphi_{w}(u)$, so the one-particle boost generator $h$ acts on $\varphi_{w}$ as $-\kappa w$; the half-density factor $e^{\lambda/2}$ is what makes $\beta_{t}$ preserve $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)$, since $\delta(e^{\lambda}(u - v)) = e^{-\lambda}\delta(u - v)$. The transverse factor $K$ is carried along as $\otimes\id_{K}$ throughout and is suppressed below.

\emph{(i)} Hypothesis (N$_{+}$) is Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}. Invariance under $\nu$ gives $e^{-iaP}Ae^{iaP} = A$ for all $a$, so $A$ is a function of $P$. A state is a ground state for $\nu$ (positive generator in the GNS representation, invariant cyclic vector) exactly when $-i\,\omega(x^{*}\delta(x)) \ge 0$ for $x$ in the domain of the derivation $\delta$ of $\nu$ (the standard characterisation of ground states, Bratteli and Robinson, Vol.~2, \S 5.3.19, cited from memory). With $x = a(g)$, $\delta(a(g)) = a(iPg) = -i\,a(Pg)$, the condition reads $-\ip{Pg}{Ag} \ge 0$, so $PA \le 0$; with $x = a^{*}(f)$, $\delta(a^{*}(f)) = i\,a^{*}(Pf)$ and $\omega(a(f)a^{*}(g)) = \ip{f}{(1 - A)g}$, the condition reads $\ip{f}{(1 - A)Pf} \ge 0$, so $(1 - A)P \ge 0$. In the spectral representation of $P$ (in which $A$ is multiplication by $A(k) \in [0, 1]$, $0 \le A \le 1$ for any quasi-free symbol), $kA(k) \le 0$ and $(1 - A(k))k \ge 0$ force $A(k) = 0$ for $k > 0$ and $A(k) = 1$ for $k < 0$; $\{k = 0\}$ is null. So $A = \chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$, unique. Since $P = i\,d/du$, $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)$ is the projection onto the span of $e^{iku}$, $k > 0$, with kernel $\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{ik(u - v)}\,dk = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$. This is the filled sea of the generator, the null vacuum.

\emph{(ii), the symbol.} The modes beyond the edge are $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{+}, du))$; it is $\beta$-invariant because $u \mapsto e^{\lambda}u$ preserves $\R_{+}$. The restriction of $\omega$ is gauge-invariant quasi-free with symbol $A_{+} = \chi_{+}A\chi_{+}$, kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$ on $u, v > 0$, homogeneous of degree $-1$. Such kernels are diagonal in the Mellin basis: with $s = \tfrac12 + iw$ and $v = ux$,
\[
(A_{+}\varphi_{w})(u) = \int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{i}{2\pi}\frac{v^{s-1}\,dv}{u - v + i0} = m(w)\,\varphi_{w}(u), \qquad m(w) = \frac{i}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{x^{s-1}\,dx}{1 - x + i0} ,
\]
and the Mellin transform $f \mapsto (2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{0}^{\infty}u^{-1/2 - iw}f(u)\,du$ is unitary from $L^{2}(\R_{+}, du)$ onto $L^{2}(\R, dw)$ (Mellin-Plancherel, cited from memory), so $A_{+}$ is multiplication by $m$. The pole of the integrand is at $x = 1 + i0$, above the axis, and the integrand is analytic in the lower half-plane and $O(|x|^{-3/2})$ at infinity and $O(|x|^{-1/2})$ at $0$; rotating the ray of integration downward through the angle $\pi$, $x = re^{-i\pi}$, crosses no singularity, and
\[
m(w) = \frac{i}{2\pi}\,e^{-i\pi s}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{r^{s-1}\,dr}{1 + r} = \frac{i}{2}\,\frac{e^{-i\pi s}}{\sin\pi s}
\]
by Euler's integral $\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{s-1}(1 + r)^{-1}dr = \pi/\sin\pi s$, $0 < \operatorname{Re}s < 1$ (cited from memory). With $s = \tfrac12 + iw$, $e^{-i\pi s} = -i\,e^{\pi w}$ and $\sin\pi s = \cosh\pi w$, so $m(w) = e^{\pi w}/(e^{\pi w} + e^{-\pi w}) = (1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1}$; equivalently $m = \tfrac{i}{2}(\cot\pi s - i)$, the principal value $\pi\cot\pi s$ plus the half residue. Numerically, at $w = -0.7, 0.3, 1.25$ the rotated integral and the $i\epsilon$-regularised integral ($\epsilon = 10^{-7}$) agree with $(1 + e^{-2\pi w})^{-1}$ to $2\times 10^{-15}$ and $10^{-6}$ respectively; the opposite prescription $-i0$ gives $(1 + e^{2\pi w})^{-1}$ up to sign, the reversed orientation. Since $h\varphi_{w} = -\kappa w\,\varphi_{w}$, $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ acts on $\varphi_{w}$ as $(1 + e^{-\beta\kappa w})^{-1}$, which is $m(w)$ for every $w$ exactly when $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$. By Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}(1) (with Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-two} lifting the two-point identity to the state), the restriction is the continuum I-state, $\beta$-KMS at $2\pi/\kappa$, and by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness} it is the unique $\beta$-KMS state on that subalgebra. It is a single KMS state of the whole subalgebra (all $w$ and all transverse labels at once): joint, not only on marginals. Being gauge-invariant quasi-free it annihilates odd monomials, so it is even. The check verifies, with $q = e^{\pi w}$ a positive rational, that $\tfrac{i}{2}(\cot\pi s - i)$ with $\cot\pi s = -i(q - q^{-1})/(q + q^{-1})$ equals $(1 + q^{-2})^{-1}$, satisfies $1 - m = q^{-2}m$, and differs from the symbols at $\beta\kappa = \pi$ and $4\pi$.

\emph{(ii), the past half.} The local-horizon premise and the Einstein derivation built on it (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius}) use generators ending on the edge, $u \in [u_{0}, 0]$, with future-directed boost $\chi = -\xi$. $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{-}))$ is invariant under $\beta$, and on it the future-directed flow is $\gamma_{t} = \beta_{-t}$. Under $u \mapsto -u$ the kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$ on $u, v < 0$ becomes $\tfrac{-i}{2\pi}(x - y - i0)^{-1}$ on $x, y > 0$, the complex conjugate of the kernel above, so on $\varphi_{w}(x) = x^{-1/2 + iw}$ its symbol is $m(-w) = (1 + e^{2\pi w})^{-1}$; in the variable $x$ the flow $\gamma_{t}$ is $x \mapsto e^{-\kappa t}x$, whose one-particle generator acts on $\varphi_{w}$ as $+\kappa w$, so the symbol is $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$ again. In strip form, for $u, v < 0$, $F(\lambda) = e^{-\lambda/2}\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(e^{-\lambda}u - v + i0)^{-1}$ continued to $\lambda + i\theta$ has denominator $e^{-i\theta}e^{-\lambda}u - v$, whose imaginary part $|u|e^{-\lambda}\sin\theta$ is positive on $(0, \pi)$ and negative on $(\pi, 2\pi)$, with no zero in the open strip and the weight factor $e^{-i\pi} = -1$ at $2\pi$: KMS at $+2\pi/\kappa$ for the future-directed boost; the past-directed boost on the same half gives $-2\pi/\kappa$. The check verifies the strip signs, a tabulated value, the reversed control and $m(w) + m(-w) = 1$.

\emph{(ii), the strip and what makes $2\pi$.} The same result in the form of the KMS condition: for $u, v > 0$ put $F(\lambda) = \omega(\psi^{*}(v)\,\beta_{\lambda/\kappa}(\psi(u))) = e^{\lambda/2}\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(e^{\lambda}u - v + i0)^{-1}$. As a function of $\lambda + i\theta$, $F$ is analytic wherever $e^{i\theta}e^{\lambda}u \ne v$; for $u, v > 0$ that fails only at $\theta \in 2\pi\Z$, so $F$ is analytic in $0 < \theta < 2\pi$. At $\theta \to 0^{+}$ the denominator approaches the real axis from above, the $+i0$ of $F$; at $\theta \to 2\pi^{-}$ from below, and the weight factor has become $e^{i\pi}e^{\lambda/2}$, so $F(\lambda + 2\pi i) = e^{\lambda/2}\tfrac{-i}{2\pi}(e^{\lambda}u - v - i0)^{-1} = \omega(\beta_{\lambda/\kappa}(\psi(u))\,\psi^{*}(v))$, the second ordering computed from (i) (its kernel is $\delta(u - v) - A(u, v) = \tfrac{-i}{2\pi}(u - v - i0)^{-1}$). This is the two-point KMS identity at rapidity period $2\pi$; smearing with test functions supported in $u > 0$ makes it rigorous, and Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-two} lifts it. Each ingredient is needed. (a) With the opposite energy sign the prescriptions swap, the boundary value at $\theta \to 0^{+}$ no longer matches, and the strip opens to $\theta < 0$: KMS at $-2\pi/\kappa$. (b) If one point lies on the other side of the edge, $u < 0 < v$, then $e^{i\pi}e^{\lambda}u = v$ at $e^{\lambda} = v/|u|$: a pole inside the strip at imaginary rapidity $\pi$, where the continued half-generator $e^{i\theta}\R_{+}$ reaches $\R_{-}$; the full-generator algebra is not KMS (the null vacuum on it is pure). (c) The weight is not a free ingredient: $e^{\lambda w_{0}}\psi(e^{\lambda}u)$ preserves $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)$ exactly when $\operatorname{Re}w_{0} = \tfrac12$, since $\delta(e^{\lambda}(u - v)) = e^{-\lambda}\delta(u - v)$; for that weight the factor at $2\pi$ is $e^{i\pi} = -1$, which carries the coefficient $i$ of one ordering to the coefficient $-i$ of the other, as the KMS identity requires. (An integer-weight bosonic field with its double-pole kernel gives the same period; the half weight is what the anticommutator forces here, not a separate reason for $2\pi$.) (d) No $\theta \in (0, 2\pi)$ is a return: $e^{i\theta}e^{\lambda}u - v$ is real only for $e^{i\theta}$ real, and at $\theta = \pi$ it is $-e^{\lambda}u - v \ne e^{\lambda}u - v$. The check verifies (a) to (d) exactly at Gaussian-rational points $e^{i\theta} = (1 - t^{2} + 2it)/(1 + t^{2})$ of the unit circle: no zero for $u, v > 0$, the sign of the imaginary part equal to that of $t$, the zero at $\theta = \pi$ for $u < 0 < v$ with $e^{\lambda} = v/|u|$, that among the weights $\tfrac{k}{4}$ only $\tfrac12$ preserves the anticommutator ($\rho^{4w_{0}}\rho^{-2} = 1$ at $e^{\lambda/2} = \rho$) and that its factor $e^{i\pi}$ maps $i$ to $-i$, and the swapped prescription failing.

\emph{(iii)} The horizons. For (a), in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein form $f\,dv^{2} - 2\,dv\,dr - r^{2}d\Omega^{2}$ (store signature) with $f = 1 - 2M/r$, the generator $\partial_{v}$ of the future horizon $r = 2M$ has $\Gamma^{r}_{vv} = -\tfrac12 g^{rr}f' = \tfrac12 ff' = 0$ there (it stays on the horizon) and $\Gamma^{v}_{vv} = -\tfrac12 g^{vr}f' = \tfrac12 f'(2M) = 1/(4M)$, the value of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}: $\nabla_{\partial_{v}}\partial_{v} = \kappa\,\partial_{v}$ with $\kappa = 1/(4M)$. For (b), the future cosmological horizon of the static patch is reached as $t \to +\infty$ at finite outgoing time $u_{\mathrm{out}} = t - r_{*}$, so it is computed in the outgoing form $f\,du_{\mathrm{out}}^{2} + 2\,du_{\mathrm{out}}\,dr - r^{2}d\Omega^{2}$ with $f = 1 - H^{2}r^{2}$: there $g^{u r} = 1$, $\Gamma^{r}_{uu} = \tfrac12 ff' = 0$ on $r = 1/H$ and $\Gamma^{u}_{uu} = -\tfrac12 f'(1/H) = H$, the surface gravity $\kappa_{\Lambda} = H$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-static-boost-frozen-point}(iii). (The ingoing chart gives $\Gamma^{v}_{vv} = -H$ on $r = 1/H$: it covers the past cosmological horizon, where the future-directed Killing flow moves points towards the bifurcation sphere, the past-half case of (ii), with the same $|\kappa|$.) In both cases, with $s$ the Killing-time coordinate along the generator ($v$, resp. $u_{\mathrm{out}}$) and $\kappa > 0$, the affine parameter is $V = e^{\kappa s}/\kappa$ ($V'' = \kappa V'$), with $V \to 0$ at the bifurcation sphere as $s \to -\infty$; the generator continues to $V < 0$ in the Kruskal, respectively de Sitter, extension, where it bounds the other exterior, so (N$_{+}$) in cases (a) and (b) is posed on the whole generator $V \in \R$ of the extended solution, a Hartle-Hawking-type condition (Bunch-Davies-type in de Sitter). For a hole formed by collapse the generators of the event horizon begin at finite $V$, there is no $V < 0$ half, and the physical state is not a ground state for the affine translations on the horizon, so case (a) is the eternal hole only. The Killing field is $\partial_{s} = \kappa V\,\partial_{V}$: Killing time $t$ acts on each generator as $V \mapsto e^{\kappa t}V$, the boost $\beta_{t}$ with $u = V$. For (c), in the store signature the rotor $B = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2} + \sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,e_{1}e_{0}$ gives $B\ell\tilde B = e^{\lambda}\ell$ for $\ell = e_{0} + e_{1}$, $Bn\tilde B = e^{-\lambda}n$ for $n = e_{0} - e_{1}$, and fixes $e_{2}, e_{3}$, so on the null plane $\{u\ell + y\}$ it is $u \mapsto e^{\lambda}u$ at fixed $y$: every generator dilated about its own edge point at unit rate in rapidity. For a gravitational field of nonvanishing field strength this holds at leading order, with the leading-order rapidity normalisation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity}(i). The check verifies the non-affinities from the inverse metrics over $\Q(r)$ (ingoing chart at three masses; outgoing chart, $+H$, and ingoing chart, $-H$, at three values of $H$), the series identities $V'' = \kappa V'$ and $V' = \kappa V + 1$ for $V = (e^{\kappa v} - 1)/\kappa$ (the same Killing field about $V = -1/\kappa$) to order 12, and the rotor action at $e^{\lambda/2} = \tfrac32, \tfrac15, 7$. Then (ii) with these $\kappa$ gives: on (a) the I-state at $\beta = 8\pi M$, Fermi-Dirac in Killing frequency $\varpi = -\kappa w$, the continuum restatement of (R) for the eternal hole; on (b) the same at $2\pi/H$, that of (R$_{\Lambda}$); on (c), on the past half, KMS for the future-directed local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$ on the patch's whole mode algebra, that of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) in Minkowski space (for a gravitational field of nonvanishing field strength it needs the local form of (N$_{+}$), a premise argued at leading order); and in all three a jointly KMS, even state, quasi-free by hypothesis: the joint KMS part of (Q). (Q)'s weight clause, the affine ladder $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ of its version 3 ($\kappa k$ in version 2), is not given: the continuum carries every weight. Remark (a comparison, not used). The period $2\pi$ agrees with the period at which the boost's Euclidean section is regular (Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity}). The rotation $x = re^{-i\pi}$ used in (ii) is the imaginary rapidity $\pi$ that carries the half-generator to the other half; the strip $0 < \theta < \pi$ on which the twistor form is definite along the imaginary boost (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.twistor-form-states-only-off-the-real-slice}(iii)) is the $\Delta^{1/2}$ half of the two-point KMS strip $0 < \theta < 2\pi$, with midpoint the $\Delta^{1/4}$ point $\theta = \pi/2$.

\emph{(iv)} For the fields, $\beta_{t}\nu_{a}\beta_{-t}(\psi(u)) = \psi(u + e^{\kappa t}a)$ in the order that conjugates translations by the boost, so $\beta_{t}\nu_{a}\beta_{-t} = \nu_{e^{\kappa t}a}$: the boost dilates $\nu$ at rate $\kappa$. If the boost multiplied each of a generating set of modes by a phase, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.point-spectrum-boost-admits-no-half-sided-translations}(ii) would make $\nu$ the identity, and (iii) of that Theorem would make its unitary implementer trivial on the GNS space; (N$_{+}$) would then have no content (a trivial translation group has the zero generator). So (N$_{+}$) is posed on one-particle spaces where the boost has no eigenvectors spanning the relevant vectors: here $h$ is multiplication by $-\kappa w$ on $L^{2}(\R, dw)$, purely continuous. The stored premises are worded on point-spectrum ladders with phase-acting flows; on the continuum the boost has no eigenvectors, a normalisable mode $f$ has occupation $\ip{f}{A_{+}f} = \int|\hat f(w)|^{2}m(w)\,dw$ in the Mellin transform $\hat f$, and a single mode's algebra is not boost-invariant, so the ladder statements are discretisations of (ii), recovering $m(w_{j})$ only for modes of vanishing Mellin width; no window carries (N$_{+}$). The check records the finite form of the obstruction: on a window with real weights $k_{j}$, $(k_{j} - k_{l})P_{jl} = icP_{jl}$ with $c$ real and nonzero forces $P = 0$.

\emph{(v)} Write $\ell = (1, \hat n)$, $|\hat n| = 1$, and $p = (p_{0}, \vec p)$ with $p_{0} \ge |\vec p|$. Then $\ip{\ell}{p} = p_{0} - \hat n\cdot\vec p \ge p_{0} - |\vec p| \ge 0$, with equality only if $\vec p = |\vec p|\hat n$ and $p_{0} = |\vec p|$, that is, $p$ on the ray of $\ell$. So in a representation with spectrum in the closed forward cone the generator $\ip{\ell}{P}$ of the null translations along $\ell$ is positive, and the null-translation group restricted to a null plane meets the positivity half of (N$_{+}$) for every invariant vector state. The check verifies this on 64 rational momenta and seven rational unit directions from Pythagorean quadruples, with equality only on the ray, and that a spacelike translation takes both signs. In the conformal model of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} ($\Cl(2,4)$, $\ip{\nO}{\nInf} = 1$, $X(x) = \nO + x - \tfrac12 Q(x)\nInf$), the rotor $T_{\alpha} = 1 + \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\ell\nInf$ maps $X(u\ell)$ to $X((u + \alpha)\ell)$; the boost $B$ above and the dilation $D = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2} + \sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,e_{-}e_{+}$ (both bivectors square to $1$) send $X(u\ell)$ to $X(e^{\lambda}u\ell)$ and to $e^{-\lambda}X(e^{\lambda}u\ell)$, the same point, while $B$ fixes $X(e_{2})$ and $D$ moves it; and $BT_{\alpha}\tilde B = DT_{\alpha}\tilde D = T_{e^{\lambda}\alpha}$. This is the relation $\Delta^{is}U(a)\Delta^{-is} = U(e^{-2\pi s}a)$ of the Borchers form of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}, read with the modular group as the boost at $-2\pi s$: the computation of (ii) is an explicit instance of that theorem on the generator, which is not otherwise used.
