synthesis.q-splits-maximum-entropy-affin.technical:
Premise (Q) bundles two assumptions about the boundary modes: that their joint state is the simplest (quasi-free, uncorrelated) one with the thermal marginals, and that the mode energies are $\omega_k = \kappa k$. This result separates them and says what each one is.

The first is a selection rule, not a consequence of (P) and (R). Among all states with the marginals (R) fixes, the uncorrelated product is exactly the one satisfying the geometric modular condition (G) and exactly the one of largest entropy: the entropy deficit of any other member equals its total correlation, which is its relative entropy to the product. So the quasi-free clause is Jaynes' maximum-entropy rule at the marginals (R) supplies.

The second splits further. For each current $a_m$ of the bosonisation bridge to be a normal mode of the boost flow, as the Planck clause reads it, the weights must be affine, $\omega_k = ck + d$; conversely, for any affine law the current occupations come out as Bose-Einstein at the frequencies $cm$, whatever the offset. So the Planck clause itself holds for every affine law; affinity is forced by the normal-mode reading, not by the occupancy formula. Particle-hole symmetry leaves two offsets: the sea level at a mode, giving one zero-weight mode per array (the choice of (Q)), or midway between two modes, giving none. What remains is the dimensionless slope $\beta c$; (Q) sets it to $2\pi$, which makes the time after which the array's flow returns to itself equal to the KMS period. The tension found earlier between (Q)'s weights and rotation invariance disappears when the array index (frequency) and the magnetic index (direction) are separate labels, as the channel identification of the s-wave reduction has them: weights depending on frequency only are rotation invariant, and each frequency level is a rotation multiplet of common weight.
synthesis.q-splits-maximum-entropy-affin.lay: One of the series' assumptions about the quantum modes at a black hole's boundary, called (Q), turns out to be two assumptions of very different kinds. The first says the modes are as uncorrelated as their individual thermal behaviour allows; this is exactly the rule "assume nothing beyond what is known", the state of greatest entropy, so it is a principle of inference rather than a derived fact. The second fixes the energies of the modes. Part of it is forced: if each combination of modes is to behave as a particle of one definite frequency, which is how the series reads its derivation of the thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation, the energies must be evenly spaced; the thermal spectrum itself comes out right for any even spacing. What is left over is a choice of where the evenly spaced ladder sits (with or without a rung at zero energy) and how far apart the rungs are compared with the temperature. A previously noted clash between these energies and the roundness of the black hole disappears once the energy label and the direction label are treated as separate.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Work on a finite window, realised by Jordan-Wigner on $(\C^{2})^{\otimes |W|}$. For an even state the single-mode marginal on mode $k$ is $\operatorname{diag}(1 - \langle N_{k}\rangle, \langle N_{k}\rangle)$, since the odd one-point functions vanish; for $\varrho \in \mathcal{C}$ it is $\operatorname{diag}(1 - n_{k}, n_{k})$ with $0 < n_{k} < 1$ (Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}(1)). The product $\sigma = \prod_{k}\bigl((1 - n_{k})(1 - N_{k}) + n_{k}N_{k}\bigr)$ is diagonal in the joint number basis and faithful, so
\[
\log\sigma \;=\; \sum_{k}\bigl(\log(1 - n_{k})\,(1 - N_{k}) + \log n_{k}\,N_{k}\bigr),
\]
an element of $\operatorname{span}\{1, N_{k}\}$. Every $\varrho \in \mathcal{C}$ has $\tr\varrho = 1$ and $\tr(\varrho N_{k}) = n_{k}$, the same values as $\sigma$, so $\tr(\varrho\log\sigma) = \tr(\sigma\log\sigma) = -\sum_{k}S(\sigma_{k}) = -S(\sigma)$, whence $\rel{\varrho}{\sigma} = -S(\varrho) - \tr(\varrho\log\sigma) = S(\sigma) - S(\varrho)$; and $S(\sigma) = \sum_{k}S(\varrho_{k})$ because the marginals of $\varrho$ and $\sigma$ agree, so this is $C(\varrho)$ in the notation of Corollary \claimref{singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-correlations}. The key identity has the same shape as in Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}, with $\sigma$ in place of the pinched state, and as there nonnegativity and the equality case are Klein's inequality \cite[\S 11.3]{NielsenChuang}: $C(\varrho) \geq 0$ with equality if and only if $\varrho = \sigma$. This gives (b) $\Leftrightarrow$ (d) $\Leftrightarrow$ (e). (a) $\Leftrightarrow$ (b): by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra} the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with diagonal symbol $\operatorname{diag}(n_{k})$ is, on a window, exactly the product $\bigotimes_{k}\operatorname{diag}(1 - n_{k}, n_{k})$, which is $\sigma$. (b) $\Leftrightarrow$ (c): $\sigma$ is the product of the Gibbs states of $\omega_{k}K_{k}$ at the common $\beta$, that is $e^{-\beta K_{\mathrm{geo}}}/\tr e^{-\beta K_{\mathrm{geo}}}$, whose modular group is the phase flow of $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$ reparametrised by $-\beta$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}), so it satisfies (G); conversely Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} shows that a state satisfying (G) is this product, and Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}(3) records that it is the only member of $\mathcal{C}$ doing so. The same Corollary (3) gives members of $\mathcal{C}$ with $C(\varrho) > 0$, so (P) and (R) alone do not imply (Q-qf). The script builds, on three modes with rational occupations, the product state, verifies that it is Gibbs for $K_{\mathrm{geo}}$, that its two-point matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(n_{k})$ and that every four-point function factorises by Wick's rule; it then builds $\varrho = \sigma + \tfrac{1}{10}(N_{0} - \tfrac12)(N_{1} - \tfrac12)$, verifies that it is positive definite (all pivots positive), lies in $\mathcal{C}$ with the same two-point matrix, violates Wick's rule at $\langle N_{0}N_{1}\rangle$, and has the same values of $1$ and $N_{k}$ as $\sigma$, which is what the identity $\tr(\varrho\log\sigma) = \tr(\sigma\log\sigma)$ uses.

\emph{(ii)} The flow acts by $e^{itK_{\mathrm{geo}}}\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{l}e^{-itK_{\mathrm{geo}}} = e^{i(\omega_{k} - \omega_{l})t}\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{l}$, the constant in $K_{k}$ dropping out. Hence $e^{itK_{\mathrm{geo}}}a_{m}e^{-itK_{\mathrm{geo}}} = \sum_{k}e^{i(\omega_{k} - \omega_{k+m})t}\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{k+m}$. The bilinears $\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{k+m}$, $k \in \Z$, are linearly independent (their one-particle images, under the injective map $X \mapsto \hat{X}$ of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}, are distinct matrix units), and for $m \neq 0$ the bilinears on different diagonals are independent as well. So the image of $a_{m}$ is a multiple of $a_{m}$ for all $t$, and more generally lies in the span of the currents, exactly when $\omega_{k} - \omega_{k+m}$ does not depend on $k$. For $m = 1$ this says $\omega_{k+1} - \omega_{k} = c$ for all $k$, that is $\omega_{k} = ck + d$; conversely affine weights give $\omega_{k} - \omega_{k+m} = -cm$ for every $k$ and $m$, so $\lambda_{m} = cm$. The script checks the one-particle criterion $[\operatorname{diag}(\omega), S_{m}] \in \C S_{m}$ for all shifts $S_{m}$ on an eight-site window, for an affine law (true) and for three non-affine ones (a single displaced weight, a quadratic law, a staggered offset; all false), and checks on a four-mode Fock space that the second-quantised commutator $[\hat{h}, \hat{S}_{m}]$ equals $\widehat{[h, S_{m}]}$ and equals $-3m\,\hat{S}_{m}$ for the affine law $\omega_{k} = 3k - 1$.

\emph{(iii)} Write $n(x) = (e^{x} + 1)^{-1}$. For all real $x, y$, $n(x)(1 - n(y)) = e^{y}/((e^{x} + 1)(e^{y} + 1))$ and $n(y) - n(x) = (e^{x} - e^{y})/((e^{x} + 1)(e^{y} + 1))$, so $n(x)(1 - n(y)) = (n(y) - n(x))/(e^{x - y} - 1)$ whenever $x \neq y$. With $x = \beta(c(k + m) + d)$ and $y = \beta(ck + d)$, $x - y = \beta cm$ for every $k$, so
\[
n_{k+m}(1 - n_{k}) \;=\; \frac{n_{k} - n_{k+m}}{e^{\beta cm} - 1} .
\]
Summing over $-K \le k \le K$ telescopes: $\sum_{k=-K}^{K}(n_{k} - n_{k+m}) = \sum_{k=-K}^{-K+m-1}n_{k} - \sum_{k=K+1}^{K+m}n_{k}$. As $K \to \infty$ the first sum tends to $m$ and the second to $0$, since $1 - n_{k} \le e^{\beta(ck + d)}$ and $n_{k} \le e^{-\beta(ck + d)}$; the limit is $m/(e^{\beta cm} - 1)$, independent of $d$. By Wick's rule for the quasi-free state, $\langle a_{-m}a_{m}\rangle = \sum_{k}n_{k+m}(1 - n_{k})$, as in Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}(3), so $\langle a_{-m}a_{m}\rangle/m = (e^{\beta cm} - 1)^{-1}$, the Bose-Einstein occupancy at frequency $cm$ and inverse temperature $\beta$, for every affine law. The script represents $e^{\beta c}$ and $e^{\beta d}$ by rationals $b = 3$ and $D \in \{1, \tfrac52, \tfrac27\}$, verifies the termwise identity, the exact telescoped value of every finite-window sum for $K = 5, 10, 20$, and the explicit edge bound $|S_{K} - m/(b^{m} - 1)| \le (mDb^{-K+m-1} + mb^{-K-1}/D)/(b^{m} - 1)$, which tends to zero.

\emph{(iv)} The map $\psi_{k} \mapsto \psi_{k_{0} - k}^{\dagger}$ preserves the CAR, so it is a Bogoliubov automorphism. With the flow $\alpha_{t}(\psi_{k}) = e^{-i\omega_{k}t}\psi_{k}$, the two composites send $\psi_{k}$ to $e^{-i\omega_{k}t}\psi_{k_{0}-k}^{\dagger}$ and to $e^{i\omega_{k_{0}-k}t}\psi_{k_{0}-k}^{\dagger}$, so the map commutes with the flow exactly when $\omega_{k_{0} - k} = -\omega_{k}$ for all $k$, which for affine weights is $ck_{0} + 2d = 0$. A Bogoliubov map carries a gauge-invariant quasi-free state to the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with transformed symbol (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}, used in the same way in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-common-weight-particle-hole}(iii)); here the transformed symbol is $n'_{k} = 1 - n_{k_{0} - k}$, and $1 - n(-x) = n(x)$ shows that $n' = n$ at a given $\beta \neq 0$ exactly when $\omega_{k_{0}-k} = -\omega_{k}$. Relabelling $k \mapsto k + r$ changes $d$ by $cr$ and $k_{0}$ by $-2r$, so the classes are $k_{0}$ even, reducible to $d = 0$, and $k_{0}$ odd, reducible to $d = c/2$. In the first class $\omega_{0} = 0$ and $n_{0} = \tfrac12$; the weights are integer multiples of $c$, so $\alpha_{2\pi/c}$ is the identity. In the second class the weights are odd multiples of $c/2$, so $\alpha_{2\pi/c}(\psi_{k}) = e^{-i\pi(2k+1)}\psi_{k} = -\psi_{k}$, the parity automorphism, and no weight vanishes. With the offset class fixed, the occupations depend on $c$, $d$ and $\beta$ only through $\beta\omega_{k} = y k$ or $y(k + \tfrac12)$, $y = \beta c$. Under (R), $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, and (Q-w) has $c = \kappa$, so $y = 2\pi$ and the recurrence time $2\pi/c$ equals $\beta$. The script checks, with $b = 4$ standing for $e^{y}$, that $n_{-k} = 1 - n_{k}$ for $D = 1$, $n_{-1-k} = 1 - n_{k}$ for $D = 2$ ($D^{2} = b$), that neither holds for $D = 3$, that the reflections map the one-particle generators $\operatorname{diag}(k)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(k + \tfrac12)$ to their negatives, and the integrality statements behind the two recurrences.

\emph{(v)} Second quantisation $X \mapsto \hat{X}$ is a Lie map (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}), injective on one-particle operators, so $\hat{h}$ commutes with $(\id \otimes J_{a})^{\wedge}$ exactly when $h$ commutes with $\id \otimes J_{a}$. For $h = \operatorname{diag}(\omega_{k,a})$ the $(k,a),(k,a+1)$ entry of $[h, \id \otimes J_{+}]$ is $(\omega_{k,a} - \omega_{k,a+1})(J_{+})_{a,a+1}$, and the principal $J_{+}$ has all superdiagonal entries nonzero, so commutation forces $\omega_{k,a}$ to be independent of $a$; conversely $\operatorname{diag}(\omega) \otimes \id$ commutes with $\id \otimes X$ for every $X$. Applying (ii) to the currents of each channel $a$ gives $\omega_{k} = ck + d$. The symbol $\operatorname{diag}(n_{k}) \otimes \id$ commutes with every $\id \otimes u$, so the state is rotation invariant. Restricted to one level $k$, the modes $\psi_{k,a}$ carry the principal representation of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.principality-indifference-sphere} and the generator acts as $\omega_{k}N_{\mathrm{tot}}^{(k)}$, which is the form Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-common-weight-particle-hole}(i) proves necessary; its clause (iv) concerns weights $\kappa m$ indexed by the magnetic label of one principal window, which is the identification of the array index with the magnetic index, not made here. In the class $d = 0$ the level $k = 0$ has $\omega_{0} = 0$ and symbol $\tfrac12\id$, which is maximally mixed and invariant under the particle-hole map of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-common-weight-particle-hole}(iii), and by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(ii) zero weight is its equality case. The script checks, for the principal triples on $\C^{2}$ and $\C^{3}$ and three array levels, that $\operatorname{diag}(-1, 0, 1) \otimes \id$ commutes with $\id \otimes e, f, h$, that the diagonal generators commuting with $\id \otimes e$ form a space of dimension three (one weight per level), that $\tfrac12 h$ does not commute with $e$, and, on the four-mode Fock space of two levels of spin $\tfrac12$, the second-quantised commutations.

\emph{Remark (computed, outside the proved statement; reproducible with 60-digit decimal arithmetic, 40 terms, tail below $e^{-250}$).} At $y = 2\pi$ the entropy of one array, $\sum_{k}s(\beta\omega_{k})$ with $s$ the thermal entropy of one mode, is $\ln 2 + 2\sum_{k \geq 1}s(2\pi k) = 0.72039669894660548\ldots$ with the sea at a site, the value of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(vi), and $2\sum_{k \geq 0}s(2\pi(k + \tfrac12)) = 0.346573590279972654708\ldots$ with the sea between sites; for the latter value, its rigorous bound and its identification with $\tfrac12\ln 2$, see the result filed alongside, synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2.

synthesis.r-lambda-regularity-cosmologic.formal:
For every mode $j$ of the boundary modes of the cosmological horizon (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.cosmological-horizon-boundary-modes}) and every pair $a, b$ of elements of its ladder $\{v_{j}, v_{j}^{*}\}$, the correlation function $F_{a,b}(t) := \omega\bigl(a\,\alpha_{t}(b)\bigr)$ of the static Killing flow $\alpha_{t} = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{it\omega_{j}K_{j}})$, an entire function of $t$, continues in imaginary Killing time to a single-valued function on the regular Euclidean section of the static patch of the de Sitter gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; its static Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart, Wick-rotated), and its two orderings meet after one period:
\[
F_{a,b}\bigl(t + i\,p\bigr) \;=\; \omega\bigl(\alpha_{t}(b)\,a\bigr), \qquad p \;=\; \frac{2\pi}{\kappa_{\Lambda}} ,
\]
the period at which the Euclidean section is smooth at its tip (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-static-boost-frozen-point}(iii)); for a state that is KMS for the Killing flow, this is also the period at which it is regular across the horizon locus in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart. The horizon locus is met on a cross-section of the cosmological horizon locus $r = 1/H$ in the static Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart of de Sitter space ($\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta = -rH$, the expanding chart, whose free-fall observers have $dr/dt = Hr$ and which contains the static observer's future horizon), of area $4\pi/H^{2}$, on which the static Killing field is null and normal with surface gravity $H$. In words: each single-mode marginal is KMS for the static Killing flow at exactly the period the smoothness of the Euclidean de Sitter section at its tip dictates; the condition is local, posed at the tip, and the closed Euclidean section as a whole is not used.

\emph{Note (continuum restatement).} Posed on the continuum of the cosmological horizon's null generators (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}), the content of (R$_{\Lambda}$) follows from Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}: by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(iii) the generators' modes are then jointly KMS for the static Killing flow at $\beta = 2\pi/H$. The wording above, on the ladders $\{v_{j}, v_{j}^{*}\}$ with a phase-acting flow, is a discretisation of that statement, recovered only for modes of vanishing Mellin width; (N$_{+}$) itself cannot be posed on point spectrum. (R$_{\Lambda}$) remains a premise.

The bifurcation surface itself, where the boost flow has its fixed points, lies beyond one flat chart (it is the meeting of the four regions of the maximal extension); the chart contains the future horizon, on whose cross-sections the area, the surface gravity and the boost flow are those stated.

It is the assumption behind the standard calculation of that horizon's temperature, and the series does not derive it.

synthesis.r-le-i-independent-spectrum-co.technical: The three thermal-chain premises constrain different things: (R) the single-mode marginals of the state, (L$_E$) the generator of the window dynamics, (I) the exterior channel map. Four two-mode models, each checked in exact arithmetic, realise every pattern in which exactly one premise fails, so none is a consequence of the other two. They are linked only through a selection rule for the state. Under the unique-ground-state condition the link is exclusive: a number-diagonal generator has a number basis ground state, which is not thermal, while a two-mode pairing generator has, for every Boltzmann factor, a unique gapped ground state whose marginals are thermal. A single premise that replaces (R) and (L$_E$) therefore cannot be a unique-ground-state selection on the window; with a degenerate ground space the exclusion fails.
synthesis.r-le-i-independent-spectrum-co.lay: Three of the series' assumptions about black-hole thermality concern different things: the temperature of each mode, which kinds of internal dynamics are allowed, and how modes reach distant observers. Small explicit models show that none of the three can be deduced from the other two. They also show that picking the state as the single lowest-energy state of the internal dynamics would force a choice between the first two assumptions, so any single principle replacing both must pick the state some other way.

proofs.main:
Work on two modes by Jordan-Wigner on $\C^{2}\otimes\C^{2}$, $a_{0} = s_{-}\otimes 1$, $a_{1} = s_{z}\otimes s_{-}$, which satisfy the CAR (checked). For mode $k$ the Killing flow continued to imaginary time $ip$ acts by $\alpha^{k}_{ip}(a_{k}) = q_{k}^{-1}a_{k}$, $\alpha^{k}_{ip}(a_{k}^{*}) = q_{k}a_{k}^{*}$, $\alpha^{k}_{ip}(N_{k}) = N_{k}$, with $q_{k} = e^{-p\omega_{k}}$, since $e^{-p\omega_{k}N_{k}}a_{k}e^{p\omega_{k}N_{k}} = e^{p\omega_{k}}a_{k}$. The KMS condition of Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus} for the marginal of mode $k$ is $\omega(X\alpha^{k}_{ip}(Y)) = \omega(YX)$ for $X, Y$ in the single-mode algebra, which is spanned by $1, a_{k}, a_{k}^{*}, N_{k}$; for a marginal of the form $\operatorname{diag}(1-n, n)$ it holds iff $n/(1-n) = q_{k}$, and the script tests it on all sixteen pairs. Only the Boltzmann factors $q_{k}$ enter the models, so every value of $p\omega_{k}$ is covered by letting $q_{k}$ range over $(0,1)$; the script uses rational values.

(i) (M1) $H = \omega_{0}N_{0} + \omega_{1}N_{1}$ commutes with $N_{0}, N_{1}$ and with the product Gibbs state $\varrho = \varrho_{0}\otimes\varrho_{1}$, $\varrho_{k} = \operatorname{diag}(1, q_{k})/(1 + q_{k})$, which is KMS for each mode at $q_{k}$; $T = 1$ is (I). (M2) With $\omega_{k} > 0$ the vacuum $\ket{00}$ is the unique ground state of $H$ (the script certifies that $H$ is positive definite on its orthogonal complement by an exact congruence signature), its marginals are pure, and the pair $X = a_{k}$, $Y = a_{k}^{*}$ gives $\omega(a_{k}\alpha_{ip}(a_{k}^{*})) = q_{k} \ne 0 = \omega(a_{k}^{*}a_{k})$, so (R) fails for every $q_{k} > 0$. (M3) is (ii). (M4) Take $T$ with $a_{0}^{\mathrm{out}} = c\,a_{0} + s\,a_{1}$, $a_{1}^{\mathrm{out}} = -s\,a_{0} + c\,a_{1}$, $c^{2} + s^{2} = 1$, $cs \ne 0$. In the product Gibbs state the cross terms vanish, so $\langle N^{\mathrm{out}}_{0}\rangle = c^{2}n_{0} + s^{2}n_{1} \ne n_{0}$ when $n_{0} \ne n_{1}$: the occupancy of channel 0 is not carried to asymptotic channel 0, and $T$ mixes the two channels, so (I) fails even when greybody loss is allowed (a vacuum-fed loss can only rescale $n_{0}$ to $|T_{00}|^{2}n_{0}$, never add $n_{1}$), while the state and generator are those of (M1). The script checks (M1), (M2), (M4) at $(q_{0}, q_{1}) = (1/4, 1/9)$ and $(2/3, 1/7)$, $(c,s) = (3/5, 4/5)$, with the out-occupation pinned, and (M2) at three values of $q$. Each model satisfies two of the three premises and violates the third, which is the standard form of an independence proof.

(ii) $H_{t}$ preserves parity. On the odd sector $\operatorname{span}\{\ket{10}, \ket{01}\}$ it is $gA$ times the identity, $A = (1 - t^{2})/(2t) > 0$. On the even sector, $a_{0}^{*}a_{1}^{*}\ket{00} = \ket{11}$ and $a_{1}a_{0}\ket{11} = a_{1}(1 - a_{0}^{*}a_{0})a_{1}^{*}\ket{00} = \ket{00}$, so the matrix in the basis $(\ket{00}, \ket{11})$ is $g\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0 & 1\\ 1 & 2A\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. On $(1, -t)$ it gives $g(-t, 1 - 2At) = g(-t, t^{2}) = -gt\,(1, -t)$ since $2At = 1 - t^{2}$ (an identity of rational functions of $t$, checked as such). The other even eigenvalue is $2gA + gt > 0$ (trace $2gA$), and the odd ones are $gA > 0 > -gt$, so $\ket{00} - t\ket{11}$ is the unique ground state, with gap $\min(gA, 2gA) + gt > 0$. Its marginal on either mode is $\operatorname{diag}(1, t^{2})/(1 + t^{2})$: Gibbs with Boltzmann factor $t^{2}$, so (R) holds for equal frequencies when $t^{2} = e^{-p\omega}$. $[H_{t}, N_{0}] \ne 0$ because the pairing term changes $N_{0}$. The script checks uniqueness and the gap by an exact congruence signature on the complement, (R) on all sixteen pairs for both modes, and $[H_{t}, N_{0}] \ne 0$, at four rational $(t, g)$ with pinned ground energies. At $t = 3/4$, after $a_{1} \mapsto -a_{1}$ and $g = 12$, $H_{t}$ agrees on the even sector with the pairing form of Proposition \claimref{angle.hop-sea-filled-pairing}(ii) and has the same ground state; the odd sectors differ ($\operatorname{diag}(7, 0)$ there against $\tfrac72$ times the identity here).

(iii) If $H$ commutes with every $N_{k}$ it is diagonal in the joint number basis, so a unique ground state is a number basis state; its marginals are pure, and (R) fails as in (M2). This is Proposition \claimref{angle.within-supplied-class-spectrum-condition-selects}(i) in the present language. Uniqueness is used: for the number-diagonal $(N_{0} - N_{1})^{2}$ the ground space $\operatorname{span}\{\ket{00}, \ket{11}\}$ contains $\tfrac45\ket{00} + \tfrac35\ket{11}$, with thermal marginals (part (ii) of that proposition), so without uniqueness (L$_E$), (R) and "$\omega$ is a ground state" coexist; the script checks this. By (ii) and (M3), (R) and (S) hold together outside (L$_E$). So in every model satisfying (S), at most one of (R), (L$_E$) holds, and each occurs.

\emph{Remarks (argued, not part of the claim).} (a) Premise \claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality} concerns ladders at points of $E$. If mode 1 of (M3) is read as a partner outside $E$ (the other side of a cut), (L$_E$) is not violated, and (S) on the doubled system with a cross-cut pairing gives the thermal marginal; but every Boltzmann factor occurs, so the period of (R) is still not supplied, in line with Proposition \claimref{angle.within-supplied-class-spectrum-condition-selects} and the stored rate-rigidity result. (b) Independence here is relative to finite windows with the premises read as above (single-mode KMS for (R), $[H, N_{k}] = 0$ for (L$_E$), no cross-channel mixing for (I)); the models do not represent the geometric origin of $\omega_{k}$ and $\kappa$, which none of the three premises fixes.

synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-para.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on four-dimensional flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose derived metric $g$ is smooth and globally hyperbolic on a region $U$ of its invertible region, $N \subset U$ geodesically convex, and $\mathcal{H} \subset N$ a piece of a null hypersurface generated by affinely parametrised null geodesics $u \mapsto X(u, y)$, with the notation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces} ($J$, $a = |\det J|$, $B = J'J^{-1}$, $\theta = \mathrm{tr}\,B$, the transverse Hessian $M(u, u')$ of $-\sigma$, $\Delta$, the canonical projector $\Lambda = \tfrac12 nk$ of the parallel null frame, the canonical generator field $\sqrt{2a}\,\Lambda\psi$, $K = L^{2}(\R^{2}, d^{2}y)\otimes V_{\Lambda}$), such that (S) points of distinct generators of $\mathcal{H}$ are spacelike separated (true on every small enough piece, and on every local Rindler horizon of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}, the null boundary of the past of a small two-surface element being achronal). For $m_{0} \ge 0$ let $G_{\mathrm{par}} = (iD_{x} + m_{0})H_{+}e_{0}$, $H = U/\sigma + V\log\sigma$, $U = \Delta^{1/2}R$, be the Dirac Hadamard parametrix (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport}), regularised by $\sigma_{\epsilon} = \sigma + i\epsilon(t(x) - t(x')) - \tfrac12\epsilon^{2}$ for a time function $t$, and let $W^{\mathrm{par}}_{\mathcal{H}}$ be its restriction to the generators in the canonical normalisation, smeared with transverse profiles $F, G \in C^{1}_{c}(\R^{2})\otimes V_{\Lambda}$, as the $\epsilon \to 0$ limit of the transverse-smeared kernel (the restriction in which Premise \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise} is posed). With $W_{0}(u, u') = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - u' + i0)^{-1}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The logarithms cancel; proved.)} In a rotation gauge in which the parallel null frame has constant images on $\mathcal{H}$, the projected kernel $\Lambda D(U/\sigma)e_{0}\Lambda$ at $x = X(u, y' + \eta)$, $x' = X(u', y')$ has numerator $N = \Lambda[(DU)\sigma - (\nabla\sigma)U]e_{0}\Lambda = O(|\eta|^{2})$, so no part of degree below $-2$ in $\eta$; the coefficient of $\log\epsilon$, which is also that of $\log(-i(u - u'))$, is
\[
2\pi\,\bigl(a(u)a(u')\bigr)^{1/2}\Bigl(\partial_{u} + \tfrac12\theta(u)\Bigr)\frac{\Delta^{1/2}}{\sqrt{\det M}}\;\Lambda\,\delta^{2}(y - y'),
\]
the derivative along the generator giving $\partial_{u}$, the projected transverse spin connection giving $\tfrac12\theta$, and the first-order spinor transport contributing nothing (it enters through a transverse divergence). Since $\Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M} = (a(u)a(u'))^{-1/2}$ and $\theta = a'/a$, the coefficient is zero for all $u, u'$: the term $-\pi\theta(u)(\log\epsilon + \log(-is))\,\delta^{2}(y - y')$ is cancelled by the connection term. The mass term and $V\log\sigma$ have degree at least $-1$ and give no logarithm.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The restricted parametrix; proved.)} The limit exists in $\mathcal{D}'$ and $W^{\mathrm{par}}_{\mathcal{H}} = W_{0}\otimes\id_{K} + r$, where in each $K$-component $r_{F,G}(u, u')$ is a bounded function, $\sup|r_{F,G}| \le C$ with $C$ depending only on a compact set containing the supports, a compact $u$-interval, $m_{0}$ and $C^{1}$ bounds on $F$, $G$. The coefficient of $(u - u' + i0)^{-1}\delta^{2}(y - y')$ is exactly that of $W_{0}\Lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces}(ii)), and no other term contributes at that order. The regularised restriction depends on the time function $t$ through the smooth kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\partial_{u}\log\varphi_{t}(u, u')\,\Lambda\,\delta^{2}(y - y')$, where $t(X(u, y)) - t(X(u', y)) = (u - u')\varphi_{t}(u, u', y)$, $\varphi_{t} > 0$ (on the flat null plane with $t$ nonlinear along the generators the limit is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\,\partial_{u}t/(t(u) - t(u') + i0)$): $r$ is defined for the chosen $t$, and $W^{\mathrm{par}}_{\mathcal{H}}$ is determined only modulo smooth kernels, which the clause of (HS) does not see.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The bound posed by (HS); proved.)} $R^{\mathrm{par}} = W^{\mathrm{par}}_{\mathcal{H}} - W_{0}\otimes\id_{K}$ has generator scaling degree at most $0$ at every $(u_{0}, u_{0})$: for every $\varpi > 0$, $\lambda^{\varpi}R^{\mathrm{par}}(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda x') \to 0$ in $\mathcal{D}'$, uniformly for profiles with support in a fixed compact set and bounded in $C^{1}$. So the clause of Premise \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise} (version 3) holds, with any $\varpi \in (0, 1)$, for every $m_{0} \ge 0$, at every point of every local Rindler horizon (Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}), whatever the field strength there.
\end{enumerate}
Nothing here uses the field equations, vanishing expansion or shear, or the value of the field strength. The components in the parallel frame do not depend on the rotation gauge. Not part of this result: the agreement of the regularised restriction with the restriction defined through the characteristic-data embedding of the generator field, which the passage from the parametrix to Hadamard states in that premise uses; by the time-function dependence above, that agreement can hold only modulo smooth kernels.
synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-para.technical: The premise (HS) was reduced, in the store, to one statement about the field: the Hadamard parametrix of the Dirac field, a fixed singular kernel built from the geometry, restricted to the light rays (generators) of a horizon through a point, should differ from the null vacuum by something less singular under scaling along the rays. The coefficient of the leading singularity was known to be the null vacuum's; what was open was whether the remaining terms are less singular, and whether certain logarithmically divergent terms, one of them proportional to the expansion of the rays, cancel. This result settles both for every gravitational field, on every piece of a null hypersurface generated by affine null geodesics whose distinct rays are spacelike separated (every small enough piece, every local Rindler horizon), for every mass, with the restriction defined by the standard regularisation of the singular kernel and transverse smearing. Expanding the projected kernel in the transverse separation of the rays, nothing is more singular than the inverse square of that separation; the logarithmic divergence is the angular mean of that part, and it splits into a derivative along the ray, a spin-connection term carrying the expansion only, and a transport term that is a total transverse derivative and contributes nothing. By the stored identity relating the Van Vleck determinant to the transverse Hessian and the area density, the first two cancel exactly, so there is no logarithm at all. The rest is bounded: the restricted parametrix is the null vacuum plus a bounded kernel, which scales away faster than any positive power. The premise's bound therefore holds, with room to spare. The regularised restriction depends on the chosen time function only through a smooth kernel, which the bound does not see. What remains for the passage from the parametrix to states is the identification of the regularised restriction used here with the restriction defined through the characteristic data of the field on the hypersurface.
synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-para.lay: The series needs every reasonable quantum state of the electron field to look like empty space along the light rays of the small horizons used to derive the equations of gravity, when looked at closely enough. The question had been reduced to a statement about gravity's geometry alone: a fixed mathematical object, which carries the short-distance behaviour shared by all reasonable states, should look like that of empty space along those light rays, up to corrections that fade at short distances. The strongest part had been checked before; two weaker pieces, which separately would grow without limit, were expected but not shown to cancel. This result shows that they do cancel exactly, on small enough pieces of the light sheets of every gravitational field (including the small horizons the series uses) and for every mass of the field, and that everything left over stays bounded. So the assumed statement is now proved, for the precise way the object is restricted to the light rays. One step remains before it applies to the states themselves: showing that this way of restricting agrees with the more fundamental one.
flags: the restriction is the epsilon -> 0 limit of the transverse-smeared, i0-regularised parametrix, the one in which (HS) version 3 is posed; its agreement with the restriction through the characteristic-data embedding (cited from memory in the stored result) is not shown here

hypothesis (S), that points of distinct generators are spacelike separated, is proved for small enough pieces of the hypersurface (transverse Hessian positive near the diagonal) and holds on local Rindler horizons (achronal null boundaries; standard causal theory, cited from memory); larger pieces need it as stated
the epsilon-regularised restriction depends on the time function through a smooth kernel; it and the remainder are defined for a chosen time function, modulo smooth kernels
the generic field is covered by the proof and by exact checks on arbitrary jets; a finite-separation computation on a generic polynomial field (no closed-form Synge function) was not made

proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions and hypotheses.} As in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces}: physical vectors as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, signature $(+,-,-,-)$; $\mathcal{H}$ is generated by the affinely parametrised null geodesics $u \mapsto X(u, y)$ with tangent $k$; the null frame $\{k, n, f_{1}, f_{2}\}$ is parallel along each generator, $k\cdot n = 1$; $J$, $a = |\det J|$, $B = J'J^{-1}$ (self-adjoint, $\mathcal{H}$ being twist-free), $\theta = \mathrm{tr}\,B = a'/a$, the Jacobi map $A$, $M(u, u') = (u - u')\bar J(u')A^{-1}J(u)$ and $\Delta = (u - u')^{2}/\det A$ on the generator are those of that theorem's (i). The piece of $\mathcal{H}$ considered lies in a geodesically convex set $N$ and satisfies (S): points of distinct generators are spacelike separated, $\sigma(X(u, y), X(u', y')) < 0$ for $y \neq y'$. (S) holds on every small enough piece: by that theorem's (i), $\sigma(X(u, y' + \eta), X(u', y')) = -\tfrac12 M(u, u')(\eta, \eta) + O(|\eta|^{3})$ uniformly for $(u, u')$ in a compact interval, and $M(u, u') \to \bar J J$ as $u' \to u$ is positive, so $\sigma < 0$ for $0 < |\eta| < \delta_{0}$ and $|u - u'| < \delta_{0}$, and a piece of transverse and generator extent below $\delta_{0}$ has (S). (S) also holds on every local Rindler horizon of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}: the null boundary of the past of a small two-surface element is achronal, and in a small caustic-free patch two null-related points of it lie on one generator (standard causal theory, cited from memory). The parametrix is $G_{\mathrm{par}} = (iD_{x} + m_{0})H_{+}e_{0}$, $H = U/\sigma + V\log\sigma$ with $U = \Delta^{1/2}R$ and $V$ smooth (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport}(a), (b)), in the form of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dirac-hadamard-form-propagates-and-adiabatic-states-are-hadamard}(a) (the Dirac operator with its mass term applied to a Hadamard parametrix of its square); its boundary value is taken with $\sigma_{\epsilon}(x, x') = \sigma(x, x') + i\epsilon(t(x) - t(x')) - \tfrac12\epsilon^{2}$ for a time function $t$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-hadamard-parametrix-of-the-squared-dirac-operator-leads-with-van-vleck-root-times-spin-transport}(c); the sign of $i$ is the one that gives the $+i0$ of $W_{0}$ in the flat computation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(ii)). Only $\mathrm{Re}\,\sigma_{\epsilon} = \sigma - \tfrac12\epsilon^{2} \le \sigma$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,\sigma_{\epsilon} = \epsilon s$, $s = t(x) - t(x')$, are used below.

\emph{Step 0 (adapted rotation gauge).} A rotation gauge transformation (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) makes the images of the parallel frame the constant vectors $k = e_{0} + e_{3}$, $n = \tfrac12(e_{0} - e_{3})$, $f_{a} = e_{a}$ at every point of the piece of $\mathcal{H}$ (any smooth rotor field on $\mathcal{H}$ extends smoothly off it). Then $\Lambda = \tfrac12 nk$ is constant on $\mathcal{H}$ and $\Lambda^{\dagger} = \Lambda$, and since $D_{V}e = \Omega(V)\cdot e$ for a frame vector with constant image: $\Omega(k) = 0$ on $\mathcal{H}$ (the frame is parallel along generators), and for $V$ tangent to $\mathcal{H}$, $\Omega(V)\cdot k = D_{V}k$, whose screen part is $B(V_{\perp})$ ($D_{E}k = D_{k}E$ for the deviation fields $E = \partial_{y}X$). So the $f\wedge n$ part of $\Omega(V)$ is $B(V_{\perp})\wedge n$. In another rotation gauge spinors change by a rotor $S(x)$, the two-point kernel by $S(x)\,(\cdot)\,S(x')^{\dagger}$, and the projector by $S\Lambda S^{-1}$ on the left and $(S\Lambda S^{-1})^{\dagger}$ on the right; the components of the restricted kernel in the parallel frame do not change (computed exactly in the model below, where the gauge is not adapted off one generator and the right projector is $\Lambda(x')^{\dagger} = e_{0}\tilde\Lambda(x')e_{0}$).

\emph{Step 1 (decomposition).} Write $x = X(u, y' + \eta)$, $x' = X(u', y')$. For scalar $\phi$ and spinor-valued $U$, $D(\phi U) = (\nabla\phi)U + \phi\,DU$, so with $\nabla\sigma_{\epsilon} = \nabla\sigma + i\epsilon\nabla t$,
\[
\Lambda D\Bigl(\frac{U}{\sigma_{\epsilon}}\Bigr)e_{0}\Lambda = \frac{N}{\sigma_{\epsilon}^{2}} + \frac{(i\epsilon s - \tfrac12\epsilon^{2})\,\Lambda(DU)e_{0}\Lambda}{\sigma_{\epsilon}^{2}} - \frac{i\epsilon\,\Lambda(\nabla t)Ue_{0}\Lambda}{\sigma_{\epsilon}^{2}},\qquad N = \Lambda\bigl[(DU)\sigma - (\nabla\sigma)U\bigr]e_{0}\Lambda,
\]
and the mass and logarithmic parts are $m_{0}\Lambda Ue_{0}\Lambda/\sigma_{\epsilon}$ and $\Lambda(iD + m_{0})(V\log\sigma_{\epsilon})e_{0}\Lambda$. In the null frame $D = nD_{k} + kD_{n} + f^{c}D_{f_{c}}$ ($f^{c} = -f_{c}$), and $\Lambda k = 0$ removes $kD_{n}$ entirely. Everything is smooth in $(u, u', y', \eta)$ on $N\times N$ except through $1/\sigma_{\epsilon}$ and $\log\sigma_{\epsilon}$.

\emph{Step 2 (no terms of degree $-4$ or $-3$; proved).} On the generator ($\eta = 0$) $\sigma = 0$ and $\nabla\sigma = (u - u')k$ for all $u, u'$, and $\sigma$ has no term linear in $\eta$ (that theorem's (i)); hence $\partial_{u}\sigma = k\cdot\nabla\sigma = O(|\eta|^{2})$. Expand $N = N_{0} + N_{1} + N_{2} + O(|\eta|^{3})$ in homogeneous degrees in $\eta$, $U = \Delta^{1/2}(1 + R_{1} + \ldots)$ with $R_{1}$ a bivector linear in $\eta$ ($R = 1$ on the generator). $N_{0} = -(u - u')\Delta^{1/2}\Lambda ke_{0}\Lambda = 0$. Since $(DU)\sigma = O(|\eta|^{2})$, $N_{1} = -\Lambda\bigl[w\Delta^{1/2} + (u - u')k(\ldots)\bigr]e_{0}\Lambda$, $w$ the linear part of $\nabla\sigma$; the second term vanishes by $\Lambda k = 0$ and the first is $-\Delta^{1/2}(w\cdot k)\Lambda$ by $\Lambda pe_{0}\Lambda = (p\cdot k)\Lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(ii)), and $w\cdot k$ is the linear part of $\partial_{u}\sigma$, zero. So $N = O(|\eta|^{2})$ and $N/\sigma_{\epsilon}^{2}$ has no part of degree below $-2$. Likewise $\Lambda Ue_{0}\Lambda = \Delta^{1/2}\Lambda e_{0}\Lambda + O(|\eta|) = O(|\eta|)$ ($\Lambda e_{0}\Lambda = 0$) and $\Lambda\nabla\sigma = (u - u')\Lambda k + O(|\eta|) = O(|\eta|)$, so the mass term $m_{0}\Lambda Ue_{0}\Lambda/\sigma$ and the term $\Lambda(\nabla\sigma)Ve_{0}\Lambda/\sigma$ of $D(V\log\sigma)$ have degree $\ge -1$; $(\partial_{u}\sigma)V/\sigma$ has degree $0$ and $(DV)\log\sigma$ is integrable.

\emph{Step 3 (the coefficient of $\log\epsilon$; proved).} For a function $g$ of $\eta$ homogeneous of degree $-2$ let $L[g] = \lim_{\delta \to 0}\bigl(\int_{\delta < |\eta|_{M} < 1}g\,d^{2}\eta\bigr)/\log(1/\delta)$, $|\eta|_{M}^{2} = M(\eta, \eta)$. With $\zeta = L_{M}\eta$, $\bar L_{M}L_{M} = M$, $L[g] = (\det M)^{-1/2}\oint g(L_{M}^{-1}\omega)\,d\omega$; for $g = \eta^{T}X\eta/\sigma_{2}^{2}$, $\sigma_{2} = -\tfrac12 M(\eta, \eta)$, this is $4\pi\,\mathrm{tr}(M^{-1}X)/\sqrt{\det M}$, and $L[1/\sigma_{2}] = -4\pi/\sqrt{\det M}$. The regularised integral has the cutoff at $|\eta|_{M}^{2} \sim \epsilon|s|$, so $\int F(y' + \eta)\,g_{\epsilon}\,d^{2}\eta = -\tfrac12 L[g]F(y')(\log\epsilon + \log(-is)) + O(1)$ (for $g = 1/\sigma_{2}$ this is the transverse-integral formula of that theorem's Step 5). The degree $-2$ part of $N/\sigma^{2}$ is $N_{2}/\sigma_{2}^{2}$, with three contributions.
(a) From $nD_{k}$: $\Lambda nXe_{0}\Lambda = X\Lambda$ for scalar $X$ ($\Lambda n = n$, $ne_{0}\Lambda = \Lambda$), and the $R_{1}$ parts are of degree $\ge -1$; so the contribution is the degree $-2$ part of $\partial_{u}(\Delta^{1/2}/\sigma)\Lambda$, and since $\partial_{u}$ acts on the coefficients, $L$ of it is $\partial_{u}L[\Delta^{1/2}/\sigma_{2}] = -4\pi\,\partial_{u}(\Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M})$.
(b) From the connection in $f^{c}D_{f_{c}}$: $\tfrac12\Lambda f^{c}\Omega(f_{c})Ue_{0}\Lambda/\sigma = \tfrac12\theta(u)\Delta^{1/2}\Lambda/\sigma + O(|\eta|^{-1})$, since only the $f\wedge n$ part of a bivector survives $\Lambda f^{c}(\cdot)e_{0}\Lambda$, with $\Lambda f^{c}(w\wedge n)e_{0}\Lambda = f^{c}w\Lambda$, and $f^{c}B(f_{c}) = \mathrm{tr}\,B$ for self-adjoint $B$ (exact Clifford identities; the shear and the other components drop). $L$ of it is $-2\pi\theta\,\Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M}$.
(c) From the derivative in $f^{c}D_{f_{c}}$: $\Lambda f^{c}\partial_{f_{c}}(U/\sigma)e_{0}\Lambda$. Its scalar part $\Lambda f^{c}\partial_{f_{c}}(\Delta^{1/2}/\sigma)e_{0}\Lambda$ vanishes ($\Lambda f^{c}e_{0}\Lambda = 0$), and what remains at degree $-2$ is $\Lambda f^{c}\partial_{f_{c}}(\Delta^{1/2}R_{1}/\sigma)e_{0}\Lambda$, a transverse derivative of a function homogeneous of degree $-1$. With $E_{b} = J_{cb}f_{c} + \alpha_{b}k$, $\partial_{f_{c}} = (J^{-1})_{bc}(\partial_{\eta_{b}} - \alpha_{b}\partial_{u})$; the $\alpha\partial_{u}$ part and the $\eta$-dependence of $J$ give degree $\ge -1$, so at degree $-2$ this is the divergence $\partial_{\eta_{b}}V_{b}$ of $V_{b} = (J^{-1})_{bc}\Delta^{1/2}\Lambda f^{c}R_{1}e_{0}\Lambda/\sigma_{2}$, homogeneous of degree $-1$. Its integral over $\delta < |\eta|_{M} < 1$ is a difference of two boundary integrals, each independent of $\delta$ by homogeneity: $L = 0$. The first-order transport therefore does not enter, whatever $R_{1}$ is.
Hence the coefficient of $\log\epsilon$ (and of $\log(-is)$) in the restriction of the leading term is, with the canonical factor,
\[
-\tfrac12 L[N_{2}/\sigma_{2}^{2}]\,(a(u)a(u'))^{1/2} = 2\pi\,(a(u)a(u'))^{1/2}\Bigl(\partial_{u} + \tfrac12\theta(u)\Bigr)\frac{\Delta^{1/2}}{\sqrt{\det M}}\,\Lambda\;\cdot F(y'),
\]
times the normalising constant (computed exactly on generic jets, below). By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces}(i), $\Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M} = (a(u)a(u'))^{-1/2}$, and $(\partial_{u} + \tfrac12\theta(u))(a(u)a(u'))^{-1/2} = 0$ because $\theta = a'/a$. The coefficient vanishes identically in $(u, u', y')$: the term $-\pi\theta(u)(\log\epsilon + \log(-is))\delta^{2}(y - y')$ of that theorem's Step 5, from (a), is cancelled by the projected transverse connection (b), and there is no $\log(u - u')$ term in the restricted kernel.

\emph{Step 4 (model integrals; proved).} Near the generator write $\sigma_{\epsilon} = -A_{\epsilon} + \rho$ with the model $A_{\epsilon}(\eta) = \tfrac12 M(\eta, \eta) + c_{0}\epsilon^{2} - i\epsilon(s_{0} + s_{1}\cdot\eta)$, where $s_{0} = t(X(u, y')) - t(X(u', y'))$, $s_{1}$ is the linear part of $s$ in $\eta$, $c_{0} = \tfrac12$, and $|\rho| \le C(|\eta|^{3} + \epsilon|\eta|^{2} + \epsilon^{2}|\eta|)$ (the $\epsilon^{2}$ coefficient of $\sigma_{\epsilon}$ is $\tfrac12$ here; for another standard regularisation it is a smooth positive $c(x, x')$, and $c_{0} = c$ on the generator). Since $\mathrm{Re}\,A_{\epsilon} \ge \tfrac12 M(\eta, \eta) + c_{0}\epsilon^{2}$, also along the shift $\eta \to \eta + i\lambda\epsilon M^{-1}s_{1}$, $\lambda \in [0, 1]$ (the real part gains $\epsilon^{2}(\lambda - \tfrac12\lambda^{2})s_{1}\cdot M^{-1}s_{1} \ge 0$), the shift of the integration plane crosses no zero, and at $\lambda = 1$ the model becomes isotropic in $\zeta$: $A_{\epsilon} = \tfrac12|\zeta|^{2} + C_{\epsilon}$, $C_{\epsilon} = g\epsilon^{2} - i\epsilon s_{0}$, $g = c_{0} + \tfrac12 s_{1}\cdot M^{-1}s_{1} > 0$. With $\int_{0}^{\infty}dq/(q + C)^{2} = 1/C$ this gives, exactly:
(a) $\int_{\R^{2}}d^{2}\eta/A_{\epsilon}^{2} = (2\pi/\sqrt{\det M})/C_{\epsilon}$;
(b) $\int_{\R^{2}}(i\epsilon(s_{0} + s_{1}\cdot\eta) - c_{0}\epsilon^{2})/A_{\epsilon}^{2}\,d^{2}\eta = -(2\pi/\sqrt{\det M})(1 + \tfrac12\epsilon^{2}s_{1}\cdot M^{-1}s_{1}/C_{\epsilon})$, bounded by $(2\pi/\sqrt{\det M})(1 + s_{1}\cdot M^{-1}s_{1}/(2g))$ (the numerator is $\tfrac12 M(\eta, \eta) - A_{\epsilon}$; the odd term of the shift integrates to zero);
(c) for $X$ with $\mathrm{tr}(M^{-1}X) = 0$ and $\hat A_{\epsilon} = \tfrac12 M(\eta, \eta) + c_{0}\epsilon^{2} - i\epsilon s_{0}$: $\int_{|\eta|_{M} < \rho}\eta^{T}X\eta/\hat A_{\epsilon}^{2} = 0$ and $\int_{|\eta|_{M} < \rho}\eta^{T}X\eta\,(s_{1}\cdot\eta)/\hat A_{\epsilon}^{3} = 0$ (angular means), while $|\eta^{T}X\eta|\,|A_{\epsilon}^{-2} - \hat A_{\epsilon}^{-2} - 2i\epsilon(s_{1}\cdot\eta)\hat A_{\epsilon}^{-3}| \le C\epsilon^{2}|\eta|^{4}(|\eta|^{2} + \epsilon^{2})^{-4}$, whose integral is bounded uniformly in $\epsilon$ and $s_{0}$.

\emph{Step 5 (the $i0$ term and the bounded remainder; proved).} Fix profiles $F$, $G$ with support in a compact set $\mathcal{K}$ of labels and $\|F\|_{C^{1}}, \|G\|_{C^{1}} \le 1$, and $(u, u')$ in a compact interval. Split the $\eta$ integration at $|\eta| = \delta_{0}$. For $|\eta| \ge \delta_{0}$, (S) and compactness give $\sigma \le -c_{1} < 0$, so $|\sigma_{\epsilon}| \ge c_{1}$ and the integrand is smooth, bounded uniformly in $\epsilon$ and uniformly convergent. For $|\eta| < \delta_{0}$, $|\sigma_{\epsilon}|, |A_{\epsilon}| \ge c(|\eta|^{2} + \epsilon^{2})$ uniformly; each term of Step 1 is its model (coefficients frozen at $\eta = 0$, denominators replaced by $A_{\epsilon}$) plus a correction bounded by $C|\eta|^{-1}$ plus finitely many terms $C\epsilon^{i}|\eta|^{j}(|\eta|^{2} + \epsilon^{2})^{-(i + j + 2)/2}$ with $i \ge 1$, $j \ge 0$, all with integrals over $|\eta| < \delta_{0}$ bounded uniformly in $\epsilon$ (scale $\eta = \epsilon\xi$; the condition $i \ge 1$ makes the $\xi$ integral converge), using $F(y' + \eta) - F(y') = O(|\eta|)$, $N - N_{2} = O(|\eta|^{3})$, the bound on $\rho$ and the $O(|\eta|)$ variation of $\Delta^{1/2}$, $\Lambda(\nabla t)e_{0}\Lambda$ and $\Lambda(DU)e_{0}\Lambda$. The models:
(1) $N/\sigma_{\epsilon}^{2}$: model $F(y')N_{2}/A_{\epsilon}^{2}$, bounded uniformly by Step 4(c), since $\mathrm{tr}(M^{-1}X) = 0$ for the quadratic form $X$ of $N_{2}$ (Step 3).
(2) The middle term: model $F(y')\Lambda(DU)e_{0}\Lambda|_{\eta = 0}$ times the integral of Step 4(b): bounded.
(3) The $i0$ term: at $\eta = 0$, $\Lambda(\nabla t)Ue_{0}\Lambda = \Delta^{1/2}(k\cdot\nabla t)\Lambda = \Delta^{1/2}\partial_{u}t\,\Lambda$, and by Step 4(a) the model is $(2\pi\Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M})\,\partial_{u}t/(s_{0} + ig\epsilon)\,\Lambda F(y')$ (the region $|\eta| \ge \delta_{0}$ of the model is $O(\epsilon)$). Since $t$ increases strictly along the future-directed generators, $s_{0} = (u - u')\varphi(u, u')$ with $\varphi > 0$ smooth, and as $\epsilon \to 0$, $\partial_{u}t/(s_{0} + ig\epsilon) \to \partial_{u}\log(s_{0} + i0) = (u - u' + i0)^{-1} + \partial_{u}\log\varphi$ in $\mathcal{D}'$ ($g > 0$ smooth). With the canonical factor, $(a(u)a(u'))^{1/2}\Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M} = 1$, and the constant fixed by the flat case, this is $W_{0}(u, u')\Lambda$ smeared with $\langle F, G\rangle$ plus the smooth kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\partial_{u}\log\varphi\,\Lambda$, which depends on the time function (on the flat null plane with $t$ nonlinear along the generators the limit is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\partial_{u}t/(t(u) - t(u') + i0)$, not $W_{0}$; the bulk time-function independence of the Fact does not pass to the restriction), so the regularised restriction is defined for the chosen $t$ and only modulo smooth kernels: that theorem's (ii), with the exclusion of every other term of this order now proved (Steps 2, 3: nothing of degree below $-2$, no $\log$ at degree $-2$, and the only source of $(u - u')^{-1}$ is the $i0$ term).
(4) The mass and logarithmic terms: degree $\ge -1$ by Step 2, so bounded by $C|\eta|^{-1}$ or $C(1 + |\log|\sigma_{\epsilon}||)$, integrable uniformly; the term $i\epsilon\Lambda(\nabla t)Ve_{0}\Lambda/\sigma_{\epsilon}$ is $O(\epsilon\log(1/\epsilon))$.
For fixed $u \neq u'$ every correction and every model other than (3) converges as $\epsilon \to 0$ (where needed, $|\sigma_{\epsilon}| \ge \tfrac12\epsilon|s_{0}|$ near $\eta = 0$ improves the bounds to $O(\epsilon^{1/2}|s_{0}|^{-1/2})$). By dominated convergence in $(u, u')$, the smeared restricted parametrix converges in $\mathcal{D}'$ to $W_{0}\langle F, G\rangle\Lambda + r_{F,G}$ with $\sup|r_{F,G}| \le C$, $C$ depending on $\mathcal{K}$, the interval, $m_{0}$ and the $C^{1}$ bounds only. This is (ii) of the claim.

\emph{Step 6 (the bound of (HS); proved).} For $r$ bounded, $|\lambda^{\varpi}\int r(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda x')\phi(x, x')\,dx\,dx'| \le \lambda^{\varpi}\sup|r|\,\|\phi\|_{L^{1}} \to 0$ for every $\varpi > 0$, uniformly over the profiles of Step 5. So $R^{\mathrm{par}}$ has generator scaling degree at most $0$ at every $(u_{0}, u_{0})$, and the clause of Premise \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise} holds with any $\varpi \in (0, 1)$, for every $m_{0} \ge 0$ and every geodesic null hypersurface, in particular every local Rindler horizon through $x_{0}$ (a smooth null hypersurface with affinely parametrised generators, Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}), whatever the field strength at $x_{0}$. Nothing in Steps 0 to 6 uses vanishing expansion or shear, the field equations, or the value of the field strength.

\emph{Exact checks (computed).} (1) The projector identities of Steps 2 and 3 in the spacetime algebra. (2) Generic jets in the adapted gauge: $M(u)$, $\partial_{u}M$, cubic terms of $\sigma$, $\Delta^{1/2}$ with transverse dependence, a transport rotor with arbitrary first- and second-order parts (all bivector components), a connection with the $f\wedge n$ part $B(f_{c})\wedge n$ plus arbitrary other components and transverse dependence, $J$ depending on $\eta$ and arbitrary $\alpha$: $N_{0} = N_{1} = 0$ and $\mathrm{tr}(M^{-1}X) = -[\partial_{u}d - \tfrac12 d\,\mathrm{tr}(M^{-1}\partial_{u}M) + \tfrac12\theta d]\Lambda$ ($d = \Delta^{1/2}$ on the generator) exactly, at four sample sets; with $B$ not self-adjoint or the connection dropped the formula fails. (3) On the plane-wave model of that theorem (tidal map rotated off the label basis, deviation map not commuting with it, Ricci and Weyl parts nonzero), $\partial_{u}\log\Delta - \mathrm{tr}(M^{-1}\partial_{u}M) + \theta(u) = 0$ exactly. (4) From first principles on that field in its Kerr-Schild gauge $\hb^{-1}(a) = a + \tfrac12 H(a\cdot K)K$ (not adapted off the central generator): with the closed-form Synge function, the exact transport rotor $R = 1 + \tfrac12\sum_{i}(t_{i} - w_{i})e_{i}\wedge K$ (the null rotations commute; $t$, $w$ the end velocities of the geodesic), $\Omega(\partial_{u}) = \tfrac12\partial_{i}H\,e_{i}\wedge K$ and the projectors $\Lambda(x)$, $\Lambda(x')^{\dagger}$ of the parallel frame, $N_{0} = N_{1} = 0$ and $\mathrm{tr}(M^{-1}X) = 0$ exactly at three point pairs ($u > u'$, $u < u'$, central and off-central generators), while freezing $\Lambda(x)$, doubling $\partial_{u}\log\Delta$ or dropping the transport breaks it. (5) The same on the flat field with an expanding and shearing null hypersurface. (6) The rotor is the spin transport ($D_{T}R = 0$ along the geodesic tangent $T$), and $\Omega$ is checked against its coordinate reading (Christoffel symbols). In this gauge the connection enters the kernel only through the transport rotor (the term $K\,\Omega(\partial_{u})$ vanishes, $K(e_{i}\wedge K) = 0$), and the rotor is built from the same $\Omega(\partial_{u})$, so a change of its sign is detected; the projected transverse connection of Step 3(b) is tested on generic jets. (7) The mass and $V\log\sigma$ numerators vanish on the generator. (8) The model integrals of Steps 3 and 4.

\emph{Status.} (i) and (ii) are proved, given the imported leading Hadamard coefficient and $i0$ prescription and Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces}(i), (ii); (iii) is proved from them. The restriction is the $\epsilon$-regularised one in which (HS) is posed; its agreement with the restriction defined through the characteristic-data embedding, used to pass from the parametrix to states, is not part of this result. Transport-absent.

synthesis.s-wave-array-is-a-boundary-mod.formal:
Let $\{\psi_k, \psi_k^{\dagger}\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be the s-wave array of boundary modes of Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}, with boost weights $\omega_k = \kappa k$ and the sea filled below the level, and let $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The tower is the model, not the count.)} The adjoined null pairs of the tower satisfy the CAR exactly at the level of vectors (Fact \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}), so $n$ rungs realise a window algebra of $n$ modes and the tower limit is the CAR algebra over a countable set (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}). On the physical closure one ascent completes the description, further rungs lying on shadow walls outside the physical region (Corollary \claimref{tower.answers-iteration-question}(1)); so the physical boundary modes are not counted by rungs, and the tower supplies the form of their algebra only.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Particle-hole conjugation makes the array a mode set.)} Put $b_k := \psi_k^{\dagger}$ for $k < 0$ and $b_k := \psi_k$ for $k \geq 0$. The $b_k$ satisfy the CAR, the boost dynamics acts as $b_k \mapsto e^{-i\kappa|k|t}b_k$, and on every finite window $\sum_k \kappa k\,N_k = \sum_k \kappa|k|\,N'_k + \sum_{k<0}\kappa k$ with $N'_k = b_k^{\dagger}b_k$, so the Gibbs state of the one is the Gibbs state of the other. Each frequency $\kappa m$, $m \geq 1$, occurs exactly twice (a particle at $k = m$, a hole at $k = -m$), and the frequency $0$ once, at $k = 0$. The Fermi-Dirac marginals $n_k = (e^{\beta\kappa k} + 1)^{-1}$ of the bosonisation theorem become $\langle N'_k\rangle = (e^{\beta\kappa|k|} + 1)^{-1}$ for $k \neq 0$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The zero mode is in its trace state.)} On one mode of frequency $\omega \geq 0$ the KMS relation at $\beta$ is $n = e^{-\beta\omega}(1 - n)$, whose unique solution is the Fermi-Dirac value; at $\omega = 0$ it is $n = \tfrac12$, the trace.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the definition of the boundary-mode algebra (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}) applies with $J = \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$ and $\omega_j = \kappa|j|$, with one provenance, the ladder pairs of the blown-up singular boundary aggregated over s-wave channels, and the tower as model. Under (Q), the state of the array with these marginals, quasi-free on $J$, is the I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state} on that mode set, and the excluded zero mode carries the trace, so the extension to the full array has no free parameter.
synthesis.s-wave-array-is-a-boundary-mod.technical:
The boundary modes have two descriptions in the series: as rungs of the tower of iterated completions, whose limit is a CAR algebra over a countable set, and as the ladder pairs of the blown-up singular boundary, one per point, aggregated over s-wave channels into an array $\psi_k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, with weights $\kappa k$ and a filled sea. The tower's null pairs satisfy the CAR exactly, so they model the algebra; but the physical closure has one ascent, further rungs sitting on shadow walls, so they do not count the modes.

The array becomes a mode set of the thermality paper's definition by particle-hole conjugation below the level: $b_k = \psi_k^{\dagger}$ for $k < 0$. The Hamiltonian changes by a constant, every frequency becomes $\kappa|k| \geq 0$, each positive frequency appears twice (particle and hole), and the Fermi-Dirac marginals stay Fermi-Dirac at $\kappa|k|$. One mode has frequency zero; the thermality paper's definition requires positive frequencies and so excludes it, but the KMS relation forces its occupation to $1/2$, the trace. So, under (Q), the singularity paper's quasi-free state on the array is the I-state on $J = \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$ with $\omega_j = \kappa|j|$, tensored with the trace on the zero mode.
synthesis.s-wave-array-is-a-boundary-mod.lay: The series describes the quantum modes at a black hole's singularity in two ways: as the steps of an infinite tower of algebraic completions, and as one pair of modes at each point of the singularity's boundary, gathered into a list by keeping the spherically symmetric part. The first description is only a mathematical model: physically the tower stops after one step. This result makes the second description fit the thermal theory exactly. Modes below the filled level are relabelled as holes, which makes every frequency positive; each frequency then appears twice, once for a particle and once for a hole; and the single mode of zero frequency, which the thermal theory's definition leaves out, is forced to be exactly half occupied. Given the singularity paper's assumption that the joint state is of the simplest (quasi-free) kind, its thermal state is then the series' unique thermal state, with nothing left to choose.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Fact \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors} gives $v_iv_j + v_jv_i = 0$, $w_iw_j + w_jw_i = 0$, $v_iw_j + w_jv_i = \delta_{ij}$ for the $k$ adjoined null pairs of $T_k$, so the pairs are $k$ fermionic modes and their algebra is a window algebra of $k$ modes, of dimension $4^{k}$; by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra} the limit is the CAR algebra over a countable set with these pairs as modes. Corollary \claimref{tower.answers-iteration-question}(1) states that on the physical closure one ascent completes the description and that the further rungs are carried by the shadow-wall sequence, displaced away from the physical region. Hence the rungs beyond the first are not physical modes, and the countable index set of the physical boundary modes is not supplied by them; what the tower supplies is a realisation of the CAR algebra, which by uniqueness of the CAR relations on each window (a finite set of modes satisfying the CAR generates a full matrix algebra, unique up to isomorphism) is the same algebra whatever indexes the modes. The script checks the CAR for the null pairs $v_j = \tfrac12(e_j + f_j)$, $w_j = \tfrac12(e_j - f_j)$ in $\Cl(n, n)$ for $n = 1, \dots, 4$, and that $v_jw_j$ and $w_jv_j$ are complementary projections.

\emph{(ii)} The array and its weights are those of Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}, whose marginal occupancies are $n_k = (e^{\beta\kappa k} + 1)^{-1}$. Conjugation $\psi \mapsto \psi^{\dagger}$ on a subset of modes preserves the CAR (it exchanges the roles of $\psi_k$ and $\psi_k^{\dagger}$ in $\{\psi_k, \psi_k^{\dagger}\} = 1$ and leaves the other anticommutators zero), so the $b_k$ are a CAR array. For $k < 0$, $\tau_t(\psi_k) = e^{-i\kappa kt}\psi_k$ gives $\tau_t(b_k) = \tau_t(\psi_k)^{\dagger} = e^{i\kappa kt}b_k = e^{-i\kappa|k|t}b_k$. With $N'_k = b_k^{\dagger}b_k = \psi_k\psi_k^{\dagger} = 1 - N_k$ for $k < 0$, $\kappa kN_k = \kappa|k|N'_k + \kappa k$, which sums to the displayed identity of Hamiltonians on any finite window; two Hamiltonians differing by a constant have the same Gibbs state, and $\langle N'_k\rangle = 1 - n_k = (e^{\beta\kappa|k|} + 1)^{-1}$. The frequency count is the observation that $k \mapsto |k|$ is two-to-one on $\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. The script builds Jordan-Wigner windows $k = -K, \dots, K$ ($K = 1, 2$) with real matrices, verifies the CAR for $\psi$ and for $b$, the Hamiltonian identity, the multiplicities, and the marginals of the Gibbs state at three rational values of $e^{-\beta\kappa}$, exactly.

\emph{(iii)} For one mode with $\tau_t(a) = e^{-i\omega t}a$, the KMS condition at $\beta$ applied to $a^{\dagger}$ and $a$ gives $\omega(a^{\dagger}a) = e^{-\beta\omega}\omega(aa^{\dagger})$, that is $n = e^{-\beta\omega}(1 - n)$, linear in $n$ with coefficient $1 + e^{-\beta\omega} \neq 0$, so $n = (e^{\beta\omega} + 1)^{-1}$ uniquely; this is the one-mode case of Lemma \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}. At $\omega = 0$ the flow is trivial on the mode, a KMS state of a trivial flow is a trace, and the trace on the mode's $2 \times 2$ matrix algebra is unique: the state is $\tfrac12\,\mathrm{tr}$, with $n = \tfrac12$. The script checks the relation and its solution for $\omega = 0, \kappa, 2\kappa, 3\kappa$ at $e^{-\beta\kappa} = \tfrac12$.

For the closing paragraph: by (ii) the $b_j$, $j \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$, form a countable mode set with positive frequencies $\kappa|j|$, which is what Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} requires; its boost dynamics is the restriction of the array's. A quasi-free state on that mode set that is KMS at $\beta$ is, by Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}, the state with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$, $h = \mathrm{diag}(\kappa|j|)$, whose marginals are those of (ii); so, under (Q) (Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}, which the bosonisation theorem holds given and which makes the joint state quasi-free), the array's state with the bosonisation theorem's marginals restricts to the I-state there; parts (i) to (iii) do not use (Q), and by (iii) it is the trace on the zero mode. The provenance statement collects (i) and the definition of the array: the modes are the ladder pairs of the blown-up singular boundary aggregated over s-wave channels, an identification the singularity paper makes and flags, and the tower is the model of their algebra. Transport content: (i) uses the series' tower; (ii) and (iii) are standard fermion bookkeeping and transport-absent.

synthesis.schwarzschild-horizon-translat.formal:
Units $c = G = 1$. Store sign (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}), signature $(+,-,-,-)$; let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be the Schwarzschild gravitational field of mass $M > 0$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) in the ingoing (Kerr-Schild) gauge $\hb^{-1}(a) = a - \tfrac{M}{r}(a\cdot k)k$, $k = e_{0} + \hat{x}$, which covers the exterior, the future horizon $r = 2M$ and the interior; $g$ its derived metric and $I$ the square of the Weyl part of its curvature $\mathcal{R}(B)$ (its Weyl square). A \emph{conformal symmetry} on an open set $W$ is a vector field $\xi$ on $W$ whose flow preserves the derived metric up to a positive function, $\mathcal{L}_{\xi}g = 2\phi g$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The invariant.)} The field is Ricci-flat and $I = 48M^{2}/r^{6} > 0$ at every point of the invertible region, inside, on and outside the horizon.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(An invariant metric.)} The Weyl square of $\Omega^{2}g$ is $\Omega^{-4}I$ for every positive function $\Omega$, so the metric $(2M)^{3}(I/48M^{2})^{1/2}g = (2M/r)^{3}g =: \hat g$ is the same when computed from $g$ or from any $\Omega^{2}g$. Hence every conformal symmetry of the field on $W$ is a Killing field of $\hat g$ on $W$. The Weyl square of $\hat g$ is the constant $48M^{2}/(2M)^{6}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Separation.)} The scalar curvature of $\hat g$ is $\hat R = (27M - \tfrac92 r)/(2M)^{3}$, affine in $r$ with nonzero slope, so every Killing field of $\hat g$, hence every conformal symmetry of the field, is tangent to the spheres-times-time $r = \mathrm{const}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The algebra.)} On every connected open $W$ in the invertible region, every conformal symmetry is $\alpha\,\partial_{t} + \sum_{j}c_{j}L_{j}$ with constants $\alpha$, $c_{j}$, where $\partial_{t}$ is the background time translation (a symmetry of the field: the gauge field does not depend on $t$) and $L_{j}$ the rotations; in particular it is a Killing symmetry of the field.
\item[(v)] \emph{(The horizon.)} On the future horizon $r = 2M$ the physical vector of $\partial_{t}$ is null and tangent to the generators, with $(K\cdot D)K = -\kappa K$ in the store's $D$, $\kappa = 1/(4M)$: the time translation by $\tau$ acts on a generator's affine parameter $\lambda$ as the dilation $\lambda \mapsto e^{\kappa\tau}\lambda$ about the bifurcation edge (the boost $\beta_{t}$ of the setup and item (ii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}). Hence the restriction of any conformal symmetry to an open piece of the horizon is $\alpha\kappa\lambda\,\partial_{\lambda}$ plus a rotation, and the affine translations $\lambda \mapsto \lambda + a$ along the generators are the restriction of no conformal symmetry on any open set meeting the horizon.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Consequence for (N$_{+}$) case (a).)} The positivity of the stored conformal energy reaches a translation only through the conformal symmetries of the field it is represented on (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-gives-positive-null-translations}; for de Sitter, whose Weyl part vanishes, the horizon translation is the conformal null rotation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation}). By (v) no element of the field's conformal symmetry algebra on a neighbourhood of a piece of the horizon, nor a limit of elements, acts on the generators as the affine translations: their positivity on the eternal hole cannot come from the field's conformal structure, nor be carried to the horizon from a region of vanishing field strength by a conformal map. It is a condition on the state of the generators' modes.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.schwarzschild-horizon-translat.technical:
The series gets positive energy for null translations from one source: a nonnegative conformal energy, generated by the central rotation $Z$ of the twistor form, which bounds every generator in a cone of the conformal algebra. That reaches the local horizons of Minkowski space, where null translations are symmetries, and the de Sitter horizon, where the uniform affine translation is a conformal null rotation of the background because the de Sitter field is a pure dilation. The eternal Schwarzschild horizon is the case left open.

Here the conformal route is closed for good. The Weyl square $I = 48M^{2}/r^{6}$ never vanishes, and because it has conformal weight $-4$ the metric $\hat g = I^{1/2}g$, up to a constant, is the same for every metric in the conformal class: a conformal symmetry of the field is an ordinary symmetry of $\hat g$. Its scalar curvature $(27M - \tfrac92 r)/(2M)^{3}$ changes with $r$, so such symmetries keep $r$ fixed, and on the shells of constant $r$ they can only be time translations and rotations. On the horizon the time translation is the boost, a dilation of each generator's affine parameter about the bifurcation edge, not a translation. So no conformal symmetry of the field, even locally, shifts the affine parameter along the generators. Positivity there must be a property of the state, as (N$_{+}$) states it; within stationary states the stored edge result says what that property is. A state-side condition at the edge that supplies the positivity is \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}.
synthesis.schwarzschild-horizon-translat.lay: In this series, the reason quantum fields near a horizon have positive energy along the horizon's light rays comes from a symmetry: in empty space, and in a universe driven only by a cosmological constant, sliding along those light rays is a symmetry of the geometry up to rescaling, and the rescaling symmetries carry a positive energy. Around an eternal black hole that argument cannot work. The black hole's tidal curvature, which never vanishes, can be used to build a measuring stick that every rescaling symmetry must respect, and with it one shows that the only symmetries, even allowing rescaling, are waiting in time and turning in space. On the horizon, waiting in time stretches the light rays about their common edge instead of sliding along them. So positive energy along the black hole's horizon cannot come from symmetry; it has to be a property of the quantum state there.
flags: beyond one flat chart: the bifurcation surface of the eternal hole lies off the ingoing (Kerr-Schild) chart used here; the statement there follows by the same argument in a chart through it, or by the time reflection of the field

proofs.main:
Conventions as in the statement (store sign of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}). The check computes every curvature below from the gauge field, as exact Taylor jets of $\hb^{-1}$ (order two) about background points $(0, 0, 0, r)$ at $M = \tfrac12$ ($2M = 1$), at $r = \tfrac14, 1, \tfrac94, 4, 9$ (inside, on and outside the horizon), with the torsion-free $\Omega$ solved from the jets; the general $M$ follows by the scaling $x \mapsto 2M x$, under which $I$ scales as $(2M)^{-4}$ and $\hat g$, $\hat R$ as stated.

\emph{(i).} The check finds $\mathcal{R}(b) = 0$ (Ricci-flat) and $2\langle\mathcal{R}(a\wedge b)\mathcal{R}(\partial_{b}\wedge\partial_{a})\rangle = 48M^{2}/r^{6}$ at the five radii (tabulated), equal to the square of the Weyl part since the Ricci part vanishes. For general $r$ this is the standard Kretschmann scalar of the Schwarzschild metric (cited from memory); the samples on both sides of the horizon are a check of it in the store's sign, not a proof of the general formula.

\emph{(ii).} Let $C^{a}{}_{bcd}$ be the Weyl tensor of $g$, of type $(1,3)$. Under $g \mapsto \Omega^{2}g$ it is unchanged (conformal invariance of the Weyl tensor), and $I = C^{a}{}_{bcd}C^{e}{}_{fgh}\,g_{ae}g^{bf}g^{cg}g^{dh}$ has one metric and three inverse metrics, so $I \mapsto \Omega^{2 - 6}I = \Omega^{-4}I$. The check confirms the weight $-4$ exactly for the two nonconstant factors $\Omega = 2M/r$ and $\Omega = (2M/r)^{3/2}$ (tabulated). Hence $\hat g := (2M)^{3}(I/48M^{2})^{1/2}g = (2M/r)^{3}g$ satisfies $\widehat{\Omega^{2}g} = \Omega^{-2}\cdot\Omega^{2}\hat g = \hat g$. If $\xi$ is a conformal symmetry on $W$, its flow $\varphi_{s}$ satisfies $\varphi_{s}^{*}g = \Omega_{s}^{2}g$ and carries the Weyl tensor of $g$ to that of $\varphi_{s}^{*}g$, so $\varphi_{s}^{*}I = I(\varphi_{s}^{*}g) = \Omega_{s}^{-4}I$ and $\varphi_{s}^{*}\hat g = (2M)^{3}(\Omega_{s}^{-4}I/48M^{2})^{1/2}\Omega_{s}^{2}g = \hat g$: $\xi$ is a Killing field of $\hat g$. With $\Omega = (2M/r)^{3/2}$ the check finds the Weyl square of $\hat g$ equal to $12 = 48M^{2}/(2M)^{6}$ at three radii.

\emph{(iii).} The check computes the scalar curvature of the gauge field $(2M/r)^{3/2}\hb^{-1}$ (whose derived metric is $\hat g$) at the five radii: $\tfrac{99}{8}, 9, \tfrac{27}{8}, -\tfrac92, -27$, equal to $(27M - \tfrac92 r)/(2M)^{3}$, with every difference quotient $-\tfrac92$. (Independently: for $\hat g = \Omega^{2}g$ with $g$ Ricci-flat, $\hat R = -6\,\Omega^{-3}\Box_{g}\Omega$ in the sign where spheres have positive curvature, and $\Omega = (2M/r)^{3/2}$, $\Box_{g}\Omega = r^{-2}\partial_{r}(r^{2}(1 - 2M/r)\partial_{r}\Omega)$ give the same affine function.) A Killing field $\xi$ of $\hat g$ preserves $\hat R$, so $\xi(r) = -\tfrac{2(2M)^{3}}{9}\,\xi(\hat R) = 0$: $\xi$ is tangent to every hypersurface $r = \mathrm{const}$ in $W$.

\emph{(iv).} Use the ingoing coordinates $(v, r, \vartheta, \varphi)$ of the derived metric ($v = t + r$ with $t$ the background time of the gauge), in which $g = (1 - \tfrac{2M}{r})dv^{2} - 2\,dv\,dr - r^{2}d\sigma^{2}$, $d\sigma^{2}$ the unit round metric, and $\hat g = (2M/r)^{3}g$. On $W \cap \{r = r_{0}\}$ with $r_{0} \neq 2M$ the induced $\hat g$ is the product $(2M/r_{0})^{3}\bigl((1 - \tfrac{2M}{r_{0}})dv^{2} - r_{0}^{2}d\sigma^{2}\bigr)$ of a line and a round two-sphere, nondegenerate. Since $\xi$ is tangent and Killing for $\hat g$, its restriction is Killing for this product. Write $\xi = \xi^{v}\partial_{v} + Y$ with $Y$ tangent to the spheres. The $vv$ component of the Killing equation gives $\partial_{v}\xi^{v} = 0$; the $AB$ components (sphere directions) say $Y$ is a Killing field of the round sphere for each $v$; the $vA$ components give $(1 - \tfrac{2M}{r_{0}})\partial_{A}\xi^{v} = r_{0}^{2}\,\partial_{v}Y_{A}$, so $\partial_{v}Y$ is a gradient field on the sphere; differentiating in $v$, $\partial_{v}^{2}Y = 0$ and $\partial_{v}Y$ is a Killing gradient field of the round sphere, which is parallel and hence zero (the round sphere has no nonzero parallel field); then $\partial_{A}\xi^{v} = 0$. So on each shell $\xi = \alpha(r)\partial_{v} + \sum_{j}c_{j}(r)L_{j}$, the Killing algebra of a line times a round sphere. Now the full Killing equation of $\hat g$ on $W$: $\hat g_{rr} = 0$ and $\hat g_{rv} = -(2M/r)^{3}$, $\hat g_{rA} = 0$, $\xi^{r} = 0$, so $(\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\hat g)_{rr} = 2\hat g_{rv}\partial_{r}\xi^{v} = 0$ gives $\alpha' = 0$, and $(\mathcal{L}_{\xi}\hat g)_{rA} = \hat g_{AB}\partial_{r}\xi^{B} + \hat g_{rv}\partial_{A}\xi^{v} = \hat g_{AB}\partial_{r}Y^{B} = 0$ gives $c_{j}' = 0$. So $\xi = \alpha\partial_{v} + \sum c_{j}L_{j}$ with constants on $W$ minus the horizon, and on $W$ by continuity ($\partial_{v} = \partial_{t}$ and the $L_{j}$ are smooth across $r = 2M$, and $W$ minus the horizon is dense in $W$). These fields are Killing symmetries of the field: the gauge field does not depend on $t$ (checked: every coframe jet has vanishing $t$ derivative) and is rotation-covariant.

\emph{(v).} The physical vector $K = \hb^{-1}(e_{0})$ of $\partial_{t}$ has $Q(K) = 1 - 2M/r$: zero on $r = 2M$, positive outside, negative inside (checked at $r = 1, 4, \tfrac14$). On $r = 2M$ the check finds $(K\cdot D)K = D_{e_{0}}K = -\tfrac12 K = -\kappa K$ with $\kappa = 1/(4M)$, so $K$ is tangent to the null generators and not affinely parametrised, with inaffinity of magnitude $\kappa$; off the horizon $(K\cdot D)K$ is not along $K$ (checked). An affine parameter $\lambda$ along a generator therefore satisfies $d\lambda/dv = c\,e^{\kappa v}$, $\lambda = (c/\kappa)e^{\kappa v}$ up to an additive constant fixed by the bifurcation edge at $\lambda = 0$ (the boost $\beta_{t}$ of the setup and item (ii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}, which acts on the affine parameter as the dilation at rate $\kappa$), and the time translation by $\tau$ is $\lambda \mapsto e^{\kappa\tau}\lambda$, generated by $\kappa\lambda\,\partial_{\lambda}$. By (iv) any conformal symmetry restricts to an open piece of the horizon as $\alpha\kappa\lambda\,\partial_{\lambda} + \sum c_{j}L_{j}$. If this were $\partial_{\lambda}$ on an open piece, the rotation part would vanish (it moves the generator) and $\alpha\kappa\lambda = 1$ on an open interval of $\lambda$, impossible. So no conformal symmetry on any open set meeting the horizon restricts to the affine translations.

\emph{(vi).} In Proposition \claimref{synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-gives-positive-null-translations} and Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation} the positivity of a translation along a horizon is obtained by exhibiting it as a limit of conjugates of $Z$ in a unitary representation of $\mathrm{Spin}^{+}(2,4)$ acting by conformal symmetries of the field (the null translation of Minkowski space; the conformal null rotation $\tfrac12 nI$ for de Sitter, whose Weyl part vanishes, which the check confirms as a control: Weyl square zero, no invariant metric). A representation of the conformal symmetries of the Schwarzschild field near a piece of its horizon is, by (iv), a representation of the time translation and rotations, whose action on the generators is the dilation and the rotations of (v); none of its elements, nor any limit of them in the Lie algebra (the algebra is four-dimensional and closed), acts on the generators as the affine translation. The statement concerns the geometric action of the field's conformal symmetries; an abstract unitary group on the generators' modes is not excluded, and that is where the positivity must sit. A conformal map of a region of vanishing field strength cannot carry a translation onto the horizon either, since it would be a conformal symmetry of the field near the horizon. So the positivity in case (a) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state} is not supplied by the conformal structure; it is a condition on the state of the generators' modes, which the affine translations act on as automorphisms of the null-surface algebra but not as symmetries of the field.
