synthesis.state-selection-r-and-le-again.technical:
The note folded into T05 states two premises under T05's names. On the boundary-mode algebra the note's (R), regularity of the state's two-point functions continued in rapidity, can be read three ways on a single mode: regularity alone constrains nothing, strict periodicity in imaginary time is satisfied by no state, and the reading T05 uses, with the two operator orderings glued across the cut, fixes the mode's occupancy at its thermal value for the geometric period, and with univalence (P) makes the mode exactly thermal (KMS). Imposed on every two-point function of the window, the glued reading also forces all correlations between different modes' ladders to vanish. It therefore sits strictly between T05's (R), which constrains single modes only, and T05's (R) together with the quasi-free premise (Q); two small even states show both gaps. The single-mode conclusions of the note's rate theorem need only T05's (R) with (P).

The two locality premises (L$_E$) describe the same generators: products of the boost bivectors at each point, which commute with every occupation number, include the cross-point products used for the controlled-$Z$ scrambling, and exclude hopping and pairing between points. The note's wording, taken literally, would also exclude the cross-point products its own proposition uses, so T05's wording is the consistent one.
synthesis.state-selection-r-and-le-again.lay: Two assumptions of the series appear twice, once in the main paper on black-hole states and once in a shorter note later folded into it, under the same names. This result compares them exactly. The two locality assumptions turn out to say the same thing. The two regularity assumptions do not: read in the only way that makes it both meaningful and satisfiable, the note's version asks for everything the main paper's version asks, plus the absence of correlations between different modes, while still asking less than the main paper's version combined with its separate assumption that the state is the simplest (quasi-free) one. Small explicit examples show both differences. What the note actually uses its version for needs only the main paper's, together with the univalence assumption both papers make.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} Under the flow, $\alpha_{t}(a^{*}) = e^{i\omega t}a^{*}$ and $\alpha_{t}(a) = e^{-i\omega t}a$, since $[K, a] = -a$ (Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2), (4)). With occupancy $n = \omega(a^{*}a)$ and $\omega(aa^{*}) = 1 - n$, the ladder correlators are $F_{a,a^{*}}(t) = e^{i\omega t}(1 - n)$ and $F_{a^{*},a}(t) = e^{-i\omega t}n$, and $F_{a,a} = F_{a^{*},a^{*}} = 0$ since $a^{2} = 0$. Each is entire, so regularity alone imposes nothing. Strict periodicity gives $(Q^{-1} - 1)(1 - n) = 0$ and $(Q - 1)n = 0$; for $Q \ne 1$ these force $n = 1$ and $n = 0$, so no state satisfies them. The glued reading gives $Q^{-1}(1 - n) = n$ (and the same equation from the other ordering), whose one root is $n = 1/(Q + 1)$, the occupancy T05's (R) asserts on the mode. The ladder correlators involve only $\omega(aa^{*})$ and $\omega(a^{*}a)$, so they leave $\omega(a)$ free; with $\omega(a) = 0$, which (P) (\claimref{singularity.p-univalence}) supplies, the marginal is $\operatorname{diag}(1 - n, n) = e^{-pK}/\operatorname{tr}e^{-pK}$, the unique KMS state at $\beta = p$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}). At $Q = 1$ both periodicity equations hold for every $n$, and the glued one reads $1 - n = n$. The check runs these equations for $Q = 3, \tfrac15, \tfrac72$ with exact density matrices, and at $Q = 1$.

\emph{(ii).} For $i \ne j$ the canonical anticommutation relations (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}) give $b_{j}a_{i} = -a_{i}b_{j}$ for $b_{j} \in \{a_{j}, a_{j}^{*}\}$. The glued condition for $(a_{i}, a_{j}^{*})$ reads $Q_{j}^{-1}\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*}) = \omega(a_{j}^{*}a_{i}) = -\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*})$, so $(1 + Q_{j}^{-1})\,\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*}) = 0$ and $\omega(a_{i}a_{j}^{*}) = 0$ since $Q_{j} > 0$; likewise for $(a_{i}, a_{j})$ with $Q_{j}$ in place of $Q_{j}^{-1}$, and for the adjoint pairs. Conversely, if every inter-mode two-point function vanishes, the mixed conditions hold trivially, and the single-mode ones are (i).

\emph{(iii).} The two-point clause of (Q) is $\omega(a_{k}^{*}a_{l}) = \delta_{kl}n_{k}$ with gauge invariance, so every inter-mode two-point function vanishes and, with T05's (R), (ii) gives (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$); (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$) implies T05's (R) by restriction to single modes. For the counter-models take $Q_{1} = 3$, $Q_{2} = 5$, $n_{k} = 1/(Q_{k} + 1)$, in the Jordan-Wigner basis. Model A is the product state with the coherence $c = \tfrac{1}{50}$ added between $\ket{01}$ and $\ket{10}$: it has trace one, is positive (its $2\times2$ block has determinant $n_{1}(1 - n_{2})\,n_{2}(1 - n_{1}) - c^{2} > 0$), commutes with the total parity, has the Gibbs marginals, and $\omega(a_{1}a_{2}^{*}) = -c$, so the mixed glued condition fails. Model B shifts $p_{11}$ to $n_{1}n_{2} + d$, $d = \tfrac{1}{100}$, with the other diagonal entries fixed by the marginals and no coherence: it is a diagonal, hence even, state with the Gibbs marginals and vanishing inter-mode two-point functions, so (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$) holds, while $\omega(N_{1}N_{2}) - n_{1}n_{2} = d$, against Wick's factorisation $\omega(N_{1}N_{2}) = n_{1}n_{2}$ for a gauge-invariant quasi-free state with diagonal two-point function. The check confirms each statement exactly.

\emph{(iv).} By (i), (R$_{\mathrm{reg}}$) with (P) makes each marginal the Gibbs state at $\beta = p = 2\pi/\kappa$, with $n = 1/(e^{\omega p} + 1) \in (0, 1)$ for every real $\omega$, so every marginal is faithful; this is the single-mode conclusion of Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, there drawn from T05's (R), and no modular group, hence no geometric modular condition, enters. The single-mode conclusions of the note's Theorem \claimref{state-selection.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii} are these.

\emph{(v).} Both premises take the generators to be the boost bivector field and its products, so the generated algebra is the one of $\sigma_{1}, \ldots, \sigma_{n}$. The check builds three modes in $\Cl(3,3)$, one hyperbolic atom per mode: the $8$ products of subsets of $\{\sigma_{1}, \sigma_{2}, \sigma_{3}\}$ are linearly independent, each commutes with every $N_{k}$ (so every generator is diagonal in the joint number basis, as Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived} states), $\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}$ lies in their span, and the hopping $a_{1}^{*}a_{2}$ and pairing $a_{1}^{*}a_{2}^{*}$ each raise the rank to $9$ and fail to commute with $N_{1}$. T05's premise states the exclusion as no off-diagonal generator, in particular no hopping, with cross-point products allowed; the note's states it as no generator coupling two ladders. Since the note's own Proposition uses the cross-point controlled-$Z$, a product of $\sigma_{j}\sigma_{k}$-type terms, the literal reading that excludes all two-point generators contradicts its first clause, and the reading consistent with it excludes exactly the off-diagonal generators, which is T05's.

synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-it.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a horizon in the scope of Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}, with the affine parameter $u \in \R$ on each generator, $u = 0$ on the edge (bifurcation) surface, and the continuum mode space $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)\otimes\id_{K}$. The boost acts as $\beta_{t}(\psi(u)) = e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$ (the boost $\beta_{t}$ of the setup of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}, for the Killing flows of the eternal hole and of de Sitter space and the local boost of Minkowski space). Write $W_{\omega}(u, v) = \omega(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u))$, and $\omega_{0}$ for the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}\otimes\id_{K}$, the state that (N$_{+}$) selects (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)). For a point $u_{0}$ of a generator and $\lambda > 0$ let $\sigma^{u_{0}}_{\lambda}(\psi(u_{0} + x)) = \lambda^{1/2}\psi(u_{0} + \lambda x)$; the \emph{scaling limit} of $\omega$ at $u_{0}$ is the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with two-point function $\lim_{\lambda \to 0^{+}}\lambda\,W_{\omega}(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda y)$ (as distributions), when the limit exists. Read the local form of (N$_{+}$) at $u_{0}$ as: the scaling limit at $u_{0}$ exists and is $\omega_{0}$ (\emph{locally the null vacuum at $u_{0}$}). Call $\omega$ stationary if $\omega\circ\beta_{t} = \omega$ for all $t$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The boost is the scaling about the edge.)} $\beta_{t} = \sigma^{0}_{e^{\kappa t}}$. Among the weights $\lambda^{p}$, only $p = \tfrac12$ makes $\sigma_{\lambda}$ preserve the anticommutator. In $\Cl(1,3)$ (store signature) the rotor $B = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2} + \sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,e_{1}e_{0}$ sends $\ell = e_{0} + e_{1}$ to $e^{\lambda}\ell$, $n = e_{0} - e_{1}$ to $e^{-\lambda}n$ and fixes $e_{2}, e_{3}$: on the null plane $\{u\ell + y\}$ it dilates every generator about its own edge point. (The same weight-$\tfrac12$ dilation, with its Mellin and rotor factorisations, is the subject of the result filed alongside, synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group, in fuller form; here only the identification with the scaling map is used.)
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Stationarity plus the edge is (N$_{+}$).)} A stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free $\omega$ is its own scaling limit at the edge. Hence $\omega$ is locally the null vacuum at the edge if and only if $\omega = \omega_{0}$, that is, if and only if $\omega$ satisfies (N$_{+}$). The same holds with the weaker condition that $W_{\omega} - W_{0}$ be a bounded function on some neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$ (in each $K$-component): a function homogeneous of degree $-1$ and bounded near the origin vanishes.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Off the edge every stationary thermal state is locally the vacuum.)} For $c \in (0, \infty]$ let $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ be the product, over the two halves $u > 0$ and $u < 0$, of the quasi-free states KMS at rapidity period $2\pi c$ for the boost future-directed on each half ($c = \infty$: the ground state of that boost). Each is stationary, even and gauge-invariant quasi-free. On $u, v > 0$, with $y = \ln(u/v)$,
\[
W_{c}(u, v) = \frac{i}{2\pi}\,\frac{(uv)^{-1/2}}{2c\,\sinh\!\big((y + i0)/2c\big)}, \qquad \text{Mellin symbol } (1 + e^{-2\pi c w})^{-1} \text{ on } u^{-1/2 + iw},
\]
the I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} at period $2\pi c$ (the mirror image on $u, v < 0$), $W_{1} = W_{0}$ there. The difference $D_{c} = W_{c} - W_{0}$ is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(uv)^{-1/2}g_{c}(y)$ with $g_{c}$ analytic for $|\mathrm{Im}\,y| < 2\pi\min(c, 1)$, $g_{c}(y) = -\tfrac{1}{24}(c^{-2} - 1)\,y + O(y^{3})$. So every $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ is locally the null vacuum at every point $u_{0} \neq 0$ of every generator. The scaling limit at $u_{0} \neq 0$ involves only the block of the two-point function on the half containing $u_{0}$, so the same holds for every stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free state whose restrictions to the two halves are those of $\omega_{c}^{\times}$, whatever its cross-edge block; for $c \neq 1$ none of these is $\omega_{0}$, since its half restrictions differ from those of $\omega_{0}$. The cross-edge block of $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ vanishes while that of $\omega_{0}$ is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v)^{-1}$; so $\omega_{c}^{\times} \neq \omega_{0}$ for every $c$, including $c = 1$, where both halves are the I-state at $2\pi$. For $c \neq 1$ the difference on each half, and for every $c$ the cross-edge difference, is homogeneous of degree $-1$, nonzero and unbounded on every neighbourhood of the edge.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The null energy.)} The point-split renormalised null energy of $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ is $\langle T_{uu}\rangle = (c^{-2} - 1)/(48\pi u^{2})$ per component, so the Killing-frame density $\kappa^{2}u^{2}\langle T_{uu}\rangle = \kappa^{2}(c^{-2} - 1)/(48\pi)$ is constant along the generator ($-\kappa^{2}/(48\pi)$ for the boost ground state), while the affine-frame density diverges at the edge for $c \neq 1$. Zero null energy does not select $\omega_{0}$ among stationary states: the quasi-free state with symbol $\tfrac14 m_{1/2} + \tfrac34 m_{\infty}$ on each half ($m_{c}$ the symbol above) is stationary, locally the null vacuum off the edge, has $\langle T_{uu}\rangle = 0$ everywhere, and differs from $\omega_{0}$ (its $y^{3}$ coefficient of $g$ is $\tfrac{21}{5760}$).
\item[(v)] \emph{(What form a principle must take.)} By (ii) and (iii), within the stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free class, (N$_{+}$) is equivalent to one temperature-free local condition at the edge, and no condition on the scaling limits at points off the edge, with stationarity, implies it, nor implies (R) on a half-generator (the family $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ restricted to $u > 0$ meets every such condition at every period); by (iv) neither does the further condition of vanishing null energy. On the eternal hole the half-generators $u > 0$ are on the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart of the store and the edge is not, so a principle stated at the points of that chart, with stationarity, through the scaling limits or the null energy, cannot supply (N$_{+}$) or (R): it must be posed at the bifurcation surface (on the manifold assembled from several charts), or fix the whole Mellin symbol on the chart, which is (R) itself. On a local Rindler horizon of Minkowski space the edge is an ordinary point of the flat chart, and for a boost-invariant state (N$_{+}$) is the local form of (N$_{+}$) at that one point.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The bifurcation surface of the eternal hole (case (a)) and of de Sitter space (case (b)), where (ii) is posed, is not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the half-generators of (iii) to (v) are.
synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-it.technical:
The store's premise (N$_{+}$) says that the modes on a horizon's light rays are in the ground state for sliding along the rays, and records that this relocates the thermal input to regularity across the bifurcation surface. This result makes that relocation exact within the stationary class. On every horizon in the premise's scope the boost acts on a light ray as a rescaling of its affine parameter about the edge, with exactly the weight that preserves the anticommutator, so the boost is the scaling map that defines a state's short-distance limit at the edge. A state invariant under the boost is therefore its own short-distance limit there: if it looks like the null vacuum at short distances at the edge, it is the null vacuum everywhere, and (N$_{+}$) holds. Boundedness of the difference from the vacuum near the edge is already enough, because the difference is homogeneous of degree $-1$.

The converse shows that the edge cannot be avoided. The stationary states that are thermal on each half of the ray at any period, including zero temperature (the boost's ground state) and the correct period with no correlation across the edge, all look like the null vacuum at short distances at every point except the edge: their kernels differ from the vacuum's by a smooth function that blows up only there. Their renormalised null energy is $(c^{-2} - 1)/(48\pi u^{2})$, constant in the Killing frame. Requiring zero null energy does not help, since a mixture of two such states has zero null energy and is not the vacuum. So any principle with no temperature in it that delivers (N$_{+}$) must speak about the state at the bifurcation surface, or fix the whole spectral symbol, which is the thermal premise again. On the eternal hole the bifurcation surface lies off the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart that carries the store's gravitational field, while on local Rindler horizons of Minkowski space it is an ordinary point. This is the null-line form of the Kay-Wald uniqueness argument and of the Fredenhagen-Haag short-distance condition, proved on the series' continuum carrier; the transport principle plays no part.
synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-it.lay: The series assumes that the quantum modes along a horizon's light rays are in their lowest-energy state for sliding along the rays, and from that it gets the horizon's temperature. This result asks where that assumption really bites. A black hole in equilibrium does not change in time, and on the horizon's light rays "not changing in time" turns out to mean "looking the same at every magnification about the point where the two halves of the horizon meet". So if the state looks like empty space at very short distances at that one meeting point, it looks like empty space everywhere along the ray, and the assumption holds. At every other point of the ray, a state at the wrong temperature, or at zero temperature, also looks like empty space at short distances; only the meeting point tells them apart. So any deeper principle that would explain the black-hole temperature must say something about that meeting point, which lies outside the single map of spacetime the series uses for the black hole.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} On a generator the boost of every horizon in the scope of Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state} acts as $u \mapsto e^{\kappa t}u$ (the setup of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}, the boost $\beta_{t}$: the Killing field is $\kappa u\,\partial_{u}$ on the generator for the eternal hole and for de Sitter space, and the local boost rotor dilates each generator of the local Rindler plane about its edge point). On fields it is $\beta_{t}(\psi(u)) = e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$, which is $\sigma^{0}_{\lambda}$ at $\lambda = e^{\kappa t}$. For $\sigma_{\lambda}f(u) = \lambda^{p}f(\lambda u)$ one has $\ip{\sigma_{\lambda}f}{\sigma_{\lambda}g} = \lambda^{2p - 1}\ip{f}{g}$, so the anticommutator $\{a(f), a^{*}(g)\} = \ip{f}{g}$ is preserved exactly for $p = \tfrac12$; the check verifies this on indicator functions of rational intervals at $\lambda = (3/2)^{4}, (1/5)^{4}$ among the weights $p = k/4$, $0 \le k \le 4$. In $\Cl(1,3)$ with $Q(e_{0}) = 1$, $Q(e_{j}) = -1$, $(e_{1}e_{0})^{2} = 1$ and $B = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2} + \sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,e_{1}e_{0}$ is a rotor; $e_{1}e_{0}$ anticommutes with $e_{0}, e_{1}$ and commutes with $e_{2}, e_{3}$, and $e_{1}e_{0}\ell = \ell$, $e_{1}e_{0}n = -n$, so $B\ell\tilde B = B^{2}\ell = e^{\lambda}\ell$, $Bn\tilde B = e^{-\lambda}n$, and $u\ell + y \mapsto e^{\lambda}u\ell + y$ for $y$ in the span of $e_{2}, e_{3}$; the check verifies these at $e^{\lambda/2} = \tfrac32, \tfrac15, 7$. So the boost is the scaling of the generator about the edge point with the weight $\tfrac12$ of a chiral field of scaling dimension $\tfrac12$.

\emph{(ii)} If $\omega\circ\beta_{t} = \omega$ for all $t$, then by (i) $\omega\circ\sigma^{0}_{\lambda} = \omega$ for all $\lambda > 0$, that is $\lambda W_{\omega}(\lambda x, \lambda y) = W_{\omega}(x, y)$; the family whose limit defines the scaling limit at the edge is constant, so the limit exists and is $\omega$. If $\omega$ is locally the null vacuum at the edge, then $W_{\omega} = W_{0}$, and a gauge-invariant quasi-free state is determined by its two-point function, so $\omega = \omega_{0}$. Conversely $W_{0}$ is invariant under translations and under $\sigma^{u_{0}}_{\lambda}$ for every $u_{0}$, so $\omega_{0}$ is its own scaling limit at every point. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i) the gauge-invariant quasi-free states satisfying (N$_{+}$) are exactly $\omega_{0}$, which gives the stated equivalence. For the weaker form: $W_{0}$ is stationary, so $D = W_{\omega} - W_{0}$ satisfies $\lambda D(\lambda x, \lambda y) = D(x, y)$. If $|D| \le C$ on a neighbourhood $U$ of $(0, 0)$, then for any $(x, y)$ and $\lambda$ small enough that $(\lambda x, \lambda y) \in U$, $|D(x, y)| = \lambda|D(\lambda x, \lambda y)| \le \lambda C$, and $\lambda \to 0$ gives $D(x, y) = 0$.

\emph{(iii)} The two halves $\CAR(L^{2}(\R_{\pm}, du)\otimes K)$ generate $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ as a graded tensor product, and the product of two even states is an even state; each half is $\beta$-invariant, so the product of stationary states is stationary. On $u > 0$ put $u = e^{x}$ and $\phi(x) = e^{x/2}\psi(e^{x})$: the map is unitary from $L^{2}(\R_{+}, du)$ to $L^{2}(\R, dx)$, the boost becomes the translation $x \mapsto x + \kappa t$, and the null vacuum's restriction becomes $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}e^{(x + x')/2}(e^{x} - e^{x'} + i0)^{-1} = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}\big(2\sinh((x - x' + i0)/2)\big)^{-1}$, the chiral thermal two-point function at period $2\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii)). The chiral two-point function KMS at period $2\pi c$ for the translations is the same function of $(x - x')/c$ divided by $c$ (the leading singularity $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(x - x' + i0)^{-1}$, fixed by the anticommutator, is then the same for every $c$), which gives $W_{c}$; its Fourier transform in $x - x'$ is that at $c = 1$ evaluated at $c\,w$, so the Mellin symbol is $m_{1}(c w) = (1 + e^{-2\pi c w})^{-1}$, the symbol of the I-state of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} for $h = -\kappa w$ at $\beta = 2\pi c/\kappa$, which is jointly KMS by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-two}. In the check the kernel is evaluated exactly in the form $(2\pi/i)W_{c} = (uv)^{-1/2}/\big(c(t^{1/2c} - t^{-1/2c})\big)$, $t = u/v$, at points $u = a^{2k}$, $v = b^{2k}$ with $k/c$ an integer ($c = \tfrac13, \tfrac12, 1, 2, 3$): $c = 1$ gives $1/(u - v)$; every kernel and every difference is homogeneous of degree $-1$ under scaling by squares; $D_{c} = 0$ exactly at $c = 1$; and along a ray towards the edge $D_{c}$ grows as the inverse scale; the symbol satisfies the two-point KMS identity at period $2\pi c$ and, for $c \neq 1$, not at $2\pi$; and $t^{1/2c} \mapsto -t^{1/2c}$ under $y \mapsto y - 2\pi i c$ makes the kernel antiperiodic there (the fermionic KMS condition), while at $c = \tfrac12$ the shift by $2\pi i$ leaves it periodic. For $c = \infty$ the symbol is $\chi_{(-\infty, 0)}(w)$ and $(2\pi/i)W_{\infty} = (uv)^{-1/2}/(y + i0)$.

With $S(z) = \sinh z/z$, $g_{c}(y) = y^{-1}\big(S(y/2c)^{-1} - S(y/2)^{-1}\big)$. Both inverses are even power series with constant term $1$, so the pole cancels; $S(z)^{-1} = 1 - \tfrac{z^{2}}{6} + \tfrac{7z^{4}}{360} - \cdots$ gives $g_{c}(y) = -\tfrac{1}{24}(c^{-2} - 1)y + \tfrac{7}{5760}(c^{-4} - 1)y^{3} + \cdots$, and the zeros of $\sinh(y/2c)$ and $\sinh(y/2)$ off $0$ lie at $2\pi i c k$ and $2\pi i k$, $k \neq 0$, so $g_{c}$ is analytic on $|\mathrm{Im}\,y| < 2\pi\min(c, 1)$. The check computes both series exactly to order $12$ in $y$ with $\gamma = c^{-2} \in \{0, \tfrac19, \tfrac14, 1, 4\}$: zero constant term, even, first coefficient $-(\gamma - 1)/24$, identically zero only at $\gamma = 1$; and as a control, omitting the factor $1/c$ leaves the pole $(c - 1)/y$. At a point $u_{0} > 0$, $\lambda W_{0}(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda y) = W_{0}(x, y)$ and $\lambda D_{c}(u_{0} + \lambda x, u_{0} + \lambda y) = O(\lambda)$ uniformly for $x, y$ in a compact set, because $D_{c}$ is smooth near $(u_{0}, u_{0})$; for small $\lambda$ both arguments stay on the half $u > 0$, so the cross-edge block does not enter. The scaling limit at $u_{0}$ is $\omega_{0}$, and the same holds at $u_{0} < 0$ by the reflection $u \mapsto -u$. Only the same-half block entered: for test functions supported in a compact set and $\lambda$ small, $u_{0} + \lambda x$ and $u_{0} + \lambda y$ lie on the half containing $u_{0}$. So the conclusion holds for every stationary gauge-invariant quasi-free state with the half restrictions of $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ and an arbitrary cross-edge block (subject only to positivity of the whole symbol), and for $c \neq 1$ such a state is not $\omega_{0}$, because its restriction to $u > 0$ is the I-state at period $2\pi c$ while that of $\omega_{0}$ is the I-state at $2\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii)) and the I-state at a given period is unique (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}). Across the edge, $\omega_{c}^{\times}(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u)) = 0$ for $u > 0 > v$ (product of even states, odd factors), while $W_{0}(u, v) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v)^{-1} \neq 0$ there, homogeneous of degree $-1$: the difference is unbounded on every neighbourhood of $(0, 0)$, and the check tabulates it at three points and three scales. So $\omega_{c}^{\times} \neq \omega_{0}$ for every $c$; at $c = 1$ both halves are the I-state at period $2\pi$ (the continuum restatement of (R) on each half) and the state is still not the null vacuum.

\emph{(iv)} For a complex chiral fermion $T_{uu} = \tfrac{i}{2}(\psi^{*}\partial_{u}\psi - \partial_{u}\psi^{*}\,\psi)$, renormalised by point-splitting against $\omega_{0}$: $\langle T_{uu}\rangle(u) = \tfrac{i}{2}\lim_{v \to u}(\partial_{u} - \partial_{v})D_{c}(u, v)$. At $u = v = 1$, with $D_{c} = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}X$, the check computes $X(1 + \epsilon, 1) = (1 + \epsilon)^{-1/2}g_{c}(\ln(1 + \epsilon))$ and $X(1, 1 + \epsilon) = (1 + \epsilon)^{-1/2}g_{c}(-\ln(1 + \epsilon))$ as exact series in $\epsilon$ and finds $\langle T_{uu}\rangle(1) = -(X_{u} - X_{v})/(4\pi) = (\gamma - 1)/(48\pi)$ for the five values of $\gamma$ ($-1/(48\pi)$ at $\gamma = 0$, $3/(48\pi)$ at $\gamma = 4$, $0$ at $\gamma = 1$). Since $D_{c}$ is homogeneous of degree $-1$, $\langle T_{uu}\rangle$ is homogeneous of degree $-2$: $(c^{-2} - 1)/(48\pi u^{2})$. The Killing time $s$ along the generator has $du/ds = \kappa u$, so the Killing-frame density is $\kappa^{2}u^{2}\langle T_{uu}\rangle = \kappa^{2}(c^{-2} - 1)/(48\pi)$, constant; at $c = \infty$ it is $-\kappa^{2}/(48\pi)$, the familiar Boulware-type deficit of one complex chiral fermion at $T = \kappa/2\pi$ (cited from memory, as a consistency check only). Symbols enter the kernels linearly, and any measurable symbol with values in $[0, 1]$ defines a gauge-invariant quasi-free state; a function of the Mellin weight alone commutes with the boost, so the state with symbol $\tfrac14 m_{1/2} + \tfrac34 m_{\infty}$ on each half (and the product across the edge) is stationary. Its difference series is the same mix: zero constant term (locally the null vacuum off the edge, as in (iii)), $y$-coefficient of $g$ equal to $-\tfrac{1}{24}\big(\tfrac14(4 - 1) + \tfrac34(0 - 1)\big) = 0$ (zero null energy at every point, by homogeneity), and $y^{3}$-coefficient $\tfrac{7}{5760}\big(\tfrac14(16 - 1) + \tfrac34(0 - 1)\big) = \tfrac{21}{5760} \neq 0$: not $\omega_{0}$. The check verifies these coefficients exactly, that $\tfrac14$ is the only cancelling weight among three tested, and that within the one-period family only $\gamma = 1$ has zero null energy.

\emph{(v)} The first two sentences restate (ii), (iii) and (iv). A condition on the scaling limits at the points $u > 0$, with stationarity, is met by $\omega_{c}^{\times}$ restricted to $u > 0$ for every $c$, which is KMS at $2\pi c$ there, so it implies neither (N$_{+}$) nor (R) on the half-generator, and adding zero null energy still leaves the mixture of (iv). In the store's Painlev\'e-Gullstrand form of the eternal hole the gauge field is invertible on the future horizon $r = 2M$, $u > 0$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-internal}), while the edge $u = 0$ and the half $u < 0$ lie beyond that chart (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}, flag beyond one flat chart). On the half-generator the stationary quasi-free states are labelled by their Mellin symbol, a function of $w$, and fixing it to $m_{1}$ is (R) in its continuum form; this is what a principle on the chart that delivers (R) must do. On a local Rindler horizon of Minkowski space the edge point is an ordinary point of the flat chart, and (ii) applies there. Transport-absent: no transport statement is used.

\emph{Remark (not part of the result).} For the outgoing chiral sector of a hole the boost acts on the outgoing affine parameter $U$ as a dilation about $U = 0$, the future horizon itself, which is on the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart; the same scaling lemma then concerns a state locally the null vacuum at the future horizon. That case, for a hole formed by collapse, is the main argument of the result filed alongside, synthesis.collapsing-hole-flux-from-ground-state-on-the-ingoing-sheet, and the mechanism of the Fredenhagen-Haag derivation of Hawking radiation (cited from memory). It needs the reduction of the outgoing modes to a two-dimensional chiral field near the horizon, which the store carries only as the postulate J3 (Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction}), and asymptotic rather than exact stationarity.

synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-hal.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On one generator of a horizon, affine parameter $u \in \R$, let $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ be the continuum mode space (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}), $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ its subalgebra over $L^{2}((a, \infty))\otimes K$, $\beta^{(a)}_{t}(\psi(u)) = e^{t/2}\psi(a + e^{t}(u - a))$ the boost about $a$, and $\omega_{0}$ the null vacuum, the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with symbol $\chi_{(-\infty,0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$, $P = i\,d/du$, the state of Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state} (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Two points fix the period.)} If, for two points $a < b$, the restriction of a state $\omega$ to $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ is KMS at some $\beta_{a} > 0$ for $\beta^{(a)}$ and its restriction to $\mathfrak{A}_{b}$ is KMS at some $\beta_{b} > 0$ for $\beta^{(b)}$, then $\beta_{a} = \beta_{b} = 2\pi$ and $\omega = \omega_{0}$ on $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The ground-state clause.)} If $A \subset \R$ is unbounded below and, for every $a \in A$, the restriction of $\omega$ to $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ is KMS at some period for $\beta^{(a)}$, then $\omega = \omega_{0}$: $\omega$ is gauge-invariant, quasi-free, invariant under the null translations with positive generator. Conversely $\omega_{0}$ is KMS at $2\pi$ about every point. No stationarity, quasi-freeness, gauge invariance or temperature is assumed. The mirror statement holds for past halves and sets unbounded above.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sharpness.)} One point does not suffice (the half-thermal products of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}), nor does a set bounded below (states equal to $\omega_{0}$ beyond its infimum and arbitrary before it).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The kernel.)} Off the diagonal, with $X = u - a$, $Y = v - a$, $s = \ln(X/Y)$, $d = u - v$: the unique KMS state at $\beta$ about $a$ has $\omega(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u)) = \frac{i}{2\beta}(XY)^{-1/2}/\sinh(\pi s/\beta) = \frac{i}{\beta d}\sinh(s/2)/\sinh(\pi s/\beta)$, which at fixed $d$ does not depend on the position exactly when $\beta = 2\pi$, where it is $\frac{i}{2\pi d}$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(De Sitter, argued.)} If the state of a free field on de Sitter space has geometric modular action for the de Sitter wedges (each wedge algebra's modular group is its Killing boost at rapidity period $2\pi$; \cite{BorchersBuchholz1999}, cited from memory, for the de Sitter-invariant vacua) and each wedge algebra is generated by the modes on the future half of its horizon, then, every point of a horizon generator being the edge of such a wedge, (ii) gives (N$_{+}$) on the cosmological horizon for that field, massive fields included (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation} reaches only conformally invariant fields). Here the period $2\pi$ is already part of the hypothesis (geometric modular action is essentially the Bisognano-Wichmann property), so the derived period does no work; the gain over the stored conformal route is the massive case only, and it rests on the assumption, not proved here, that the horizon modes generate the wedge algebras (for massive fields the restriction to the horizon is not automatic). The eternal hole is not reached: only its bifurcation surface carries a Killing boost.
\end{enumerate}
Status: (i) to (iv) proved, with exact checks of the affine algebra, the kernel identities, the residue series and the finite counter-model; (v) argued, given two hypotheses not proved here. Standard: the I-state kernel and the forward direction. Transport-absent.
synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-hal.technical:
(N$_{+}$) asks that the modes on a horizon's light rays be in their ground state for sliding along the rays; the Hadamard results now give its short-distance form at every point, and within stationary states it is that short-distance form at the edge. What has been missing is a form of the global clause that does not presuppose stationarity. This result gives one, in the language of modular theory: on one light ray, the state is the (N$_{+}$) vacuum exactly when, beyond each point of a set of points reaching arbitrarily far into the past, it is thermal for the boost about that point. No temperature is specified: the period $2\pi$ is forced, because dilations about two different points compose to translations, and the thermal kernel about a point is translation invariant only at period $2\pi$. Nothing about the state is assumed in advance; it need not be quasi-free or gauge-invariant, since a thermal state for a boost is unique.

The condition cannot be weakened to one point (the stored half-thermal states are thermal about the edge only) or to points bounded below (the state below them is then free). It is the generator form of what modular theory calls geometric modular action, the property that the Bisognano-Wichmann theorem gives the vacuum of a relativistic field. So a single premise of modular covariance, which through the Guido-Longo theorem, or through the geometric action of the wedge reflections (\claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}), would also give spin-statistics for interacting fields, gives the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$) wherever every point of a generator is the edge of a wedge with geometric modular action. On de Sitter space this is so (argued, given that the wedge algebras are generated by their horizon modes and that the state has geometric modular action, which de Sitter-invariant vacua have); there the period is already in that hypothesis, so what is gained is only the massive case, which the stored conformal-energy argument does not reach and which rests on the horizon modes generating the wedge algebras; on the eternal black hole it is not, since only one point of each generator is the edge of a Killing wedge.
synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-hal.lay: The series assumes that the quantum modes running along a horizon's light rays are in their lowest-energy state. For particles of the electron's kind (fermions), this result gives an equivalent condition that sounds quite different: from every point along a light ray, looking forward along the ray, the modes appear warm, as the modes beyond an accelerated observer's horizon do. Surprisingly, the temperature does not need to be specified: asking for warmth about two different points of the same ray already fixes it at the standard value, and asking for it about points reaching arbitrarily far back fixes the whole state as the lowest-energy one. This links the assumption to a well-studied property of the vacuum in relativistic quantum theory, and it shows how it could hold on the horizon of an expanding universe for massive particles too, given an assumption about how the horizon's modes relate to the region behind it, though not, by this route, on a black hole that has always existed.

proofs.main:
\emph{Set-up.} Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On one generator of a horizon, with affine parameter $u \in \R$, the modes form the continuum mode space $\CAR(L^{2}(\R, du)\otimes K)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}, with fields $\psi(u)$, $\{\psi(u), \psi^{*}(v)\} = \delta(u - v)\otimes\id_{K}$. For $a \in \R$ let $\mathfrak{A}_{a} = \CAR(L^{2}((a, \infty), du)\otimes K)$, the modes of the future half beyond $a$, and $\beta^{(a)}_{t}(\psi(u)) = e^{t/2}\psi(a + e^{t}(u - a))$, the boost about $a$ (rapidity $t$, weight $\tfrac12$, the weight that preserves the anticommutator), which maps $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ onto itself. Its one-particle generator $h_{a}$ is self-adjoint on $L^{2}((a, \infty))\otimes K$, diagonal on the Mellin modes $(u - a)^{-1/2 + iw}$ with spectrum $\R$. The null vacuum $\omega_{0}$ is the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with symbol $\chi_{(-\infty, 0)}(P)\otimes\id_{K}$, $P = i\,d/du$, two-point function $\omega_{0}(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u)) = \tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}\otimes\id_{K}$; it is the unique gauge-invariant quasi-free state of (N$_{+}$) (Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i), which characterises the states satisfying it).

\emph{Step 1: the KMS states about one point.} By Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} with Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness}, for each $\beta > 0$ there is exactly one state of $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ that is KMS at $\beta$ for $\beta^{(a)}$, among all states: the quasi-free I-state $\omega^{(a)}_{\beta}$ with symbol $(1 + e^{\beta h_{a}})^{-1}$. Its two-point function is $\int\frac{dw}{2\pi}(1 + e^{\beta w})^{-1}(XY)^{-1/2}(X/Y)^{iw}$ with $X = u - a$, $Y = v - a$. Off the diagonal the Fermi transform is a sum of residues at $w = i\pi(2n + 1)/\beta$: with $r = e^{-\pi s/\beta}$, $s = \ln(X/Y) > 0$, the residue series is $\sum_{n \ge 0}r^{2n + 1} = r/(1 - r^{2}) = 1/(2\sinh(\pi s/\beta))$ (checked, with the exact remainder $r^{2N+1}/(1 - r^{2})$ of the partial sums); so, standard,
\[
\omega^{(a)}_{\beta}(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u)) = \frac{i}{2\beta}\,\frac{(XY)^{-1/2}}{\sinh(\pi s/\beta)}\otimes\id_{K}\qquad(u \ne v),
\]
the value for $s < 0$ following by the same computation. Distinct periods give distinct states (distinct symbols), and a KMS state is invariant under its dynamics.

\emph{Step 2: the kernel at fixed separation.} Put $d = u - v = X - Y$ and $E = e^{s} = X/Y$; then $X = dE/(E - 1)$, $Y = d/(E - 1)$, $XY = d^{2}E/(E - 1)^{2}$ and $(XY)^{-1/2} = (E - 1)/(d\sqrt{E}) = 2\sinh(s/2)/d$. So, off the diagonal,
\[
\omega^{(a)}_{\beta}(\psi^{*}(v)\psi(u)) = \frac{i}{\beta d}\,\frac{\sinh(s/2)}{\sinh(\pi s/\beta)}.
\]
Translating $u$ and $v$ together by $\tau$ keeps $d$ and moves $s$ monotonically through an interval. At $\beta = 2\pi$ the ratio is $1$ and the kernel is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi d}$, the null vacuum's, for every position (checked exactly on $E = q^{4}$ at four values of $q$ and two of $d$). For $\beta \ne 2\pi$ the ratio $\sinh(s/2)/\sinh(\pi s/\beta)$ is not constant on any interval: it is analytic in $s > 0$, it tends to $\beta/2\pi$ as $s \to 0$ and behaves as $e^{(1/2 - \pi/\beta)s}$ times a constant as $s \to \infty$, so constancy on an interval would make it constant on $(0, \infty)$ and force $\pi/\beta = \tfrac12$. So $\omega^{(a)}_{\beta}$ restricted to any $\mathfrak{A}_{a'}$, $a' > a$, is translation invariant exactly when $\beta = 2\pi$ (the check confirms that the kernel takes distinct values at four positions for $\beta = 4\pi, \tfrac43\pi, \pi, \tfrac23\pi, \tfrac12\pi$).

\emph{Step 3: two points fix the period.} The affine maps $D_{a}(\lambda)\colon x \mapsto a + \lambda(x - a)$ satisfy $D_{a}(\lambda)\circ D_{b}(1/\lambda) = T((\lambda - 1)(b - a))$, a translation (checked). Let $a < b$ be two points such that the restriction of a state $\omega$ to $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ is KMS at some $\beta_{a} > 0$ for $\beta^{(a)}$ and its restriction to $\mathfrak{A}_{b}$ is KMS at some $\beta_{b} > 0$ for $\beta^{(b)}$. By Step 1, $\omega|_{\mathfrak{A}_{a}} = \omega^{(a)}_{\beta_{a}}$, and $\omega|_{\mathfrak{A}_{b}}$ is invariant under $\beta^{(b)}$. On $\mathfrak{A}_{b}$, the boost $\beta^{(b)}$ with $\lambda = 1/\mu < 1$ followed by the boost $\beta^{(a)}$ with $\mu > 1$ (both map $(b, \infty)$ into itself, and $\omega^{(a)}_{\beta_{a}}$ is invariant under the second) is the translation by $(\mu - 1)(b - a) > 0$; every positive translation is reached. So the two-point function of $\omega^{(a)}_{\beta_{a}}$ on $(b, \infty)^{2}$ is invariant under positive translations, and by Step 2, $\beta_{a} = 2\pi$. Then $\omega|_{\mathfrak{A}_{a}} = \omega^{(a)}_{2\pi}$, whose kernel is the null vacuum's, $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$: it is $\omega_{0}|_{\mathfrak{A}_{a}}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii) at $a = 0$, carried to every $a$ by the translation invariance of $\omega_{0}$; the weight-$\tfrac12$ dilation invariance of $(u - v)^{-1}$ about every point is checked). Its restriction to $\mathfrak{A}_{b}$ is $\omega_{0}|_{\mathfrak{A}_{b}} = \omega^{(b)}_{2\pi}$, so by uniqueness of the period, $\beta_{b} = 2\pi$ as well. (Proved.)

\emph{Step 4: a set unbounded below fixes the state.} Let $A \subset \R$ be unbounded below, with at least two points, and suppose that for every $a \in A$ the restriction of $\omega$ to $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ is KMS at some $\beta_{a} > 0$ for $\beta^{(a)}$. By Step 3 (every $a \in A$ has another point of $A$ below it) every $\beta_{a} = 2\pi$ and $\omega = \omega_{0}$ on every $\mathfrak{A}_{a}$, $a \in A$. These algebras increase as $a$ decreases, and $\bigcup_{a \in A}L^{2}((a, \infty))\otimes K$ is dense in $L^{2}(\R)\otimes K$; since $\|a(f) - a(g)\| = \|f - g\|$ in the CAR algebra, $\bigcup_{a \in A}\mathfrak{A}_{a}$ is norm dense, and two states agreeing on a dense subalgebra agree. So $\omega = \omega_{0}$: gauge-invariant, quasi-free, invariant under the null translations with positive generator, the state of (N$_{+}$). Conversely $\omega_{0}$ is KMS at $2\pi$ about every point (Step 3). No quasi-freeness, gauge invariance, stationarity or temperature is assumed. (Proved.) The mirror statement holds for past halves $(-\infty, a)$, $a$ in a set unbounded above, with the boost future-directed there.

\emph{Step 5: what does not suffice.} (a) One point: the stationary states thermal on each half at period $2\pi$ about the edge with no cross-edge correlation are KMS about $0$ on $\mathfrak{A}_{0}$ and are not $\omega_{0}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stationary-horizon-state-is-its-own-edge-scaling-limit}). (b) Points bounded below: if $A \subset [b, \infty)$, any state equal to $\omega_{0}$ on $\mathfrak{A}_{b}$ and arbitrary on the modes below $b$ (for instance a product with an even state there) satisfies the hypothesis at every $a \in A$; the check exhibits a finite model in which a symbol with the vacuum's compression on every $[a, \infty)$, $a \ge b$, differs from it. (c) A common period other than $2\pi$ at two points: impossible by Step 3.

\emph{Step 6: de Sitter horizons (argued).} On de Sitter space every point $p$ of a null geodesic $\gamma$ lies on the bifurcation surface of a Killing horizon generated in part by $\gamma$ (the horizon is the past light cone of the endpoint of $\gamma$ at future infinity, cut by the future light cone of a point of past infinity chosen so that it meets $\gamma$ at $p$), and on that horizon the Killing boost acts on $\gamma$ as the affine dilation about $p$, at rapidity period $2\pi$ in its own normalisation (as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}, case (b)). If the state of a free field has geometric modular action for the de Sitter wedges (the modular group of each wedge algebra is its Killing boost at rapidity period $2\pi$, the form in which the Bisognano-Wichmann property holds for the de Sitter-invariant vacua \cite{BorchersBuchholz1999}, cited from memory) and if each wedge algebra is generated by the modes on the future half of its horizon, then on $\gamma$ the hypothesis of Step 4 holds for every $p$, so the state of the modes on $\gamma$ is $\omega_{0}$: (N$_{+}$) case (b) for that field, massive fields included, which the store's conformal-energy route does not reach (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation}). The two hypotheses (geometric modular action, generation by the horizon modes) are not proved here. The period $2\pi$ is part of the first (it is essentially the Bisognano-Wichmann property, from which the null-vacuum restriction on the horizon is already known for de Sitter-invariant vacua), so the derivation of the period in Steps 3 and 4 does no work here; the gain over the stored conformal route is the massive case only, and it rests on the second hypothesis, since for massive fields the restriction to the horizon is not automatic. On the eternal hole only the bifurcation surface carries a Killing boost, so Step 4 does not apply there.

\emph{Scope.} Steps 1 to 5 concern the fermionic (CAR) continuum mode space of one generator; the bosonic analogue needs the uniqueness of CCR KMS states and is not claimed. The hypothesis is natural where every point of a generator is the edge of a Killing wedge: Minkowski null planes (Rindler wedges) and, argued, de Sitter horizons; not the eternal hole. The geometric action of the wedge reflections, which gives spin-statistics for interacting fields, is the companion statement for the modular conjugations (\claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}).

\emph{Status and novelty.} Steps 1 to 5 proved (Step 1 by the stored uniqueness of the I-state, the residue series standard and checked); Step 6 argued, given two unproved hypotheses and a literature result cited from memory. Standard: the I-state kernel; the forward direction (the null vacuum is KMS at $2\pi$ about every point, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(ii) with translation invariance); the use of half-sided modular structure to obtain translations is in the spirit of Borchers and Wiesbrock (Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses}). New: the converse for arbitrary states, with the period derived rather than assumed, and its reading as a temperature-free equivalent of (N$_{+}$) on one generator; the de Sitter reading. Transport-absent.

synthesis.weyl-flat-fields-need-no-scali.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose Weyl curvature vanishes on an open region $U$, globally hyperbolic for the derived metric, written on $U$ in a gauge where $\hb(b) = b/\varphi(x)$ with $\varphi$ smooth and positive (derived metric $\varphi^{2}$ times the flat one, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}), and let $\psi$ be the massless Dirac field (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}). Hadamard is as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}; generators, the continuum mode space with the chart's comoving transverse labels $K = L^{2}(\R^{2}, d^{2}y)\otimes V_{\Lambda}$, the null vacuum and the generator microlocal condition are as in Theorems \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes} and \claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Conformal transfer and bulk scaling limit; standard, re-derived.)} The flat null lines with $d\tilde\lambda = \varphi^{2}d\lambda$ are the affine null geodesics of the derived metric and carry the flat covectors, so a state of $\psi = \varphi^{-3/2}\chi$ is Hadamard exactly when the corresponding state of the flat field $\chi$ is. For every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state $\omega$ and every $x_{0} \in U$, the scaling limit of $\omega$ at $x_{0}$ (weight $\tfrac32$ per leg) is the flat massless vacuum in the local inertial coordinates $\varphi(x_{0})(x - x_{0})$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Generators; proved.)} On every null generator in $U$ the physical affine parameter $\tilde\lambda$ satisfies $d\tilde\lambda = \varphi^{2}d\lambda$, $\lambda$ the flat one. With the comoving transverse labels fixed as the multiplicity space (the physical area element $\varphi^{2}d^{2}y$ changes along an expanding generator), the CAR makes the generator field carry weight $\tfrac12$ in $\tilde\lambda$, and the restriction of $\omega$ satisfies the generator microlocal condition in $\tilde\lambda$. Hence the local form of (N$_{+}$) holds at every point of every null plane of the chart in $U$, for every such state, with no further premise. The chart's null planes through $x_{0}$ agree with the local Rindler horizons at $x_{0}$ (expansion-free there) at the leading order, tangent at $x_{0}$, at which the scaling-limit premise (HS) and (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) define them; at that order the conclusion of (HS) is, on Weyl-flat regions, a theorem for the massless Dirac field.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Robertson-Walker generators; proved and computed.)} For $\varphi = a(t)$, $t = x\cdot e_{0}$, the restriction of the conformal vacuum to a null generator, read in $\tilde\lambda = \Psi(\lambda)$ with $\Psi' = a^{2}$, is the null vacuum of $\tilde\lambda$ plus the Schwarzian kernel of $\Phi = \Psi^{-1}$, whose leading term is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\cdot\tfrac{1}{12}S_{\Phi}\,(u - v)$ with $S_{\Phi} = -S/a^{4}$, where
\[
S = S_{\Psi} = \frac{\Psi'''}{\Psi'} - \frac32\Bigl(\frac{\Psi''}{\Psi'}\Bigr)^{2} = \frac{2a''}{a} - 4\Bigl(\frac{a'}{a}\Bigr)^{2} = -2a\Bigl(\frac1a\Bigr)'' ,
\]
derivatives in conformal time, $a$ at the point. $S$ vanishes on an interval exactly when $1/a$ is linear in $t$ there: de Sitter ($a = -1/(Ht)$) or the flat field. For $a = t^{n}$, $S = -2n(n + 1)/t^{2}$: radiation $-4/t^{2}$, matter $-12/t^{2}$. So the conformal vacuum is the ground state of the physical affine translations on every null generator exactly on de Sitter and flat fields (the ground-state clause of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i) in $\tilde\lambda$); on a radiation- or matter-dominated field it satisfies only the local form.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Note (2 November).} Clause (i) is subsumed by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field}: every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field, of every mass, has the flat massless vacuum as its scaling limit at every point of every globally hyperbolic gravitational field, whatever the Weyl curvature (standard, Sahlmann and Verch, re-derived). The conformal-covariance part of (i), which (ii) and the deposit result use, and clauses (ii) and (iii) stand: the generator statement (ii) is not given by that theorem. The premise (HS), \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}, has since been restated (version 3) as a statement about the Hadamard parametrix restricted to horizon generators; "the conclusion of (HS)" in (ii) is the scaling limit on the generators, the clause (b) of its version 2. The statements above are unchanged. \emph{(Added 2 November, later.)} (HS) is now a theorem (version 4 of \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}): its conclusion holds at every point of every local Rindler horizon, for every mass and whatever the Weyl curvature; this result stands as a separate route on Weyl-flat regions and does not use it.
synthesis.weyl-flat-fields-need-no-scali.technical:
The adopted scaling-limit premise (HS) says that at a point of a gravitational field with nonzero field strength a Hadamard state of the Dirac field looks, at short distances, like the flat field's massless vacuum, also on the null generators through the point. This result proves that statement for the massless Dirac field wherever the Weyl part of the field strength vanishes, on a globally hyperbolic region, including the Robertson-Walker fields of cosmology.

There the field is conformally flat and the massless Dirac field is conformally covariant, so a Hadamard state is carried to a flat-field Hadamard state, whose scaling limit is the vacuum (standard). On a null generator the physical affine parameter differs from the flat one by the factor $a^{2}$; with the comoving transverse labels as multiplicity space, the canonical anticommutator makes the generator field transform with weight one half, so the vacuum kernel changes only by a smooth Schwarzian term and the generator condition, hence the local form of (N$_{+}$), holds, at the leading order at which local Rindler horizons are defined. So, for the massless Dirac field, (HS) was needed only where the Weyl curvature is nonzero, and for massive fields everywhere. (HS) has since been proved in general, Weyl-curved and massive cases included; this result is a separate route on Weyl-flat regions.

Since 2 November the bulk scaling limit holds at every point of every globally hyperbolic gravitational field, for every mass, by a separate theorem, so the first part of this result is subsumed; the generator statement and the Robertson-Walker computation stand.

On a Robertson-Walker field the Schwarzian is $2a''/a - 4(a'/a)^{2}$ in conformal time, and the remainder in the physical affine parameter has leading coefficient $-S/a^{4}$ over twelve. It vanishes exactly for de Sitter and flat fields, where the conformal vacuum is the ground state for the physical affine translations on every null generator; on radiation- or matter-dominated fields it is not, and only the local form holds. Transport-absent.
synthesis.weyl-flat-fields-need-no-scali.lay: The series assumes that, very close up, the quantum field always looks like empty flat space, even where gravity is present. This result proves that assumption, for massless spin-one-half particles, wherever space-time is a rescaled copy of flat space, which includes the uniform expanding universe of cosmology. So, for those particles, the assumption is only needed where gravity distorts shapes, as near a black hole; for particles with mass it is still an assumption. It also finds that the universe's natural empty state counts as the lowest-energy state along light rays only if the expansion is of the accelerating de Sitter kind, not during the radiation era.
flags: massless Dirac field only: for a massive field the conformal map does not apply; the Weyl-flat massive case is covered by the scaling-limit theorem (HS), version 4, not by this result
local conformal chart: the Weyl-flat region is written as hb(b) = b/phi(x) in a gauge; global conformal flatness is not assumed

transverse labels: the generator continuum mode space uses the conformal chart's comoving transverse labels; the physical area element a^2 d^2y changes along an expanding generator, and weight one half in the physical affine parameter follows from the CAR once the comoving labels are chosen

local Rindler horizons: the chart's null planes through a point agree with the local Rindler horizons there (expansion-free at the point) at the leading order, tangent at the point, at which (HS) and (C_loc) define them, not beyond it
globally hyperbolic region U assumed (or a globally hyperbolic neighbourhood of each point), so that the Hadamard Facts apply on it

proofs.main:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$; $\Cl(1,3)$ with $e_{0}^{2} = 1$, $e_{i}^{2} = -1$.

\emph{Set-up.} $U$ is globally hyperbolic for the derived metric (hypothesis), so the Hadamard Facts apply on it. On $U$ the field $\hb(b) = b/\varphi$ has $\hb^{-1}(b) = \varphi b$ and derived metric $\varphi^{2}$ times the flat one (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i)). That a four-dimensional field with vanishing Weyl curvature is locally of this form in a suitable gauge is the local conformal flatness of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-covariance-of-massless-fields-and-local-conformal-flatness}(a); the frame $\hb^{-1}(e_{\mu}) = \varphi e_{\mu}$ is the flat one rescaled, so spinor frames are identified without rotation. For the massless Dirac field of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation} the equation is conformally covariant with weight $\tfrac32$: $\psi = \varphi^{-3/2}\chi$ with $\chi$ a solution of the flat massless equation on $U$, and the map preserves the conserved current, hence the CAR (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-covariance-of-massless-fields-and-local-conformal-flatness}(b)). The two-point kernels of a state of $\psi$ are $\varphi(x)^{-3/2}\varphi(y)^{-3/2}$ times those of the corresponding state of $\chi$; multiplication by a smooth nonvanishing function does not change wave-front sets, and the null geodesics of the derived metric are the flat null lines, affinely reparametrised by $d\tilde\lambda = \varphi^{2}d\lambda$ with unchanged covectors (along $x_{0} + f k$, $k$ null, the geodesic equation of the derived metric, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(iii) read in the chart, reduces to $f'' + 2f'^{2}\,\partial_{k}\varphi/\varphi = 0$, solved by $f' = \varphi^{-2}$; the covector $\varphi^{2}f'(k\cdot\,) = (k\cdot\,)$ is the flat one; checked as exact identities at rational times for three polynomial $\varphi$ of $t$, with the non-affine $f' = \varphi^{-1}$ failing), so the sets $C^{\pm}$ of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition} agree and $\omega$ is Hadamard for $\psi$ exactly when the corresponding state is Hadamard for the flat field $\chi$ on $U$.

\emph{(i)} This is the standard scaling-limit property of Hadamard states of free fields, transferred by conformal covariance. By Fact (b) the flat-field state differs from the flat massless vacuum by smooth kernels on $U \times U$, bounded near $(x_{0}, x_{0})$, which the scaling $l^{3}R(x_{0} + lx, x_{0} + ly)$ sends to zero. The vacuum kernel, off the cone the vector-valued $W(z) = z/Q(z)^{2}$ up to a constant, $z = x - y$, is homogeneous of degree $-3$, so $l^{3}\varphi(x_{0} + lx)^{-3/2}\varphi(x_{0} + ly)^{-3/2}W(lz) \to \varphi(x_{0})^{-3}W(z) = W(\varphi(x_{0})z)$: the flat massless vacuum in the coordinates $\varphi(x_{0})(x - x_{0})$. The check verifies $c^{3}W(cz) = W(z)$ for $c = a(t_{0})$ and that the factor $(s(t_{0} + lt_{1})s(t_{0} + lt_{2}))^{-3}$ for $a = s^{2}$ tends to $s(t_{0})^{-6}$ with error at most a constant times $l$.

\emph{(ii)} A null generator in $U$ lies on a flat null plane of the chart, and the restriction of the flat-field state of $\chi$ to that plane has, on every interval $J$ of every generator, kernel $W_{0}(\lambda, \lambda')\otimes\id_{K} + R$ with $R$ smooth in the flat affine parameter (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}(ii), (iii), applied on $U$; the result is local in $J$). Write $\tilde\lambda = \Psi(\lambda)$ with $\Psi' = \varphi^{2}$ along the generator. The physical generator field is $c\,\varphi^{-3/2}\chi_{N}$ for a positive function $c$ of $\lambda$. The physical area element $\varphi^{2}d^{2}y$ changes along an expanding generator, so the multiplicity space must be fixed by a choice; with the chart's comoving transverse labels fixed as $K$, the CAR in $\tilde\lambda$, $\delta(\tilde\lambda - \tilde\lambda')\delta^{2}(y - y')$, together with $\delta(\lambda - \lambda') = \Psi'\,\delta(\tilde\lambda - \tilde\lambda')$, gives $c^{2}\varphi^{-3}\Psi' = 1$, that is $c\varphi^{-3/2} = (\Psi')^{-1/2} = (d\lambda/d\tilde\lambda)^{1/2}$: weight $\tfrac12$. The kernel in $\tilde\lambda$ is therefore the weight-$\tfrac12$ pullback of $W_{0} + R$ by the smooth regular map $\Psi^{-1}$. The pulled-back $R$ is smooth; the pulled-back $W_{0}$ differs from the null vacuum of $\tilde\lambda$ by the kernel $\bigl((\Phi'(u)\Phi'(v))^{1/2}(u - v)/(\Phi(u) - \Phi(v)) - 1\bigr)\cdot\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v)^{-1}$, $\Phi = \Psi^{-1}$, which is smooth: $(\Phi(u) - \Phi(v))/(u - v) = \int_{0}^{1}\Phi'(v + s(u - v))\,ds$ is smooth and positive, the bracket is smooth and vanishes on the diagonal, and by Hadamard's lemma the quotient by $u - v$ is smooth (the bracket is $\tfrac{1}{12}S_{\Phi}(u - v)^{2} + O((u - v)^{3})$, so the kernel's leading term is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\cdot\tfrac{1}{12}S_{\Phi}(u - v)$; the expansion is the stored computation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-normality-at-the-edge-gives-the-null-ground-state}(iii)). So the remainder relative to the null vacuum of $\tilde\lambda$ is smooth on $\Psi(J)\times\Psi(J)$, the generator microlocal condition holds in the physical affine parameter, and by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state}(ii) the scaling limit at every point of the generator is the null vacuum: the local form of (N$_{+}$). This holds at every point of every null plane of the chart in $U$. A local Rindler horizon at $x_{0}$ is the null surface through a spacelike two-surface element at $x_{0}$ that is expansion-free at $x_{0}$; the chart's null plane with the same tangent at $x_{0}$ has physical expansion proportional to $\partial_{k}\varphi$ there, so the two agree at the leading order, tangent at $x_{0}$, at which (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) and the scaling-limit premise (HS) define the horizon, and the scaling limit at $x_{0}$ (the only thing the local form uses) is computed at that order, where it is the null vacuum on the common tangent generator. The statement is not made beyond that order.

\emph{(iii)} For $\varphi = a(t)$ and a null line $x_{0} + \lambda k$ with $k\cdot e_{0} = 1$, $t = t_{0} + \lambda$ and $\Psi' = a(t)^{2}$ along it. The conformal vacuum is the flat vacuum of $\chi$, whose restriction is exactly $W_{0}\otimes\id_{K}$ in $\lambda$ ($R = 0$), so in $\tilde\lambda$ it is the null vacuum plus the Schwarzian kernel above. By the bracket expansion of (ii) its leading term, read in the physical parameter, is $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}\cdot\tfrac{1}{12}S_{\Phi}(u - v)$, with the Schwarzian of $\Phi = \Psi^{-1}$ given by the inversion rule $S_{\Phi}(\tilde\lambda) = -S_{\Psi}(\lambda)/\Psi'(\lambda)^{2} = -S_{\Psi}/a^{4}$ (standard; computed: for the radiation $\Psi$ and rational $\lambda$ points the squared ratio in $\tilde\lambda$, which is the reciprocal of the one in $\lambda$ at the image points, satisfies $(r^{-2} - 1)/\tilde x^{2} \to -S_{\Psi}/(6a^{4})$ at rate $\tilde x$), so it vanishes exactly where $S_{\Psi}$ does; equivalently the null vacua of $\lambda$ and $\tilde\lambda$ differ by the weight-$\tfrac12$ Schwarzian kernel of $\Psi$, read in either parameter. With $\Psi' = a^{2}$, $\Psi'' = 2aa'$, $\Psi''' = 2a'^{2} + 2aa''$:
\[
S_{\Psi} = \frac{2a'^{2} + 2aa''}{a^{2}} - \frac32\cdot\frac{4a'^{2}}{a^{2}} = \frac{2a''}{a} - \frac{4a'^{2}}{a^{2}}, \qquad \Bigl(\frac1a\Bigr)'' = \frac{2a'^{2} - aa''}{a^{3}}, \qquad S_{\Psi} = -2a\Bigl(\frac1a\Bigr)'' ,
\]
checked at rational times for four polynomial $a$ by computing $\Psi'$, $\Psi''$, $\Psi'''$ from $a^{2}$, and as identities of rational functions for $a = t^{n}$, $-3 \le n \le 3$, and $a = 1/(\alpha t + \beta)$. Hence $S_{\Psi} \equiv 0$ on an interval exactly when $1/a = \alpha t + \beta$ there; then $\Psi = -1/(\alpha(\alpha t + \beta))$ (or $\beta^{-2}t$ for $\alpha = 0$) is a M\"obius map of $\lambda$, the weight-$\tfrac12$ kernel $\tfrac{i}{2\pi}(u - v + i0)^{-1}$ is invariant under it ($\Psi'(u)\Psi'(v)(u - v)^{2} = (\Psi(u) - \Psi(v))^{2}$ exactly, checked), and the conformal vacuum is the null vacuum of $\tilde\lambda$, the ground state of the physical affine translations (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(i)). synthesis.wick-rotor-chiral-angular-roto.formal:
Let $\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}$ be the radial boost bivector ($\sigma^{2} = +1$), $I_{4} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$, $E = e_{+}e_{-}$ and $I_{6} = I_{4}E$ as in Proposition \claimref{field-theory.where-each-lives}, and $I_{4}\sigma = e_{2}e_{3}$ the angular member of the curvature-selected pair (Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected}). Take as the unit of the continuation $\lambda \mapsto i\theta$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies} the complex unit $I_{6}$ of the conformal spinors $\CS$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $I_{6}\sigma = E\,(I_{4}\sigma) = E\,e_{2}e_{3}$, a $4$-blade of the real even algebra $\Cl^{+}(2,4)$, commuting with $\sigma$ and with $E$, with $(I_{6}\sigma)^{2} = -1$; so $R^{W}_{\theta} := \exp(\theta I_{6}\sigma/2) = \cos(\theta/2) + \sin(\theta/2)\,E\,e_{2}e_{3}$ is a real even element, with $R^{W}_{2\pi} = -1$ and $R^{W}_{4\pi} = +1$.
\item[(ii)] With the idempotents $\varepsilon_{\pm} = \tfrac12(1 \pm E)$ and the angular rotor $R_{\theta} = \exp(\theta I_{4}\sigma/2)$,
\[
R^{W}_{\theta} \;=\; \varepsilon_{+}R_{\theta} \;+\; \varepsilon_{-}R_{-\theta} .
\]
On $\CS = L_{0} \oplus L_{\infty}$, the $E = \pm 1$ eigenspaces on which $I_{6} = \pm I_{4}$, the continued boost therefore acts on $L_{0}$ as the real angular rotor $R_{\theta}$ and on $L_{\infty}$ as $R_{-\theta}$: on each chiral doublet the Wick-rotated radial boost is a real rotation of the angular plane, its sense fixed by the chirality, that is by the relative sign of $I_{6}$ and $I_{4}$.
\item[(iii)] $R^{W}_{\theta}$ is not a rotor: $R^{W}_{\theta}\rev{R^{W}_{\theta}} = \cos\theta + \sin\theta\,E\,e_{2}e_{3} \neq 1$ for $\theta \notin 2\pi\Z$, and for $\theta \notin \pi\Z$ conjugation by it does not map vectors to vectors. For $\theta \notin \pi\Z$ it is no isometry of the ambient vectors, so clause (3) of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies} stands for vectors and for every holonomy of a real connection, while the identification of the Euclidean rotation with the angular member in Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected} holds on each chiral half of the conformal spinors, up to the orientation sign.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.wick-rotor-chiral-angular-roto.technical: The singularity paper continues the radial boost $\exp(\lambda\sigma/2)$ to imaginary rapidity with an external unit $i$ and finds that the result is no real rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$; the state-selection note instead reads the Euclidean rotation as the real angular rotor $\exp(\theta I\sigma_r/2)$, $I\sigma_r = e_{2}e_{3}$. Taking for $i$ the conformal spinors' own unit $I_{6} = I_{4}E$ reconciles the two. Since $I_{6}\sigma = E\,e_{2}e_{3}$ with $E$ and $e_{2}e_{3}$ commuting, the continued boost is the real even element $\cos(\theta/2) + \sin(\theta/2)E\,e_{2}e_{3}$, equal to $\tfrac12(1+E)R_{\theta} + \tfrac12(1-E)R_{-\theta}$. On the chiral halves $L_{0}$, $L_{\infty}$ of the conformal spinors ($E = \pm1$) it is the angular rotor turned one way or the other, so the state-selection reading holds on each chirality, the sense of rotation being the orientation bit. For $\theta \notin \pi\Z$ it is not even in the Clifford group, so the singularity paper's statement that no real rotor, and no holonomy, realises the Euclidean rotation is untouched.
synthesis.wick-rotor-chiral-angular-roto.lay: A standard way to see that black holes are hot is to turn the time of a static observer into an angle. Two of the series' texts seemed to disagree about which real rotation that angle belongs to: one says no real rotation of spacetime does the job, the other says the rotation along the horizon sphere does. Using the imaginary unit that the series' twistor-like spinors already carry, this result shows both are right in their own place: acting on spinors of one handedness the turned boost is exactly the rotation along the sphere, in a direction set by the handedness, while acting on ordinary directions in spacetime it is not a rotation at all.

proofs.main:
\emph{Step 1 (the generator).} By Proposition \claimref{field-theory.where-each-lives}, $I_{6} = I_{4}E$ with $E^{2} = 1$ and $[I_{4}, E] = 0$; $E$ is the product of two vectors orthogonal to spacetime, so it commutes with $\sigma$ and with $e_{2}e_{3}$. Hence $I_{6}\sigma = I_{4}E\sigma = E\,I_{4}\sigma$, and $I_{4}\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{0}e_{1} = (e_{0}e_{1})^{2}e_{2}e_{3} = e_{2}e_{3}$ (Proposition \claimref{state-selection.euclidean-partner-curvature-selected}). So $I_{6}\sigma = E\,e_{2}e_{3}$, the blade $e_{+}e_{-}e_{2}e_{3}$, and $(E\,e_{2}e_{3})^{2} = E^{2}(e_{2}e_{3})^{2} = -1$. It commutes with $\sigma$ because $I_{6}$ is central in the even algebra and $\sigma$ is even. The exponential of an element of square $-1$ is $\cos(\theta/2) + \sin(\theta/2)\,I_{6}\sigma$, which is $-1$ at $\theta = 2\pi$ and $+1$ at $4\pi$, as in Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}(1). By Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion} $I_{6}$ is the complex unit of $\CS$. The store's conventions define that unit as right multiplication by $I_{6}$; on $\CS$ left and right multiplication by $I_{6}$ agree, because $I_{6}$ is central in $\Cl^{+}(2,4)$. So on $\CS$ this element is the continued rotor $R_{i\theta}$ with $i$ read as $I_{6}$.

\emph{Step 2 (the splitting).} $\varepsilon_{\pm} = \tfrac12(1 \pm E)$ are orthogonal idempotents summing to $1$ and commute with $e_{2}e_{3}$, and $\varepsilon_{\pm}E = \pm\varepsilon_{\pm}$. So $\varepsilon_{\pm}R^{W}_{\theta} = \varepsilon_{\pm}(\cos(\theta/2) \pm \sin(\theta/2)e_{2}e_{3}) = \varepsilon_{\pm}R_{\pm\theta}$, and summing gives the displayed identity. The identity holds in the algebra, hence on every left module. On $\CS$ the eigenspaces $L_{0}$, $L_{\infty}$ of $E$ are $\varepsilon_{+}\CS$ and $\varepsilon_{-}\CS$, and on them $I_{6} = \pm I_{4}$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.where-each-lives}(3)), which gives (ii).

\emph{Step 3 (not a rotor).} The reverse of a $4$-blade is itself, so $\rev{R^{W}_{\theta}} = R^{W}_{\theta}$ and $R^{W}_{\theta}\rev{R^{W}_{\theta}} = (R^{W}_{\theta})^{2} = R^{W}_{2\theta} = \cos\theta + \sin\theta\,E\,e_{2}e_{3}$, which is $1$ only for $\theta \in 2\pi\Z$. For a vector $x$, $(E e_{2}e_{3})x(E e_{2}e_{3})^{-1}$ is a vector, but the cross term $\cos(\theta/2)\sin(\theta/2)\,[E e_{2}e_{3}, x]$ of the conjugate of $x = e_{2}$ is $2\cos(\theta/2)\sin(\theta/2)\,E\,e_{3}$ up to sign, of grade three, so the conjugate is not a vector unless $\cos(\theta/2)\sin(\theta/2) = 0$. An isometry of the ambient, or a holonomy of a real spin connection, is implemented by an element of the Clifford group, so $R^{W}_{\theta}$ is neither; the angular rotor $R_{\theta}$ is a rotor and fixes $e_{0}$ and $e_{1}$. This is (iii).

The script \file{check.py} verifies in exact arithmetic in $\Cl(2,4)$ the identities of Step 1, the idempotents, the splitting of (ii) at four rational points of the circle, the inverse, the failure of $R\rev{R} = 1$ and of vector preservation at those points, the rotor property of $R_{\theta}$ and its fixing of $e_{0}$, $e_{1}$, and the periods at $\theta = \pi, 2\pi, 4\pi$.

synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-e.formal:
\emph{The window reading (adopted).} Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a half-generator of a horizon in the scope of Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}, with surface gravity $\kappa$, Killing time $\tau$ and affine parameter $u = e^{\kappa\tau}$, let an array be an evenly spaced set of modes with weights $\omega_{k} = \kappa(k + \delta)$, $k \in \Z$, $0 \le \delta < 1$ (an s-wave array of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}, whose version 3 has $\delta = \tfrac12$). The array is read as one chiral complex component of the continuum of that light ray on a window of Killing time of length $2\pi/\kappa$ (its real-time recurrence window), and its Killing energy, in every state, is the Killing energy of the continuum over that window measured from the null ground state that (N$_{+}$) selects, that is, in the normal ordering at that state, in which $\langle T_{uu}\rangle = 0$.

\emph{What it is for.} It is the hypothesis of clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric}, which with it decides the ordering question left open by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.counted-unit-energy-at-half-offset}: the boost ground state carries $-\kappa/24$ per complex component over one window measured from the null ground state, and an array's zeta-regularised symmetric sea energy $\tfrac{\kappa}{2}B_{2}(\delta)$ takes that value exactly at $\delta = \tfrac12$. Given the reading, (i) the half offset of (Q) version 3 is singled out by (N$_{+}$), being the only offset at which an array's own sea is consistent with the null ordering window by window; (ii) at that offset the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering is the physical ordering of the sea's energy; (iii) a counted unit of two arrays carries mean Killing energy $0$ at the Hawking temperature, the equality case of clause (v) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}; (iv) the constant of the hole's Hamiltonian in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hole-mass-is-ground-energy-label}(iii) is all of $M$, so the ground-energy label carries all of $M$ and the counted units none. It does not fix the count unit (two arrays per registered unit remains a decision), the label's energy function, or which fields form the sea.

\emph{What it costs.} It is a reading of the arrays, not a consequence of (N$_{+}$): (N$_{+}$) cannot be posed on point-spectrum mode sets (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises}(iv)), and the reading applies that theorem's discretisation reading, by which the point-spectrum wordings of the thermal premises are discretisations of the continuum statements, to energy. It also identifies the spectrum of an array, of spacing $\kappa$, with a twisted identification of real Killing time over one window, which the continuum does not supply. The numbers it relates are equalities proved without it; without it the ordering is not decided.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The reading is false if any of the following is established: (a) a derivation, from the series' premises, of the Killing energy of an array (for example from a construction of the arrays out of the continuum modes of a light ray) that differs from the continuum's window energy measured from the null ground state; (b) a derivation that the arrays' offset is not $\tfrac12$, since under the reading no other offset is consistent with the null ordering window by window (at $\delta = 0$ the symmetric sea is $+\kappa/12$, not $-\kappa/24$); (c) a derivation, from the series' premises, that the counted units carry a nonzero mean Killing energy, or that the hole's energy $M$ is shared between the label and the counted units.
synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-e.technical: The series counts a black hole's entropy in units of two arrays, evenly spaced sets of modes on each light ray of the horizon, and the energy those units carry depends on where the zero of energy is put. The null ground-state premise (N$_{+}$) puts the zero of null energy at the state of the light rays it selects, but it is a statement about the continuum of each light ray and cannot be posed on an array. This reading bridges the two: an array is one stretch of a light ray's continuum, one recurrence window of Killing time $2\pi/\kappa$ long, and its Killing energy is the continuum's energy over that window, measured from the null ground state. With it, the stored equality of numbers becomes a decision of the ordering: the half offset of (Q) version 3 is the only offset at which an array's zeta-regularised sea takes the null ground state's window value, the symmetric ordering is the physical one, the counted units carry no mean Killing energy, and the whole of the hole's mass sits in the ground-energy label. It is adopted, not derived, and would be refuted by a derivation of an array's energy that disagrees, by a forced offset other than one half, or by a derivation that the counted units carry part of the mass.
synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-e.lay: The series counts a black hole's entropy in small units on its horizon, and whether those units carry energy depends on where the zero of energy is placed. The series' premise about the state on the horizon's light rays places it, but only for the light rays as a whole, not for the counted units. This assumption connects the two: a unit's energy is the energy of the stretch of light ray it stands for. With it, the units carry no energy on average and the hole's mass sits in a single overall constant. It is an assumption of the series, stated so that it can be refuted.
